### R7-A (WS-4.6): the policy-gate bypass is closed by one shared x-edge refusal; the edge probe reads 0 out-of-band fires / 0 bypasses and the shipped interface byte-unchanged

**Scope (2026-10-14, branch `r7-bypass` from `main` at `6d71cdb`, tag
`v0.10`).** Phase R7-A of the R7 PLAN (`.slim/deepwork/sorting-pipeline-v3.md`
"R7 PLAN"): the WS-4.6 interface item - `should_fire`'s
`FRUIT_POLICY_TRIGGER_X_MAX` refusal filtered only the trigger arm of the
env's `policy_close or intercept` union, so the learned close gate
(`finger < 0.030` + 6 cm) could attempt a refused fruit anyway. The mechanism
first, then the bounded fix; the edge-band probe + the refusal cross-check as
the yardsticks; Tier A solo. **No shipped default change** (the guard stays
default off, owner R5; the fix is inert and every added branch `None`-gated
while `x_max` is unset). Three files: `policy/trigger.py` (the shared
`x_edge_refusal` predicate; `should_fire` refactored onto it,
behaviour-identical), `rl_env.py` (the module-level `direct_fire` union + the
gate-tick refusal and its once-per-fruit note + the `trigger_x_max` provenance
key), `scripts/811_trigger_test.py` (the truth table). Full evidence
`logs/r7/A_RESULTS.md`.

1. **The mechanism, measured on a pre-fix control.** `policy_close = finger <
   0.030 and distance < 0.06` and `intercept, info = should_fire(...)` are
   evaluated independently from the same pose; the refusal note (`x_refuse`)
   is recorded but the union fires on either path. The pre-fix record: R2 P1
   4/7 refusals attempted anyway (4/4 flailed), R6 C0/C1/C2 3/3, 4/4, 3/3
   (all flailed) - **14/17 refusals attempted anyway** across the four
   controls. The paired pre-fix control (`logs/r7/A_control_edge.log`; its
   tree pin md5-verifies against `HEAD` `6d71cdb`, so the fix runs have a
   one-tree-one-change companion) repeats R6-C0 verbatim (edge band
   0.36-0.42, reseed + cap, `moe_v13s`, seed 77, N=1x15): **5 flails (1
   premove-cap + 4 fast-stall), 6 refusals, 1 attempted-anyway** (ep3: the
   close at finger=0.0286 / 4.4 cm ran a 3.92 s premove cap, close-start
   residual 1375.7 mm - the control's premove-cap *is* the attempted-anyway).
2. **The fix.** `x_edge_refusal(settings, fruit) -> x | None` is the refusal;
   `direct_fire(intercept, policy_close, gate_refuse) = intercept or
   (policy_close and gate_refuse is None)` is the union with the refusal
   folded in; a gate-refused tick records the canonical once-per-fruit note
   (if absent) plus one `x-edge policy-gate refuse` note (`finger` /
   `|jaw-fruit|xy` at the tick) and runs no primitive. The offline truth
   table is pinned in `811_trigger_test.py` (7 new checks).
3. **The probe: the refusal binds; the bypass reads 0.** F1 (edge, reseed +
   cap): **1 flail (fast-stall), 9 refusals, 4 gate refusals (x =
   0.400/0.399/0.395/0.426), 0 out-of-band fires**; F2 (the repeat sample):
   2 flails (fast-stall), 6 refusals, 3 gate refusals (0.415/0.398/0.414),
   0 out-of-band fires; F3 (cap only, the R2-P1 shape): 3 flails (2
   premove-cap + 1 fast-stall), 5 gate refusals, **0 out-of-band fires / 0
   bypasses - the strict legacy signature (canonical refusal + learned close)
   reads 0 in F1+F2 and 1 in F3** (ep5, below); its one re-qualification
   (refused at x=0.394, an in-band intercept fired later, the attempt lost
   with a 246.2 mm fast-stall leg; the close was also armed on that in-band
   tick, which is why the strict signature counts it) shows the fix refuses
   the out-of-band tick, not the in-band fire - the strict marker is
   necessary, not sufficient, on a fix tree; F4 (shipped band + cap): 0
   refusals / 0 flails, no starvation. All seven of F1/F2's gate-refused
   episodes ride past (`fruit fell off the line`), no primitive leg runs; the
   residual fast-stalls (26.5-155.8 mm residuals) are the W7-B catch-up
   class.
4. **Scope.** The R7-A endpoint is the mechanism, not a rate: the N=5
   protocol was not run (no adoption/rate claim; the guard stays default off)

   controls above. The residual is the reach cliff itself (the refusal is a
   screen; the station/reach geometry is the D screen's second item - the grip
   plane / cradle is first, per the R7-C order unification) plus the
   fast-stall / in-band-fire nuances.
5. **No-harm.** `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS** (0 failures, 1 skipped; the

### R8-A (the D screen): the lower grip plane, the cradle/scoop and the raised station are all measured negatives; the grip-geometry lever space is closed around the carry class and the no-harm is a bit-identical replay

Lane: phase R8-A of the R8 PLAN (`.slim/deepwork/sorting-pipeline-v3.md`), executing
the **pre-registered D screen** (`logs/r7/FRONTIER_R7.md` section 4) on branch
`r8-dscreen` (from `main` at `38304b8`, tag `v0.11`). Tier A solo, one claim lane
11:39:40 -> 13:48:41 (**2 h 09 m**). Report: `logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md`; drivers
`logs/r8/run_r8a_screen.sh` / `run_r8a_d3_noharm.sh` / `A_report.sh`; readouts
`A_bands.txt` / `A_probe.txt` / `A_taxonomy.txt` / `A_battery_report.txt` /
`A_gate.txt` / `A_compare.txt`. **No shipped default changed** (owner R5 stands);
both new levers are default-off env knobs, and the shipped path is proven
byte-unchanged rather than asserted (below).

1. **The candidates and their implementations.** *D2a* - a new default-off
   `FRUIT_GRIP_PLANE_DROP` [m] in `tasks.py::_pad_standoff` that seats the
   moving catch's whole hand lower on the payload (candidate 0.008; a labelled
   0.004 boundary sample). *D2b* - a new asset variant `FRUIT_FINGER_SCOOP=1`
   in `scene.py::_add_finger_scoops`: one ledge per finger link (4), authored in
   the `_finger_face_frame` contact frame before `play()`; top edge 2 mm past
   the fingertip on the true face plane, inward 6 mm over 12 mm, 14 mm wide,
   4 mm thick - a sloped passive shelf under the pinch, open along the belt
   axis. *D3* - the bounded proxy: the existing default-off pick platform
   (`FRUIT_NEST=0.02 FRUIT_NEST_WIDTH=0.05`, 100 mm wide, 20 mm tall), i.e.
   "a pick station the hand reaches clear of the belt"; the second half of the
   D3 form (a descent command that respects the boundary) is not implemented
   (the pre-registration says the properly-scoped variant needs the multi-seed
   IK / self-centring feeder).

2. **D2a FAILS; the reach boundary is the leading hypothesis, not isolated.**
   Direct probe (-8 mm): 3/15, classes ok 3 / carried 1 / **no-contact 11**,
   flails **1 -> 14** (9 fast-stall + 5 hover-cap), close-start y median
   **-3.8 -> +59.0 mm**, the lift-leg population **moved up** out of the
   100-400 mm band (11 -> 2) into the **>400 mm** band (2 -> 10, all lost):
   escape signature present, negative branch move. Battery x2 bit-identical:
   **5/20 = 25 %** (control 12/20) with gripper-loss notes **1 -> 11** plus a
   `fruit left the pick station during the close (357 mm)` note, and one
   descent **out of the speed budget** (`|v|max` 0.172 vs 0.161) - `105
   --write-fingerprint` refuses the run (a pre-registered fail condition on
   its own). Mechanism: the catch-up caps (**14/15** at -8 mm) are **expected
   even with a reachable target** - the drop moves the *commanded* catch
   target (`catch_target` uses `_pad_standoff`, tasks.py:6112-6114) but NOT
   the catch-up break test (`desired_tip` uses `_dynamic_pad_lift`,
   tasks.py:6094), so a -8 mm drop shifts the loop's residual equilibrium by
   ~the drop; the control's own catch-up floor (**5.3-6.0 mm** against the
   6 mm tolerance) is the loop's threshold-crossing value, not a measured
   reach margin. What remains of the reach reading: the shipped dynamic grip
   target also sits near the arm's vertical boundary (the same boundary as
   the every-descent 40-90 mm shortfall), so any downward drop shrinks an
   already narrow window; the labelled **-4 mm boundary sample** (direct only)
   is the better-isolated realization - its hover converges (0 caps) but the
   catch-up still mostly caps (11/15, no-contact 8) and it fails with the
   >400 mm population persisting. The missing control that would isolate the
   reach reading: the drop **+ a drop-adjusted break test + a -2 mm
   magnitude**. The in-band pad-plate alternative is already closed (v6 exp 2:
   5/10 at 12 mm, 7/10 co-planar-only); the -4/-8 mm realizations cannot be
   measured in-band at any magnitude that matters.

3. **D2b FAILS - the ledges bat the payload (the P3/D additive-face class the
   pre-registration warned about).** Direct probe: 2/15, classes
   ok 2 / carried 4 / **no-contact 9**, flails **1 -> 7** (2 premove-cap + 5
   hover-cap), close-start offsets **0.3-1.1 m** (`fruit drifted 1169 mm off
   the pick centre`; `[carry]` slides to **3972 mm**), the lift-leg population
   **reduced 15 -> 14**, the 100-400 mm leg count 11 -> 3 with the population
   redistributed into **>400 mm** (2 -> 8). Battery x2 bit-identical:
   **6/20 = 30 %**, gripper-loss notes **1 -> 12** (all the control's class -
   the genuinely new battery notes on this screen are D2a's station-close and
   D3's never-settled); the descents stay in band
   (worst `|v|max` 0.119 vs 0.116) and `190` fails only on the rate floor.
   Mechanism (two classes in the rows): the ordinary failures repeat the known
   loaded-slide class (onset rows 70-98, `force@onset` 4.95-7.10 N, one-sided
   contact), while the new flicked class is the `grasp_lift` rows registering
   in the first 1-2 ticks with `sep@onset` <= 22 mm (the next-smallest onset
   sep is 59.2 mm) - **7 rows**: 17.7/22.0/10.0/9.8/10.0/15.0/9.9 mm,
   `force@onset` 0/0/0/13.14/0/35.69/16.80 N - the payload was batted off the
   station before the close and the hand chases a phantom. The ledges sit in
   the close's swept volume; the nominal ~3.7 mm proximal clearance is smaller

4. **D3 FAILS - the platform obstructs the supply.** Direct probe: 2/15,
   no-contact **12**, flails **11** (9 premove-cap + 2 fast-stall), closes

5. **The criterion, applied (the pre-registered reading).** (a) zero carry legs

6. **No-harm is proven, not asserted.** The scripted control battery (default

### R9 (the bounded RL/DAgger lane): AWR-clipped RWR iteration 2 on fresh on-policy rollouts - the carried class does not convert, the handover state degrades, and the lane closes negative (published)

**Scope (2026-10-14, branch `r9-rl`, from `main` at `328332d`/tag `v0.12`,
Tier A solo).** Phase R9 of the plan (`.slim/deepwork/sorting-pipeline-v3.md`
"R9 PLAN", the R8-A fallback; `logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md` section 7). Report
`logs/r9/RESULTS.md`; committed drivers `scripts/195_r9_chain.sh`,
`scripts/196_r9_report.py`, `scripts/197_r9_merge_rollouts.py`. **Env-only: no
`src/` change, no shipped default change, no adoption.** The whole chain (56
recorded rollouts -> AWR fine-tune -> fidelity -> N=5 A/B -> no-harm) ran in
~3.5 h wall.

1. **The lane and the not-the-nulls argument.** AWR-clipped reward-weighted
   regression - the RWR iteration-2 item, never run - fine-tuning
   `moe_v13s` (`61da390a`) on fresh on-policy direct rollouts with
   `w = clip(exp(4*(R-Vbar)), 0.05, 4)` and the `demos_v11` base (`922ca995`)
   at 1.0. The two published nulls (W7-C `moe_v13p` N=3, W8-A N=5 21/75 vs
   22/75 p=1.0000) are **off-policy behaviour cloning** (`weight_mode=ones`
   on 158/173 successful scripted/two-line episodes); this lane weights the
   policy's own outcome distribution. The P4 trigger-margin fix has no object
   in the pinned interface (encoder-fed arrival trigger, ACQ=1; W8-A records
   zero policy-gate fires) and the per-tick correction head has a measured
   negative prior (path-3 A2C2 -20 pt). `moe_v12` `3a9ccfc0` is pinned as the
   shipped default but not the fine-tune base (arm A of the pre-registered
   baseline is `moe_v13s`; a v12 base would confound the paired test).

2. **Environment finding (operational).** Recorded multi-seed runs hit the
   known RTX `multitick.render` stall after ~3.5 min in this session (driver
   log frozen, sim 0.03x, GPU idle; two attempts), while single-seed runs of
   the same shape completed 15 episodes in 6.7-7.0 min (both a non-recorded
   and a recorded control). The rollouts were collected as **single-seed
   recorded shards** under a 300-s freeze + GPU-idle watchdog and merged by
   the new `scripts/197_r9_merge_rollouts.py` (byte copy + renumbering; store
   schema untouched): seeds 909/505/606/707 -> **56 episodes, 18 successes**
   (`datasets/rl_rollouts/r9_awr`; the four shard index md5s in its
   `merge_manifest.json`). Recorded episodes carry only the policy phase
   (25-92 frames) - the primitive owns everything after the trigger.

3. **Training + fidelity.** `WEIGHT_MODE=awr BETA=4 EPOCHS=4 LR=5e-5`:
   Vbar=0.3103 -> successes 4.0 / failures 0.289 / base 1.0; 4 epochs at 61 s;
   candidate `checkpoints/rl_awr1/policy_best.pt` md5
   `a1766ecdf29031944e4c3b5499e8931e`. Offline fidelity (192 windows,
   DDIM-16): on its **own rollouts** 0.087 -> **0.174 rad** (24 improved /
   168 worse; phase 94 -> 86 %), on `demos_v11` 0.079 -> 0.081 - the same
   demo-anchoring movement RWR-1 measured: even at a 4x success weight the
   fine-tune overwrites the policy's own approach.

4. **The N=5 endpoint (pre-registered; one claim, 17:55-19:06, 10/10 runs

### R10-A: the reach-anywhere dynamic catch - the coverage/interval goals are delivered, the success and no-new-class criteria fail, and the knob stays default-off

1. **What was asked.** The owner correction (binding): the moving catch must
   generalize across the arm's reachable workspace - any reachable (x, y), on
   the fly, never stopped; the station-fixed catch (the fruit must arrive under
   a fixed y) is the limitation to remove. R10-A: measure the reachable
   intercept set, design the interception-point catch, implement it behind a
   default-off knob, and measure coverage / success / interval / per-leg motion
   against the station-fixed control. Pre-registered in
   `logs/r10/PREREGISTRATION.md` before the implementation edit; results in
   `logs/r10/A_RESULTS.md`.

2. **The reachable-intercept map (new measurement).** `scripts/183_reach_intercept.py`
   extends the `174_station_reach` approach to the y dimension (3 x-columns x
   11 dy, the top-down grip/hover poses, the calibrated seed, 6 mm tolerance,
   plus the sweep-end poses and the setup-timing ladder; raw rows
   `logs/r10/reach_intercept_{left,right}.json`). Clean grip bands: left
   x=0.20 `-0.10..+0.15`, x=0.28 `-0.05..+0.10`, x=0.36 `0.00..+0.10`; right
   x=0.20 `-0.10..+0.10`, x=0.28 `-0.10..+0.05`, x=0.36 `-0.10..0.00`; the
   cliffs are sharp (29.6-186.5 mm one 0.05 step outside). **The left x=0.28
   cell was corrected in place by the A1 pass**: the first write read
   `-0.05..+0.20` off the 6.5 mm dy=+0.20 row; the run summary
   `11_reach_left.log` reads `-0.05..+0.10 (4/11)` (the +0.15/+0.20 rows are
   8.2/6.5 mm, outside the 6 mm tolerance) and the measured ranges nest, so a
   fruit between columns takes the next column's band. The arms mirror
   across the belt: each reaches upstream on its own side and cliffs across
   it. **The setup ladder: the hover move costs 0.57-0.78 s (68-94 ticks) at
   every reachable offset** (base ~0.60 s + ~1.2-1.4 s/m marginal, ~0.8 m/s
   lateral); unreachable targets burn the 600-tick cap - the R2 flail class.
   The sweep-end rows are clean on only 4/33 + 3/33 points, but that is **not**
   the sweep constraint: the shipped line already holds the payload through
   ~0.1 m of belt travel with millimetre relative motion (W8-B `clean_slip`),
   because the close tracks the fruit and the pads are loaded - the band is the
   *grip/aim* band only.

3. **The design (implemented behind `FRUIT_REACH_ANYWHERE`, default off;
   `tasks.py` `7e20255c`).** `_reach_predict` computes the interception point
   (`y_int = y_f + vy*(t_setup(y) + t_desc + margin)`, a bounded fixed point
   with contraction `v/v_hover`, clipped into the arm's measured x-columned
   band; feasible iff the unclipped prediction is at or above the downstream
   edge). `_reach_prepare_aim` caches it at the pre-pose end (the hover move,
   both wait loops and `_approach` are unchanged - they already time relative
   to the grip target); `_dynamic_aim` returns it. `_reach_anywhere_select`
   replaces the station floor (`0.399 m` at 0.12 m/s) with the band-relative
   floor and picks the minimum fruit travel to the clipped intercept, ties to
   the nearest; the shipped station-fixed rule is the fallback (it never fired
   - the reach rule is a strict superset on the measured bands). Scoped to the
   scripted OpenArm moving-catch line; the two-line and direct/policy paths
   keep their rules; off = byte-unchanged. Tooling: `198_r10_selftest.py`
   (offline pins, a selfcheck leg), `199_r10_battery.sh`, `199_r10_report.py`
   (read-only re-derivation), `FRUIT_REACH_DIAG=1` rows.

4. **The measurement (W6-A patch sheet, single arm, 20 attempts, seed 5;
   control `logs/r10/30_control.log`, treatment `31_reach.log`).** Coverage
   (the primary): **73 vs 45 candidate-fruit across the same 20 selection
   instants (+62 %)** (re-derived by `199` from the `[reach] select` rows;
   the first write's 72/+60 % was a miscount, corrected in place by the A1
   pass); instants with >= 1 catchable candidate 20/20 vs 19/20;
   the treatment ran 20 attempts vs the control's 18 (2 starved). Interval:
   per-attempt span **15.24 -> 13.98 s (-8 %)** (the wait segment 3.06 ->
   1.68 s), but inter-placement interval 27.62 -> 45.14 s and throughput
   2.17 -> 1.33 placed/min (window). Success: **13/18 = 72 % -> 8/20 = 40 %**.
   Classes: placed-False 5/18 -> 7/20; **"fruit did not follow the gripper"
   0/18 -> 5/20** (3 carry escapes after contact, attempts 2/5/14 + 2 timing
   chases, attempts 15 the fallback and 19 the band cap; the re-seat count is
   **13 vs 0**); diverted 1 -> 3. Per-leg motion: 19/20 descents inside the
   profile budget; the one over (0.165 vs 0.162) is the **attempt-15 fallback**
   leg (36.2 cm, `end=262.8 mm`; the attempt-19 chase leg itself is inside).
   Mechanism:
   intercepts min -0.059 / p50 +0.011 / max +0.180 m (early, not late); the
   descent-end error p50 +3.4 mm; catch-up p50 14 ticks; **the descent wait is
   0 ticks in 16/20 treatment attempts against 59-89 in the control** - the
   just-in-time handover removes the shipped line's hover settling (the
   leading hypothesis; its named test is the `FRUIT_REACH_HOVER_SETTLE` A/B), and the
   grip phase grows 1.60 -> 2.52 s.

5. **The verdict.** The pre-registered fail condition fired: success 8/20 vs
   13/18; a carry/grip class absent from the control appears 5/20; one motion
   leg over (the fallback). **No adoption; the knob stays default-off; no shipped
   default changes.** The named residuals: (a) the just-in-time catch loses
   the hover settling (leading hypothesis; the measured test is the priced
   `FRUIT_REACH_HOVER_SETTLE` A/B, `logs/r10/A1_RESULTS.md`); (b) the band cap
   and the long hover move (attempt 19: the aim at the old +0.20 cap, a 2.67 s
   hover against a 0.83 s estimate, the 661 mm chase; the corrected band caps
   at +0.08 inset and the default-off capped-hover fallback is the general
   protection - the R2 knobs are direct/trigger-scoped, not this lever);
   (c) the setup model has no x-term (the hover move
   also travels to the fruit's measured x; a named design item with its own
   pre-registration); (d) setup-time variance (a 2.02 s
   pre-pose after a failed carry) breaks the just-in-time feasibility (attempt
   15, the one fallback chase).

6. **No-harm.** The control run is **byte-identical to the W6-B single-arm
   patch record** (`logs/w6/20_battery_single.log`, 643/643 physics `[fruit]`
   lines) - the knob-off path is unchanged. Determinism: both double-runs are

   The acceptance (`logs/r10/50_accept.log`): **9/10 + motion gate PASS +
   `fingerprint: matches`**, its physics stream **365/365 identical to the R9
   acceptance** (`logs/r9/60_accept_r9.log`). The two-line dense re-record
   (`logs/r10/70_twoline_dense.log`, 7/10, 9.1 s/attempt) is **442/442
   identical to the W7-A record** (`logs/w7/10_dense_twoline_1.log`) and
   `scripts/190_twoline_gate.sh` **PASS**. Pins: `tasks.py`
   `7e20255cd32e4d438cfa9ffc5f4dc5e7`, `rl_env.py` `TASKS_MD5` metadata-only

### P1 (2026-10-15, owner #1 "为什么会要等那么长时间的果？你增加流水线上果蔬数量不行吗"): the supply-density lever is the largest single win since the park gate, and the interval is cadence-bound not arrival-bound

The owner's hypothesis (raise the fruit on the line) was pre-registered before any run
(`logs/p/PREREGISTRATION.md`) and measured on the two-line patch sheet (ATTEMPTS=20, SEED=5, Tier A
solo). The lever is `FRUIT_SUPPLY_PATCH_DENSITY` (D, default 1.0, `fruits.py`
`88b76b572b16224313a0ff3860e2940c`): the along-slice gaps divide by D (floor 0.085 m = the
`_release_clear` 0.08 m rule + a margin) and the abreast probability rises toward 1; D=1 is
byte-identical (the 172 selftest, 52 checks).

**Result (the dose-response has an optimum):** control 12/20 = 60 %, 3.64 placed/min, interval
16.53 s -> **D=1.5 15/20 = 75 %, 4.48 placed/min, 13.34 s** -> **D=1.5 + belt 0.15 m/s 17/20 =
85 %, 5.31 placed/min, 11.10 s** (+46 % throughput, -33 % interval). **D=2.0 overshoots to 25 %**
(interval 39.22 s). The D=1.5 and D=2.0 pairs are bit-identical on the double runs, so each is one
sample of a deterministic branch.

**The mechanism (this corrects the W6-B/R3 "arrival-bound" framing):** the per-attempt arm span
is **constant ~15 s** in every config and the **lock-on latency does not fall** (left 3.73 -> 4.57
-> 4.27 s, right 5.27 -> 5.01 -> 6.08 s). The left's mean inter-placement interval falls **50.7 ->
20.1 s** because the **attempts inside the interval fall 40.4 -> 15.7 s** - the density removes the
failed/empty attempts between two placements, not the wait. So the interval was never purely
arrival-bound; it is **cadence x success**, and at D=1.5 + 0.15 the interval (11.10 s) is within
15 % of the 9.6 s attempt span, i.e. **the per-attempt span is now the binding term**. The faster
belt trades descent 3.03 -> 2.25 s against place+release 4.99 -> 5.95 s (the placed fruit pile up
in the lane) and costs the right's lock-on, net zero on the span.

**The classes:** no new class (the pre-registered fail item (b) passes). D=2.0's collapse is
**crowding breaking the acquisition** (18 "fruit did not follow the gripper" rows plus mostly
`grasped=False`), not starvation; the best config's 3 residual failures are all
**carried-not-placed** (the W8-B loaded-slide class, lift 0.136-0.217 m) and its squeeze-class
count is **0**. Item (a) is read honestly as: the raw starved-slot count rises 41 -> 54 (the
denominator effect - more successful attempts means more selection instants) while the
normalized idle fraction is flat (20 -> 22 %), so the prediction "the starvation falls" is
**half false** and the gain is attributed to the wasted-attempt removal instead.

**The no-harm:** acceptance **9/10 = 90 %**, motion gate **PASS**, **`fingerprint: matches
configs/motion_reference.json`**, exit 0 (the knob reads only on the patch schedule, so the
single-arm default is byte-unchanged); `172` 52 checks PASS; `105_motion_regression.py` on both
winning logs: **every descent inside its profile's speed and lurch bound** (the carry cones are
reported on the dynamic line, not gated).

**Not flipped:** both configs pass the pre-registered gate, but a two-line supply default is a
scenario change and the flip is the owner's. The named recommendation is **D=1.5 alone** (one
knob, +23 % throughput) with the belt left at 0.12 m/s, and a re-recorded
`configs/motion_reference_patch.json` for the adopted branch. Full detail: `logs/p/RESULTS.md`.

### P2 (2026-10-15, the density's dose ladder and its transfer): the peak is D=1.60, the lever transfers to both other supplies, and the two supplies show two different mechanisms

`logs/p2d/RESULTS.md` (pre-registered `logs/p2d/PREREGISTRATION.md`, evidence `logs/p2d/`). The
ladder on the two-line patch battery (ATTEMPTS=20, SEED=5, Tier A solo), quoted as the curve of
one deterministic sample per point with the continuous interval as the comparator:

| D | 1.00 | 1.25 | 1.40 | 1.50 | **1.60** | 1.75 | 2.00 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| success | 60 % | 55 % | 80 % | 75 % | **90 %** | 75 % | 25 % |
| placed/min | 3.64 | 3.36 | 4.48 | 4.48 | **5.27** | 4.20 | 1.53 |
| interval mean | 16.53 | 15.82 | 12.81 | 13.34 | **11.25** | 14.27 | 39.22 |

**P1's recommendation (D=1.5) is superseded: the peak is D=1.60** (18/20, 11.25 s, p90 20.30 s,
the patch D=1.60 double physics-identical). The success column swings 11/16/15/18/15/5 of 20
between adjacent D - branch quantisation - so the interval and the throughput are the comparators
and the success is quoted beside them; the one unambiguous shape is the D=2.0 collapse, whose
mechanism is the **crowding breaking the acquisition** (measured in P1), not starvation.

**Both transfers confirm, and the wave sheet is the strongest configuration measured in this
project on the two-line: 19/20, 6.07 placed/min, interval 9.59 s against a 9.4 s attempt span**
(98 % of the theoretical cadence), p90 31.70 -> 15.70 s - against the W6-C patch branch
(12/20 at 3.63) that is +1.67x placed/min, and against the W7-A dense branch (7/10 at 4.60)
+1.32x. The single arm on the patch sheet goes 70 % -> **90 %** (30.34 -> 24.36 s), so the density
is a cell-level lever, not a two-line-only one. On the wave schedule D saturates the 0.085 m
separation floor by D=1.5, so there the knob is "how close to the floor the clusters run" - the
dense sheet has one step of headroom and D=1.6 uses it.

**Two mechanisms, both favourable:** on the **patch** sheet the density removes the *failed/empty
attempts between placements* (the lock-on stays flat, left 3.73 -> 4.57 -> 4.27 s; the attempts
inside the interval fall 40.4 -> 15.7 s); on the **wave** sheet it relieves the *arrival wait*
itself (the left's lock-on falls 35.02 -> 19.06 s). The single measured "arrival-bound" symptom is
a property of the wave supply, not of the cell.

**The carry class is absent from the peaks**: the patch D=1.60 residual is 2 x `grasped=False`
(`N=0.00`, no contact - the acquisition class the R7-A/ACQ work targets) and the wave D=1.60
residual is 1 x `grasped=False`. First two-line configuration with no carry escape in the tail.

**One design defect found and fixed:** the first wave-transfer config set `FRUIT_SUPPLY_WAVE=1`
**and** `FRUIT_SUPPLY_PATCH=1`, and patch wins the schedule branch - so "the wave sheet at D=1.5"
had silently re-run the patch sheet (the tell: its readouts were bit-identical to the patch run,
which is what the determinism convention is for). The fix extends the knob to the wave schedule's
two gap bands (`wave_gap_*`, `wave_sep_*`, same 0.085 m floor); `D=1.0` stays byte-identical on
both (`172` 52 checks PASS).

**Not flipped:** the flip is the owner's (a two-line supply default is a scenario change). The
recommendation is now `FRUIT_SUPPLY_PATCH_DENSITY=1.60` on both scattered schedules, the belt left
at 0.12 m/s, plus a re-recorded `configs/motion_reference_patch.json` and a `190_twoline_gate.sh`
re-run on the adopted branch. The binding term after the change is unchanged: **the per-attempt arm
span** (~15 s; place+release 5.2 s, descent 3.0 s, grip 1.8 s, lift 1.8 s).

### P3 + P1c (2026-10-16): the Oracle review retracts the P1/P2 adoption recommendation, and the place-lengthening lever is closed by geometry

**The retraction first, because it is the important one.** An Oracle review of P1/P2
(`logs/p3/ORACLE_REVIEW.md`) found three defects, and I re-derived its central claim independently
before accepting it (`scripts/200_composition_audit.py` -> `logs/p2d/82_standardised.txt`):

1. **The two pre-registered endpoints are one number.** `186`'s placement-window throughput *is*
   `60 / pooled_interval_mean` by its own definition, and the batch throughput is
   `success / s_per_attempt`. With a fixed 20 attempts and a flat 9.8-10.7 s cadence, **every
   P1/P2 headline is a monotone transform of the success count.** My "quote the continuous
   interval instead of the quantised rate" hedge was an algebraic step, not a robustness argument.
2. **The success count is class-dominated and the mix moves with D.** The density changes the
   release geometry, so each arm is handed a different species mix at every D; the pooled
   per-(arm, fruit) placement rate spans **0.44 (left orange) .. 1.00 (right peach)**.
   Class-standardised: patch ladder **13.89 / 13.92 / 14.05 / 14.68 / 14.43 / 15.12** against the
   observed **12 / 15 / 11 / 16 / 18 / 15** - **flat**. The wave branch likewise
   (12.76 / 13.39 / 13.05), and its 19/20 run is the one where the left arm was given five oranges
   and no tomato or kiwi.
3. **My own headline stat was n=3.** "the left's inter-placement falls 50.7 -> 20.1 s (2.5x)"
   rests on three control intervals (p90 93.2 s); the robust pooled figure is 16.53 -> 13.34 s
   (1.24x). And the pre-registered fail item (a) ("the starvation does not fall") **fails on the
   named metric**: the left polls 1.9 -> 4.4 times per attempt at the same attempt count, so the
   "denominator effect" I wrote to explain it away does not apply.

**What survives:** the cadence (~15 s) and the lock-on are unchanged across the whole ladder (two
independent measurements); the knob is inert at D=1 (byte-identical, `172` 52 checks); **D=2.0's
collapse is a real density effect** (-7.3 slots class-adjusted) with the measured crowding
mechanism; and the **binding term is the per-attempt arm span**, which is a kinematic fact that
does not depend on the mix. Also newly stated, not previously: the wave peak's carried-grip cone
rises 2.80x -> 4.07x, and the **single arm starved on half its slots** at D=1.5 (10 empty slots vs
0; 10 picks in 19 slots vs 20 in 20), so that "transfer" was never like-for-like.

**The test that decides it** is pre-registered (`logs/p1c/PREREGISTRATION.md`): a **single-grade
supply** (`FRUIT_SUPPLY_GRADES=apple:1`) holds the presented multiset fixed *by construction*, so D
is the only variable - the single arm, the patch sheet, D=1.0 vs D=1.60 with a determinism double.
If the density helps there, the claim shrinks to "within a species"; if not, P1/P2's positive
results were composition and the phase closes with only the D=2.0 negative published.

**P3, the place leg, is closed by geometry.** `FRUIT_PLACE_INNER_SHIFT` (default off) moved the
release point 10 cm toward the body: the kinematics worked (place 45.1 -> 36.1 cm, 297 -> 237
ticks, ~1.0 s off the arm span) and the success rate **collapsed 90 % -> 30 %**, because the
payload releases at |y| 0.21-0.41 while the belt's inner edge is at 0.375 - the log says
`placed=False (on/next to output belt 0)`. The lever is closed because the control's release
already sits ~35 mm inside the belt: the maximum safe shift is ~30 mm, i.e. **~0.2 s, 1.3 % of the
span**, against a 4 % bar. The measured displacement was also 0.14-0.36 m for a commanded 0.10 m,
so the shortened transfer also scatters the wrist configuration. The next span target is the
**descent's documented boundary shortfall** (40-90 mm short on every leg), not the place.

**No shipped default changed** in either phase (both knobs are default-off and env-scoped), and the
adoption of D=1.60 is **withdrawn** - it needs the P1c result first, and a re-record of *both*
`configs/motion_reference_patch.json` and `configs/motion_reference_twoline.json` (the review
caught that my handover list named only the first) plus a `collection.patch_density` field in the
collector's shard manifest.

### P1c (2026-10-16): the composition-controlled test refutes the density lever outright - on a single-species pool the denser sheet starves the single arm (0/20 -> 14/20 empty slots, success 65 % -> 17-30 %, placed/min 2.54 -> 0.63)

`logs/p1c/RESULTS.md`, pre-registered `logs/p1c/PREREGISTRATION.md`, evidence `logs/p1c/`. This is
the test the Oracle review of P1/P2 named as decisive, run on the single arm with the presented
class multiset held fixed **by construction** (`FRUIT_SUPPLY_SPECIES=apple` - a knob added for
this test, because `_mix_env` rejects a zero weight so neither mix knob could express a
one-species pool; the first attempt with `FRUIT_SUPPLY_GRADES=apple:1` was silently rejected by
its own warning and ran the mixed pool, so that attempt is void and is not used).

**Result:** D=1.00 -> 13/20 placed (65 %), **0 empty slots**, 15.4 s/attempt, 2.54 placed/min.
D=1.60 -> 1/6 placed (17 %), **14/20 empty slots**, 15.9 s/attempt, 0.63 placed/min; the double is
**physics-identical**; a 40-slot repeat gives 3/10 (30 %) with **30/40 empty**. So with the fruit
held constant the density is **strongly negative on the single-arm line**, and the pre-registered
primary fails both clauses.

**Mechanism (measured):** the density turns the steady trickle into a single burst - the 16-fruit
pool is released almost at once, so at attempt 3 the most-upstream live apple sits at y = +0.375,
just under the selection floor (~+0.40 m), and at attempt 0 the whole pool is already downstream.
The arm's 15.4-16.0 s cycle is slower than the burst's transit, so it polls a floor it cannot
satisfy. **The two-line hides this** because its worker parks and waits (the W7-A lever) and two
arms drain the pool; the single arm's selector polls and gives up. The asymmetry is now measured
on both sides (the two-line completes 20/20 slots at D=1.60).

**What this closes:** the density as a positive lever - the ladder's gains were the mix, and the
composition-free effect runs the other way. The knob stays default-off and is now documented as a
**measurement instrument**, not a candidate default. Two real effects survive, both negative and
both measured: **D=2.0's crowding collapse** (-7.3 slots class-adjusted) and **the D>=1.5-1.6
single-arm starvation** (this test, plus the Oracle's D=1.5 reading of 10 empty slots). The
binding term is unchanged by any of it: **the per-attempt arm span (~15 s, flat across the whole
ladder)**.

**Tooling fixes the review forced:** `172` now covers the density knob and the species lock
(**52 -> 63 checks** - the knob previously had no coverage at all, so "byte-identical at D=1" was
code inspection rather than a test); the `WAVE=1 PATCH=1` combination now warns and the density
banner names the *resolved* schedule (it used to print the inert wave bands on a patch run, which
is what made `compare_streams.py` report a false DIFFERENT). The branch's acceptance must be re-run
before merge (an open item, not a claim).

### P4-A (2026-10-16, branch `p-supply`, Tier-A solo): the wait diagnosis - the pool arrives as one burst per attempt boundary and drains below the 0.399 m floor faster than the arm cycles; the single arm polls once and forfeits, the two-line parks and waits

P4-PLAN's first gate. No `src/` change, no default change, no control-loop instrumentation. One new
simulator run (the transport probe); everything else offline re-derivation. Evidence:
`logs/p4/A_DIAGNOSIS.md` + machine-readable `logs/p4/10_singlearm_availability.json`,
`11_twoline_wait.json` (with thirteen verbatim `*_186.txt` harness outputs),
`12_schedule_arithmetic.json`, `14_composition_p2d.txt`, `00_transport_probe.log`;
tool `scripts/201_p4a_wait_audit.py` (`--self-test` PASS, floor computed 0.399 m via
`fruit_sorting.motion`, t_desc 0.775 s / lead 0.189 m matching the code comments).

**Availability:** the empty-slot `active=` pool is never refused above the floor (0/56 slots
audited). D=1.6 apple drains as a sawtooth - fresh 6-body bursts (3 abreast pairs) at
y ~= 0.32-0.38, then -0.06 m/poll (belt travel between polls), below the floor in 1-2 polls;
`supply_skipped`/released = 1.7-1.9x on *every* log including healthy D=1.0 (even the 0-empty
runs release 90-110 fruit to collect 18-20). `reached_end` 0 everywhere; the river flows past as
`fell_off`. At D=1.0 only ~10.3 slices (~16 fruit) come due per cycle ~= the 16-body pool, so
releases spread ~1.5 s apart and polls find fruit; at D=1.6 ~30 fruit come due per cycle, the
pool exhausts at the first pump, and the 20.7 s wall cycle polls a belt whose floor transit is
3.33 s. Starvation is timing, never count.

**Two hidden waits (both flat across D, both supply-independent):** in-descent hover wait
~2.3-2.9 s (`descent` block minus 0.75 s motion approach, all real attempts paired) and the
inter-attempt gap **~5.1-5.5 s** (outcome windows are true sim time; `[stats] sim=` sums spans
only - `tasks.py:962-968` vs `:1021`). The gap is ~0.75 s feed/pump + ~4.3-4.7 s dual-arm
`go_ready` transit by subtraction (direct split unresolved). A real slot is 15.4 + 5.3 ~= 20.7 s
wall, ~37 % waiting. **Denominator discipline:** span-sum (D0 2.54), wall (D0 **1.88**), 186
window (accept 2.90) differ up to 1.9x - the P1c 2.54 -> 0.63 column is span-based, wall-corrected
1.88 -> 0.44; cross-line reads must use 186 wall/window, never the span rate.

**Reconciliation:** the single-arm driver polls once per slot and `continue`s past `go_ready`
(`20_pick_place.py:219-226`) - an empty costs 0.5 s and one placement (D1 wall 135 s < D0 415 s
because giving up is fast). The two-line worker re-polls every ~0.5 s through 3-14 empty reads
per lock-on (52_d160 retries), converting the same drain into idle seconds (left starvation
19 -> 44 control-to-D=1.6 while placements rise 6 -> 9). Composition is the second confound
(pooled cells 0.44-1.00, adjusted ladder flat 13.9-15.1 vs observed 11-18).

**Transport (new probe, current tree):** fruit `|vy|` 0.121 m/s = 1.008x command, roll ~0
(cleat-driven slide), 0 stalls; encoder NaN is the cleat-less build's instrument gap, not a
finding. Transport and branch (D1/D2 physics-identical, D3 same sawtooth) are excluded from the
lever ranking. Ranking: (1) 15.4 s arm span, (2) 5.3 s gap, (3) floor starvation at D >= 1.5,
(4) two-line lock-on wait, (5) mix as confound, (6) transport/branch sound. Hypotheses: H1
trickle-feed cap, H2 `FRUIT_SUPPLY_POOL` 16 -> 24 -> 32 sweep first (knob exists, no code),
H3 single-arm park-and-wait as the causal proof of the reconciliation. Unresolved: gap split,
worker pool dump, probe encoder, denominator discipline, H3.

coupling: the truncated attempt shifts the belt phase the next lock-on waits on) is a larger
change than the monitor itself. **Decision: close the lane, publish the two-battery record,

implemented and stub-verified; -1.75 s/gap code-exact, on the measured binding term, no

frozen at `12feced3`, run 5 on `255f2819`). The battery lane caught it, split the cohort,
and showed every pre-registered verdict unchanged - but the whole-battery pin is invalid and
the practice was wrong. **Rule going forward: no `src/` writer may run while a Tier-A
battery is live; implementation lanes queue behind the battery's completion (add it to the
OPS/P9 discipline).**

### P30-A (2026-10-21/22, branch `p-supply`): the belt's side rails - the census says no rail touches the grasp, the one in the place path is a 35 mm ledge the transfer lift already clears, and the removal is delivered default-off with a measured 40 mm height cost

**The directive and the scope.** Owner: *"if the conveyor's side rails/edges interfere with fruit
grasping and placing, remove the belt's side rails/edges"* - rails/fences only, no frame, no slab,
and the scattered dynamic supply stays. The phase answers it with a geometry census, a
default-off removal/lowering knob, and the simulator arms.

**The census** (`logs/p30a/rails_geometry.py`, offline, `--assert` pins 16 clearances;
`logs/p30a/RAILS_DESIGN.md`). Eight rail-like boxes exist in the cell; three facts settle the
question. (1) The main belt's **frame rails** (`conveyor.py:266-277`, `main_frame_rail_width/
_offset`) are **outside the slab and carry no `CollisionAPI`** - render only. (2) The main belt's
**guide rails** (`conveyor.py:278-294`, `FRUIT_RAIL_HEIGHT` 0.075, `belt_channel_x` 0.13) are
**off by default** (`FRUIT_RAILS=0`, `assets.py:230`); their inner faces are at x=0.2095/0.4705,
so with them on the *supply band* (x=0.20-0.36) loses its lower 25-45 mm and the open hand
(+/-0.066) **overlaps the N rail by 15 mm** at a band-edge grasp. They were the original
interference and were removed in the v2 belt work (WORKLOG "why the belt got wider" line 701:
"the fingers were jammed against the rails at the open position and could never close"). (3) The
only **always-built rail colliders** are the raised output belts' four side rails
(`conveyor.py:573-611`): 25 mm thick, 50 mm tall, standing **35 mm proud of the belt top**, the
inner pair's outer face flush with the slab's inner edge (|y|=0.425).

**The grasp is not a rail problem - it is the slab, and that is out of scope.**
`scripts/47_robot_collision.py` (usage documented in `RESULTS.md` section 1) drives the jaw 0.35 m
straight down from the grasp pose: the jaw stops at z=1.229 (59 mm above the belt top) with both
finger boxes *inside the slab*, and the run is **bit-identical with the output belts absent, with
their rails present, and with the inner rail removed** (`logs/p30a/10/12/13`). With
`FRUIT_RAILS=1` it is a *different, worse* stop: 18 mm higher, 56 mm off in x, and the right
finger's final box (x to 0.493, z 1.182-1.254) **inside the P guide rail's box**
(`logs/p30a/11`) - the regression evidence for keeping that knob off. The descent shortfall of
`logs/166`/`167` is the belt slab, as before.

**The place: the rail is a transit constraint at +21..+54 mm and a landing ledge.**
The payload crosses y=0.4125 on every place transit; at the shipped transfer height
(`output_place_z + FRUIT_OPENARM_TRANSFER_LIFT = 1.53`) its lowest point is ~1.420, i.e. **+35 mm
over the rail top** (measured +31..+54 on `logs/692`, and +33..+55 on this phase's arms; no place
leg in four arms comes closer than +33 mm, and every negative row there is the escaped-payload
class at -215..-219 mm), and fingertips +61 mm. The lift exists *because*
the rail used to be swept (48 m/s², `logs/445`); at lift 0 the payload would be **-45 mm to the
rail top and -10 mm inside the slab**. The population read (all 10 195 `released at` rows in the
repo) says the rail is also a *catch ledge*: releases landing on its 25 mm top face (|y|
0.400-0.425, n=234) are **placed 96.6 %** of the time, releases inboard of it (n=552, 5.4 %)
only **47.6 %** - so removal would turn the rail band into gap releases, and the real place-path loss is
the *short* lateral release, not the rail.

**The change** (default = the shipped geometry, **byte-inert**): `FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAILS`
(`assets.py:340-348`, `output_rail_keep` at 516: `both`|`outer`|`inner`|`none`, validated in
`__post_init__`) and `FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAIL_HEIGHT` (`assets.py:349-355`, default 0.05). `OutputBelt.
build` authors the kept rails only, with the height; the default arithmetic reproduces the shipped
boxes exactly (`rail_bottom = output_belt_top_z - 0.015`, `centre = rail_bottom + h/2` = the old
`+0.01` at h=0.05) and the audit `say()` line prints **only when a knob is off its default**.
`scene.py` untouched. Byte-identity: the acceptance replays `logs/p28/noharm_accept.log`
**381/381** and the two-line patch battery replays `logs/p12a2/10_seed11_mass.log` **950/950**
(the tree also carries the P30-B `FRUIT_HOME_HUB` lane's uncommitted `tasks.py`/`rl_env.py`/
`20_pick_place.py` changes, untouched here and inert at their defaults - which is what those two
replays demonstrate).

**The runs** (`logs/p30a/RESULTS.md`, all via `154_claim_run.sh`+`run.sh`, same tree).
Acceptance (baseline 7/10): control **7/10**, 15.1 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`
(`406745c5`), gate FAIL only on the 0.75 rate floor - the pre-existing P25-flip branch
(`logs/p28/CLOSE_OUT.md` item 7), not this phase; `outer` **8/10**, 15.2 s/attempt, budgets pass
but the fingerprint **differs** - a moved branch whose first differing row is a *placed* fruit's
post-release state, with the place legs' clearance unchanged (min +35 mm, zero rail skims in
both). Two-line patch battery (SEED=11, 20 attempts; baseline 11/20): control **11/20**, 9.5
s/attempt, 3.47 fruit/min; `outer` **11/20**, 9.5 s/attempt, 3.47 fruit/min, per-arm 5/6 -> 3/8
and `diverted` 3 -> 2 (a moved branch, first differing row a release x of 0.666 vs 0.688); supply
unchanged (`queue_peak=0`, `recirculated=0`, same `[supply]` pool line), the same 10 placed fruit
reach the tray in both. The **viable-lift pair** isolates the contact: at `lift=0.04` the payload
is 5 mm under the rail's top and 30 mm over the slab, and rails-on reads **18-20 m/s² on the
3/9 place legs that go below the rail** against **4.0-7.6 m/s²** with the inner rail removed -
**same rate, 6/9 both** (the `-9/-7/-4 mm` rows in the rail-free arm have *no* jolt, which is
what proves the metric alone cannot claim a contact; the clean named runs `06b`/`07` reproduce
both arms' leg tables exactly - `logs/p30a/A4A5_place_legs.txt`). The lift-0 arms fail on the **slab**, not
the rail: acceptance `outer`+lift0 **3/10** (|a|max 37.2 m/s², payload released at z=0.58/0.81),
battery `outer`+lift0 **4/20** vs rails+lift0 **3/20**, both 8.6-8.8 s/attempt.

**The verdict**: grasp - no rail interference, and the slab is out of scope; place - the inner
rail is a +21..+54 mm transit constraint at the shipped lift and costs **~40 mm of transfer
height** when it is lowered (measured as the 18-20 m/s² contact), while it is also a
96.6 %-effective ledge for short releases; so **no shipped-default change** (the shipped lift does
not need the 40 mm and the A4/A5 pair is rate-neutral), the knobs are the operator option, and the
named residuals are the short lateral release (P3 territory) and P3's "0.375 inner edge" that does
not exist (the real edges are the slab at 0.425 and the rail's inner face at 0.400 -
`RAILS_DESIGN.md` section 4).

### P33 phase 1: the mid-attempt pump fills the band, not the catchable window (2026-10-23)

The P32 phase-C follow-up (`FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE=1` never armed on a bimanual
attempt) is closed with the lever built and measured. `TickRelay` gained one
optional hook: `CoopSession.feed_pump` (installed by `run_bimanual` only for
`two_line and self._feed_cadence`) is forwarded to the relay and called on the
main thread **once per shared physics tick**, right after `step_fn` and before
the run permit is granted; it is the same `_feed_tick` the single-arm line calls
from `_step_sim`, so the stride (`FRUIT_FEED_STRIDE`=4 = 33 ms = 4 mm of belt
travel) and `advance_furniture=False` are identical by construction. The relay
calls it per *physics* tick, not per schedule round (`schedule` can execute
several); the workers are parked on their requests while it runs, so the
spawner's live set cannot be mutated concurrently. Default off; the F2
shared-station pipeline, the single-arm driver and the policy path are
unreached. `scripts/152_biarm_selftest.py` pins the invariant (50 shared ticks
-> 50 pump calls, main thread only). The two-line `bed_diag_report` gap is
closed too: with `FRUIT_BED_DIAG=1` the worker prints one `[bed-sel] arm=...`
census row per slot selection (`live/on_belt/admitted/window/band`,
`_biarm_bed_census`), pure reporting.

The A/B is A0's exact scenario (`FRUIT_BIARM=1 FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE=1
FRUIT_SUPPLY_BED=1 ATTEMPTS=20 SEED=5 FRUIT_BED_DIAG=1 FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1
FRUIT_CYCLE_REPORT=1`) plus `FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE=1` on the pump arm, one
simulator at a time via `154_claim_run.sh` (`logs/p33/10` vs `11`). **The band
is delivered:** at the pump instants it runs 2-8 (mean 4.2, n=20) -> 2-11
(mean 8.3, n=157, 14 at the 10 cap), `late_dropped` 139.6 -> **7.9 s** (the
batch-start prime residual, the first pump's own rebase on both arms),
rebased 16 -> 1, holds 0 -> 14, bed_placed 107 -> 358. Quote the band with its
sample type: **the same-instant census reads 5.5/6.9 -> 8.4/8.8** (left/right
means at the selection instant, `[bed-sel] band at pick`); the 4.2 -> 8.3 pair
puts 20 boundary-pump samples against 157 continuous ones. **The catchable
window is not:** the selector's per-arm count at the selection instant (the
census's `window`, candidates above the moving catch's ~0.40 m floor) reads
left 1.5 -> **0.9**, right 2.4 -> **2.2**. The aperture is a **stock-depth
ceiling, not a stock shortage**: the bed caps its stock at **10 bodies over a
0.58 m stocked depth** (4.1 rows x 2.4 bodies), and the slice above the ~0.40 m
floor (release line at 0.68 m) is **0.28 m ~= 2 rows ~= 4.8 bodies ~= 1.8 per
grade-pure lane** at the balanced mix - so the pump already delivers **8.3/10 =
83 % of the band's capacity**, the right's 2.2 is about the ceiling, and the
left's 0.9 is the grade-mix shortfall below it. **The pump arm is starved more
often per slot, not less**: left **5/15 = 33.3 % steady-state** (**37.5 %** of
all slots, 6/16) against the control's **0/10** (1/11 = 9.1 % of all slots;
Fisher two-sided ~0.057 on the steady-state pair 5/15 vs 0/10), right 2/12 =
16.7 % against 0/10. The census names the mechanism - a
**grade drought**: at the starved selections the band is FULL and the
grade-pure lane has nothing admitted (`band=7/10 admitted=0` t=31.50;
`band=10/10 admitted=2 window=0` t=68.46, admitted but all below the floor;
`band=9/10 admitted=0` t=68.96/69.46/69.96; right `band=9/10` and `band=8/10`
with `admitted=0` t=153.94/154.44), and of the 8 starve episodes **6 are
`admitted=0` (the grade)**, 1 is `admitted=2 window=0` (the floor), 1 is the
empty-belt prime. The interval (pooled 14.23 -> 13.68 s mean, p50 15.50 ->
14.20) is **a different branch**: 13/20 (left 9/right 4) vs 12/20 (left 6/right
6), right idle 15 -> 22 %, right lock-on 2.92 -> 4.14 s, three retry episodes
(left 1 retry at t=31.5 s + 4 at 68.5-70.0, right 2 at 153.9-154.4) against the
control's one batch-start starve. The wall is **+20.9 %** (484 -> 585 s) **=
+4.4 % sim span (171.8 -> 179.4 s) x +15.7 % per sim-second (2.82 -> 3.26 s
wall per sim-second)**; `105` passes every descent budget (6/34 legs >0.45 m/s
vs 9/32; worst cone 3.52x vs 5.81x, reported). **The supply burn:** the pump
arm's `[feed]` records **432 releases / 348 bed placements for 13 arm
placements** (444 draws / 358 bed-placed on the `[bed]` line, `reached_end=320`)
against the control's **126/107 for 12** - ~27 bed bodies per placed fruit
against ~9, i.e. the pump buys the band by burning the pool 3.5x faster, not by
sorting more.

The single-arm pair (the phase-A M2 re-run, `logs/p33/20` vs `21`) reproduces
the phase-A read and is the knob's own control: **selector window 4.6 (4-6)
-> 3.9 (2-7)**, live 6.6 -> 20.4, band 2.6 -> 7.9, `late_dropped` 160.9 ->
5.5 s, wall **282 -> 367 s (+30.1 %)** at **essentially equal sim span
(149.7 -> 148.7 s, -0.7 %)** - the clean form of the same fact: the cost is per
sim-second (1.88 -> 2.47 s wall per sim-second; phase A recorded +24 %, 285 ->
352-356 s; the same physics, 20 vs 6.6 live bodies). 6/10 -> 8/10 is a branch.

Verdict: **the density is a physics lever, not a free win.** The pump does
what it says - the bed's approach band runs at its design depth and the stale
backlog disappears - but the aperture is a stock-depth ceiling (10 bodies over
0.58 m, ~1.8 eligible per grade-pure lane above the floor) and the row pitch,
not the stock depth, sets the catchable slice; the line's cost is **+20.9 %**
(two-line) / **+30.1 %** (single arm) wall. `FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE` stays default
off (a measurement interface), no shipped default changed. Named next, with
their measured bounds: **a lower floor is CLOSED** (R3: the 1.5 s setup is
measured 1.467/1.516 s and 0/20 selections are floor-bound; R11-A/R11-A.1 cost
the shipped acceptance 9/10 -> 4/10 and 4/9 floored); **a higher station is
bounded at <= 0.10 m** (the R10-A intercept map; the station pair separation is
fixed at 0.10 m); **the row composition is a drought/variance lever only** (the
mean ~1.8 eligible/lane is unchanged; it needs its own pre-registration, motion
reference and clearance report - the both-hands 1.9-2.6 mm class). More stock
is not among them.

No-harm / byte identity: the shipped acceptance (10 attempts, no knobs) is
**374/374 `[fruit]` lines identical** to the P32 close-out `D1` after the two
static output-belt clearance prints (they carry the Gate-D 1.06 -> 1.07
instance-bound text), 6/10 + `fingerprint: matches` 25ade92b; the two-line
control is **826/826 identical** to A0 after its 20 new census rows and the
same two static prints (`190 -m 0.5`, bed reference `dcd19758`, PASS); the
single-arm control is **436/436 identical** to the P32 phase-A R1/R2 record
`87` (window 4.60, 6/10). Selfcheck PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped; the 152 leg
extended). Residuals: the single-arm cadence's `live_recycled=1/510` is **not a
failed payload** - `orange idx=13` is attempt 3's **successfully placed** fruit
(`[belt] ... discharged to the tray at x=1.56`; attempt 3 placed=True), later
re-released by the feeder; the cause is the **pool/capacity invariant**
(`_bed_note_live_draw` fires when a draw finds no parked body, ~51 draws per

body was already past the recycle line - the normal end-of-line recycle, not a

is default off, the pool/capacity invariant holds at the shipped/boundary
cadence (**0/72**) and reads **1/510** only at the pump's draw rate, and the
victim was already past the recycle line (`recycled_dy=-0.17 m`); the pump's
draw rate is the named residual, not a defect to fix.
The pump's carry warnings include the known frame-contaminated `slip_max` (do
not quote it - W8-B). Pins: `tasks.py`
`cdde6bd20670331ffbe8deb5d4f60b13`, `bimanual.py` (the hook), `rl_env.py`

- so the census measures the *bundled* left

**predated** P32's pear (this phase adds the first post-pear pair), and the pear
changes the per-instance RNG draw count and
every authored mesh (`meshes.py 41efc522`), so a policy number measured on an old
store is not this tree's. The P32 phase-D note named two ways to close that: a
post-pear store + the direct A/B, or the owner-accepted OOD risk. This phase ran
the first. The store is `datasets/p33_pear`, the checkpoint
`checkpoints/p33_pear`, and both carry the pins that identify them.

sequential runs in 2 h 58 m** (11:15:42-14:13:38; `logs/p33/C_collect_s*_*.log`,

**The paired endpoint is class-matched, not instance-matched.** `A_pairs.py`
compares `ea["fruit"] != eb["fruit"]` - the parser's fruit *species* string - so
after the branch diverges it pairs a 3.6 cm strawberry with a 4.3 cm one and
still calls it "same-fruit". Its 3-1 B / p = 0.3125 is therefore the
**class-matched** read. The stricter **exact-instance** read (same run, episode,
species, diameter and arm - the same spawned instance, **inferred**: there is no
stored instance id in the rollout record, so the match is a fingerprint, not a
read-back) has 13 pairs and **2 B-only /
0 A-only** (two-sided sign p = 0.50; one-sided 0.25); the re-derivation is
`logs/p33/E_ab/E_pairs_exact.py` -> `E_pairs_exact.txt`. Both reads are quoted; the
exact one is the stronger instance claim and it is **2-0**, not 3-1; the
class-matched 3-1 includes two pairs whose diameter differs
(`r1 ep13` A ok -> B no-contact is the one A-only; `r2 ep2` is a B-only).

The pooled difference is 16/45 vs 8/45 (two-sided Fisher **p = 0.094**); no
per-arm or per-class comparison separates on its own (left p = 0.57, right
p = 0.17, carried 26 vs 33 p = 0.18), so the honest read is "the candidate's rate
halves in this batch, below significance at N=3x15". **The deficit is the
carried-not-placed class** - 33 of B's 37 failures and 26 of A's 29 - all on the
trigger path (zero policy-gate fires on either arm), and **acquisition is
unchanged** (close-start |y| medians A 3.4/3.0 mm, B 3.3/3.2 mm). Nothing new
fails and the cycle is flat, so the recollection bought no time either.

(`logs/p33/C_collect_md5_before.txt` == `..._after.txt`: `tasks.py cdde6bd2`,

**Verdict and what it means.** The post-pear store and checkpoint exist and are
pinned; on this interface the candidate shows **no measured improvement and is
not adopted**: pooled **8/45 vs 16/45** (Fisher p = 0.094; A better in 2/3 seeds
at run level, run-level exact permutation 4/20 = 0.20), the **class-matched
paired carry 3-1 B** and the **2 exact pairs 2-0 B** (the exact pairing is
**inferred** - run + episode + species + diameter + arm, no stored instance id),
with **29/45 unpairable**.
The rate deficit is real in this batch but below significance, so do not call it
a significant regression either; the pre-registered "improvement" reading fails
and the negative is what publishes. **The store-transfer vs overwrite question
is not separated** - this phase cannot say whether the two-line store does not
transfer to the direct presentation or this fine-tune overwrote the direct
carry/place, the same ambiguity W8-A named. **Three attribution gaps** keep the
candidate's scope to "this checkpoint on this interface":
(a) the store is collected on the **two-line** branch, whose right-arm station is
`y = -0.10` with its own solved pre-pose, while the direct env presents at
`y = 0.00` - and the right arm is where B lost (14/29 -> 7/24), so a station
geometry difference is confounded with the policy change;
(b) the store is **successes-only** (288 attempts -> 180 episodes; the **52
carried-not-placed and 56 no-grasp** attempts were discarded), so it contains
**no example of the class the deficit is in** - a recollection anchored on
successes cannot teach the failure mode;
(c) the 6-epoch / lr 5e-5 schedule cannot be separated from an **overwrite** of
the direct behaviour (no frozen-trunk or replay control was run).
Two things it does settle: the acquisition/trigger interface is unchanged (so
the W7-B acquisition readout is not what moved), and the store's own interface is
the two-line while the A/B is the direct one. **The two-line has no policy eval
harness** (`60_eval_policy.py` / `accept_policy.sh` drive the single-arm
presentation), so `p33_pear` is **not** evaluated on the two-line interface -
out of scope for the direct OOD closure. **The closure is therefore the
pinned artifacts + this measured negative, not a policy win**: no checkpoint is
adopted (`accept_policy.sh` keeps `moe_v12`), and the clause "every checkpoint
and rollout store on this tree is pre-pear" is now false by exactly these two
artifacts - every **other** store/checkpoint is pre-pear.

### P35 phase 1: the inactive arm's park is the sightline lever (the marginal cover 0.382 -> 0.002), the camera is second, and the P34-B right-arm `first_rel` is the stale frame (2026-10-24)

**The lever is measured, the outcome is not.** The inactive **left** arm at the
shipped `ready` pose sits between the head camera and the belt's approach band:
its silhouette covers **98 %** of a 58 mm fruit's disc at along +0.35, **57 %** at
+0.40 and **0.382** of the scored stream on average (depth-gated: an arm pixel
counts only in front of the fruit's surface), while `212` reads the belt at 1.00
there - so this is arm occlusion, not the output belt. The park named **`back`**
(ready + j1 -0.50 / j2 -0.60 / j4 -0.50 rad; `configs/arm_parks.json`) moves the
arm up and downstream into the spawn corner and takes the **marginal** cover -
the share of the stream the belt would have shown and the arm hides - to
**0.002**; the stream's mean visible fraction then equals the belt-only ceiling
(0.77). Rendered, with static fruit proxies on *current* frames (two identical
renders required): a 68 mm pear at (0.219, +0.399) reads **0.378 -> 0.878**, a
58 mm fruit at (0.19, +0.35) **0.000 -> 0.953**, the inner band (0.30, +0.40)
0.051 -> 0.940. The `outer_edge` proxy (0.23, +0.40) stays 0.105 under every
park because its occluder is the output belt's **frame** prim, not the arm.

**The sweep and the safety reads.** 53 parks per side (`ready` + 7 joints x 3
magnitudes x 2 signs clipped + 5 named folds + a 4-step ladder of the deepest),
each with both arms' `link_pose` chains, the rendered silhouette + depth, the
90-tick hold, the lowest link, the belt footprint, the parked-to-active link gap
and the torso gap. No single-joint move clears the band without **relocating**
the occlusion: `j2+080` and `high` clear +0.30..+0.55 and then cover the decision
zone (0.87/0.65 at +0.20/+0.25 for `high`), `j1-080` covers more (0.58), and
`fold_85` re-enters at 0.41/0.33 because its hand lands on the belt's inner edge
(x 0.102). `j1+080` is the lowest-cost pose measured (0.007) and is **not a
park**: clipped at the limit it settles 0.209 rad from the command and puts a
link below the belt top (1.141). `back` holds **0.0007 rad over 900 ticks** with
a 0.3 mm jaw drop (`30_park_hold.log`), the hand 0.287 m above the belt, 0.187 m
from the active arm's chain and 0.688 m from the torso; `side_deep` is the
runner-up (cost 0.036, hold 0.0001 rad, hand out of the belt footprint but 9 mm
above it at x ~0). The **right** arm is not part of the lever: at `ready` it
covers 0.00 everywhere, and its `back` vector does not hold (0.174 rad) and puts
the fingertip in the belt footprint - so the park is **one-sided, left only**,
and the population it can act on is the **right-arm** episodes (the direct env
presents B/C to the right).

**The camera is priced and dominated.** Rendered through one `RtxCamera` per
pose (the shipped pose through its own camera reproduces the head camera's mask
at IoU 0.959/0.937): the best camera (`x -0.10`) reaches marginal cost 0.075 /
visible 0.69 against the park's 0.002 / 0.77, and every camera moves every
pixel. Named second, not proposed.

**A correction to P34-B (and to this lane's premise).** The right-arm
`first_rel` 0.077/0.131 at along +0.441/+0.445 is the **pre-reset frame** - its
bboxes there are 222/213 px of `/World/Conveyor/Belt` with the fruit absent, and
the arm contributes 24/12 px *beside* the disc; the +0.399 row is real (the arm
dominates the bbox at 127 px) and the proxies quantify it as 0.378 visible at
`ready`, not 0.115. The arm's occlusion is real but sits at along **+0.30..+0.45**
(the approach/decision band); at the shipped first call (along +0.541) the
occluder is the **output belt** (`212` 0.00), not the arm. The first-call mask
stays unusable as a manipulation check: with `back` the same call still reads
`target_px=0` and now shows `link3`/`link4` in the bbox - the park applied, the
frame still one render behind - so the pre-registered check is read **per call** at
the first target along in +0.30..+0.45 (target mask vs the episode max + the
parked arm's pixels in its bbox; a default-off diag), not at the first call.

**Default off, no shipped default changed.** `rl_env.py` `FRUIT_ARM_PARK`
(+46/0; `arm_park` in the manifest; unset = one `dict.get` per arm at reset) and

### P35 phase 2: the arm-park A/B - the park removes the fruit's band occlusion and the right's carried class 26 -> 0, the mediator is not identified, and adoption stays blocked (2026-10-24)

**The lever moves the outcome, on the arm the pre-registration predicted.** N = 5
runs x 15 episodes per arm, seeds 77/101/202/303/404, policy seed 11, interleaved
in one claim, the P33/W8-A scenario verbatim, `moe_v13s` `61da390a` on **both**
arms; A = the shipped env, B = `FRUIT_ARM_PARK=back` (the inactive **left** arm
only). **Pooled 29/75 (39 %) -> 47/75 (63 %)**; the lever is one-sided by
construction, and the effect is where it must be: the **right** arm (the
population the direct env presents grade B/C to) goes **28/57 (49 %) -> 45/48
(94 %)**, its **carried-not-placed class 26 -> 0**, its no-grasp 3 -> 3 (no class
relocation), the composite 29 -> 3; the **left** arm - the treatment's no-op,
because the park never touches the active arm - is **1/18 -> 2/27**, flat. Per
run (right ok/ng/carried): A 7/2/2, 1/0/8, 8/0/6, 5/1/5, 7/0/5 vs B 8/2/0,
9/1/0, 8/0/0, 11/0/0, 9/0/0 - **B >= A in 5/5 seeds**, strictly better in 4/5
(one-sided p = 0.0625). The primary pairing (exact instance: run, episode,
species, diameter, arm) has **22 usable pairs** of 75 slots (53 excluded - the
streams diverge), 5 both-ok / 7 both-fail / **8 B-only / 2 A-only**
(**p = 0.0547**), and the **carried-class conversion is 7 B-only / 1 A-only**,
which **meets** the pre-registered bar (>= 5 / <= 1). The outer-band subgroup
(right, check-frame x < 0.26) is A n=24 ok 4 / carried 18 / no-grasp 2 vs B n=15
**ok 15 / carried 0 / no-grasp 0**. Cycle 1851 -> 1821 ticks (-1.6 %; right 1823
-> 1793). The sign test is one pair short of 0.05, as the pre-registration said it
would be at this N - the primary read is the class conversion and the per-run
consistency, not the pooled sign test.

**The mechanism is measured in vivo, per call, on the frame the model
conditioned on.** The new default-off `FRUIT_PARK_DIAG=1` census (`[park]` rows,
one per band call in +0.30..+0.45, the band the arm occludes and the +Y belt
does not): with the park, the inactive arm's pixels inside the target's own
rendered bbox are **0.000 at every one of the 1645 band calls** (control: median
`arm_frac` **1.125**, max **3.000**, 56/57 episodes above 0.10); the fruit's
**median visibility over the band rises 0.423 -> 0.942** of the episode's own
depth-corrected maximum (`px * d^2`, the `[align]` `pfc`/`pcm` normalisation);
and the band's **fully-hidden calls fall 1017/2010 = 51 % -> 17/1645 = 1.0 %**.
The within-batch negative control is clean: on **left-active** episodes the
tournament arm is the **right** one, which `configs/arm_parks.json` leaves
shipped, so both arms run the same scene - episode-median visibility 0.940 (A,
n=18) vs 0.933 (B, n=27), `arm_frac` 0.000 on 18/18 and 27/27.

**Both pre-registered check instruments failed on their own smoke data, and the
amendment was written before the A/B** (`logs/p35/B_PREREG_AMEND.md`, on the
check's three smoke pairs only, no outcome read): **M1**'s 0.02 rad bar sits
below the reset's own teleport accuracy - the shipped `ready` misses its command
by **0.027-0.038 rad** and the park by **0.090-0.102 rad**, because
`ArmController.teleport_joints` re-bases `sync_command_to_measured()` after a
30-substep settle and the 0.5 rad j1 move is unfinished; the residual is stable
(+0.011 rad first-call -> band-call) and reproducible (0.091/0.090). **M2**'s
"first call in the band" is the band's **least-occluding edge** (phase 1's cover
0.81/0.98/0.57/**0.01** at +0.30/+0.35/+0.40/+0.45), so the control passes it
23/57. The amended gate reads the same questions at the pose and over the whole
band: **M1'** (applied + stable: `|q-back| <= 0.15`, `|q-ready| >= 0.30`, drift
<= 0.02) **48/48** treatment / **0/57** control; **M2a'** (the arm term,
`max arm_frac < 0.10`) **48/48** / **1/57**; **M2b'** (episode-median visibility
>= 0.85) **48/48** / **1/57**. The strict per-call visibility form is **not
usable** and the reason is measured: the small-fruit mask is 24-30 px, so +-2 px
is +-8 %, and the no-op side (where the arm is not an occluder at all) fails it
**0/27** while passing its median form 25/27. Where the visibility term still
fails under the park, the largest instance at the worst visible call is the
**target itself** (24/24) - mask jitter and the outer x's belt frame, the phase-1
`outer_edge` (0.105 visible under every park), not the arm.

**The verdict: the falsifier does not fire; the adoption blocks are the
pre-registered ones.** The **park is a measured interface lever on this
scenario** - check passed, class converted, guard flat, cycle -1.6 % - and the
check shows it **removes the fruit's band occlusion**. **The mediator is not
identified**: the park is a static scene change on the image (3497 -> 4155 px of
silhouette in every frame) *and* on the **7 inactive-arm joints of the 25-D
proprio** (every store frame has the left arm at `ready`), and this A/B does not

argues against a simple perception bottleneck (see the next entry). It ships

`fruit drifted 6160 mm off the pick centre` -> `fruit left the pick station
(17977 mm cross-belt); aborting` - a 6-18 m displacement is a runaway body state,
not a mechanism, and it lands in the existing **no-grasp** class, but the string

**0.090-0.102 rad** from its command (> 0.02) - a teleport-settle artifact (the
census is 48/48), but the bullet is the bullet. The shipping path is a
**recollection**, and its own A/B is the adoption gate.

### P35 phase 2, Gate-1 P0 revision + re-run: the check is fixed, the park still converts the right's carried class 25 -> 0 (run-level 5/5; 7-0 on the exact pairs), the record of record is `C_ab`, and the mediator is not identified (2026-10-24)

**Gate 1 blocked the batch on the check's *instrument*, not on the lever, and all
five items were measured defects.** (1) **M1 vs the configured command** was
unreachable by construction: `ArmController.teleport_joints` writes the pose,
steps 30 substeps and then `sync_command_to_measured()`, so the pose is *held*
where the drive reached it - the shipped `ready` sits **0.037 rad** from its own
command and the park **0.088**, while the bar was 0.02. The fix keeps the bar's
intent and changes its reference: **held vs the pose the reset achieved**
(<= 0.02 rad, so a drift or an overwrite still fails), with the
achieved-vs-commanded residual reported (the gate's second option, a 0.04 rad
command bar, would fail the *shipped* reset too, so it cannot be the gate).
(2) **M2 was read at +0.45**, where phase 1's cover is 0.01 - the band's
least-occluding edge, which is why the pre-P0 control passed it 23/57; the census
is now **+0.30..+0.40** and read at the band's **worst** call. (3) **The bbox was
the visible-mask extent**, i.e. the disc minus the occluder it is measuring, so the
arm's share of it was under-counted; it is now the **projected disc**
(`r_px = f r / sqrt(d^2 - r^2)`, exact area `pi r_px^2`, the `212`/`217` camera
model). (4) **The stale first call** is skipped (`_infer_calls >= 1`,
`stale_skipped` = 1/episode) - it conditions on the pre-reset frame, `px=0` on
72/75. (5) The diag is **documented** (sentinels `px=0`, `rel=-1`, `frac=-1`),
selfcheck PASS before/after, the tree re-pinned, and a **2-episode pilot per arm**
ran before the batch (`23`/`24_pilot_*`). The revision is pre-registered in
`logs/p35/C_PREREG_AMEND.md`; the pre-P0 batch (`B_ab`) is kept as provenance and
its file is marked superseded. Two of my own bugs were caught by the pilot/early
runs and fixed before the record batch: a bbox-`pi` disc area that over-read small
fruit by ~40 % (now the exact analytic silhouette, calibrated offline: 157 px for a
68 mm fruit vs a 174 px render; 39 vs 27 for a 36 mm one) and a `ZeroDivisionError`
in the `[park]` row when the control's first band call is fully occluded (it killed
three arm-A runs of the first attempt at the record batch).

**The record batch (`logs/p35/C_ab/`, N=5x15, seeds 77/101/202/303/404, one claim,
`moe_v13s` `61da390a` both arms, `FRUIT_ARM_PARK=back` vs unset).** **Pooled 24/75
(32 %) -> 49/75 (65 %)**; the **right** (the lever's population) **23/51 (45 %) ->
47/50 (94 %)** with its **carried-not-placed class 25 -> 0**, no-grasp 3 -> 3, the
composite **28 -> 3**; the **left** (no-op guard) 1/24 -> 2/25 flat; **B > A in
5/5 runs, every one strict (one-sided sign p = 0.031)**; median cycle 1867 -> 1802
ticks (-3.5 %, on **different outcome mixes** - right 45 % vs 94 % success, so it
is not a like-for-like speed read). **The design-valid leg is the run level +
the standardised counts**: the right's **94.9 % class-standardised / 94.1 %
size-standardised** success against the control's 52.3 % / 45.2 % (the raw 45 % ->
94 %), with the per-class deltas `113` prints (apple +42, kiwi +7, ...) carrying
**different denominators** each, i.e. not mix-adjusted effects. **The
exact-instance pairing is conditioned on a post-treatment variable** (the streams
diverge with the outcomes, so which slots stay pairable is a consequence of the
treatment): **22 usable pairs** of 75 slots, 6 both-ok, 8 both-fail, **8 B-only /
0 A-only (one-sided sign p = 0.0039)**, **carried-class 7 B-only / 0 A-only** (the
pre-registered bar >= 5 / <= 1 met). The **outer band** (right, check-frame
x < 0.26): A n=23 ok 6 / carried 16, B n=17 **ok 16 / carried 0**, pairs 13 usable
**6 B-only / 0 A-only** (p = 0.0156), carried 5-0. `C_pairs.txt` is the looser
**same-species** set (`113`): **24 pairs, 8 B-only / 1 A-only** (p = 0.0195) - the
extra A-only pair is run4 ep10 **orange 6.5 vs 6.1 cm, a different fruit**, which
the diameter-matched exact pairing excludes. `112_rl_ab.sh` runs **A then B** in a
fixed order per run (no randomisation), so an order term is not separated here.
**No new failure reason**; per-class B >= A in all eight classes.

**The check, in exact counts (no bar, no normalisation).** The lever's population
(inactive = the left arm): the band's **fully-hidden target calls 856/1257 =
68.1 % -> 0/1236 = 0.0 %**, and calls carrying **any** inactive-arm pixel inside
the fruit's **projected-disc bbox** **1257/1257 = 100 % (worst arm/target pixel
ratio 333) -> 0/1236 = 0 %**; **M1 applied** (realized pose is `back`, not
`ready`, drift <= 0.02) **0/51 -> 50/50**, **M1 held** 51/51 / 50/50, **M2a** (arm
term at the worst call) **0/51 -> 50/50**. **The gate of record is M1 + M2a**; the
control fails M2a 51/51. The **no-op side is the within-batch negative control**
(left-active episodes, the right arm shipped in both): hidden 65/584 (11.1 %) vs
55/610 (9.0 %), inactive-arm pixels 0/584 vs 0/610 - the instrument behaves
identically when the lever is absent. **M2b (the episode-relative `rel >= 0.85`
at the worst call) is a recorded report at 36/50 = 72 %, not the gate**: all 14
misses have **`arm_px = 0`** (masks of 22-47 px whose largest instance is the
**belt**), the disc-relative `vis` is **0.57-1.02** (**2** >= 0.98, 3 >= 0.97),
and `rel` divides by a **running** `px*d^2` maximum (updated on every non-stale
call, not the episode's final maximum) - so a band call is normalised against
another call's geometry, and the small-mask raster drift is the rest. So the
claim rests on the exact counts (hidden 68.1 % -> 0.0 %, arm 100 % -> 0 %) and
M2b is reported beside them. `C_attribution.py` counted a `frac = -1` row as
passing the arm term; fixed (`max(frac) >= 0` required), re-run and annotated:
**A's inactive-left arm term is 0/51, not 11/51** - the 11 were the
never-visible rows (`arm 40, never-visible 11`).

**Verdict.** The **falsifier does not fire**: the check passes on M1 / M2a / the
census and the right's carried class converts 25 -> 0 (run-level 5/5; 7-0
paired). **The park is a measured interface lever on this scenario; the check
shows it removes the fruit's band occlusion; the mediator (image vs the 7
proprio channels) is not identified - the control's invisible-fruit successes
argue against a simple perception bottleneck** (9 of its 23 right-arm successes
read `px=0` at every band call; the successes' median fully-hidden share 0.84
against the failures' 0.60). **Default off, no shipped default changed, no
commit.** Adoption still needs a **recollection** and its own A/B, but a
recollection fixes both channels at once and **can erase a checkpoint-specific
input-shift win**, so it should not be the first spend on the mechanism: the
named discriminator is a small-N **2x2 spoof** - the **proprio-spoof** (the
park's joint values in the observation, the arm *not* moved) x the
**image-spoof** (the arm moved to `back`, the `ready` proprio). **`PREREG.md`
section 5's literal "arm-pose residual > 0.02 rad" block is failed** by the
park's 0.088 rad achieved-vs-commanded residual (the shipped `ready` reset is
0.037 from its own command, so the block is a teleport-settle property); the
conclusion - not adopted - is unchanged. The `113` line "B PASSES the
improvement criterion" is a **P33-era harness readout, not the decision** (its
criteria are the old rate/sign/strawberry set). **No-harm**: `selfcheck.sh` PASS
(0 failures, 1 skipped) before and after; the scripted acceptance with both
knobs unset **6/10 + `fingerprint: matches`** (its `exit=1` is the expected
rate-only result) and its **376 `[fruit]` lines IDENTICAL** to
`logs/p34/73_accept_no_harm.log` - the identity was re-verified after the
driver's premature `cat` (14:22 vs the 14:25 file); the tree md5s identical

### P35 phase 3 (Gate 2): the claim narrowed to the lever it measured, the pairing labelled as post-treatment, the attribution bug fixed, and P35 committed (2026-10-24)

**Gate 2 rejected the headline, not the measurement.** (1) **The sightline is not
shown to be the mediator.** The control **succeeds with the fruit invisible** -
**9 of its 23 right-arm successes read `px=0` at every band call**, and the
successes' median fully-hidden share is **0.84** against the failures' **0.60**
(the successes are the *more* occluded population) - so "the policy could not see
the fruit" is not an established mechanism, and the park moves **two** input
channels at once (the image, 3497 -> 4155 px of silhouette in every frame; and the
**7 inactive-arm joints of the 25-D proprio**). The claim is now, everywhere
(WORKLOG headings + this entry, `logs/p35/C_RESULTS.md` §0/§3, `B_RESULTS.md`,
`.slim/deepwork/p35-arm-park.md`, `AGENTS.md` §2, `README.md`): **"the park is a
measured interface lever; the check shows it removes the fruit's band occlusion;
the mediator (image vs the 7 proprio channels) is not identified - the control's
invisible-fruit successes argue against a simple perception bottleneck"**. The
**named mechanism test** is a small-N 2x2 input spoof: the **proprio-spoof** (the
park's joint values in the observation, the arm *not* moved) x the **image-spoof**
(the arm moved to `back`, the `ready` proprio) - and a recollection fixes both
channels at once and **can erase a checkpoint-specific input-shift win**, so it
should not be the first spend on the mechanism question.

(2) **The occlusion term is "inside the disc's bbox"**, with the exact counts
(the target mask empty 68.1 % -> 0 %, the arm silhouette intersecting the disc
bbox 100 % -> 0 %, `C_attribution`'s `arm 40/51, never-visible 11`). (3) **The
exact-instance pairing is conditioned on a post-treatment variable** - the streams
diverge with the outcomes, so which slots stay pairable is itself an effect of the
treatment; the design-valid leg is the **run level (B > A in 5/5, all strict,
one-sided p = 0.031)** plus the standardised counts. `C_pairs.txt` is now labelled
as the **same-species** set it is (**24 pairs, 8 B-only / 1 A-only**; the extra
A-only is run4 ep10 **orange 6.5 vs 6.1 cm, a different fruit**), against the
exact **22 pairs, 8/0**; and `112_rl_ab.sh` runs **A then B** in a fixed order per
run (no randomisation), which an order term would confound. (4) The `vis >= 0.98`
read is **2** of the misses, not 4 (3 at >= 0.97). (5) `C_attribution.py` counted
`frac = -1` (no bbox) as **passing** the arm term, which is how A read 11/51;
fixed (`max(frac) >= 0`), re-run and annotated - **A's arm term is 0/51**, the 11
being exactly the never-visible rows; the docstring's band corrected to
+0.30..+0.40. (6) **The gate of record is stated as M1 + M2a**; M2b is a
**recorded report at 36/50 = 72 %**, not the gate; and `PREREG.md` §5's literal
"arm-pose residual > 0.02 rad" block is **failed** by the 0.088 rad
achieved-vs-commanded residual (the shipped `ready` reset is 0.037 from its own
command) - the conclusion, **default off / not adopted**, is unchanged. (7) M2b's
miss cause is the **running** `px*d^2` maximum (updated on every non-stale call,
not the episode's final maximum) plus **small-mask raster drift** (22-47 px masks,
the belt/frame the largest instance where present) - `park_ab_report.py`'s

IDENTICAL**. (9) The diff pin is **+424/-1** (`fd18bb1b` matches); the three P35
scripts are pinned; `logs/p35/` is force-added. (10) The cycle's **mix** is
