**Committed** as "P35: the inactive-arm park removes the band occlusion; the A/B

### P36 phase 1: the proprio-spoof knob and the 2x2's pre-registration - the offline diff and the six-cell smoke pass, the shipped stream is byte-identical, and no outcome is claimed (2026-10-24)

**The phase delivers the mediator test's instrument, not its answer.** P35 closed
with the park as a measured interface lever whose **mediator is not identified**
(the image's 3497 -> 4155 px silhouette and the **7 inactive-arm joints** of the
25-D proprio move together). This phase adds the other channel's manipulator and
freezes the design before any 2x2 run.

(1) **`FRUIT_PROPRIO_SPOOF=<pose>`** (`rl_env.py`, direct presentation only,
default off): `proprio()` writes the **inactive** arm's 7 joint values into the
observation from `configs/proprio_spoof.json` through the pure
`apply_proprio_spoof(dof, active, indices, vectors)` - a copy, no simulation
state touched. The indices are the arm's own `arm_dofs`, read from the measured
dof order (`logs/33_dof.log`): **left `0,2,4,6,8,10,12`, right
`1,3,5,7,9,11,13`**; the active arm, the four fingers (14,15,17,18), the hands
(16,19) and the TCP joints (20,21) are untouched. **The vectors are measured,
not commanded**: they are the `q_settled=` values of the P35 `[park]` rows (the
pose the reset *achieved*; `teleport_joints` re-bases onto the measured state,
so `back`'s command is 0.088 rad off), each string repeating identically across
its population in `logs/p35/C_ab/` (left ready n=51, left back n=50, right ready
n=24) on the same tree. `back` has **no right-arm vector** (the park file has no
right park), so a left-active episode is a no-op in this channel - the 2x2's
within-batch negative control. `FRUIT_SPOOF_DIAG=1` prints one `[spoof]` row per
episode: the 7 indices and their live/written values, the md5 of the assembled
proprio before/after, the md5 of the same vector **with the 7 zeroed**
(`rest_same`), and `drift = max|live-written|`. The manifest gains a
`proprio_spoof` block and the vector file is in `_MANIFEST_SOURCES`.

(2) **The offline check** (`scripts/218_proprio_spoof_check.py`, now a selfcheck
leg, 0.08 s; `logs/p36/offline_obs_diff.txt`): **failures=0**, and it compares
against artefacts rather than transcriptions - the three vectors == the P35
`q_settled` rows, the layout == the measured dof order, one call writes 7 and
**reads 6 changed** (j7 is 1.559 in both poses) with the other **15
bit-identical**, the caller's array unmutated, the 25-D assembly's finger/tactile
channels unchanged and the rest-of-vector hash equal, and the no-vector and
empty-dict paths bit-identical no-ops. `ready -> back` is
`[0.448, 0.603, 0.015, 0.497, 0.002, 0.002, 0.000]` rad (max 0.603).

(3) **The smoke** (`logs/p36/run_smoke.sh`, six one-episode runs at seed 77 in
one claim, the P35 scenario verbatim with all four diags; checked by
`logs/p36/smoke_check.py` -> `P1_smoke.txt`, **failures=0**): cells 1-4 plus two
source-vector controls (`s1b` writes the ready vector onto a ready arm, `s2b`
the back vector onto a parked arm). **S1** the no-op drift **0.0059 rad**
(ready) / **0.0141 rad** (back) against the 0.02 pre-registered bar, the probe
cells' drift 0.6035/0.6036 (the substitution bites); **S2** `rest_same=1`
everywhere; **S3** `[park]` M1 holds each cell's pose (0.002/0.004); **S4** the
inactive arm is in the target's disc bbox in the ready cells (`arm_px` 234,
frac 4.5) and absent in the parked ones (0, 0.000) - the image follows the arm,
not the spoof, reproducing P35's ep0 rows. **The strongest part**: the pre-spoof
proprio hash is **bit-identical inside each physical pair** (cells 1/4
`68e0e753`, cells 2/3 `98b0df03`), so the two cells of a pair differ in nothing
but the 7 values and the image at the first call. The six single episodes
already disagree in outcome (and `s1b` vs `s1` differs by <= 0.006 rad in 7
channels) - the documented non-reproducibility of the policy loop, which is why
the 2x2 is 3 x 15 per cell; **nothing in the smoke is a rate**.

(4) **No-harm**: the scripted acceptance reads **6/10 + `fingerprint: matches
configs/motion_reference.json`** with **376/376 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical**
to the P35 record (`logs/p36/P1_accept_identity.txt`; the 6/10 is the
pre-existing P32 pear-on branch, so the rate-only `exit=1` is expected);
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS** (0 failures, 1 skipped) with the new leg. Off,
the knob is one empty-dict test and no copy in `proprio()`; the scripted line
does not construct the env at all.

(5) **The pre-registration** (`logs/p36/PREREG.md`, written before any 2x2 A/B):
the 4 cells (ready/ready, park/park, park-image/ready-proprio,
ready-image/park-proprio), the endpoints (the right's carried-not-placed primary,
the placed/composite, the pooled, the per-class standardised, no-new-reason, the
cycle), **N = 3 runs x 15 episodes per cell** (180; seeds 77/101/202, policy seed
11, **rotated cell order** per run, one claim), and the fixed analysis: the two
exact Fisher main-effect tables (image `((r2+r3)-(r1+r4))/2`, proprio
`((r2+r4)-(r1+r3))/2`) on the right-arm population, the interaction
`(r2-r3)-(r4-r1)` with a within-stratum permutation (5 000 draws, seed
20261024) read as **redundancy vs synergy** (0 = additive; negative = the
both-parked cell beats the additive prediction; positive = the single-channel
cells do), the **effect fraction** `(r1-r_c)/(r1-r2)` with the full/partial/none
bands, and the power statement (at n = 30 right/arm a channel cell at 0.10 is
detected with 0.90 power, at 0.15 with 0.75; a third-carrier is not). The
falsifiers are one-directional: **a positive names the channel, a null is
ambiguous** (the probe cells are inconsistent input pairs the checkpoint never
saw); the decision matrix's last row is "not identified", with the conjunction
pattern noted to move each main-effect table by half. Phase-2 tooling written
and self-tested: `scripts/219_p36_cells.sh` (the rotated 4-cell driver) and
`scripts/220_p36_report.py` (the analysis + a `--self-test` that pins the five
synthetic tables' readings). **No commit; no shipped default changed.**

(6) **Named risks for phase 2**: the OOD probe cells; the spoof is a constant
with a <= 0.014 rad live drift (so "same proprio" is a <= 0.02 rad
substitution); the right-arm inference population (~30/cell) means the design
sees a channel carrying >= ~72 % of the P35 conversion at 80 % power; and the policy loop's
run-to-run variance is why the left-arm episodes (a no-op in all four cells) are
quoted as the batch's noise scale.

### P36 phase 2: the park's win travels the image channel - the parked image alone reproduces the whole conversion (0/28 carried) while the parked proprio alone sits at the control level (0.567); the fruit's sightline is the leading but unseparated candidate, the interaction is the pre-registered descriptor only (nothing measurable under the ceiling), and the proprio contribution is inside the batch's own no-op noise (2026-10-24)

**The mediator question P35 left open is answered for one channel.** P35 measured
the inactive-arm park as a real lever (the right's carried class 25/51 -> 0/50)
but could not separate the two channels it moves: the image (the arm's silhouette
3497 -> 4155 px, the fruit's band occlusion 68 % -> 0) and the **7 inactive-arm
joints** of the 25-D proprio (`[0.448, 0.603, 0.015, 0.497, 0.002, 0.002, 0.000]`
rad). This phase crosses them 2x2: cell 1 ready/ready (the control), cell 2
park/park (the lever), cell 3 park-image/ready-proprio, cell 4
ready-image/park-proprio, with the proprio written through
`FRUIT_PROPRIO_SPOOF` and the image moved by the real `FRUIT_ARM_PARK`.

(1) **The batch.** 4 cells x 3 runs x 15 episodes = **180**, seeds 77/101/202,
policy seed 11, one simulator session per cell, **one claim**
(`RUN_LIMIT=25200`, 19:39-21:04, wall **5146 s** = 85.8 min, 7.1 min/cell). The
cell order is a **randomised rotation** (`P36_ORDER_SEED=20261024`, base
`2 3 1 4`: run 1 `2 3 1 4`, run 2 `3 1 4 2`, run 3 `1 4 2 3`), replacing the plain
rotation whose cell-position alias was fixed within each run. Right-arm
denominators 27/30/28/30 (the arm follows the grade, so the per-cell fruit mix
differs - the standardisation exists for that), left 18/15/17/15.

(2) **The manipulation check passes, from the batch's own rows** (S1-S4, 180
episodes, no separate instrumented run): the probe cells write the file's vector
bitwise (`28/28`, `30/30`), the written vector matches the **physical
counterpart cell's live pose** to **0.0020 / 0.0040 rad** (per-episode max, bar
0.02), `rest_same=1` in **180/180**, the parked arm holds its pose **115/115**,
and - the design's point - **the image follows the arm, not the spoof**: the
inactive arm has pixels in the target's disc bbox in **27/27** cell-1 and
**30/30** cell-4 right-active episodes (the call census **670/670** and
**724/724**) and **0** in cells 2 (`30/30`) and 3 (`28/28`) (**0/741**,
**0/680** calls), with the no-op side (the inactive right arm at ready) **0/1555**
in every cell. So cell 3 presents the parked image with an in-support ready
proprio and cell 4 the shipped image with the parked proprio - the channels moved
independently.

(3) **The result (right-arm carried class, the primary).** Cell 1 **18/27 =
0.667** [0.478, 0.814]; cell 2 **0/30 = 0.000** [0, 0.114] - the lever
replicates; **cell 3 0/28 = 0.000 [0, 0.121]** - the image alone reproduces
**100 %** of the conversion; **cell 4 17/30 = 0.567 [0.392, 0.726]** - the
proprio alone is at the control level (effect fraction **+0.15**, band **none**).
The pre-registered exact tests: **image 0/58 vs 35/57, p = 8.8e-15** (the exact
hypergeometric tail); **proprio 17/60 vs 18/55, p = 0.687**; the **interaction
+0.100, permutation p = 0.581** (exact enumeration 0.587) - the pre-registered
**redundancy/synergy descriptor only**, reading 0 = additive, i.e. the
conjunction **adds nothing measurable under the ceiling** (the image cell is
already at 0/28 carried, so the descriptor cannot exclude a contribution above
it, and it is not a second channel test). **The reading is IMAGE-BORNE** in the
sense of the decision matrix: the **image channel** carries the win. Per run
(consistency, not a test): the image contrast is
negative **3/3** (-0.631/-0.611/-0.625) with cells 2 and 3 at **exactly 0
carried in every run** (0/12, 0/10, 0/8 and 0/10, 0/9, 0/9), the proprio **2/3**
(-0.169/-0.056/+0.125) with cell 4 at 6/13, 5/9, 6/8, i.e. **cell 4's effect
fraction per run is +0.42/+0.17/-0.50** - indistinguishable from no effect.

(4) **The composition and the noise floor.** Class-standardised to cell 1's
right-arm species mix (coverage 1.00/0.85/0.93/0.96): crude -> standardised
**carried** 0.667/0.000/0.000/0.567 -> **0.667/0.000/0.000/0.597**, so the
standardised fractions are **+1.00/+1.00/+0.10** - the mix does not make the
result (cell 4 moves *up*, the image cells stay at zero). The per-class table
shows the conversion is class-wide (cell 4's carried mass is orange 6/6, apple
4/6, lychee 2/5, peach 2/3, pear 2/2, strawberry 1/5, tomato 0/3). **The left
arm - the no-op population - is at the carried ceiling** (0.889/0.800/0.882/0.733,
1-4 ok per cell), so it is a one-sided noise floor: its own contrasts read image
**+0.030**, proprio **-0.119**, interaction **+0.073**, spread **0.156** - and
**the proprio main effect (-0.050) is smaller than the no-op population's own
proprio contrast (-0.119)**. The honest sentence is therefore "the image carries
the win and no proprio contribution is measurable at this n", not "the proprio is
proven irrelevant": the cell-4 null is also weakened by the OOD asymmetry
(`logs/p36/ood_proprio.txt`; PREREG section 8a: the written ready proprio is
in-support, max |z| 0.59, while the parked vector's **j2 (-0.978 rad) is the one
channel outside either store's observed range** - [-0.777,+0.175] direct,
[-0.792,+0.175] training; the paired -4.26/-5.13 sigma summary is a
pooled-population mixture statistic, and the two other >1.7-sigma channels j1/j4
sit inside their ranges). Secondary: composite 20/27, 1/30, 2/28, 17/30; pooled ok
7/45, 32/45, 27/45, 17/45; the cycle 1867/1796/1781/1850 ticks (ok-only
1756/1796/1781/1768, flat <= 5 %); **model calls/attempt 63/60/60/60** (medians) -
the probes cost no extra inference; **no new failure reason** in any cell.

(5) **The tooling, fixed before the batch and pinned** (`logs/p36/PREREG.md`
section 10). **H1**: the claim's `RUN_LIMIT` is part of the invocation
(`RUN_LIMIT=25200`, not exported inside the driver) and the driver refuses to
start below 7200 s - the 1800 s default would have killed the batch at run 4-5.
**H2**: the report refuses any batch that is not 3 complete runs of 15
episodes/cell (verified on the partial tree during the batch: exit 2, no numbers).
**M1**: the interaction permutation was **miss-centred** (`|T* - did| >= |did|`,
which reads >= 0.5 on every table: it read **0.5013** on a table whose fixed p is
**0.0050**) - now `|T*| >= |did|` with `(1+count)/(1+B)`, an exact-enumeration
cross-check and a self-test pin. **M2**: S1-S4 written as real assertions parsed
from the `[spoof]`/`[park]` rows, S4 filtered to right-active episodes, the
0.02 rad aggregation defined per episode, and the **outcome read gated on it**
(exercised: the self-test makes a parked cell show arm pixels and a wrong vector,
and both close the gate). **M3**: the power text corrected to the design's real
arm (60 right-arm episodes per main-effect arm, not 30/45) with the computed
quartet **0.998/0.977/0.894/0.724** (`logs/p36/power_check.py`) and the
run-clustering caveat. **M5**: the per-channel OOD asymmetry added (section 8a).
Also: the Fisher helper's **absolute** `+1e-12` tolerance inflated an extreme p
(it read 8.1e-13 on a table whose exact tail is **8.8e-15**, by counting every
table below 1e-12 as "at least as extreme") - now relative, pinned by the
self-test. **L**: cell 1 is described as the P35 scenario + `TRIGGER_ACQ=1` + the
four diags (not "the shipped env"), the class-standardised **carried** fraction
and the **model calls/attempt** are in the report, the failure reasons and the
cycle are right-arm only, and a **recording** rollout under the spoof is refused
(`store_guard_reason`, so a probe cell cannot poison a store).

(6) **No-harm.** The scripted acceptance (one claim 21:13-21:18) reads **6/10 +
`fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference.json`** with **376/376 `[fruit]`
lines byte-identical** to the P35 record (`logs/p36/A2_accept_identity.txt`;
the 6/10 is the pre-existing P32 pear-on branch, so the rate-only `exit=1` is
expected). `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS** (0 failures, 1 skipped), the
`proprio spoof check` leg now also pinning the store guard. Tree md5s unchanged
before/after except the phase's own files (`A_tree_md5_before/after`).

(7) **What this licenses and what it does not.** The park's win travels the
**image channel**, and *which* image statistic carries it is **not separated** -
the fruit's **sightline** (the P35 occlusion census) is the leading
**unseparated** candidate, because the probe moves the parked arm's silhouette as
well as the fruit's pixels. So the shipping path - a **recollection's own A/B** -
is the right spend, and this read is **consistent with** a recollection that
fixes the pixels (it does not substitute for it); the image-only cell is
synthetic and ships nothing. The design is a **probe at N = 3 runs**: the
**WS-4.2 N = 5** convention governs the recollection's own A/B. Cell 1 is not
the shipped default (carried 0.667 is this batch's control). One post-batch
**print-only** fix: `219`'s per-cell summary
grep also counted the env's `[rl] episode N: <fruit> grade=...` row and printed
"episodes 30" for a 15-episode run; the report's parser was never affected (it
requires `success=`). **No commit at write time; no shipped default changed.**

### P36 phase 2 (Gate 2): the channel claim, not the mechanism; the OOD caveat on j2's range; the gate's population pinned; the probes do not ship (2026-10-24)

**Gate 2 accepted the measurement and narrowed the reading.** (1) **The claim is
the image channel, not the sightline.** The 2x2 moves the *parked arm's
silhouette* as well as the fruit's pixels, so the phase-2 entry's "the park's win
is image-borne" is now, everywhere (`logs/p36/A_RESULTS.md` §3/§5, the WORKLOG
heading and (7), `scripts/220_p36_report.py`'s `READING_TEXT`): **"the park's win
travels the image channel; which image statistic carries it is not separated,
and the fruit's sightline (the P35 68.1 % -> 0 % occlusion census) is the leading
**unseparated** candidate."** The recommendation is unchanged - a recollection's
own A/B is the shipping path - and the read is now stated as **consistent with**
a recollection that fixes the pixels, not as a substitute for it. (2) **The OOD
caveat rests on j2's range, not on the sigma summary.** The z is a
pooled-population **mixture statistic**; the support claim is the **range**:
`back`'s **j2 = -0.978 rad** is the *only* one of the 7 channels outside either
store's observed range (`[-0.777,+0.175]` `r9_awr`, `[-0.792,+0.175]`
`demos_v11`), while the other two >1.7-sigma channels (j1 -1.912, j4 0.818) sit
inside theirs. `PREREG.md` §8a, `A_RESULTS.md` §5 and the report's reading
paragraph now say that; `logs/p36/ood_proprio.py` prints the range verdict per
vector and its table is byte-identical on re-run (it reads the stores, never the
batch). The direction is **conservative** - it weakens the cell-4 null, not the
image cell - so **no downstream change**. (3) **The interaction is the
pre-registered descriptor only** and reads 0 = additive: what it licenses is "the
conjunction adds nothing **measurable under the ceiling**" (the image cell is
already at 0/28 carried), not a synergy measurement; it is 1 of 3 contrasts.
(4) **The manipulation gate pins its own population** (`220`'s M2): every episode
writes one `[park]` row, so `len(records) == 4 x 15 x n_runs` and at least one
row per cell-run is asserted; a deleted row refuses with **exit 2**, and the
self-test deletes one and expects exactly that (the batch reads **180/180**).
(5) **N = 3 is a probe**: the **WS-4.2 N = 5** convention governs the
recollection's own A/B (the phase-2 text says so in `A_RESULTS.md` §5 and above).
(6) **Provenance, disclosed rather than tidied**: `ood_proprio.py` was edited

**The Gate-1 H1/H2 implementation, before the batch**
(`logs/p37/p37_report.py`, md5 `e17aef37` at batch time, self-test PASS). **H2**

`q_settled`, and it rejects a `ready` arm - the P35 A arm reads 0/51 on it, so

per episode; `arm_px = 0` is the **census report only**, not a bar. **H1** prints

comparisons) and the **Newcombe hybrid-score one-sided 95 % lower bound**; S1
the left noise floor; S2 species- and diameter-tertile standardisation with the
**crude-vs-standardised straddle = ambiguous** rule; S3 the new-reason set diff
with count/arm; S4 the cycle; S5 the manipulation gate; the realized n; the
`119` fidelity readout; and the **conservative label** (a pass at
`p_hat < 0.94` and/or a near-zero change <= 0.01 rad prints "PASS inside the
ambiguous band / no-op", never "preserved").

The candidate produced **one** reason the base never did: `timeout: no grasp

45-episode arm meets the class in ~40 % of batches, so **which arm it lands in

W7-C saw the same class once). The pre-registered rule is mechanical and has no
severity threshold, so the **adoption candidate is NO** (primary pass, S3 fail,
S4 pass, manipulation pass) - **the preservation read stands, and the S3 fail is
the pre-registered formal gate on a scenario tail (~1 %/episode, not a candidate
behaviour); it carries essentially no evidence about the checkpoint** (the
erasure branch's "negative and published" wording does not apply: the falsifier

together so the preservation read and the failed adoption gate cannot be
confused. **Not the fix**: widening the gate - the reach-edge ladder reads

no-re-selection on a lateral refusal** (the 1500-tick timeout class), each a
scenario change needing its own pre-registration.

### P38 phase 1: the delivered x is the spawn band plus a fixed per-instance settle offset and the transport contributes exactly 0.000 mm (the cascaded lateral-drift hypothesis is falsified); the S3 class is 2/3103 = 0.06 % on the shipped interface with per-arm floors 0.1730 right / 0.1800 left, so no A/B at the project's N can measure it and phase 2 pre-registers a forced-band mechanism endpoint instead (2026-10-25)

The P37 Gate-2 named this lane (a "supply/transport drift tail" + "the harness's
no-re-selection"). Phase 1 is the measurement and the pre-registration only:
**no `src/` change, no `configs/` change, no shipped default changed**, tree
unchanged (`rl_env.py` `aa54b022`, `trigger.py` `d7ec85fc`, `tasks.py`
`cdde6bd2`, `fruits.py` `6f65e423`, HEAD `dd53d15` before and after; pins in
`logs/p38/MD5.txt`). The record is `logs/p38/P1_RESULTS.md`, the
pre-registration `logs/p38/PREREG.md`, the census
`logs/p38/drift_census.py` -> `drift_census.txt`, the probe
`logs/p38/probe_drift.py` (five claimed runs).

**The delivered-x distribution, from the committed logs.** Three populations,
all deduped (a bit-identical replay reproduces an attempt's `(x, along)` to
4 dp; the scripted buckets carry 3-6x more raw rows than unique attempts):
(a) the scripted station-zone x per attempt (`wait step=0 fruit_x=`): single
scatter n=209 p50 0.272, min 0.177, **0 below 0.173**, 8/209 = 3.8 % below the
spawn floor 0.20; single patch n=272 p50 0.270, **min 0.158**, 1/272 = 0.37 %
below 0.173, 6.6 % below 0.20; two-line wave n=682 p50 0.276, 2/682 = 0.29 %
below 0.173, 3.4 % below 0.20; two-line patch n=2016 p50 0.280, **min 0.143**,
9/2016 = 0.45 % below 0.173, 6.5 % below 0.20; two-line bed n=38, 15.8 % below
0.20 (the 0.36 column drifts up); single bed n=47 with one unique attempt at
0.172. (b) the direct station-zone x per episode (`[park] call ... x=`, the
P35/P36/P37 band census, n=653): p1 0.187, p50 0.264, p90 0.341, **min 0.159**,
max 0.376, **2/653 = 0.31 % below 0.173**, 5/653 = 0.77 % below 0.180,
23/653 = 3.5 % below 0.20 (kiwi 8, orange 7, strawberry 5, lychee 2, apple 1)
and 11/653 = 1.7 % above 0.36. (c) the on-belt design reading
(`[supply] lateral x:`): the shipped scatter free cadence min 0.148 / p10 0.205
/ p50 0.279 / p90 0.348 / max 0.364 (`v1/12b`), the patch probe min 0.187 /
p50 0.264 / max 0.373 (`w6/00_probe_supply_free`), and the **pre-v9 fixed line**
as the control: min 0.308 / p50 0.334 / max 0.365 with no low tail at all. The
KS distance to the spawn band is 0.035-0.13 for the freely-drawing schedules, so
the *core* is the band; the patch/bed schedules do not draw uniformly (a pair's
first member is `U(x_min, x_max - sep)`), so the tail counts are the reading and
the KS is not. Within an episode the band census's `along` spans a median
0.096 m while x does not move: the delivered x is fixed before the band.

**The drift mechanism (measured, not assumed).** `logs/p38/probe_drift.py`
(scene + spawner, free cadence, **no attempt**, one `(x, y, vx)` sample per
physics tick per live fruit, one transit per release because the pool is
recycled) over **475 full transits in five configurations** (scatter/patch x
arms none / both `ready` / left `ready` + right `grasp`, seeds 5 and 77):

* **the transport contributes exactly 0.000 mm** (`transport mean 0.00 sd 0.00
  min 0.00 max 0.00` in every run). A sphere rolling on a plane whose surface
  velocity is along -y has a contact slip along -y only, so the friction is
  along -y, the spin about x, and there is **no lateral force term**; the cleats
  - the only part of the conveyor that could push a sphere sideways - are **off
  by default** (`conveyor.py:186-197`, `FRUIT_CLEATS=0`). The belt/cleat/
  friction/rolling drift hypothesis is **falsified**, and so is "the belt's own
  drift does not stay inside the spawn band" as a *transport* statement;
* **the release/settle is the only stage that moves x, and its displacement is
  a fixed per-instance offset.** The pool carries two instances per class; each
  instance reproduces its own value to 0.2 mm across the schedule (scatter vs
  patch) and across the arm pose. At seed 77: kiwi **-20.20 / +15.04**, peach
  -10.53 / +0.72, orange -2.66 / -1.23, apple +0.39 / +2.58, pear +1.24 /
  +2.24, lychee -0.17 / +6.40, strawberry -0.17 / +3.48, tomato +3.88 / +4.59
  (the per-class mean is the mixture of its two instance values, so it moves
  with the sample composition, n = 7-16 - which is why a class mean is the
  wrong summary). Seed 5 draws different instance scales (the spawner seeds the
  diameter/ripeness/friction draw from `SEED`), hence a different set:
  kiwi +12.06 / +26.22, strawberry **-35.89** / +19.96, peach +5.12 / +6.83,
  apple -2.46 / -0.71. The measured instance range is **-35.9..+69.2 mm** (the
  +69.2 is a patch-run kiwi drawn at 0.343 and delivered at 0.413, twice,
  identically). The delivered x is `spawn x + offset(instance)`, the low tail is
  the negative offsets meeting a draw near the 0.20 floor, and the §1 class
  ordering (kiwi, orange) is the ordering of the instance offsets. **The
  corollary names the real supply lever**: because the offset is fixed per
  instance it can be measured once (this probe) and compensated at `respawn`
  (`target x - offset`), which removes the tail instead of buying margin;
* **the open residual**: the deepest low-side delivered x in the *attempt* loop
  is 0.143-0.159, i.e. -41..-57 mm from the 0.20 floor, while the probe's worst
  instance offset is -35.9 mm (-20.2 at seed 77). A further ~5-20 mm of
  low-side displacement therefore happens inside the attempt loop and this
  probe does not see it; the named candidates are the active arm's jaws/links
  sweeping the fly-by band (the direct reset puts the active arm at `grasp` and
  the selection floor keeps the target at along >= ~0.40 m), a re-release under
  a moving arm, and a pair depenetration at release. The discriminator (a
  recorded action replay through the probe) is named for phase 2 as optional -
  the harness lever does not need it and the supply floor is computed from the
  empirical delivered distribution, which already includes it.

**The S3-class census, over every direct-loop log in the repository** (549
logs, grouped by the log's own `[rl] trigger=... lateral=...` and by whether it
carries any `x-edge refuse` row): **the shipped interface (gate 0.16, guard
off) is 3103 episodes with 2 never-fired = 0.06 %** - `logs/p37/B_ab/B_1.log`
ep 6 (kiwi, right, **x = +0.159**, 25 band calls, the P37 Gate-2 event) and
`logs/w7/C_eval/direct_ab/B_3.log` ep 12 (peach, left, x not recorded). A third
low-x episode did **not** become a timeout: `logs/p35/B_ab/A_4.log` ep 14
(orange, right, **x = +0.162**) ended at tick 1298 as `fruit fell off the line`
- so the low-x tail's measured terminal notes are 1 timeout + 1 fell-off among
the 2 episodes below the right floor. The other two never-fired episodes in the
gate-0.16 population are the **opt-in reach-cliff guard's own high-x refusals**
(120 guard episodes, 2 never-fired = 1.7 %: `x-edge refuse: fruit x=0.398`
`logs/r6/A_c2_hsteps150.log` ep 1 and `x = 0.412`
`logs/r7/A_cap_only_fix.log` ep 2) and must not be pooled with the low-x class.
The contrasts: the pre-W4 gate 0.06 is **180/3195 = 5.6 %** (nearly all
`arm=left`, the documented W4 no-fire class - widening the gate is what fixed
it) and the pre-trigger logs are 414/864 = 47.9 % (the historical policy-gate
no-fire, a different class). **The per-arm admission floor is not the same for
both arms** (650 episodes with both a band x and an intercept `dx`, so
`fruit_x - dx` recovers `_trigger_station`): **right station 0.3330 (n=431) ->
x >= 0.1730; left station 0.3400 (n=219) -> x >= 0.1800**, i.e. the left
refuses a 7 mm wider slice of the tail than the right - the P37 text's 0.173 is
the right arm's number. **Power**: at 0.06 %/episode a WS-4.2 arm of 75 episodes
expects 0.05 events; the P37 batch's 1/150 is batch clustering (one supply seed
stream per batch), not a rate - so **no A/B at the project's N can measure this
class**, which is why phase 2's primary is a mechanism endpoint at 100 %
incidence.

**The harness path and the levers.** The candidate is chosen **once per
episode** (`rl_env.py:1538-1560`, `task.select_target(..., reach_anywhere=False)`,
the arm/bin from the grade); `should_fire` refuses on `|dx| > lateral` and
returns `False` **with no marker** (`trigger.py`), so the env cannot tell a
lateral refusal from "not yet in the reach window" and does not try; the only
exit is `_tick >= reward.horizon` = 1500 control ticks of the *policy phase*
(`rl_env.py:2668-2674`; the scripted primitive's own steps run after the cap),
which leaves the note `timeout: no grasp within 1500 ticks` - a class with no
severity and no mechanism. Options: **(a)** a bounded re-selection inside the
same grade lane at the *provable* refusal (every other gate passes and only the
lateral one refuses), **(b)** an explicit terminal class
(`no firable fruit: candidate x=... beyond the lateral gate`) that ends the
episode at the refusal instead of burning the horizon, **(c)** both - and the
reporting constrains the design: `113_rl_report.py`'s `reasons()`
digit-normalises every note, so **any new note text is a new failure reason**;
the attribution note must therefore be a **run-neutral diagnostic ON in every
arm** (`FRUIT_POLICY_REFUSE_DIAG=1`) with only the *terminal* behaviour
differing (the AGENTS §3b rule). The re-selection is feasible inside the
horizon (the refusal is detectable at dy ~ 0.30 m ~ tick 300; the re-selected
fruit sits at along >= the moving-catch floor ~0.40 m; only the *fire* has to
happen before tick 1500) but it **changes `_goal` mid-episode**, an input pair
the checkpoint never saw (the default-off P4b2 `present` path is the only
precedent) - which is why the phase-2 primary is on a *forced* band and the
shipped-band endpoint is a **safety** check with the exposure reported.

**The supply lever is a margin purchase, not a drift fix.** Admission floors
0.1730 (right) / 0.1800 (left); the delivered low tail 0.143 (two-line patch),
0.159 (direct), 0.148 (on-belt) -> a worst downward excursion of **-0.057 m**
from the 0.20 floor; holding the delivered x above 0.180 needs the release floor
**>= 0.237**, and the patch pair rule (`x0 ~ U(x_min, x_max - sep)`, sep
0.085-0.12) then needs the ceiling at >= 0.38 (a 0.24-0.36 band degenerates the
pair rule), which is still inside the measured reach band (0.18-0.39, cliff
0.42). The delivered p50 would move 0.264 -> ~0.30, *closer* to the right arm's
0.333 station, so the mean |dx| falls ~0.035 - the lever's real value. The
**cost** is a scenario change: three motion references re-recorded
(`configs/motion_reference.json`, `motion_reference_twoline.json`,
`motion_reference_twoline_bed.json`), the scripted acceptance re-run and
re-referenced, both two-line gates re-run, and every dataset/checkpoint store
becomes a pre-change store. It is registered as **P38b**, not phase 2. A
*lane keeper* on the transport would be a no-op (0.000 mm to damp); the honest
transport-side fix is the per-instance offset compensation at `respawn`.

**Phase 2's pre-registration** (`logs/p38/PREREG.md`, written before any code
change): four default-off direct-only knobs (`FRUIT_POLICY_REFUSE_DIAG`,
`FRUIT_POLICY_REFUSE_END`, `FRUIT_POLICY_RESEED`, `FRUIT_POLICY_RESEED_MAX` = 2),
three arms (A diag-only control, B diag+END, C diag+RESEED+END) and four
scenarios: **M1 the forced band** (x draw 0.10-0.17, 100 % refused: A 15/15
1500-tick timeouts vs B 15/15 and C 15/15 attributed, median ticks <= 500 for
B); **M2 the mixed band** (0.10-0.36, 28 % refused: A's refused episodes end at
1500 ticks vs C's fire on a re-selected fruit, >= 10 of 12 paired, exact
McNemar p <= 0.01); **M3 the shipped patch band** (P37's scenario, five supply
seeds 77/101/202/303/404, A then C interleaved, 15 episodes each) for the
right-arm placed non-inferiority (> -0.10, the P35-P37 margin), the no-new-reason
set after mapping the attribution notes to the class `lateral-refuse`, and the
cycle over *fired* attempts only (<= +5 %); **M4 the scripted no-harm**
(`accept.sh` twice + selfcheck: the 376 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical and
`fingerprint: matches`, the knobs being direct-only). Six falsifiers, with
Fa/Fb/Fc/Ff stopping the phase and Fd/Fe killing the lever. The endpoint that
matters most is **P3: `timeout: no grasp within 1500 ticks` = 0 in B and C** -
the class is *named*, not fixed: `no firable fruit` is still a failure and stays
in the rate denominator, so the owner-facing sentence must never be "the
failure is fixed". Two claims (~90 + 150 episodes) plus one acceptance pair;
the recommendation is the only output, no shipped default changes in phase 2.

### P38 phase 2: the lateral-refusal harness attributes the class and halves its cycle (M1: 15/15 refused in every arm, the named class at 510-562 ticks against A's 1335) but the re-selection cannot act — the direct harness freezes the feeder inside an episode (54 + 83 scans, 0 candidates) — and on the shipped band the one refusal in 150 fell in the control arm, so the pre-registered rule reads not-adopted while P4/P6 are clean (2026-10-25)

Phase-2 measurement, same tree (`tasks.py` `cdde6bd2` untouched); the code diff is
`policy/trigger.py` `d7ec85fc -> b09d3cb2` and `rl_env.py` `aa54b022 ->
f25f6b61`. **No shipped default changed**; all four knobs default off,
`presentation == "direct"` only. Record: `logs/p38/P2_RESULTS.md`, the binding
Gate-1 amendment `logs/p38/PREREG_A1.md`, the batches `logs/p38/P2`/`P3`/`M4`,
the report `logs/p38/p2_report.py` -> `P2_report.txt`.

**The Gate-1 conditions, and what they changed.** **H1** — the "provable
refusal" ignored the learned policy-close path (`direct_fire = intercept or
(policy_close and gate_refuse is None)`, and `gate_refuse` is only the opt-in
`X_MAX` guard), so the terminal class is now named for the *trigger* and gated
on a **measured joint closure**: the trigger refuses, `x` is frozen (checked
per episode; the measured in-loop drift is 0.0-12.9 mm), **and the learned close
never fired** from the reset through the fruit passing the station
(`dy <= -0.05`) — the END fires at the *departure*, not at the latch. **The
closure's scope is exactly that**: "no close fired **before** the fruit's
departure" - and the Gate-2 rerun measured the limit rather than assuming it:
**1 of 3 closes latched after the departure** (`dy = -0.074 m`, 7.4 cm past the
station, tick 506), which is `PREREG_A1.md` falsifier #1 **firing**. So C3 is
not a total closure, `no firable fruit` over-claims on 1/15 of the forced band
(the episode is a failure either way - the swap is close-chase -> `no firable
fruit`), and a flip needs a re-registered definition or a post-departure grace
window; the shipped-band readout is owed in the B-arm batch. This is
not pedantry: on the forced band the close fired in **5/15 (B) and 6/15 (C)**
episodes and **placed 3 in each**, and in the M2-A smoke 2 of 4 refused episodes
ended in a close-chase grip loss. **H2** — the registered supply bands are not
bands: at 0.13-0.17 the *delivered* x spans **0.117-0.191 (12 % above** the
right arm's 0.173 floor, `logs/p38/z2_drift_m1.log`) and the free-cadence
envelope runs **0.080-0.529** (depenetration kicks push fruit off the **low**
belt edge only: 0.080 against the 0.110 edge, while the 0.529 maximum is still
inside the 0.570 high edge, `z1_supply_m1.log`), because 16 fruit in a 4 cm lane
interpenetrate. So M1/M2
use no supply override at all: the forced-refusal instrument is the **gate** on
the shipped supply (`TRIGGER_LATERAL=0` in M1, `0.06` — the P2b-era gate — in
M2), which also makes the learned close a *live* second path (at a below-floor
band it is geometrically impossible, so the registered M1 could never have asked
H1's question). **H3** — P4/P6 are run-level **unanimity** gates over the five
seed pairs (fail iff all five per-pair deltas are negative **and** the pooled
delta <= -0.10), because 47 right-arm episodes/arm at a ~40-45 % base put the
1-sd at ~0.10 and the old point rule false-failed ~1 in 6.

**M1 (the forced refusal, SEED=5, 15/arm)** — P1 attribution **15/15 in A, B
and C** (deterministic); P3 **0 timeouts**, the named class 10/15 (B) and 9/15
(C) at median **562/510 ticks vs A's 1335**, the complement being the episodes
whose close fired; the END tick bar (<= 600) met; C scanned **54** times (**max
4/refusal**, the budget) and **adopted 0**; Fb' clean; A's terminals are
`fruit fell off the line` 12/15 + close 3/15 — the timeout class does not appear
on a forced band at all, so what the END replaces is the *lost* episode, not a
timeout. **That is also a registered deviation, recorded as a finding**:
`PREREG_A1.md` A1 predicted A would "end at the horizon" (`timeout: no grasp
within 1500 ticks` or `policy closed`), and it measured **0 timeouts / 12
fell-off / 3 close** — because a refused fruit *rides off the end of the belt*
before the 1500-tick horizon (median 1335 ticks, so the line ends it first). The
**END's strength follows from the deviation, not from the prediction**: it
collapses *both* terminals (the horizon timeout and the lost episode) into one
named class at the departure, which is why its median (510-562) is not a
timeout-saving but a *terminal*-saving.

**M2 (the mixed refusal, `LATERAL=0.06`, 3 seeds x 15 x A/C)** — the refused
fraction is **62 % (A) / 47 % (C)**, above the registered ~28 %; the refused
episodes' terminals are `fell-off` 23 + `close` 5 in A and `no_firable` 19 +
`close` 2 in C; **P2a-i is UNEXERCISED: 83 scans, 0 non-empty**, so no adoption
ever happened and P2b reads 2/28 vs 1/21 placed (p = 0.82) with the pooled
success 9/45 in both arms. The pairing is broken (13/45 `(arm, category)`
agreement) exactly as A4 predicted — an early END moves the belt state — so the
unpaired Fisher is the read.

**The mechanism that matters: the re-selection has nothing to select because the
harness freezes the feeder.** The direct env calls `spawner.update` only in the
reset's feed loop and `enforce_transport` after it, so no fruit is released
inside an episode; the upstream window empties and every scan returns `None`.
The amendment had hypothesised the lane's ~46 % station starvation — measured
and **superseded**: the starvation number is the free/driver cadence, not the
frozen episode. A live-feeder re-selection is a scenario change the checkpoints
were never trained on, i.e. its own phase.

**M3 (the shipped patch band, A/C x 5 seeds x 15, `lateral=0.16`)** — **one
refused episode in 150 (0.67 %)**, against the patch-band expectation 0.31-0.77 %
(the phase-1 number, not the pooled 0.06 %), and it landed in **A** (seed 303,
ep 14, orange, **x = 0.157** — the drift tail, which the diag named where the
shipped note reads only `fruit fell off the line`); **C had 0 refusals and the
lever executed no action**. P4 right-arm placed **A 20/51 = 39.2 % vs C 25/58 =
43.1 %, delta +0.039 [-0.138, +0.220]**, per-pair +0.050/-0.111/-0.292/+0.179/
+0.269 → the unanimity gate does not fire (**PASS**); P6 fired-only cycle
-3.9/+0.3/+2.8/-2.0/-2.0 %, pooled **-2.0 %** (**PASS**); **P5 FAILS** on the
symmetric note-level rule, both A-only keys (`lateral-refuse`,
`fruit fell off the line`) coming from that single episode. **P5 is
structurally a false-fail and that is named**: an arm-only key with a **0.5-1.2
event expectation per 150 episodes** (the amendment's own exposure arithmetic)
is *necessarily* arm-unique - one event lands in one arm by construction - so
the symmetric rule fires whenever the exposure is realised, and here the
**DIAG's own `lateral-refuse` key is what fires it** (the diagnostic counts
against the treatment that did nothing). The literal pre-registered read stays
**`not adopted`**; a **power-controlled form** of the reason endpoint belongs in
the next registration, not in a post-hoc repair of this one. The un-parked
**right-arm** base is **39.2 %** (20/51), not the 45 % the amendment assumed:
the P35 mechanism is the *inactive left arm occluding the right arm's fruit*, so
the un-parked right rate is the depressed one - the left's own 2/24 (C 0/17) is
a separate number that drags the **pooled** total (A 22/75), not the right-arm
base, and the right is the primary as registered. The A/C arm-mix differs
because **the direct loop is not reproducible** (rendered frames), not because
the lever moved the reset: ep 0 is the same fruit in both arms (apple, C,
y = +0.642) and ep 1 already differs (peach, A, y = +0.532 vs +0.546) while C
executed **zero** actions in the batch.

**M4 (the scripted no-harm)** — `accept.sh` twice: knobs off **6/10 +
`fingerprint: matches`**, knobs on **6/10 + matches**, the two `[fruit]` streams
**byte-identical (376 lines, md5 `bc7ca8f0` both; the full logs differ only in
the startup timestamps)**, selfcheck **PASS 0 failures / 1 skipped**. The 6/10
and the `exit=1` are the shipped tree's rate-only result (the AGENTS P35/P36/P37
entry records the same pair), not this phase's. **What M4 proves is narrow**:
the knobs are **unset by default and the scripted line never reads them**, so
the identical stream is *near-tautological for this change* (the scripted path
cannot reach the `if self._refuse_knobs` branch - `226_p38_m4.sh` said so before
the run). The pin that matters for the `trigger.py` edit is
`scripts/811_trigger_test.py` (the lateral truth table + `no_firable_ready`)
plus the **analytic reorder equivalence** (the moved lateral check was already a
hard `False`, so the return value is unchanged for every input). **M4 did not
run `accept_policy.sh`**: the four knobs raise on any presentation other than
`direct`, so the hybrid canary cannot read them - an omission of coverage of the
shipped default, not of the direct interface.

**Verdict: `not adopted` by the pre-registered rule** (P5's 1-event artefact
plus P2 unexercised), published as such, with the substantive split: **DIAG is
recommended as the direct loop's diagnostic** (a note-only instrument that names
the class), **END is not adopted but is the measurement interface** with a
B-arm shipped-band safety batch as its named precondition - and that batch's
readout set **must include `PREREG_A1.md` falsifier #1** (any A close latched
after the departure voids the END) - and **RESEED is not adopted because it is
structurally inert here** (137 scans, 0 candidates). The `no firable fruit` note
stays a failure in every denominator: the endpoint is attribution, never
elimination. **What the offline pins actually cover**: `811` pins
`should_fire`'s lateral key and `no_firable_ready`; the reseed's adoption path
(`_goal` rebuild, the protection handover, the `Ff` guard) has **no test** and
**no episode exercised it** - "pinned offline" would overstate it.

**Gate-2 (applied 2026-10-25, `logs/p38/G2/`): the two conditions the batch left
open are closed by measurement, and one of them comes back negative.** Two
15-episode runs on the M1 band in one claim (`scripts/225_p38_batch.sh g2`):
`G2_diag0` with **no** refuse knob and `G2_diag1` with **DIAG only** (the arm the
batch called "A"); `rl_env.py` `dba80de6` (one `[refuse] close:` diagnostic
print added, `DIAG`-gated, no control read), `225` `eae2d89a`, `811` `00ebe772`.

* **H1 - the close tick's `dy`, and the falsifier FIRES.** `[refuse] close:
  tick= dy=` prints the second fire path's own timing: ep 2 **tick 430
  `dy=+0.071`**, ep 9 **tick 506 `dy=-0.074`**, ep 13 **tick 171 `dy=+0.314`**.
  The middle one is **after** the departure (`dy <= -0.05`): the jaw chased the
  fruit 7.4 cm past the station and closed on it, then lost the grip. The END
  would have ended that episode ~24 ticks earlier, so **`PREREG_A1` falsifier #1
  fires** - C3 is not a total closure, the class must be read as "no close
  **before** the departure", `no firable fruit` over-claims on **1/15** of the
  forced band (a failure either way: the terminal swaps close-chase -> `no
  firable fruit`), and a flip needs a re-registered definition (the
  post-departure rate quoted with the name) or a post-departure grace window.
  The shipped-band readout stays owed in the B-arm batch. The other two closes
  are inside the closure, one of them 31.4 cm upstream (the ACQ lead).
* **H4 - the DIAG=0/1 pair, measured, and read honestly.** `diag0`: close 5,
  fell-off 10, placed **2/15**, median 1362; `diag1`: close 3, fell-off 12,
  placed **0/15**, median 1360; class agreement **9/15**, fruit agreement
  **6/15**. The two **DIAG=1** samples (`M1_A` vs `G2_diag1`) agree **14/15**
  and **12/15**, so the loop's run-to-run agreement is *not constant* (both
  DIAG arms held one attractor to ep 11; `diag0` left it at ep 4, where its
  ep-3 fell-off ends 90 ticks earlier) and **one pair cannot demonstrate
  neutrality at n=15**. The doc claim "A behaves as the control" is therefore
  **withdrawn** and replaced by the pair plus the construction argument (with
  `END`/`RESEED` off, `_track_refuse` writes notes, bookkeeping and one
  fruit-pose read per refusal - none of it is a control input).
* **H2/H3/H5 corrections carried** (so the record matches the code): P5's
  **structural false-fail** named (an arm-only key at a 0.5-1.2 event
  expectation per 150 is necessarily arm-unique; the DIAG's own key fires it;
  a power-controlled form is the next registration's); the M4 claim rephrased
  (unset by default, the scripted line never reads the knobs - near-tautological

  non-reproducibility** (rendered frames - ep 0 the same fruit, ep 1 already

  "ends at the horizon" prediction is recorded as a **deviation** (12/15
  `fell off the line`, 0 timeouts) with the END's strength re-stated (it

### P39: the finger tip lane closes negative — the left's composite does not move at -4 mm in any evaluable comparison (the pear primary is not evaluable, the acceptance is inadmissible for the arm and the matched-count null holds in one mode only), F1 is the tree's first bimodal arm, the `47` probe jams laterally so the belt-clearance claim is untested, the lane-0 "solved pre-pose" does not exist, and the two-line reference predated the P32 pear (re-recorded) — no adoption, both knobs default off (2026-10-25)

Registered on `e061d94` before any asset edit (`logs/p39/PREREG.md` + A1 + A2;
A3 is the post-run withdrawal). **Two levers, one arm set.** **L1**
`FRUIT_FINGER_TIP_DELTA` (`scene.py`, signed, **presence-gated**: unset = the
shipped mesh colliders byte-identically, `=0` re-authors each plate as a convex
box of the same mesh (arm **S**), `=-0.004` shortens it (arm **F1**)). **L2** the
lift-only wrist hold was **closed as a code fact before any run** (A1.1): the
shipped `grasp_lift` already holds the commanded top-down attitude - `_carry`
clears `arm.hold_quaternion` only for `name != "grasp_lift"` - so
`FRUIT_CARRY_HOLD_QUAT=1` only swaps the hold *target*, and `logs/444`'s negative
is the *place* leg; no W arm exists. Batch: one `154_claim_run.sh` claim per
battery, arms **interleaved C -> S -> F1** - pear (primary), acceptance, `47`
probe, mechanism (`FRUIT_CARRY_ATTITUDE=1`), two-line - plus five F1 determinism
runs added after the first pair diverged. **Pins:** `scene.py` `988985ef`,
`tasks.py` `112d2cb1`, `rl_env.py` `238e90a4` (the `TASKS_MD5` metadata-only
follow), `configs/motion_reference.json` `25ade92b` untouched; the two-line
reference moved `181c9151 -> d0326030` (this phase). Evidence `logs/p39/p3/`
(`RESULT.md`, `P3_report.txt`, the logs), `p2/NOTES.md`, `selfcheck.log`.

**F-6: the control is valid, and the batch reads.** C's pear battery is
**345/345 physics lines identical** to `logs/p32/90_pear_battery_new.log` and its
acceptance **374/374** to `logs/p32/D1_accept_pear.log` (only the two print-only
`output belt` message rows differ); C's acceptance reads **6/10 +
`fingerprint: matches`**. Pear battery (left placed/composite, right placed):
C **1/3**, 5/5 (6/9, one starved slot); S **0/2**, 8/8 (8/10); F1 **1/3**, 6/6
(7/10). Acceptance: C **6/10** left `1/3/1` (placed/cnp/no-grasp), right 5/5;
S **8/9** left `5/1/0`; F1 **8/9** left `5/1/0` (one starved slot each). No new
failure reason in any arm (the only note anywhere is C's own `fruit did not
follow the gripper`); motion budgets pass in every arm (worst descent `|v|max`
0.110-0.111 against 0.160-0.161, lurch 0.017-0.019 against 0.291).

**The primary is not evaluable, and no arm improves.** A1.3's count invariance
fails on the pear battery - the left takes **2** attempts in S and **4** in F1
(they share attempts 0-5 and diverge at attempt 6: S a 6.1 cm pear, F1 a 7.0 cm
one; the named mechanism is attempt 1's differing close leaving the escaped pear
elsewhere on an absolute-schedule feed, **inferred** from the shared prefix) - so
the census is a snapshot, and it reads **no arm improving** (C 1/3, S 0/2,
F1 1/3). S is a control, not a verdict arm (A2.6).

**The acceptance is inadmissible for the arm (the Oracle gate-3 correction).**
C's left takes **5** attempts and S/F1 take **6**; the left's fruit diverge from
the third left attempt (C `peach 6.5 / peach 6.9 / kiwi 5.6 / orange 6.4 / lychee
3.0` vs S,F1 `peach 6.5 / peach 6.9 / kiwi 5.4 / tomato 6.6 / tomato 6.2 / ...` -
S a second 5.4 cm kiwi, F1 an orange 6.4); and **inside S** the same 5.4 cm kiwi
at the same read interference (grip-dia `+5.60` mm, close 22 ticks) **cnp's at
attempt 3 and places at attempt 9**. The per-slot class is therefore not a stable
function of the fruit, and the acceptance's 5/6 left is **not evidence for the
arm** (AGENTS §2). The matched-count "no fall" statement (S 6 / F1 6, census
`5/1/0` both) survives **only as F1's mode A**; mode B's left is `1/3` (composite
3 against S's 1). The secondary band does **not** fall either (left carry legs
> 0.34 m/s: pear S 4 -> F1 5, acceptance 3 -> 3), and there is no new failure
reason.

**F1 is bimodal, and that is the phase's structural finding.** Five
same-configuration acceptance runs land in **two bit-identical modes** - **348
filtered `[fruit]` lines, 8-of-9** (`accept_F1`, `f1_repeat2`) and **382,
7-of-10** (`claim_f1_repeat`, `mech_F1`, `f1_repeat3`) - whose first-attempt
pick-pose settle differs by **one tick** (0.88 vs 0.87 s; residual 0.0431 vs
0.0432 m, i.e. the mode is *not* a monotone function of the residual). C (3
same-config pairs: `accept_C` vs `mech_C`, vs `logs/p32/D1_accept_pear.log`, and
`pear_C` vs `logs/p32/90...`) and S (1 pair) are **single-mode**, so the shipped
line's per-configuration determinism is **not contradicted** - but one
configuration is multi-modal run-to-run, **its numbers are one draw**, and
**configuration vs harness is not separated** (the separators: more C/S repeats;
a fixed-pose contact read). Two consequences are carried in the record:
**F-1 is not adjudicable on F1** (a byte-identity falsifier cannot be run on an
arm that is not self-identical, so the "contact-neutral" algebra is **untested**,
not confirmed), and the pear-battery F1 row is one draw of a marginal arm.

**The `47` probe jams, so the belt-clearance claim is untested (N5, via a
different route than registered).** The probe is registered as a straight
`-0.35 m` z descent that seats the distal plane on the belt; it instead
**translates laterally** - jaw end `[0.210, -0.161, 1.229]` (C) /
`[0.183, -0.179, 1.207]` (S) / `[0.176, -0.181, 1.208]` (F1) from
`[0.341, 0.003, 1.262]`, i.e. **0.13-0.17 m in x** and **0.16-0.18 m in y** for
**0.03-0.06 m of z** - and C ends in a different hand configuration (finger long
axes along world X vs S/F1's Y). `47` prints **no tool axis**, so **N4 is not
computable as registered**; the `+1.00 mm` F1-vs-S jaw-floor difference and
N4b's `-22.0 mm` are configuration outcomes of two different jams, not
distal-plane shifts. The re-author itself **is** proven by the **build print**
(long `84.9 -> 80.9 mm`, distal `80.5 -> 76.5 mm` at `delta = -4 mm`). Two
readings were **deleted** from the record on the gate's finding: the
"`delta` footprint <= 1 mm in every geometry read" sentence (the 0.3 mm `dz`
pair is a **pad-fruit contact height**, insensitive by construction to a shorter
distal extent) and "the AABB bottoms are a second, independent read" (that bound
is the union of the link's visual mesh and the authored box). The valid
instrument, if the clearance bit is ever wanted, is a **static-pose read of the
authored collider prims** (`S - F1` must differ by `4*cos(theta)`). **PREREG A3**
therefore withdraws §6's "still adoptable as a hardware/clearance change": the
claim is **untested, not measured-zero**, and F1 has no adoptable form on this
evidence.

**The lane-0 pre-pose lever does not exist (the phase-1 audit fact, which also
corrects the P33 record).** `_prepare_two_line_stations` skips the arm whose
station **is** the calibrated pick point, and the two-line's **left** station is
exactly that (`y = 0.00 = cfg.pick_y`), so the left runs the shared `grasp` config
and the same aim (the two-line catch lead is `0.0`). The "station-specific
pre-pose" is true for the **right** station only: the two-line left differs by
the **supply**, the **scheduler** and the adopted two-line carry monitor, not by
a pose. `logs/p33/51_phase2_read.md` (§1.2's inline clause, §3.1's "only
unmeasured bounded candidate", §4.1 (C)'s "solved pre-poses" and §4.1 (B)'s
"a different pre-pose") now carries a
**superseded-by** annotation pointing at `logs/p39/03_prepose_audit.txt`; the one
surviving pose term on that candidate is the **wrist attitude** (the flattest
posture is the 93.6 deg place solve), whose hold-all-legs form is measured
negative (`logs/444`) and whose lift-only scope is spanned by L2's code-fact
closure. Offline pins: `logs/p39/prepose_audit.py` `--assert`, 11/11 PASS.

### P40: the grip chain is measured end to end and the carry class is not converted (the command is at the 10 N cap while 22 % of it arrives; the physics rate doubles the force for 3.08x wall), and the one adoption is a path-scoped `FRUIT_REGRASPS` (2 dynamic / 3 otherwise) worth a measured 1.42-1.52 s on the `k=3` class whose third probe is 0/17 — the selector and the substeps stay opt-in, and both motion references are re-recorded from the flipped tree (2026-10-26)

Started on the P39-final tree `1790b87` (clean) with `logs/p40/PREREG.md` + A1
before any edit. **One shipped change** (`FRUIT_REGRASPS` path-scoped); two
opt-ins measured and **not** flipped (the selector, the substeps); three
measurements published (the grip effort chain, the regrasp yield, the arrival
split). Evidence `logs/p40/`: `GRIP_CENSUS.md`, `RATE_CENSUS.md`,
`LIT_REVIEW.md`, `PREREG.md` (+A1), `EFFORT_READ.md`, `REGRASP_YIELD.md`,
`ARRIVAL_SPLIT.md`, `P3_RESULTS.md`, `P4_RESULTS.md`, `p2/`, `p3/`, `p4/`,
`selfcheck.log`, and the two archived references.

**The grip chain, measured (G0, `FRUIT_GRIP_EFFORT=1`, default off, reporting
only).** Two claimed acceptance runs, `logs/p40/p2/` (`effort_sub1.log`,
`effort_sub4.log`; `effort_table.txt` re-derives every row):

* **The 2.2x under-read is REFUTED.** On the shipped substeps the tactile sum is
  **4.42 N** and the same-tick **projected joint reaction** - a different buffer -
  sums to **4.42 N** (ratio **0.999**; per face 2.24/2.28 vs 2.25/2.23).
  A sensor-only 0.44x scaling cannot produce that agreement, so `GRIP_CENSUS`
  §3/§4's capacities and margins stand as written and **nothing is multiplied by
  2.2**. `get_dof_efforts` returns **+0.00 N on 98/98** rows in both runs (this
  build's implicit-PD drives do not populate the actuation buffer), so the
  claim rests on `get_dof_projected_joint_forces` + the drive law.
* **The drive's *command* is at its 10 N/joint cap on 40/40 contact rows; what
  it *delivers* is 22 % of it.** The authored `k*err` is 4-8 kN (`err`
  3.95-7.57 mm x `k` 1e6 N/m), so `Fsat` clips to 10.00 N on every row, while
  the delivered reaction is **2.21 N/joint (22.1 %)** - and 5.00 N/joint
  (50.0 %) at 480 Hz. **The 10 N cap is never the limiter**: what limits the
  force is what the drive/contact pair can transmit inside one timestep.
  The **`F/err` ratio is an operating point, not a stiffness** - 377 N/m at
  120 Hz, 1045 N/m at 480 Hz, i.e. a **timestep signature** - and the *law* is
  **unidentified**; this pair does not separate stiffness from damping from the
  solver's implicit-spring regularisation. (`PREREG` A1.1's stated ground, "the
  drive is at its 10 N/joint cap", therefore does **not** hold; A1 was executed
  as written - G1 not run - and the post-freeze load phase, if ever revived,
  needs its premise re-registered.)
* **`FRUIT_SUBSTEPS=4` is the force lever, and it is not free.** 4.42 -> **9.95 N
  (2.25x)**, verified by both instruments (tactile/joint ratio 0.995), at
  **3.08x wall** (266 -> 819 s) and **+0.66 s/attempt** of span (`[stats]`
  150.2 -> 156.8 s over 10 attempts - say that, *not* "+0.90 s" and *not*
  "+4 %"). It takes the **worst-case fruit's friction margin 1.20x -> 2.70x**
  (`mu_eff` 0.45 against the 1.66 N transient; `mu_eff` 1.20 reads
  3.20x -> 7.19x). Its **8/10 is a different attractor** (480 Hz is a physics
  setting, not an instrument state, `fingerprint: DIFFERS`) and **the class is
  not deleted**: the left still carries-not-places **2/7** (attempt 3's orange,
  `lift +0.218`; attempt 9's tomato, `lift +0.136`) against the shipped run's
  4/4 left. It ships as a **finding, not a setting**: the controller stays
  120 Hz (`common.py:13-20`), so a store's *consumability* is not the issue and
  the **`write_manifest` `substeps` field is the unconditional precondition**
  for any store; a **real-jaw clamp-force anchor** gates only a *fidelity*
  claim, and the 2.25x/3.08x pair is **one pair**.

**The regrasp yield (`REGRASP_YIELD.md`, offline, 109 attempts).** A third probe
has **produced nothing**: the **17/17** attempts that burned all three never
closed on the fruit (`grasped 0/17`, `lift <= 0.004 m`), and the only conversion
in the corpus came on the **second** probe (`k=1`: 2/3 grasped, 1/3 placed). The
per-failed-probe price is **1.24 s (two-line) / 1.50 s (single arm)**, and on a
`k=3` attempt the `grip` segment is 5.45 s against a healthy 1.74 s. `=2` keeps
probes 1 and 2 (so the only measured conversion path) and removes only the third.

**The arrival split (`ARRIVAL_SPLIT.md`, offline).** The wait is
**supply-bound to within one tick** (`N/120` equals
`(dy0 - dy_arr)/0.12` with a **0 ms median residual and a 10 ms worst case over
109 attempts**; the within-attempt belt slope is **-0.1200 m/s on all 109**). The
arm's pre-pose + hover block is **overlapped, not additive** (1.49 s two-line =
46 % of the 3.26 s gap, 0 s of it additive), so **nothing on the pre-pose/hover
speed can shorten the gap** - the lever is the commit distance.

**Phase 3 (`P3_RESULTS.md`).** **R-R**: `FRUIT_REGRASPS=2` on the two-line reads
**7/10, 88.2 s, 8.8 s/attempt, 5 re-seat rows** against the control's **6/10,
90.2 s, 9.0 s, 13 rows**; on the acceptance **5/9, 133.0 s, 14.8 s/attempt,
2 rows** against **6/10, 150.2 s, 15.0 s, 3 rows**. Both are **moved attractors**
(`diverted` 0 -> 1; `no eligible fruit` from attempt 4 on the single arm), and
the countable mechanism is the same-attempt one: the two capped attempts are the
control's own `k=3` rows (`right peach idx 12`, `left kiwi idx 13`), they end
identically (`grasped=False`, `lift +0.003 / +0.000`, `fruit did not follow the
gripper`) and only the time moves - **5.45 -> 3.93 s** and **5.42 -> 4.00 s**,
the measured **k=3 tax of 1.42-1.52 s**. **The `k=1` row the treatment creates is
NOT a rescue**: it is a *new* two-probe attempt on slot 2's right pear, which the
**control placed first-try** (`k=0`, grip 1.77 s, span 15.3) -> treatment grip
3.23 s, span 16.8 s. The corpus rescue (`twoline_C` slot 4) has **no counterpart
in the battery**; `=2` preserves that path by construction but this run does not
exhibit it. **The two-line rate columns are captioned "NOT a rate claim"** in
`P3_RESULTS.md` and stay out of AGENTS: `4.76 placed/min` is `60 x 7 / 88.2` and
the `9.27 s` pooled interval is `60 / 6.47`, i.e. monotone transforms of the
count on a moved branch (the P1/P2 lesson). **R-S**
(`FRUIT_SELECT_NEAREST_ABOVE_FLOOR`, default off): the arrival wait falls
**1.41 -> 0.97 s** mean (1.20 -> 0.63 median), loop-entry `dy0` 0.358 -> 0.305 m,
span 15.01 -> 14.64 s, s/attempt **15.0 -> 14.6**, placed 6 -> 7, discharge
4 -> 5, no new failure reason - a positive at 10 attempts on one branch. Its
**commit distance is a lower-bound artefact** unless the ~0.76 s hover is
counted: the naive 0.463 -> 0.411 m excludes 0.09 m that the floor's 1.5 s setup
*includes*, so the true commit is **~0.553 -> ~0.501 m** against a 0.399 m
floor - **~0.15/0.10 m above it**. The rule therefore **does not spend the
floor's margin** (risk downgraded); it removes 0.05 m of the 0.21 m median
over-commit.

**Phase 4 — the adoption.** `FRUIT_REGRASPS` is now **path-scoped**: `2` when
`_dynamic_capture_active`, `3` otherwise, an explicit env value winning on both
(`tasks.py`, the single resolved `regrasp_cap`; the `FRUIT_REGRASP_REOPEN` slot
reads the same value, so the default-off recovery cannot disagree with the loop
bound). The scope is not cosmetic: every re-seat row is
`dynamic_capture`-**and**-`verbose`-gated, and the direct/policy handover is
`scripted=False` with `DirectSortEnv(verbose=False)`, so **no number in this
phase covers the indexed/policy retry** - it is a different mechanism (no moving
fruit, no re-seat-in-place) and it keeps 3 (`grasp.py`'s separate
`GraspPrimitive` loop, reached only under `FRUIT_NO_ATTACH=1`, is untouched).
Measured with the knob **unset**: `logs/p40/p4/accept_flip.log` **5/9, 133.0 s,
14.8 s/attempt, 2 re-seat rows** and `logs/p40/p4/twoline_flip.log` **7/10,
88.2 s, 8.8 s/attempt, 5 rows** (`diverted=1`, left 4/5, right 3/5) - **byte
identical** to the phase-3 `FRUIT_REGRASPS=2` arms (`filter_stream.py --diff`:
**339/339** and **430/430** filtered `[fruit]` lines), so the flip *is* the
measured arm and not "equivalent to" it. **Both references re-recorded from
these same-batch runs** (the flip moves both): `configs/motion_reference.json`
`25ade92b` -> **`adef05c9`**, `configs/motion_reference_twoline.json`
`d0326030` -> **`d87c3cdf`**; the pre-P40 files are archived
(`logs/p40/motion_reference_single_pre_p40.json`,
`..._twoline_pre_p40.json`). Every motion budget passed and only the rate floor
refused, so both writes landed; the gates then read **`fingerprint: matches`**
(rate-only FAIL, 5/9 < 75 %) and **`190` PASS** (7/10 at the 0.60 floor).
`scripts/189_w7a_chain.sh` was **not** run.

**Phase 4 — the two opt-ins.** `FRUIT_SELECT_NEAREST_ABOVE_FLOOR` stays **off**:
its single-arm return is also the **direct loop's** episode rule
(`select_target(..., reach_anywhere=False)` with no lane at `rl_env.py:1656`;
the reseed path at `3233` passes a lane and is excluded), so a default flip would

value, as a **finding** (the preconditions above). Nothing else was adopted: no

**Corrections applied to the record this phase (Oracle gate 3).** (1) the
two-line R-R rate columns are captioned **"NOT a rate claim"**. (2) the
"`k=1` converted again" sentence is **replaced** (it is a new two-probe attempt on

R-S commit distance is **re-stated with the hover term** (~0.553/0.501 m,
~0.15/0.10 m above the floor), so the rule does **not** spend the margin. (4)
`EFFORT_READ` §0/§6/§7: "the drive sits at 22 % of the cap" -> **the command is
at the cap on 40/40 rows, the delivered reaction is 22 % of it**; and
"`k_eff`/effective stiffness" -> an **operating-point `F/err` ratio**, a timestep

(`[stats]` 150.2 -> 156.8 over 10). (6) `logs/p40/__pycache__` excluded from the

**No-harm.** `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS, 0 failures, 1 skipped**
(`logs/p40/selfcheck.log`) and `scripts/96_motion_check.py` "all motion checks

### P41: the finger drive ships the `finger_damp02` profile by **recorded deviation from F2** — the grip was a parameterization defect (4.4 N = 44 % of what the same drive gives at 480 Hz) and the 2.2x pinch is free (1.00-1.01x wall), but the carried class does not convert at 10/30/60 N and the sim's hold limit is geometry, not force; `FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE` is not adopted, both references are re-recorded, and the `physics` provenance block is now shared by the collector and the direct env (2026-10-26)

Started on the P40-final tree `ae0a579` (clean) with `logs/p41/PREREG_DRAFT.md`
drafted before any edit; four phases (the sweep, the profile + provenance, the
force cap, this close) with one Oracle gate each. Evidence `logs/p41/`:
`FIDELITY_SWEEP.md`, `P2_RESULTS.md`, `P3_RESULTS.md`, `DEVIATION.md`,
`PREREG_DRAFT.md`, `p2/`, `p3/`, `p4/`, `selfcheck.log`, and the two archived
pre-P41 references.

**The profile (phase 2, `control.py`).** `finger_drive_profile()` ships
**`finger_damp02`**: **k = 100000 N/m, c = 2000 Ns/m, both pinned explicitly** -
`c` is *not* derived from `k`, because the **ratio c/k = 0.02** is the mechanism.
`FRUIT_FINGER_STIFFNESS=0` skips the gain call and leaves the asset's own drive
(k = 1e6, c = 100) - the pre-P41 line - and both env knobs still win. The old
`FRUIT_FINGER_PADS=1` 60000 N/m default is **removed**: it only ever unstuck a
padded close and a softer-than-default override would undo the profile on the one
hand that has pads. **Caption, for everywhere:** the delivered pinch goes
**4.38-4.42 → 9.75-9.9 N (2.2x)** at **1.00-1.01x wall per attempt** (14.8 →
15.0 s; the totals differ because the branches take 9 vs 10 attempts), and 9.8 N
is **50 % of the per-face cap** - 5.0 N per face of the `Fsat` 10.0 N per joint,
the tactile pinch summing both faces to 9.8-9.9 N of the 20 N the two caps could
apply - **the same ceiling `FRUIT_SUBSTEPS=4` reaches at 480 Hz (9.95 N, P40)**
for a third of the wall. The plateau's onset is **c/k >= ~3e-3** (bracketed:
0.002 → 7.2 N, 0.0033 → 10.0 N) and the mechanism behind the ratio is **not
identified** (`FIDELITY_SWEEP.md` §6.4), so no threshold number is carried into
the documents.

**The census that decides it (phase 2 §4).** `sep_max` - the pad span on the
escape leg, from the trace twins, which are byte-identical to the claimed runs
(`[fruit]` 437/437 and every `[carry]` row) - against the mechanical stop
`0.010 + 2·0.044 = 98 mm`: the control reads **98.3 / 98.2 / 77.9 mm**, the
profile **98.5 / 76.0 / 77.4 / 64.2 mm**. The profile's worst escape still
reaches the pads' **own open stop**, with the onset force at 8.03-18.19 N and the
loss 12-63 ticks later, single-sided, `F → 0.00 N`, 38-54 servo trips. **The pads
hold and the payload slides** - the W8-B loaded-slide class - so the carried class
is **not force-starved on this scenario**. `sep@loss` (the loss-tick span) cannot
carry that verdict: the servo has already closed by the tick contact is lost
(43.2-78.0 vs 61.9-82.4 mm), which is why the trace's `sep_max` is the field of
record.

**F2 fired, and the profile ships anyway - the recorded deviation
(`logs/p41/DEVIATION.md`).** The pre-registration's F2 said: force rises, class
does not move → a fidelity record, **not** the default and **no** reference
re-recorded. The class did not move (acceptance 5/9 → 6/10, pear left cnp 3/4 →
4/6 with the attempt count moving 4 → 6, two-line 6/10 → 8/10 - all **different
attractors**, and the pry intact at 98.5 mm), so F2 fires on both clauses. The
close flips the default and re-records both references because the shipped 4.4 N
is **44 % of what the same drive delivers at 480 Hz** (9.95 N): the 120 Hz
setting contradicts the asset's own authored drive, i.e. it is a
**parameterization defect, not a lever**, and F2's clause treats it as a lever.
**Mechanism-positive, class-negative** - stated plainly in `DEVIATION.md` §3,
with the two consequences (the force is free and moves no trajectory; leaving the
defect would make every future force number and every store's metadata describe a
22 % drive).

**The force family's top end (phase 3, `FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE`, default off,
NOT adopted).** The knob writes `drive:linear:physics:maxForce` on `joint1` (both
arms) in `build()`, i.e. **before** the articulation exists, so PhysX parses it;
proven twice (stage readback `30.0`, live articulation
`joint1/joint2=30.00/0.00 N`), and the unset path is **457/457 `[fruit]` lines
identical** to phase 2's profile run. **The cap deletes the pry** - `sep_max`
**98.5 → 43.5 → 31.2 mm** at **10 → 30 → 60 N** (44 % → 40 % of the open stop;
the cleanest causal pair is attempt 0's peach, identical up to the close, 0.1 mm
vs 278.3 mm of slip) - **and the class does not convert**: acceptance
**6/10 → 8/9 → 9/10** are **three attractors**, the pear **6/10 → 4/10**, the
two-line **8/10 → 6/10**, and **60 N crushes a 3.7 cm strawberry** out of the
hand (`clean_slip` 641.2 mm at `F@onset` 62.32 N). The surviving escapes start at
16-31 N of the ~28-30 N the grip delivers (the contact is degrading, not the
drive out of travel) with the pads held closed - a **loaded slide**, not a pry.
The pear control is **P41's same-tree 6/10**, *not* P39's 6/9 (a different tree).
**So the sim's hold limit is geometry/hardware, not force**: jaws that cannot
oppose an off-centre payload and pads with no feature that resists an axial walk.
Nothing in this phase says the sim now holds the fruit.

**Provenance (phase 2, and this close's A2/A4).** `control.py` and `common.py`
were **absent from the collector's `sources`**, so a pre-profile shard and a
post-profile one were indistinguishable by their own metadata. Both are pinned,
and one builder - `scene.finger_physics_provenance(arms=None, control_dt=…)` -
now writes the **`physics` block** for **both** the collector's shards and
(`rl_env._build_manifest`, phase-4 A2) the direct env's rollout manifests:
`profile`, `substeps`, `control_dt`, `dt`, `c_over_k`, the **intent** level
`FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE` (null when unset), the contact **pair**, and the
**per-joint runtime read-back** of k / c / `maxForce` (`joint2`'s 0.0 N is the
drive-less mimic; `readback_matches` now compares the **caps too**, A4, so a
`nan`/absent cap cannot read like an `mf10` shard). Verified on a real shard
(`logs/p41/p4/collect_manifest_smoke.log`: `matches=True maxForce=10.0N`) and on
a direct rollout (`logs/p41/p4/rl_manifest_smoke.log`: four joints, k/c/maxForce,
`readback_matches: true`). The build print names the drive
(`profile=finger_damp02 k=… c=… maxForce=10.0/0.0N`). **A4 also closes a
latent defect**: `_finger_drive_caps` read its caps through
`UsdPhysics.DriveAPI.Get`, the call `_finger_drive_rows`' docstring forbids, which
constructs a schema object on the **drive-less joint2 mimic** it is describing;
both readers now take the raw attribute `drive:linear:physics:maxForce`.
Measured (`logs/p41/p4/a4_drive_read_out.txt`): the attribute name is the API's
own, `joint2` answers `None`, the readers leave its applied schemas alone, and
`DriveAPI.Get` is **inert** on this USD/lib (no opinion authored) - so the
pre-fix builds were sound and the fix removes the question; the post-fix
one-attempt run is **65/65 physics lines identical** to the pre-fix control
(`a4_prefix_compare.txt`).

**References (both moved).** `configs/motion_reference.json` `adef05c9` →
**`8a399626`**, from `p2/accept_profile.log` (6/10); the control arm **matches
the archive**, so the move is the flip's, and the trace twin matches the new file
too; gate `fingerprint: matches` with a rate-only FAIL at 6/10 < the 0.75 floor
(the documented branch). `configs/motion_reference_twoline.json` `d87c3cdf` →
**`2246f83c`**, from `p2/twoline_profile.log` (8/10); `190_twoline_gate.sh`
**PASS** at the 0.60 floor. Pre-P41 archives
`logs/p41/motion_reference_{single,twoline}_pre_p41.json`. `189_w7a_chain.sh` was
**not** run.

**The phase-4 canary (A1) is a smoke, and it sits inside the recorded spread.**
One claimed `SKIP_SELFCHECK=1 scripts/accept_policy.sh` run (shipped `moe_v12`,
the fixed pre-v9 supply, ten episodes,
`logs/p41/p4/accept_policy_profile.log`; verdict in
`logs/p41/p4/accept_policy_claim.log`) reads **7/10 = 70 %** at the 0.60 floor -
inside this interface's recorded **5-8/10** (`moe_v11` 8, `moe_v12` 6, P2b 5 and
6, P32 D0 5) - with **2 grip losses + 1 pick-station escape**. The gate
**FAILs on its reason clause only**: `episode 6`'s note (`fruit left the pick
station during the close (1416 mm)`) is outside the recorded baseline's set, and

### P42: the seat is centred and the seat family is **closed in this parameter space** — the pads sit 1.36-4.65 mm off the payload's centre on 20/20 grips, the bounded centring lever's 2.99 mm is **absorbed** because the close re-aims the pose itself every tick, and `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md` becomes the canonical record of the loaded-slide limit (2026-10-26)

Started on the P41-final tree `c2760bf` (clean) with `logs/p42/PREREG.md`
drafted *after* the phase-1 census and before the phase-2 run. Two phases (the
census, the lever) then this close-out; Oracle verdict at the gate **ACCEPT WITH
AMENDMENTS** (five, all landed here). Evidence `logs/p42/`:
`SEAT_CENSUS.md`, `PREREG.md`, `P2_RESULTS.md`, `SIM_LIMIT.md`, `p2/`, `p3/`,
`selfcheck.log`. Nothing is adopted and **no shipped default changed**;
`configs/**` is untouched (**8a399626** / **2246f83c**).

**The census (phase 1): the pads are on the payload.** The default-off instrument
(`FRUIT_SEAT_DIAG=1`, one `[seat]` row per read, five samples per grip at leg
fractions 0.02/0.60/0.99 + the place leg's first ticks) reads, on two 10-grip
corpora (the acceptance and the species-locked pear battery,
`ATTEMPTS=10 SEED=5`): the pads' midpoint is **1.36-4.65 mm** from the fruit's
centre in x/y on **every one of the 20 grips** (median 1.72-2.41 mm), the contact
is **two-sided on 20/20** with the per-pad split `asym` 0.01-0.35 (median
0.06-0.17), and the only systematic axis is **z**: **+69.3..+71.7 mm**, identical
in the placed and escape classes and equal to `_pad_standoff(True, sample)` - the
**commanded** standoff, so "centring z" is the grip-plane question whose D2a form
is measured negative (`logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md`). The jaws cannot be biased by a
finger asymmetry: the second finger joint is a `PhysxMimicJointAPI:rotY` with
`gearing = -1`, `naturalFrequency = 0` and no drive of its own, i.e. a **rigid
1:1-opposed mimic** (`assets/openarm_flat/openarm_flat_deinst.usda:3822-3843`).
**The offset does not predict the escape**: on the pear the four escapes are the
*tightest* seat cluster (1.36-2.06 mm, median 1.72) while the corpus's largest
offset (4.65 mm) **placed**, and the inversions hold for the z term, the force
split and the span-vs-command wedge too. **That rank inversion is noise at
n = 4/6 and is not the claim** - the claim is the **magnitude**: the whole
available correction is ~3-4.6 mm against a **104-276 mm** mid-lift walk, a factor
of **30-60**. What separates the classes is the **walk**, and it separates late:
the payload's hand-frame displacement by the lift's 99 % sample is
**104-276 mm on the pear escapes vs 28-58 mm on the placed legs** (acceptance
30.6-259.4 vs 33.0-57.3), with one pad out of contact on **18/32 escape carry
samples vs 0/48 placed** and the first one-sided sample never at the freeze; at
the first lift sample both classes read the same **2.8-9.9 mm**. Four of the
pear's four escapes lose the grip *inside* the lift (the acceptance's peach
survives at 24.3 mm and goes on the place leg's first ticks).

**The lever (phase 2): `FRUIT_SEAT_CENTRE=<m>`, one pre-close `ik_step`, and the
close removes it.** Registered as one read of `pad_centre() - spawner.position()`
and one command of `clip(-d_xy, +-m)` (x/y only, `m = min(env, 0.020)`, unset =
off and byte-inert) in the window after the catch-up's last tick and before the
close ramp. Measured (pear + acceptance pair, one branch each): the command is
issued on **every grip**, **|c| median 2.99 mm** [2.30, 4.02] pear and **2.91 mm**
[2.50, 3.64] acceptance, the 10 mm clamp **never binding** - and at the freeze
18-22 ticks later the seat is the control's again: paired per grip **+0.00 mm**
median (pear, n = 6: [-0.1, +0.9]) and **+0.01 mm** (acceptance, n = 10:
[-1.2, +0.4]), with pooled medians 1.81 -> 1.83 mm. **The seat family's ceiling in
this tree is therefore ~3 mm of commanded correction against a 100-350 mm walk,
and it does not survive the close.**

**Why: the close is coherent, and the registration read the wrong variable.** The
close's *own* local `coherent` - the flag that gates the per-tick `ik_step` -
reads **True 20/20** grip closes; `PREREG §2` quoted the **carry bookkeeping's**
`self._coherent[arm_name]`, which reads **False 60/60** and is a **different
variable** (it is only ever set `True` on the `pad_error <=
FRUIT_COHERENT_FALLBACK` branch, never reset on the "closing anyway" branches, and
the OpenArm's pre-grasp `pad_error` exceeds 20 mm, so it keeps its `False` for the
session). It is structural, not these runs: `coherent` is set `False` in exactly
two places and **both are guarded by `if openarm: ... else:`**, so with the only
hand this line runs the close can never take the non-coherent branch. What the
close actually issues is an **absolute** `ik_step` on every close tick with
`aim = [frozen_x, fruit_y + vy*lead, z = _pad_standoff]`
(`tasks.py:10064-10074`; the freeze at `tasks.py:9996-10007`): with the shipped
P2b x-lock (`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_CLOSE_LOCK_X=1`) **x is pinned** at the first close
tick, **y is live** and **z is commanded** - so the sub-clause "the close re-aims
live in x" is false too, but y and z alone are enough to overwrite a one-shot. The
residual **1.4-4.6 mm** the freeze reads is **servo following error, not a seating
error**. By the registration's own mandatory evaluability clause ("if any leg
reads `coherent=True` ... that leg is not evaluable") **P1/P2/P3 are not
evaluable**; **P4 PASS** (span 15.7 -> 15.5 s pear, 15.0 -> 15.0 s acceptance);
**P5** as measured (knob unset: structural + the phase-1 control still
`fingerprint: matches` - no re-run spent; the lever arm's own acceptance
fingerprint **DIFFERS** at leg 3, `|v|max` 0.109 vs 0.108 m/s). Falsifiers: F1
fired (phase 1), **F2 fired by its letter, not by its named mechanism** (the arm
executes the command - no `unavailable` row, no clamp binding - and the *close*
removes it; F2 named the reach boundary), F3 clear (40/40 `notes=[]`), F4 clear
(the catch-up residuals are the shipped 5.6-6.0 mm on all 40 attempts), **F5
fired** on the pear.

**No count from this phase is a rate, and there is no bare 6/10 -> 7/10.** The
pear reads 6/10 (left 2/6, right 4/4, 4 cnp) against 7/10 (left **1/4**, right
6/6, 3 cnp) - the **left attempt count moved 6 -> 4**, the first divergence is
attempt 5's *selected fruit* (control pear A lane 0, lever pear B lane 1), so F5
makes the class endpoint a report. The acceptance is 6/10 in **both** arms (left
1/5, right 5/5, span 15.0 s in both) but on **two different attractors** (the
fingerprint line above), and its escapes are attempts 0/1/3/9 vs 1/2/3/9. The
phase's sharpest single row is a class-sensitivity fact, not a lever effect: the
*same* peach reads a freeze seat of 2.63 mm (control 2.62, +0.01) and lifts
**27.5 mm** of `slip_max` in the lever run against **266.2 mm** (cnp) in the
control - i.e. a fully re-aimed 3.5 mm jog still changes the close's *approach
history* enough to flip that attempt, and the kiwi at attempt 2 flips the other
way.
