### P43: the arm park becomes the **direct env's default** (right-arm carried 20/54 -> 0/56, placed 32/54 -> 53/56, 5/5 runs) after re-measuring it on the P41 9.8-9.9 N grip profile — one shipped change, scoped to `presentation="direct"`, with `FRUIT_ARM_PARK=ready` as the escape hatch and the whole direct interface re-baselined; the phase-2 rate lever (nearest-above-floor) and the loop's RTC/VLASH cell are both measured **not adopted** (2026-10-26)

**What ships.** `FRUIT_ARM_PARK=back` is the **`direct` presentation's default**.
The resolution is one module function (`rl_env.resolve_arm_park`):
`_park_default = "back" if presentation == "direct" else ""`, an explicit env
value wins everywhere, `=ready` restores the shipped pose, and `handoff`
resolves to **no park** so it cannot raise (the guard for a *named* park on a
non-direct presentation is unchanged). No `configs/` file moved and no motion
reference was re-recorded.

**The numbers of record** (`logs/p43/P3_RESULTS.md`, batch 4423 s = 73.7 min,
one claim, no wedge; N = 5 runs x 15 episodes per arm, seeds 77/101/202/303/404,
policy seed 11, interleaved A-then-B, `moe_v13s` `61da390a` on **both** arms, the
P35/P36/P37 patch scenario verbatim, `ACQ`/`CARRY`/`PARK`/`RESET_ALIGN` diags on
both arms):

* right-arm carried **20/54 = 0.370 -> 0/56 = 0.000**, exact two-sided Fisher
  **p = 7.31e-08**;
* right-arm placed **32/54 = 0.593 -> 53/56 = 0.946**, delta **+0.354**
  (bar >= -0.10), Fisher **p = 7.75e-06**, Newcombe one-sided 95 % lower bound
  **+0.228**; species- and diameter-tertile-standardised deltas **+0.349 /
  +0.355** (coverage 1.00);
* run level **B > A in 5/5** (one-sided sign **p = 0.0312**; MH OR 13.03,
  CMH chi2 18.92, p = 1.36e-05);
* pooled **33/75 = 44.0 % -> 53/75 = 70.7 %** — **a report, never a test** —
  with the arm-standardised forms **0.320 -> 0.473** (50/50) and 0.440 -> 0.681
  (A's own 0.720 right mix);
* left **1/21 -> 0/19**, cycle **+0.2 %** (pooled median 1826 -> 1830 ticks;
  right arm only -0.9 %), **no new failure reason** (both arms the same three
  normalised reason sets).

**The Oracle's corrections (Gate 3), which the documents carry verbatim.**
(1) **P4 is "not failed", not "PASS"**: 1/21 -> 0/19 clears the -0.05 bar by
**0.0024 = one episode**, which is inside the no-op noise P36 measured on the
same guard (0.050 vs 0.119); the informative read is the left's **carried 20 ->
18** — the built-in no-op, since `configs/arm_parks.json` has a **left-only**
vector and the left-arm episodes never move. (2) **P1 and P2 are one 3-way
outcome counted twice** (`placed = n - carried - no-grasp`): "+0.354 placed,
p = 7e-8 carried" is **one count**, and the independent legs are **P7 / P8 / P5
/ P6**; because **5/5 at five runs has p = 0.031 as its minimum attainable**,
P7 is the design's **ceiling**, not a strong standalone result. (3) **"0 carried"
is 0/56** — `<= ~5 %` at 95 % by the rule of three — and **2 residual
`force_min = 0` legs survive** (16 -> 2, ~8x reduced, **not deleted**). (4) the
band census's **1364 calls are ~56 clustered episodes**, i.e. **"0 in 56
episodes"**, not 1364 independent reads. (5) **"94.6 %" is one draw of a
non-reproducible loop** (rendered frames; CI ~0.85-0.99), not a rate. (6) the
**re-baseline rule** below.

**The check** (P8, read before any outcome): the park arm holds the pose the
reset **achieved** **56/56** on both reads (M1-held, and M1-applied against the
0.088 rad settle), **M2a 56/56**, band census **0/1364 fully hidden in 56
episodes**; the control reads M1-held 54/54, shipped-pose negative 54/54, M2a
0/54 and **903/1340 = 67.4 %** fully hidden — the pre-treatment state
reproduced. The 0.088 rad achieved-vs-commanded residual is the
`teleport_joints` settle property (the shipped `ready` reset sits 0.037 from
*its* own command), which is why the gate is written against the achieved pose.
M2b (`rel >= 0.85`) stays a report (39/56 = 69.6 %; its denominator is a running
`px*d^2` maximum and the batch's masks are 20-192 px).

**The mechanism** is the W8-B loaded slide, on the right: `force_min = 0`
(payload out) **16/53 -> 2/55**, `clean_slip > 50 mm` **15/53 -> 2/55**, the
retained pinch **9.31 N (A, n = 37) / 9.74 N (B, n = 53)** against the pre-P41
direct corpus's **3.57 N** median, and the left (no park vector) unchanged
(16/21 -> 15/19 lost legs, `clean_slip` median 268.5 -> 253.8 mm). The channel is
the **image** (P36's 2x2: image p = 8.8e-15, proprio p = 0.687); *which* image
statistic remains unseparated.

**The scope, and what the flip costs.** Direct presentation only: the canary
(`scripts/60_eval_policy.py`) never constructs `SortingRLEnv`, so
`moe_v12` + park is **untested** and has no deployment path. The flip
**re-baselines the direct interface** — every direct/policy number quoted before
this entry (P33, W7-C, W8-A, R9, P35, P36, P37, P38, P43-p2's F5 pair) is a
**pre-park** number, and **to reproduce any of them set `FRUIT_ARM_PARK=ready`**;
park/no-park stores must not be mixed (P37's transfer confound). `121`/`136`/
`127`/`130`/`195` and the `110`-driven workflows **silently re-baseline**. **No
motion reference was re-recorded**: the scripted gate never imports `rl_env`, so
`fingerprint: matches` is an **import guard** on this change — stated as the
P38-M4-style near-tautology it is, not as evidence about the park.

**A1 — the state is named in every log and every store.** (i) `[rl] env ready:`
now prints `park=back(default)` / `park=ready(explicit)` / `park=ready(shipped)`;
(ii) the manifest's `arm_park` block gains **`defaulted: true|false`** (absent =
pre-P43), so a defaulted store, an explicit `=back` arm and a pre-P43 store are
distinguishable; (iii) the `[park]` row prints the name, the origin **and the
per-arm resolution** — `park=back(default)[left:back,right:ready]` — because the

config's vector is left-only) and the old row invited the opposite reading. The
`[park]` token stays one whitespace-free field, so the pinned P35/P43 parsers

**The two negatives that ride the same commit.** (1) **L1 — the
nearest-above-floor selector is scoped and NOT adopted.** The scope is the

**0.32-0.73 s** in **4/4** pairs, the 2 ms mechanism reads **1.958 s predicted
vs 1.960 s measured** on the seeded attempt (convert factor 1.0, not the
registered 0.6), and the descent is the only segment that moves — but `placed`

slot to `no eligible fruit`, the pear's left cnp rose 4 -> 5, and the mechanism's

and the flip stays `"0"`. The machinery ships, so `=1` reproduces the treatment
byte-identically with no code change; the reopen condition is a supply whose
floored set carries two candidates on >= 50 % of attempts. (2) **L2 — the loop's
pause is 10.7 % and there is no loop lever.** One instrumented run

in `control_ms` 9.2 → 32.7 ms, and its other-checkpoint rate record is
null-to-negative).

### P44 phase 2: the speed cells are the cap arithmetic, the grip guard is the acquisition class, nothing adopted

**The cells.** Three default-off knobs (`tasks.py`, the `speed_cell_defaults()`
block + seven caps / ten read sites): `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.52` (place `v_max`
0.35 -> 0.52, `a_max` left at 1.089 - inside the census's 0.61 m/s ceiling),
`FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=1` (dwell 20 -> 0, pad/finger 3 -> 2), `FRUIT_SPEED_LIFT=0.36`
(lift 0.30/1.0 -> 0.36/1.9) and `FRUIT_SPEED_ALL=1` (S13, the union). Each sets
only the *default string* of an existing per-leg override. **A defect the cell
found:** `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PLACE_VMAX` was `min()`'d against `FRUIT_CARRY_VMAX`
(0.38), so 0.52 would have silently resolved to 0.38 (-0.42 s, not -1.09 s); the
place branch now assigns its own cap - byte-identical for every recorded
configuration (the shipped 0.35 is below 0.38 and no driver sets
`FRUIT_CARRY_VMAX`). Offline contract pinned by the new selfcheck leg
`scripts/225_p44_speed_selftest.py`; `rl_env.py` `TASKS_MD5` follows
(`a1b3d673` -> `b6de439c`, metadata only); `selfcheck.sh` **PASS 0 failures**.
**Default off proven four ways** (the acceptance seed 5 **387/387** `[fruit]`
lines vs `logs/p43/p2/post_revert_accept_unset.log`, seed 6 **388/388** vs
`r_accept_A_s6`, the pear **388/388** vs `d0_pear_A_s5` minus its `[bed*]` rows,
and the two-line `190` **fingerprint: matches** + the single-arm `105`
**fingerprint: matches**).

**The measurements** (11 runs, arms interleaved, one instrumentation set on every

### P44 phase 2 amend: S3-v is the clean lift cell, the release floor is 130 ticks, and the diags are provably run-neutral

**The Oracle's correction, measured.** Three runs added/exchanged on the same
tree with **existing knobs only, no `src/` edit** (`logs/p44/p2/amend_*`, §9 of
`logs/p44/P2_RESULTS.md`): **S1** re-run through `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PLACE_VMAX=0.52`,
**S3-v** = `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_LIFT_VMAX=0.37` with **`a_max` untouched at 1.0**, and
**S2** = the release clock's **floor** form (`FRUIT_RELEASE_DWELL=0`,
`..._PAD_HOLD=1`, `..._FINGER_HOLD=1`). **The instruments are part of the
measurement and are ceiling-proven neutral**: the core stream (`[run] attempt` +
`[stats]` + `[cycle]` + `[motion]` + `[supply]`) is **row-identical** for
phase-2 C vs `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1` C (83 rows), phase-2 S1 vs `CARRY_DIAG` S1
(81), and `CARRY_DIAG` C vs `+RELEASE_DEBUG +PLACE_TRACE` C (83), so **S1
reproduces the first pass exactly** (14.20 s/attempt, `diverted=1`).

**E1 as the per-leg tick delta** (the amend's primary): S1's `place0/place1` lose
**135.4 / 64.2 ticks** (-1.13 / -0.53 s) with its lift at -3.6; **S3-v's
`grasp_lift` loses 29.4 ticks (-0.245 s)** with the place legs at -3.6/-1.4
(untouched, branch distances). **`a` staying at 1.0 is right**: the phase-2 S3
(0.36 + `a` 1.9) measured `lift` 1.59 s against S3-v's **1.57 s** - the extra
acceleration buys **0.00 s** and only spends transient (its worst `grasp_lift`
cone 1.42x against S3-v's 1.19x). **The release floor is real and the amendment's
arithmetic is confirmed**: S2's `release` block reads **1.08 s = 130 ticks**
against the control's 2.04 s, i.e. the Oracle's **132-tick / 1.10 s floor to 2
ticks**, so the census's "3 -> 1 = -1.02 s" over-states the clock (the floor caps
it near -0.95 s; the measured saving is **-0.96 s**, and s/attempt 15.00 -> 14.00).
The holds are the ramps' opening **rates** (a 40-step pad ramp and a 16-step
finger ramp times the hold), which is why the saving is bounded.

**E4 on the amended instruments** (`CARRY_DIAG=1` on every arm; the gate is the
new grip row and `force_min == 0`; `clean_slip_max` arm-vs-control only):
**no arm adds a lost leg** (C **7**, S1 **7**, S3-v **5**, S2 **5**), and
**S3-v draws no grip row at all** - it is the only single cell that passes the
gate. The residue the cells leave is a live `clean_slip_max` of **8.8-17.7 mm on
one surviving leg each** (the control's clean legs read 0.1 mm), the largest
S1's `grasp_lift` (17.7 mm at `force_min` 7.4 N) - a transient, not a loss. S2's
`--strict-cone` 5.25x outlier is the **empty-hand flail on the never-held
attempt** (in-hand 5.007 m/s), not a loaded grip. **`--strict-cone` fails on the
control too** (5 legs, worst 1.53x), so it is not an absolute gate here: the
counts read C 5 / S1 3 / **S3-v 7 (max 1.19x)** / S2 4 - the faster lift buys a
narrower magnitude for a **broader** count (the take-off transient is a larger
share of every leg), which is the lift cell's measured cost. **No PASS is claimed
on any reference**: every moved arm's fingerprint differs by construction; C
matches. **F4 verified, not inferred**: with `FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE=1` on both F
arms, **every payload that reached the release landed on the belt** (C 6/6, S2
**7/7**, release bottom 47-67 mm, impact -0.92..-0.81 m/s, bounce <= 6 mm, settle
467-1000 ms), and the off-belt traces read `release_bottom = -184 mm`,
`impact = 0.00` - lost **upstream**, never at the release. Pins unchanged
(`tasks.py` **`b6de439c`**, `rl_env.py` **`93e35ef7`**); new evidence
`logs/p44/p2/{amend_E_*,amend_F_*,run_amend*.sh,amend_report.py,amend_table.txt,amend_gates.txt}`.
**Nothing adopted**; S3-v is named the amended phase's best cell (no new row,

### P45 phase 1/2: a lighter fruit makes the walk worse and leaves the fling alone - the mass is not the speed term (2026-10-27)

Owner: "速度快甩飞是不是因为果蔬质量大的缘故 是否可以先大幅减小果蔬质量 先以提速尝试为主" + a frontier retry.

`FRUIT_MASS_SCALE=<x>` (default off, a named **physics** change): `meshes.mass_scale()`
parsed once at import (hard errors on 0/negative/inf/nan), applied at the **two**
mass sites in `fruits.py` (the pool build and the recycle `rescale`), behind
`if scale != 1.0` so unset skips the multiply; inertia needs no second attribute
(no fruit authors `diagonalInertia`; PhysX derives it), the sizes/meshes stay
fixed, one build banner. Battery (5 arms x acceptance + pear, `CARRY_DIAG` +
`RELEASE_DEBUG` + `CYCLE_REPORT` on every arm): acceptance **C 6, M50 6/9, M25
4/10, M50S 5, M25S 5**; pear **C 6, M50 7, M25 7, M50S 7, M25S 6**. The speed is
entirely the P44 cells (15.0 -> 13.4-13.5 s/attempt; the mass contributes
0.0-0.1 s), so **the mass buys nothing**.

**The census's fling prediction was wrong, and the measurement says why**: the
release is a **displacement-controlled pad ramp**, not a fixed impulse, so
`v = J/m` does not apply - the in-hand release peak is **0.93-1.08x** of the
control at 0.25x mass. What *worsens* is the **walk**, on the mixed pool only:
at 0.25x the acceptance's escape legs go **7/20 -> 12/20**, its zero-force
(loaded-slide) legs **7/20 -> 13/20**, `clean_slip_max` p50 **0.1 -> 228 mm** -
the loaded slide is not mass-starved (4-5 N on one face while the payload walks),
so less mass gives the contact less to resist; the single-class pear reads
*better* than a control that lost 8/20 legs - the branch, not the mass. At a
fixed size 0.25x is 205-225 kg/m3 (cork) - **the cell can never ship**; the
physical equivalent is a smaller real fruit, a new scenario.

**Frontier** (`logs/p45/FRONTIER.md`, the live survey succeeded on the third
attempt done directly after the tool failed twice): ForceDelta-VLA verified
against the abstract (a correction-distillation from a frozen teacher's paired
force-conditioned/agnostic predictions, a separate delay-correction target,
asynchronous schedule replay with cached context, a lightweight policy adjusting
the reference from recent force history **without regenerating chunks**; 82.2 %
vs 54.4 %, the Stage-1 teacher 70.6 %, ~26 % lower peak contact force); the ICLR
2026 *time-optimal execution of action-chunk policies*; the delta robots'
>100-200 picks/min as vendor claims on a different kinematics; and **no measured
study of a light payload being flung out of a parallel jaw**. The transferable
shape is the **bounded force-derived pose residual between reference updates**
(the named remedy for the P44 speed cells), not the distillation.

Pins: `fruits.py`/`meshes.py` (the P45 faces), `scripts/227_p45_mass_selftest.py`
(a selfcheck leg), the cells default off, `configs/` untouched; evidence
`logs/p45/{MASS_CENSUS,FRONTIER,PREREG_DRAFT,P2_RESULTS}.md`, `p2/`.

### P46 phase 1: the two-line speed union does not replicate at a fresh seed - the acquisition class is the cost (2026-10-27)

The P44 two-line positive (8/10 at 9.8 -> 8.7 s/attempt, +12 % placed/min) was one
seed. P46 pre-registered a **2-seed** confirmation before running and did it with
the existing knobs only. Seed 5 is a P44 replay (C 453/453 and U 446/446 rows
identical to P44) and reproduces: placed 8 -> 8, -1.05 s/attempt, 4.90 -> 5.49
placed/min. **Seed 6, the fresh draw, loses two placements** (9 -> 7) for -0.47
s/attempt and 5.41 -> 4.42 placed/min. The guard is clean (0 held-then-lost rows,
held >50 mm slip 0/0, clean_slip p50 0.00-0.05 mm; the s6 force_min==0 legs are
never-held, contacts@onset 0, pads closing on air 52-65 mm) and the landing is

-> no flip**, the union and the single-arm cells stay opt-in. The lesson: the

branches, and the moving class is the **pre-contact acquisition** - so a speed

### P47 phase 1: the "closing anyway" row is a standing property, and the real pre-close discriminator is the catch-up residual - the guard is not run (2026-10-27)

The census of 317 closes (shipped + P44 + P45 + P46 corpora) settles the lever
before it was built: the `... mm from the fruit; closing anyway` row fires on
**317/317** closes with a **7 mm band** = the hover clearance (70 mm nominal,
`hover + pad_lift`) measured **against the station, before the hover and the
descent**; its value carries no outcome information (Fisher p = 0.61) and the
axis sibling is dead (0/317). The fallback it names is unreachable
(`pad_error > 20 mm` always true -> `self._coherent[arm]` never set, 0/317 - a
dead code path). **The live pre-close error does separate the classes and is
already printed**: `[task] dynamic catch-up: residual` above its 6 mm tolerance
reads **8/8 no-grasp** vs **11/309 = 3.6 %** below (p = 3.3e-11), but it explains
only **42 %** of the class and its failing values are **220-481 mm** - a
hand-over-timing failure, not a distance-to-close. The registered 35 mm/40 tick
guard was predicted to fire on **2.5 %** of closes and convert **~0**, so the
battery was not spent (the PREREG keeps the prediction). The named next lever:
the hand-over timing/selection (a target 2.4x the catch-up's reach budget away)
and the 11 converged close losses. Evidence `logs/p47/{ACQ_CENSUS,PREREG}.md`.

### P48 phase 1: the acquisition misses are the delivered-x tail, not the hand-over timing - both levers catch 0/4 (2026-10-27)

The catch-up residual's >6 mm band is 8/8 no-grasp vs 3.6 % below
(p = 3.3e-11) and the 6.0 -> 219.6 mm band is empty. The four events share the
**x tail**: |x| >= 0.390 is 6/6 failed (p = 2.1e-11 vs 2/311), >= 0.38 is 8 rows
with 0 placed, within kiwi 8/8 vs 2/27 (p = 1.9e-06); 3/4 are kiwis at
x 0.391-0.397, i.e. 0.8-6.9 mm past the 0.39 m clean lateral band, while the arm
recovered only 20-51 mm of the 200 mm the fruit moved; the fourth (480.6 mm) is
the corpus's only cross-belt displacement (379 mm drift) - a supply event. The
hand-over lead is a constant 0.189 m on all 317 attempts (it cannot
discriminate); the reach budget is 200 ticks x 1.0 mm = 200 mm and the residuals
are 1.10/1.23/1.26/2.40x it (P47's 2.4x was the maximum, on the non-timing
event). Both registered levers catch 0/4 (the lead 0.03 -> 0.20 lifts the floor
to 0.569 m against a dy0 max of 0.570 for +1.42 s/attempt; the 400-tick catch-up
helps only the displaced fruit and worsens the other three by ~200 mm), so the
battery was not spent. The 11 converged losses are the closed grip class (the
loaded slide). The named next lever is a scripted selector x-ceiling (x > 0.39),
plus the supply-displacement event. Evidence `logs/p48/{HANDOVER_CENSUS,PREREG}.md`.

### P49 phase 1: the selector's x-ceiling refuses nothing - the failing x is the post-selection drift (2026-10-27)

The `[bed-sel]` census across the shipped / P44 / P46 corpora: the chosen fruit's
x never exceeds **0.38** (max 0.3653-0.3802), so a ceiling at 0.39/0.40/0.42
refuses **0 of 40** selections at every threshold - inert by construction, because
the P48 failures' x (0.391-0.397) is the **drifted x at the close**, measured
after the selection. The drift is P38's per-instance release offset (delivered x =
spawn x + offset(instance)). A binding ceiling would also cost: a usable set of 1
in 25/40 selections means a skip, and the 14/40 with two substitute at +1.08 to
+2.08 s. The named next lever is P38b's per-instance release-offset compensation
at respawn, not a selection rule. Evidence `logs/p49/{SELECT_CENSUS,PREREG}.md`.

### P50 phase 2: the per-pool release-offset compensation works at the cell level (8/96 -> 0/96) and the acceptance's count gate fails, so it is NOT adopted (2026-10-27)

The lever P49 named was implemented (default off) and run: `FRUIT_RELEASE_OFFSET=1`
+ `FRUIT_RELEASE_OFFSET_TABLE=<pool table>` shifts the value `respawn` already drew
(`x_spawn = planned - offset(instance)/1000`), so the delivered x lands back on the
planned one and the **draw sequence is untouched**. Seven claimed runs
(`logs/p50/p2/`, ~30 min, one claim each, all exit 0), no commit, no existing
`configs/` file touched.

**The tables are per pool because the offset is a per-instance constant, not a
(species, diameter) function** (phase 1). `configs/release_offsets_accept_s5.json`
(16 instances, seed 5) carries the pre-registered rule: the live mean per instance,
and the two rollers' **minimax midpoint** - kiwi|55.8 **+44.80** (mid of +34.98 /
+54.63) and strawberry|37.2 **-28.91** (mid of -35.73 / -22.10). The pear table is
**identity** by design (its offsets are -3.33..+2.69 mm, no tail), i.e. the phase's
inertness control. Each run proves its own coverage: the banner reads
`instances=16/16`.

**P1 (the powered endpoint) passes decisively**: the compensated isolated probe
delivers **0/96 cells outside [0.180, 0.390]** (min 0.1932, max 0.3785,
pass-to-pass spread 0.00 mm) against the control's **8/96** (min 0.1730, max 0.4131
- the four pre-registered cells x 2 passes: kiwi idx 02 @0.36 0.3998, kiwi idx 13
@0.36 0.4131, strawberry idx 05 @0.20 0.1780, orange idx 10 @0.20 0.1730).
**The live line confirms it is the same draws**: 65 vs 65 attributed releases with a
**bit-identical planned-x sequence (65/65)** while the residual falls from
**-35.73..+54.63 mm to -9.84..+9.83 mm** (p50 |.| 5.45 -> 0.00, max 9.84 = the
kiwi's two modes either side of the midpoint). The compensation **re-selects modes**:
the strawberry collapses (spread 13.63 -> 0.25 mm) and tomato idx 06 becomes newly
bimodal (0.03 -> 7.05 mm, one mode exactly on the table); F1's 20 mm bar is not
crossed (max 19.67 mm) but by 0.33 mm only. No clamp was needed: the table's
excursion over `U(0.20, 0.36)` is **0.1552..0.3889 m** against a belt of 0.11-0.57 m
(45 mm to the near edge), and the run's actual spawns were 0.1642..0.3888 m.

**P3 is the gate that fails, and it is a count in a moved branch** (AGENTS section
2): the acceptance reads **C 6/10 at 15.0 s/attempt vs O 4/10 at 15.1 s/attempt**

### P51 phase 1: the speed cells' cost is the closed grip class, not the tail - the speed arc closes (2026-10-27)

The hypothesis (the speed cost is P48's x tail, so P50's compensation + the speed
would be class-clean) fails its offline map: of the 5 cell-attributable acquisition
events, **1 is tail and 4 are mid-band** (x 0.22-0.38) with a **converged close**
(catch-up residual 5.5-6.0 mm, inside the 6 mm tolerance) - the closed grip/hold
class. So `O + U` cannot be class-clean and the battery was not spent. The speed
gain stands separately (union -1.45 s/attempt; two-line -0.76 pooled, -10.7 % on
the seed-5 branch); its count cost is branch-draw cnp (single arm) and converged
closes (two-line). No remaining lever on the acquisition/tail side: the distance
guard, the hand-over timing, the x-ceiling and the combination were all refuted by
measurement, the speed is real, and its cost is the closed grip class - a future
adoption must be argued on the time with the cost named as the documented class.

### P52: the model lane - the policy-side speed is capped at ~3-5 %, the two success hypotheses die offline (2026-10-28)

Frontier gate: RoboPace (arXiv 2610.09696, a dual-arm OpenArm) - the same chunks at
10/30/50 Hz read 22/50 / ref / 4/50, kinematic-only RACE-style 1/50, contact-gated
32/50 at half the slow arm's time: the trade-off is speed AT CONTACT, and 1.67x
uniform costs 84 % of the success. This tree's policy does not own the cycle: the
policy phase is 14.2 % of a placed episode (256/1800 ticks), so a 1.5x re-timing is
worth <= 4.8 %, and with the gate firing on 44.1 % of decisions the measured gain is
-48.1 ticks = -2.7 % (n = 23, 17/23 negative) - the arithmetic to the tick, and the
-8 % bar was unreachable. FRUIT_POLICY_TIME_SCALE / _RETIME_GATE stay default off.
Two success hypotheses died offline: the reached-state supervision is not a defect
(0/581455 labels out of range, HOLD residual 0.84/0.01 mm; the defect is the policy's
own emissions: 13.1 % of joint steps out of range on 74.3 % of ticks, a 19.3 mm p50
dither), and PACE dies structurally (the chunks are noise: 0/60 below 0.30 rad/s, so
h = 16 everywhere; 64 -> 16 decisions, wall -12 %, sim/placements unchanged; the
policy's phase is the belt-arrival wait). Corrections: the decisions/episode is
53-84 (not 246-259 - a tick count), the latency bound is h <= 7 (not 13), and the
intra-chunk rates were 4x understated. Named next: the action-hold (more ticks per
action) + a joint clamp - a success-first cell.

Recorded with `scripts/121_policy_video.py` (`moe_v13s` `61da390a`, the patch

not placed**. The clips: `logs/p54/video_acq_on/` and `logs/p54/video_acq_off/`
(each `observer.mp4`, `head.mp4`, `gripper.mp4`, `side_by_side.mp4` + a

observer shows the 2-D |jaw-fruit| trigger quantity and the outcome), not a rate -
the rate is P54's N = 3 x 15 (16/45 vs 34/45).

### P55: the direct interface's live feeder (the "one burst per episode" fix)

Observed from the P54 continuous video: the fruit arrives in **one burst per
episode**. The cause is structural, not a recording artifact: the direct env's
**only** `spawner.update` site was the reset's target-selection loop
(`rl_env.py:2200`), so the supply is built at `reset` and then frozen - the belt
drains, the episode ends, the next reset re-feeds. `FRUIT_DIRECT_FEED=1`
(default **off**) runs the spawner's own absolute schedule every `advance`, so the
belt stays stocked and the policy works back-to-back. Two integration defects
surfaced and were fixed: (1) the first live update hit
`KeyError: 1` in `_pick_recyclable -> position` because the direct pool can gain
samples after the env's setup `refresh_rigids`; the feeder now does a **one-shot
`refresh_rigids()`** before its first update, and (2) a per-tick `KeyError` guard
remains as a backstop (it printed once before the refresh fix, zero times after).
Smokes: 2 and 3 episodes ran clean; the 12-episode recording
(`logs/p54/video_fed/`, 171 s side-by-side, seed 77, capture-every 2) reads
**right 7/8, left 0/4, pooled 7/12 = 58.3 %** against the unfed 12-episode run's
8/12 = 66.7 % - a **different branch** (the fed stream is pears/tomatoes/kiwis
vs apples/peaches/oranges), so the counts are not a rate comparison (AGENTS §2).
The knob stays **default off**: its own A/B (fed vs unfed, the same seeds) is the
named next measurement.

### P56: the continuous scenario is the episode boundary, and the feed round is supply-load-bearing

The owner's "the fruit comes in waves" (and "the candidate-fruit planning was
for continuous conveying and sorting") is **structural**, not a recording
artifact. The census (`logs/p56/CENSUS.txt`) separates the three things:

* **the belt and the pool are never rebuilt** - `create_pool()`/`prime()` are
  `__init__`-only, so the world is already continuous;
* the only `spawner.update` site was the reset's selection loop, so the
  **release schedule** and the **episode** are the discontinuous part;
* the belt is **already stocked** at every selection (farthest-upstream `y` =
  0.491-0.675 m against `spawn_y` 0.68 = **72-99 %**), and the P55 live feeder
  moves that median only **+11 mm** while costing **+11.1 % wall** (452.7 vs
  407.5 s).

So the wave is the **episode boundary**: the inter-attempt gap reads **exactly
140 ticks = 1.167 s** (30 feed + 3x30 teleport + 20 settle) = **6.4-6.7 %** of
the span in both runs, with **0/11 starvation**. The larger wait is the
**arrival** (2.07-2.13 s = 13.5-14.4 % of the cycle), which continuity does not
touch - so the mode's sim ceiling is **2.97-4.45 %** of a pick (the arm-switch
rate 55-64 %).

P56 implemented the multi-pick episode (`FRUIT_DIRECT_CONTINUOUS=<n>`, default
**off**, direct + `ablate=none` only, **implies** `FRUIT_DIRECT_FEED=1`):
`reset` split into its run-level half and `_begin_pick`, `_finalize` continues
via `_begin_next_pick` (same `select_target`, `protected` cleared, the recorder's
index incremented, the reward/outcome accumulated), `[cont]` rows, and the
`[bed-sel]`/`[grasp]` census wired into the direct env. Two implementation
deviations are recorded (`logs/p56/PREREG_A1.md`): the design's literal split
measured **110 ticks/transition** (`p0/C3_literal_split.log`) so the reduced
continuation setup is used (**50** same-arm / **80** arm-switch), and the
design's "end on `None`" killed a 3-pick run (`p0/C3_norec.log`), replaced by the
reset's own 40x30-tick bound with a printed wait round.

The battery (seed 77, `logs/p56/p2/`; A = `--episodes 15` vs B = `--episodes 1`
with `FRUIT_DIRECT_CONTINUOUS=15`) reads gap A **140x14** vs B **[50, 80x9,
110x4] (med 80, max 110)** = **-53.6 ticks = -0.45 s = 2.7 %** of a pick - and
**8/14 transitions starved**: the 30-tick feed round the mode removes is
**supply-load-bearing**. The mechanism is the catch floor **0.399 m** against the
queue interlock's edge `pick_y+0.45` with `FRUIT_QUEUE_MAX=6`, which leaves a
**5 cm** catchable sliver: a 15 s pick drains it and the next selection reads
`window=0` with `on_belt=8` (the P33 aperture class, now measured on the direct
line). Placed A **11/15 (2.67/min)** vs B **8/15 (2.00/min)** is a **different
branch** (right 10/10 vs 8/9, left 1/5 vs 0/6) and carries no rate claim. P1
FAILs on its max (the median sits *at* the 80 bar), P3 FAILs (73.3 % < 90 %; the
control itself 80 %), **P6 fails as registered** - but the **shipped** line's own
first-tick pose is outside the same 0.011 rad bar on **14/15**, so the bar is the
finding and the continuation's two right-arm outliers (0.0330/0.0217) are
unseparated; P4/P5 PASS (no new reason; 15 distinct indices and 15 npz files in both
stores, `ticks_total == sum`). By F1 the P2/P3/P4 readings are void; **nothing is
adopted** and seeds 101/202 were not spent. No-harm: `--ablate scripted` **44/44
lines byte-identical** across the pre-edit, measured and final trees; the policy
pair's 1-tick delta is reproduced *within* one tree; selfcheck PASS.

### P57 phase 1: the "wave" was the feeder's scope gate

The direct line's supply arrived in **one burst per policy phase** because
`FruitSpawner.update` - the only release clock - ran only inside
`SortingRLEnv.advance` (the ~2-3 s policy phase) and the reset's selection loop.
The primitive phase (~12-13 s of a ~15 s pick) never pumped it, so
`_next_release` fell **12-16 s behind**, the late backlog was placed at its
virtual position and every slot past the station was **skipped**: measured
`lag=+15.72`, `skipped` 2 -> **50** over 15 picks
(`logs/p56/p3/Q12_s77.log`). The mid-attempt pump existed all along
(`FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE=1` -> `_feed_tick` on every control tick of every phase) but
resolved through `_prepared_scope()`, which is `False` when `not scripted` - right
for the pre-pose/return levers (a `reset()` discards a pre-positioned hand), wrong
for a supply clock. The fix is a new `_feed_scope()` = "no `CoopSession`"
(`tasks.py` `b6de439c` -> `c7eef701`; the two-line installs its own `feed_pump`),
leaving `_prepared_scope` untouched. With `FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE` unset the shipped
path is byte-unchanged (`0 and ...` in both trees). Measured on the same 15-pick
episode: lag **-0.11..-1.64 s** (was +11.9..+15.7), `skipped` 2 -> **3** (was 50),
`on_belt` **9-13 (median 12)** vs 5-6, `window=0` at **2/16 selections** vs 8/14
transitions, gaps [50x4, 80x8, 82, 110x2, 230] vs [50, 80x9, 110x4], placed 7/15
(right **7/7**, left 0/8 - the closed `cnp` class) vs 8/15 (right 8/9, left 0/6):
different branches, no rate claim. The **catchable band is still ~0.15 m**, so a
selection can still read `window=0` - the supply clock is now correct, the
aperture is not.

### P57 phase 2: the release interlock counted the wrong region

`_queue_depth()` counts `[pick_y - 0.05, pick_y + 0.45]` - the **station window**.
With the dynamic catch's 0.399 m floor, everything the window counts is already
too close or past, so six bodies "south" of the floor hold the release shut while
the 0.281 m segment the selector draws from is empty. The census names it
(`logs/p57/cad_s77.log` attempt 3: nine of eleven bodies at along -0.581..+0.068,
four usable at +0.464..+0.611). The bed had already solved this
(`_bed_stock_depth`, `logs/p32/60_probe_nocap.log`); the single-file schedules had
no equivalent. `FRUIT_SUPPLY_BAND_INTERLOCK=1` (+ `FRUIT_SUPPLY_BAND_MAX=3`) paces
them on `_approach_depth()` with a density-preserving depth ceiling through two
new helpers used at both release sites; off = the shipped rule byte-for-byte
(selfcheck PASS, `211` 115 checks). Measured on the same 15-pick episode as P57
phase 1: `admitted` 3-6 in the band, `window=0` at **1/16** selections (phase 1:
2/16, P56: 8/14 transitions), longest gap **110** (was 230), placed **11/15**
(right **10/10**, left 1/5) - a different branch, no rate claim. The 12-pick video
run reads 9/12 (right 7/7, left 2/5) with no starvation gap. Still true: the
catchable segment is 0.281 m against the 1.8 m a pick consumes, so 1-2 picks in
16 can still find nothing - station geometry is the remaining lever, not supply.
Both knobs default off; no `configs/` change.

### P58: the direct supply profile - the clock pair plus the band interlock at cap 4

The owner's second requirement ("fruit must appear continuously, not in bursts or
on a timed refresh") is now a **shipped default for the `direct` presentation
only**: `FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE`, `FRUIT_SUPPLY_BAND_INTERLOCK` (+
`FRUIT_SUPPLY_BAND_MAX=4`) and `FRUIT_DIRECT_FEED` resolve on when
`presentation == "direct"`, an explicit environment value winning;
`FRUIT_DIRECT_CONTINUOUS` stays **0** (opt-in `--continuous N`). The mechanism is
in P57's entry (the clock ran only inside the policy phase, so the schedule fell
12-16 s behind and skipped 50 slots) and P58 adds the measurement + the scoping.

**Four cells, 3 seeds x 15 picks, the shipped per-pick interface** (`window`
mean / `==1` / starved rounds `sel_gap>=169` / final `skipped` / `on_belt` /
wall s/pick): control **2.57 / 4/45 / 0/42** (the 0 is bought by the reset's
re-stock) **/ 104-107 / 5.2 / 29.66**; A' cap 3 **2.02 / 12/45 / 1/42 / 41-36-39
/ 9.2 / 34.07**; **A'' cap 4 2.38 / 9/45 / 0/42 / 8-4-9 / 11 / 35.40**; A'''
interlock off **2.20 / 12/45 / 5/42 (169/380/170/289/291) / 2-0-2 / 10.8 /
35.43**. The pre-registered branch rule reads **B2**: dropping the interlock
starves **5/42** against A' 's 1/42 and A''s 0/42, so the interlock is
load-bearing - and it must be **cap 4**: at cap 3 the cap binds and refuses ~2.5
patch partners per pick, which thins the window and starves once. **Cap 3 is a
measured regression.**

**Two instrument lessons, both now in AGENTS.** (1) `supply_skipped` does not
count the non-bed interlock's drop - that branch re-bases `_next_release` without
touching the counter, so the loss shows up as a **starved feed round**; A'''s
"best skips (2/0/2), worst boundary (5/42)" is exactly that. (2) `on_belt` is
not a catch metric: `on_belt = admitted + below_window` on all 45 blocks, and at
cap 4 **54 %** of the candidate rows are already past the 0.180 window floor -
the catchable read is the `window` distribution. The control's deeper window
(2.60) is a **post-reset-burst** instant - the timed refresh the owner rejected -
so it is the rejected baseline, not the bar.

**Wall +19.3 %** (29.66 -> 35.40 s/pick) at a **flat sim span**: a harness cost
(0.01623 -> 0.01941 s/tick with 6 -> 12 live bodies; P55's feeder alone +11.1 %,
P33-A's body physics +24 % for 21 vs 6.6), reported and never gated.

**Implementation**: the profile is resolved once by `rl_env._resolve_supply_profile`
and passed as **kwargs** (`FruitSpawner(band_interlock=, band_max=)`,
`PickAndPlaceTask(feed_cadence=)`, `None` = the shipped env read) - never by
mutating the environment, because `tasks.py`/`fruits.py` have no `presentation`
and a global default would arm the scripted line and move the two-line supply.
The manifest gains a `supply` block (`cadence`/`band_interlock`/`band_max`/
`direct_feed`/`continuous`/`defaulted`) and the run prints
`[supply] direct profile: cadence=on(default) band=on(4)(default) feed=on(default)`.
`--continuous N` is added to `110/121/136`, and a continuous run's summary is
**pick-level** (`[rl] picks placed k/n` + `rollout success k/n ... unit=pick`) so
`113`/`129` stop reading a `0/1`.

**Validation**: selfcheck PASS (the new `230_p58_supply_selftest.py` leg);
`accept.sh` **6/10 + `fingerprint: matches`** with **377/377** `[fruit]` lines
identical to `logs/p41/p2/accept_profile.log` (an import guard - the scripted
path never builds `SortingRLEnv`); the two-line dense run **PASS** at `190`'s
floor 0.60 against `2246f83c`; `211` ok (115 checks); the direct smoke prints the
profile row and writes the manifest block with `defaulted` all true.
**Re-baseline:** every pre-P58 direct number is a pre-profile number
(`FRUIT_FEED_CADENCE=0 FRUIT_SUPPLY_BAND_INTERLOCK=0 FRUIT_DIRECT_FEED=0`, plus
`FRUIT_ARM_PARK=ready` for pre-P43 and `FRUIT_POLICY_TRIGGER_ACQ=0` for pre-P54).

The shipped profile keeps 2.38 bodies in the catchable window against the pre-P58

seeds, per-run exact p = 0.125), upstream-edge reads 2.267 / 10/45; both 0/42
starves, `skipped` 21 = 21, placed 27 vs 28, wall 530.2 vs 531.1 s/pick.

### P60: the left arm is the closed loaded-slide class at a 47x rate - no seat, occlusion, band or trigger object

P59 left one dominant term: the post-profile direct number is 26/45 = 57.8 % with
**left 2/20** against **right 24/25**. P60 asked what that is, in three steps.

**Phase 1 (census, 180 episodes, four post-profile corpora)**: left **7 placed /
58 cnp / 4 never-held (n=69)** against right **103 / 2 / 6 (n=111)** - 93.5 % of
the left's failures are the carry class, and the payload-absence measurement is
sound rather than inferred: `_place_low` (`tasks.py:12259`) is called
unconditionally on every place leg, after the `spawner.detach`, and reads the
fruit's **own** position, so **0/58 cnps against 110/110 placed** printed the row
(p = 6.7e-13). The four never-held are the **+x reach cliff** (x 0.347-0.398,
dx +14..+58 mm). The x band does **not** differ (0.278 vs 0.280 m, Mann-Whitney
p = 0.876) while the outcome-vs-offset does: `|dx| <= 66 mm` left **7/33** vs right
**54/62**, `|dx| > 66 mm` left **0/36** vs right **49/49** - and the left's 36 are
**100 % cnp**, the same class, so there is no second mechanism there and no
trigger-side lever (it would refuse 52 % of the left's attempts to leave 21 % on
the rest, and re-selection is structurally inert, P38 phase 2).

**The "where" is the take-off, not mid-carry** (a correction the Oracle made): lane
0's release is `(0.43, +0.55)` (`assets.py:486-494`; grade A -> bin 0 -> the left,
`rl_env.py:2516`), so the left carries toward **+y**, while the only positional
evidence - 5/58 `[bed-fall] ... held=True` rows - reads **y -0.153..-0.424**, the
opposite side: the payload is out of the hand **before** the carry turns to the
bin. The coordinate is a feed-tick snapshot (`fruits.py:1750-1780`) and `held` can
be stale, so only the **direction** is quoted.

**Phase 2 (occlusion map, P35's own scorer and masks)**: the inactive **right** arm
at `ready` covers **0.000** of a 58 mm disc anywhere in the delivered band (fire
band +0.209..+0.304 decide mean/max 0.000/0.000; 0/45 selection points >= 0.10);
its silhouette unprojects to y -0.196..-0.025, entirely downstream on the -y side
with the camera at y = 0; and `ready` is the **minimum** of the 53-pose sweep, the

**0.592** for the last 0.8 s before the fire while the right's covers 0.000
upstream - but that is the reset pose, the trigger is geometry/encoder-only and the
close is the scripted primitive, and the seat evidence contradicts it (the left's

**Phase 3 (`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1`, 3 seeds x 15, the cell the Oracle named)**: left

**Verdict: no shipped change, no new lever.** The direct left's loss is the object

that confounds the physics and costs both references plus the acceptance).

### P61: the left's payload leaves out along the finger axis, off the distal lip - and the 47x is not attributable here

P60 closed with the left's deficit characterised but unexplained. The one
asymmetry never measured was the **direction** of the slip: the two arms' grasp
attitudes are exact mirrors (`configs/waypoints_oriented.json`) while the belt
drags -y, and `clean_slip` is a **norm**.

**The instrument** (default off, reporting-only under `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG`): the
`[carry]` row gains `slip_xyz=(x,y,z)mm`, the payload-minus-pads displacement **at
the running maximum**, in the leg (TCP) frame; `tasks.py` **`9a5e0459`**, pinned by
`scripts/231_p61_slip_selftest.py` (`202b40c7`, a selfcheck leg). It holds its
identity on **88/88** rows, max `abs(|slip_xyz| - clean_slip_max)` **0.072 mm**
against the print's 0.137 mm bound. **The frame is not carried by that identity** -
a rotation preserves the norm - but by the held-payload corpus (**right
`grasp_lift` 25/26 legs <= 2.3 mm** against the code's measured 34-88 mm
pre/post-step artifact) and by P42's attitude-free `[seat] drift`, which agrees
with the mapped vector on all three signs.

**The cell** (3 seeds x 15 picks, the shipped profile, no wedge): **left n = 14
in-hand slides**, leg-frame mean unit **(-0.351, +0.240, +0.905)** = **25.2 deg
from the tool axis**, 76.1 deg from the jaw-opening axis, **48.9 deg from belt
-y** (a pure drag would read (+0.034, +0.858, +0.513)). In world terms
**(+0.623, -0.658, -0.422)**: belt -y is the **largest single component (0.658)**
and **y < 0 on 14/14**, but **+x 0.623 and -z 0.422 are predicted by no registered
hypothesis** - a **downward, distal, cross-belt walk**, and only the tool-axis half
is **frame-free** (leg z *is* the finger axis; the world split is a grasp-quaternion
approximation whose threat is measured - P42's `tilt` reaches **38.2 deg** on an
escape leg against the 25.2 deg the reading uses).

**The motion candidate is refuted**: achieved `|v|max` **0.987x** the right's, and
the 1.637x `|a|max` is entirely the loss tick (placed lifts 3.170 vs 2.196).

**The 47x is not attributable on this interface**: `rl_env.py:2516` makes `active =
left if grade == "A"`, so **arm = grade = lane**. The contrast is unmeasurable on
*escapes* (**right 1 in 27**) but complete on *magnitudes* - **left 18/18
`grasp_lift` legs >= 11.3 mm vs right 25/26 <= 2.3 mm, zero overlap** - and that
one right leg is **sign-opposite** (world-y **+224.8 mm upstream**, leg y
**-0.404**) to what a belt drag (+0.858) requires: **the observation a belt-drag
mechanism cannot produce**.

**The follow-up the brief named is a commanded constant**: the along-tool seat is
`_pad_standoff(True)` = `FRUIT_FINGER_LEN` 0.060 + `PAD_LIFT` 0.010 = **70.0 mm for
both arms and every fruit**, P42's `[seat] tool=` reads **-69.3..-71.7 mm** without
separating escape from placed, and both levers that move it (`FRUIT_GRIP_PLANE_DROP`
D2a 4/8 mm; `..._PAD_LIFT_FRAC` 0.15) are **measured negative** - so the seat family
closes on the direction side too and **no batch was spent on it**. The tactile
carries no contact geometry, so a contact-patch read is not buildable. **Nothing
adopted**: no default changed, no `configs/` file moved, both references untouched.

### P62: the left is already commanded top-down - it cannot hold it, and that tilt is the mechanism

The owner's directive: try a left-specific grasp attitude, because a plain mirror of
the right may not suit the dynamic catch. Both halves turned out to be measurable.

**Phase 1 (the attitude family).** `configs/waypoints_oriented.json` is `[w,x,y,z]`
(verified through `_grasp_quat` -> `hold_quaternion` -> `quaternion_error`), its left
tool axis is **(+0.8543, -0.5132, -0.0819)** with a **belt (-y) projection of
+0.5132**, and re-projecting P61's slip gives **0.9045** against the published
**0.905** - the same frame. **The yaw family is infeasible, monotonically measured**:
+15.5/21/31/46.5/62 deg give projections 0.266/0.161/**0.000**/-0.266/-0.513 against
IK residuals **10.6/13.6/19.9/48.9/118.0 mm**, j2 margins 0.182 -> 0.001 rad and
pad-to-belt clearance **+20.2 -> +3.0 -> -14.2 mm**: the left's station reach is
**azimuth-limited**, so no yaw removes the projection without removing the station.
**Rolls about the tool axis cannot** (a rotation fixes its own axis: exactly 0.0).
The one attitude that reaches projection **0.000** *and* solves is the harness **T0**
(`[+0.0, -0.7071, +0.7071, +0.0]`, fingers straight down, jaws 90 deg across the
belt): 2/3 solves at the control's residual (6.0/5.8 vs 5.9/5.7 mm), 0.8 deg
attitude error, +15..26 mm more pad clearance, 100.7 deg away from the right's -
with a j3 margin of +0.007 rad and 32.8 mm at the x = 0.398 cliff (control 8.3).

**Phase 2 found the knob is a no-op**: `configs/waypoints.json`'s left grasp is
already `mirror_across_xz(top_down_quaternion("x"))` - **bit-identical to T0** - and
`_run_impl` discards `_grasp_quat` before the descent, so the override prints
`file_same=1 hold_same=1` and moves the achieved projection by **-0.0018/+0.0001**
against a 0.05 gate (the right's own noise floor is 0.0675/0.0174, 37x/174x larger).
The knob is built, **default off**, and proven inert.

**The finding that matters**: the left is **commanded** T0 but **achieves 26.3-28.7
deg of tilt (+0.32..+0.36 belt projection)** on every carry leg. So the residual is
**the attitude the arm can hold at this station, not the attitude it is told to
hold** - exactly the +0.513 the slip direction was projected onto. The
commanded-attitude family is **exhausted**; the remaining levers are the **re-solved
grasp seed** (T0 solves from the shipped seed at a j3 margin of +0.007 rad) and the
**hold stiffness**, each needing its own pre-registration.

**No-harm**: `accept.sh` with all knobs unset is **377/377 identical** to
`logs/p41/p2/accept_profile.log` + `fingerprint: matches` (6/10, the recorded
branch); `configs/*` untouched, no reference re-recorded, no default changed.

### P63: the 26-29 deg is the hold's, it is arm-common, and the arm-specific part is its azimuth - along the belt on the left

P62 left one question: the left is *commanded* the pure top-down attitude and
*achieves* 26.3-28.7 deg of tilt. The instrument (`[carry] hold_drift=<deg>`,
`2*acos(|dot(hold_quaternion, tcp_quat)|)`, reporting-only, `tasks.py` `1d27566c`,
pinned by `scripts/233_p63_attitude_selftest.py`) and its cell (3 seeds x 15, both
arms, 87 `[carry]` rows) answer it in three parts:

1. **The command is right, the arm cannot hold it**: the left's failing legs carry a
   median `hold_drift` of **24.6 deg** (n = 11, 22.4-29.4) while the command is T0
   (belt projection **0.0000**, verified three ways - the file, the mirror identity,
   and the independent `[attitude] tilt` agreeing to <= 4.6 deg on 9/9 legs).
2. **The command path is closed by construction**: `tasks.py:3488` - the only line
   that would re-point the hold at an achieved attitude - is gated on
   `FRUIT_CARRY_HOLD_QUAT`, unset in this cell.
3. **The drift does NOT split the class**: the right places **29/30** `grasp_lift`
   legs at a median drift of **25.8 deg** (20.9-52.3), the same distribution as the
   left's *failing* legs; the left's two placed legs read 23.7 and 36.1. The tilt is
   an **arm-common attitude-tracking residual** (Spearman -0.36 left / +0.20 right).

**What is arm-specific is the tilt's azimuth, and it is sign-consistent**: the
left's achieved tool axis is **downstream on 3/3** legs (tool_y -0.326..-0.366,
**77 % of the tilt on the belt axis**) while the right's is **downstream on 0/6**
(3 upstream, 3 across, median share 0.23). So the ~25 deg lands **along the belt**
on the left and **across it** on the right - which is exactly the +/-0.513 the P61
slip was projected onto.

**The mechanism chain is now closed at every link**: command T0 -> an arm-common
~25 deg tracking residual -> whose azimuth is the belt axis on the left -> the
belt's drag walks the payload out along the tool axis (P61) -> the `cnp` class at
47x the right's rate. **The lever this hands on is a pre-compensated command**: if
the residual is deterministic (~25 deg at a stable azimuth), commanding T0 rotated
by its inverse puts the *achieved* attitude at projection ~0 without touching the
arm's kinematics. No default changed; `configs/*` untouched; no reference moved.

### P64: the pre-compensated command is live and INVERTED - the achieved attitude is a 6-DoF IK trade, not an offset

The last parameter-level lever the chain handed on (P63) was a pre-compensated
command: command `q_drift^-1 (x) q_T0` so the *achieved* attitude lands at
projection ~0. Two things were measured.

**The channel is real, and it is not P62's.** `_grasp_quat`/`grasp_quat_override` is
inert on the lift (P62), but the command `ik_step` actually tracks during
`grasp_lift` is **`arm.hold_quaternion`**, installed by the never-stop catch before
the hover and **inherited** by the lift (the `_carry` clear is `name !=
"grasp_lift"`; every place leg clears it). Writing it at the lift's start moves the
achieved attitude by 17-32 deg in the gate smoke - so the brief's "if no path
exists, stop" branch does not apply, and a scoped, default-off knob
(`carry_hold_override_for`, `tasks.py` `7a8a163a`) is in the tree.

**The response is inverted.** The drift from 7 left `grasp_lift` legs is `axis
(-0.7564, -0.6541, 0)`, `angle 26.798 deg` (median achieved tool axis
`(+0.3035, -0.3509, -0.8859)`, per-leg tilt 25.1-28.7 deg, azimuth spread +-3.2
deg), giving a command projection of **-0.3410**. Commanding it takes the achieved
projection **from +0.32..+0.37 to +0.51..+0.83** (achieved tilt 38.5-57.9,
`hold_drift` 54.9-107.4 deg against the control's 20.5-29.4), the holds lose
contact **earlier** (onset rows 37-39 vs 97-127) and the left places **1/16**
against the control's 2/15. **E1 fails by sign.**

**Mechanically**: `ik_step`'s 6-DoF solve at a station whose grasp seed already
sits at the reach edge **trades orientation against position**, so the achieved
attitude is a function of the whole task rather than of the orientation target -
at `q_cmd = T0` it settles 25-29 deg downstream, at `q_cmd = T0 - 26.8 deg` it
settles 38-58 deg. **No constant pre-compensation can set it.**

**So the pose family is exhausted in every form measured**: the yaw family is
IK-infeasible (P62), the command is already T0 (P62), the residual's magnitude is
arm-common with only its azimuth left-specific (P63), and a constant
pre-compensation is inverted (P64). What remains is **structural** - the station's
reach (P58's `GEOMETRY.md` priced a station move NO-GO at the current margins) or
the arm/gripper hardware - **never a command parameter.** Knob default off, no
`configs/` change, no reference re-recorded.

### P64 errata + the screen: my own treatment command was inadmissible, and the lift (not the station) creates the drift

The gate asked the one question I had skipped: **was `q_cmd` ever screened for
admissibility?** It was not, and the screen (P62's own `ik_probe.py`, 2 min)
answers it: **`q_cmd` (`[+0.01675, -0.68786, +0.68786, +0.23113]`, command
projection -0.3410) solves 0/3** with a residual of **42.6-72.9 mm (7-12x
tolerance)**, a joint margin of **0.000/-0.000 at j6-j7** (the control holds
+0.204 at j2), and **`jaw_z = +0.2949` -> a 28.9 mm pad-height difference across
the 98 mm jaw** - the exact class `configs/waypoints_oriented.json`'s note rejects.
**So "the response is inverted" is withdrawn: it was an inadmissible command, not
a mechanism.** The two-point "no command can set it" is withdrawn with it (P64's
own prereg §6 said the slope was not identifiable).

The screen's **reachable** directions: **`q_drift (x) q_T0` (+0.341) solves 3/3**
(better conditioned than T0's 2/3 at +0.007 @j3) but carries the same 28.2-28.6 mm
jaw twist and **is the attitude already achieved**; the `waypoints_oriented` left
quaternion (+0.513) is **exactly the shipped control** (row for row).

tracks its command to **<= 1 deg at both projection 0 (T0: 0.77 deg) and +0.35
(`q_drift`: 0.78-0.93 deg)**, while P63's failing **carry** legs read **24.6 deg**.
So **the drift is created in the lift**, not by the station's reach - the
"6-DoF trade at the reach edge" reading is retired with it, and
`hold_quaternion` pre-compensation has **no station-level target in either sign**.
What is not yet measured: why the lift drifts when the station tracks
(`control.py:423` `max_step` and `:494`'s hard joint clip are the named suspects),
and the pads' line (the jaw axis was never printed; `tasks.py:3237`'s `rot[:,1]` is
free).

**Also corrected**: `logs/p58/GEOMETRY.md` prices the **station y** for the
*catchable-segment* question (R10), **not** a general station NO-GO - the P64
paragraph's citation was out of scope. Evidence `logs/p64/{SCREEN.md,ik_screen.*}`.

### P65: both IK suspects for the lift's drift are measured out, and the drift's cause is still open

The instrument (`q_margin`, `q_cmd_margin`, `q_step_max`, `jaw_z`, `drift_on` on the

### P66: the left's 25 deg carry rotation is a HEIGHT problem - and lowering the lift fixes most of it

The arc that began at P60 ended here: the rotation is not a controller defect, not a
pose command, not a joint limit - it is what the arm does when the lift asks it to
hold a top-down attitude above the belt.

**Phase 1 (offline, free).** A 150-cell station sweep finds **no point in the
delivered band where T0 holds** (0/75 of its own cells passing the 0.05 rad margin
clause; best +0.010 rad) while the shipped C0 passes 31/75; at the **lift's end
height** T0 is **statically unsolvable** (qerr 24.3-60.0 deg, margin 0.000), i.e.
P63's live 24.6 deg with no payload, no controller, no transient. The
finger-tip identity (`S` 84.902 -> `F1` 80.902 mm = `4*cos(0)`) holds to <0.001 mm,
but at the descent's vertical fingers the -4 mm buys 4.00 mm - 4.4-10 % of the
40-90 mm shortfall - so the pad lane stays closed on measurement and scale.

**Phase 2 (the ladder, 3 seeds).** `FRUIT_LIFT_DZ` shifts the `grasp_lift` target
height: 0.36 / 0.28 / 0.20 gives `drift_end` **23.8/25.7 -> 9.7 -> 0.7 deg**,
`res_end` **80.6 -> 33.7 -> 13.3 mm**, and the left **1/34 -> 1/18 -> 10/16**, with
the right flat in shape and the cycle flat (sim 15.0 -> 14.7 s/pick). F1 fired
*favourably* (0.7 vs the predicted 3 +- 2); F4 fired **falsely** (`fruit fell off
the line` is shared with the pre-grasp supply class, 4/4 events right-arm
`grasped=False`, 2 of them in the control); P3 was self-contradictory and its
"share" dose is withdrawn in favour of `|tool_y|` (0.322/0.327 -> 0.162 -> 0.002).

**Phase 3 (the rung batch, N=4 of 5).** The control **0/19**, C24 (0.24) **11/23
(47.8 %)**, C20 (0.20) **11/19 (57.9 %)**, `drift_end` **25.2 / 3.4 / 0.7**. The
rungs are **flat** (Fisher p ~ 0.75) so **0.24 is the economical one**; the class
effect is one-sided (Fisher ~3e-4). Seed 404 was lost to a **server restart**, not
a wedge.

**Nothing was flipped.** Two gates are unmeasured: the **place-transit clearance**
(the new `clr` field prints the leg's *minimum*, including the on-belt phase, not
the crossing - the reading that could block the flip does not exist yet) and the
**right-arm no-op** (structural, but 85.4-100 % at N=4 sits inside its own branch

no reference re-recorded; every pre-P66 direct number is a **0.36-lift** number
(`FRUIT_LIFT_DZ=+0.08` restores it).

The last gate (a) of P66 is measured. With the `clr` reduction fixed to the
rail-crossing form (`clr_x` at the crossing, `clr_win` over the transfer window;
one seed, 2 runs, `p4_report.py --check` PASS):

  scenario;
- **no held leg goes negative in either arm (0/16)** - there is **no contact** -

### P70: the rails are the lever (1:1, inert here) and the belt height is not (0.175:1, it costs placements)

The owner's directive: remove the output belts' side rails (the "ledges") and lower the
output belt's height as appropriate. Nothing adopted at P70 - the deliverable is the
measurement and the knob; **P71 ships the rail half**.

**The knob and the instrument.** `FRUIT_OUTPUT_BELT_TOP_Z` (default **1.35**, an env-read
`field(default_factory=...)`, so the shipped scene is built by the same float) lowers the
whole output station; the **eleven** read sites are pinned by an AST census in
`scripts/238_p70_belt_top_selftest.py` (`output_place_z`, `on_output_belt`,
`output_chute_top/bottom`, `on_output_discharge`, `conveyor` slab/build,
`tasks._place_low`/`_place_trace_report`/`_grasp_carry_place_impl`/`_payload_clearance`),
and `rl_env.py`/`fruits.py` reach it only through a property. **The instrument defect
that made the cell unreadable is fixed**: `tasks._payload_clearance` hard-coded
`belt_top + 0.035`, so it was blind to `FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAIL_HEIGHT` *and* to a removed
rail; it now reads `output_rail_keep[0]` and `SceneConfig.output_rail_proud =
output_rail_height - OUTPUT_RAIL_INSET` (one constant, two readers: the builder and the
report), and at the shipped geometry the reported surface is unchanged to 1e-12 m.

**The cells** (scripted, 10 attempts, one claim each, `FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1
FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1`): C (shipped `both`, 1.35) **6/10**, `clr` +30..+120 @rail,
`clr_win` +29..+96, 4/10 loaded slides; A (`RAILS=none`, 1.35) **6/9** (one slot
starved), +65..+156 @obelt / +64..+113, 3/9; B (`RAILS=none`, **1.31**) **4/10**,
+126..+167 / +91..+108, 6/10. **The 1:1 proof is one leg at one tick**: the same 5.6 cm
kiwi on the same left arm crosses at `+30 @rail / t275` in C and `+65 @obelt / t275` in
A - **+35.0 mm**, exactly the rail box's `0.05 - 0.015` proud height. Only ep2 has both
a matching tick and the same fruit; the rest are branch-shifted inside the leg.

**The arithmetic** (derived): the place leg is a straight line and the crossing sits at
`f = 0.4125 / 0.50 = 0.825` of the `|y|` span, so `z_crossing = f * transfer + (1-f) *
lift_end` and **`d clr / d(belt top) = f - 1 = -0.175`** - 40 mm of lowering buys
**+7.0 mm** while spending **1:1** of the 40 mm under-slab audit (at 1.31 the build's
print reads 0.006 m nominal / **0.000 m** at the tallest instance). Removing the rail
buys **35 mm** in one step, 5x the biggest admissible height dose. Cell B is also the
only arm whose count falls (4/10) and its place legs are 6.8 % longer.

**The ledge census** (the reason P30-A's register had the rails in): of 16 in-hand
releases across the three arms, **16/16 sit 116-122 mm outboard** of the slab's inner
edge, **0** in the rail's top-face band (0.400-0.425) and 0 inboard of 0.400 - the
2.3 %-of-10 195 class is a property of the *pooled* population, not this scenario's.
With the rail gone that band has **no surface under it** (the slab starts at 0.425, the
main belt is 180 mm below), so a release landing there falls instead of parking; the G2
fixture for it is registered and **not run**.

**The direct pair, the low lift with and without the rails** (`logs/p70/run_direct.sh`;
all-A supply so every attempt is a left place leg, `FRUIT_LIFT_DZ=-0.08` explicit in
both, `FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1` on both for the contact channel, seed 77, 15 picks):
**D0 (rails both) 6/15 placed, 6 loaded slides, 3 held legs, crossing `clr` +7/+16/+17
@rail**; **D1 (rails none) 10/15, 3 loaded slides, 10 held legs, `clr` -1..+54 @obelt**
(`clr_win` -6..+50). That is the rails isolated at the low lift: **+4 placements and
half the loaded slides**, and it is the pair that made P71's rail flip safe.

**Verdict**: the rails are the lever and the height is not; the recommendation on the
height is **0 mm** (1.33 / 1.31 are the conservative / endpoint picks if it is ever
wanted for another reason). P70 itself adopted nothing: the knobs defaulted to the
shipped geometry, no reference was re-recorded, no commit.

The owner authorized 方案 b from P70: **remove the output belts' side rails**, keep the
belt height at the shipped **1.35**. Two defaults flip, both to values already measured:

| `FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAILS` (`assets.SceneConfig`) | `both` | **`none`** | `FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAILS=both` |

## P72 - the canary smoke, the corner instrument, the new-frame boundary, the scene manifest

The four residuals `logs/p71/RESULTS.md` §5/§6 named. No `configs/` edit, no default change,
no commit. Tree: `tasks.py` **`f61323f2`**, `assets.py` **`540406fa`**,
`rl_env.py` **`92a25c8e`**, `scripts/40_collect_demos.py` **`86b3d6ba`**,
`scripts/239_p72_clr_edge_selftest.py` **`c3027c4f`**, `236`/`238` re-pinned, ckpt
`moe_v13s` `61da390a`, references `8952c320` / `eb697f23` untouched.

**The hybrid canary smoke is inside its spread and the rail flip is not implicated.**
`SKIP_SELFCHECK=1 scripts/accept_policy.sh` (the interface of record: `60_eval_policy.py`,
`moe_v12`, the pre-v9 fixed supply, ten episodes) reads **8/10 = 80 % PASS** at the 0.60
floor with **2 grip losses** (`fruit did not follow the gripper`), **0
grasped-not-placed** and **no failure reason outside the recorded baseline** - the gate's
own reason clause prints the PASS. It **inherits the rail flip** and that is proven in-log
rather than assumed (`output belt rails P: FRUIT_OUTPUT_RAILS=none authors 0/2 (inner
y=+0.4125 REMOVED), height 0.050 m (top +1.3850, shipped)`, and the same for `N`), and it
**cannot** see the lift flip (no `[rl] env ready`, no `[grasp] lift_dz:` row - the canary
never constructs `SortingRLEnv`). **8/10 is the top of the interface's recorded 5-8/10
spread** (`moe_v11` 8, `moe_v12` 6, P2b 5 and 6, P32 D0 5, P41 p4 7), so it is one draw of
a non-reproducible loop and says nothing about a rail effect in either direction; the two
failures are pick-side grip losses (ep6 tomato 6.5 cm, ep9 peach 6.5 cm, both
`grasped=False`, `lift=-0.0 cm`), i.e. upstream of the output line, and every placed
episode lands on the slab, whose top plane is 25 mm *below* where the rail's face was.

**`clr_edge` - the corner instrument, and why its threshold is 0.425 and not the 0.400
switch.** `tasks._payload_clearance` switches surfaces at a **literal** `|y| = 0.40`; that
number is the **removed inner rail's inner face**, not the slab's edge. The rail box is
25 mm thick with its bottom `OUTPUT_RAIL_INSET` (0.015) inside the slab, so on the shipped
geometry it spans **0.400..0.425 m** and its **outer face is flush with the slab's inner
edge** (`assets.SceneConfig.output_rail_keep`'s own docstring; `z_cross`'s fraction is
`0.4125/0.50 = 0.825`). So the band 0.400-0.425 is **inboard of the surface** - a payload
there is over the main belt (1.17 m), 180 mm below the raised slab - and the plane charge
is conservative by construction, which is exactly the leg P71 flagged (`clr_win = -6 mm`
on a leg that **placed** with 0.4 mm slip). The new fields are the **first** tick the
payload's `|y|` reaches **0.425** (the slab's own inboard edge, `_output_belt_edge_y` =
`|output_belt_y| - size[1]/2`, derived not hardcoded) with its tick, plus
`clr_edge_min`, the minimum over the same band - printed beside `clr`/`clr_win`/`clr_min`,
through the existing `_clearance_field`. **Reporting only**: both trackers sit inside
`if guard_armed:` (whose first condition is `_carry_guard_active or _carry_diag`,
`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG` default `"0"`), so the diag-off path runs nothing new and its row is
byte-identical, and the armed path consumes the `(clearance, where, i)` triple and
`_abs_y` the leg already computes - **no new read** (`_payload_clearance`, `pad_centre`,
`tcp_pose`, `spawner.position` are all absent from the tracker body and the new leg
asserts it). Pinned by `scripts/239_p72_clr_edge_selftest.py` (a selfcheck leg): the row
and its order, the containment and the no-new-read property, the executed `_output_belt_edge_y`
body on stub configs (a wider or further-out slab moves the edge 1:1, no `0.0125` in it),
that the edge is 25 mm outboard of `rail_inner` (a *different, later* tick - not a rename
of `clr_win`), the parse-back form, and the `scene` block (§below). **The field's own
read** - one direct run, seed 77, 15 episodes, the P66/P71 cell verbatim, `moe_v13s`
`61da390a`, the flip proven in-log (`dz=-0.0800(default) -> 1.3700 m`, `park=back(default)`,
`tasks_md5=f61323f2`): **`clr_edge` n = 10 held place legs, min +26, median +77.5, max
+109 mm; `clr_edge_min` min +26, median +77.5, max +104; `<= 0` on 0/10** - every value
`@obelt`, every held leg's `|a|max` **<= 4.49 m/s²** (G0's contact floor is 14.9) and no
slip above 0.1 mm, i.e. **positive with no contact signature on all ten**. The draw is
right-heavy (13 place legs right, 8 held; **2 held left**), and the left - the arm the
package targets - sits **+4..+5 mm above its own centreline sample** (ep0 +33 -> +38, ep6
+22 -> +26) while the right's is flat, so P71's left `clr` +14..+50 maps to roughly
+18..+55 at the corner by that measured delta (an inference from two legs, flagged).
**P70's hand estimate is confirmed to 1 mm where the two runs share a leg**: P70 D1 ep0 and
this run's ep0 are the same leg (`clr = +33 @t329`, `clr_win = +29 @t323`, 430 ticks,
`res_end` 31.6 mm) and `edge~+37` (a slope model, `clr + 4 mm`) reads **+38** measured.
Outcome mix (not a rate): 10/15 placed, 3 carried-not-placed (loaded slide), 2 never-held
(`fruit fell off the line`, the supply tail).

**The new-frame boundary is `clr_edge > 0`, and it is a bracket, not a calibrated floor.**
With `output_rail_keep = (False, False)` the rail branch of `_payload_clearance`
(`if y <= 0.46 and cfg.output_rail_keep[0]`) is never entered, so the only surface a place
transit can clip is the slab - its **top plane** (1.35) and its **inboard edge** (0.425) -
and contact requires the payload's lowest point **below the plane while horizontally over
the slab**, i.e. `clr_edge <= 0`; **no raised surface exists, so no `+N mm` rail convention
transfers to this frame.** The record's only sub-zero *plane* sample is **P70 D1 ep8's
`clr = -1 mm @obelt / t247`**, taken 25 mm inboard of the surface, and it carries **no
contact signature** (`|a|max` 0.98, `sep_end` 69.9 mm, slip 0.4 mm) against **G0's measured
contact population 14.9-32.7 m/s²** (27-76 mm displacement, `sep_end` 97.5-98.3 on 4/5);
G0's boundary (`clr <= +7` touches, `>= +14` clean) was calibrated on the rail's 25 mm top
ledge. **No dose ladder was spent, and none can close a gap anyway**: `z_cross =
f*z_transfer + (1-f)*z_lift_end` with `f = 0.825` at the rail centreline (0.85 at the
edge), `z_transfer = output_place_z + hand = belt_top + 0.10 + hand` moves **1:1 with the
belt top** (i.e. with the obstacle) while `z_lift_end = main_belt_top + 0.28 + dz` is
anchored to the **main** belt and does not move with the output belt at all - hence
`d clr/d(lift) = +(1-f) = +0.175` and `d clr/d(belt top) = f - 1 = -0.175` (0.15 each at
the edge sample), the lift lever buys 17.5 % of its travel at the crossing, and the
belt-height lever spends the 40 mm under-slab audit for +7 mm (`logs/p66/P4_RESULTS.md`,
`logs/p70/RESULTS.md` §3 - both measured negative on the count). The honest shipped
statement is therefore: **the floor is `clr_edge > 0`; the package's measured minimum is
+26 mm with no contact signature; the +33 convention has no counterpart surface now** -
and the evidence is a **bracket** (one sub-zero plane sample with a clean signature plus
the measured corner values), not a contact-calibrated boundary at the corner. Calibrating
one needs a forced descent into the edge band (the G2-style fixture) and a contact read;
named, not run.

**The scene's collider set is a manifest field now.** `assets.scene_provenance(cfg,
lift_dz=None, lift_dz_defaulted=False)` - pure `SceneConfig` arithmetic, so it imports
without the simulator and the offline leg executes it - is the **one builder both writers
call** (the P41 `physics` rule): `scripts/40_collect_demos.write_manifest` writes
`scene_provenance(cfg)` (its `lift` is **`null`** by construction - a scripted shard has no
lift rung) and `rl_env._build_manifest` writes `scene_provenance(self.cfg,
lift_dz=self._lift_dz, lift_dz_defaulted=self._lift_dz_defaulted)`. Fields:
`output_rails` (the resolved mode string) + `rail_keep` (the `(inner, outer)` pair the
builder actually reads), `rail_height` / `rail_proud` / `rail_inset` (a pre-P71 clearance
row is reconstructible from them - `rail_proud` is what `_payload_clearance` reports a kept
rail against), `output_belt.{top_z,y,size,inboard_edge_y}` (P70's height knob, kept at
1.35, and the P72 corner), and `lift = {dz: {arm: m}, defaulted: bool}` / `null`.
Shipped: `none`, proud 0.035, inset 0.015, top 1.35, edge 0.425, `dz.left -0.08 defaulted`.
**Metadata only** - nothing reads it, both callers wrap the call in `try/except` (a
reported state, never a failed run) - and **a store without the key predates P72**
(`arm_park.defaulted`'s convention), so the mixing rule P71 wrote is now checkable from the
store itself. Exercised end-to-end on **both** writers: `logs/p72/manifest_probe.py` (run
under the simulator python, since it imports `isaacsim` - not an offline leg) calls the real
`write_manifest` for `none` and `=both` and prints `none` -> `rail_keep` both false,
`=both` -> both true, `lift` null in both, `inboard_edge_y` 0.425; and the phase's direct
run wrote its own `manifest.json` with the block live (`lift.dz.left -0.08`,
`defaulted true`).

**Re-pins the work forced** (each test's meaning kept, not weakened): `236`'s tracker-init
list and its `inf` assertions (the init line grew `edge_y`), `236`'s print-containment
check (a **character budget** -> the file's own `indented_body_contains`, the `235`
helper), `236`'s "one construction site" count (the new `scene` call also passes
`lift_dz=`, so the check is now scoped to the `PickAndPlaceTask(` call), and `238`'s
`output_belt_top_z` read census, which **declared** the new consumer
(`assets.py:scene_provenance`) exactly as designed. `rl_env.py`'s `TASKS_MD5` follows
`7c00e555` -> **`f61323f2`** (metadata only; the direct run logs `tasks_md5=f61323f2`).
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` PASS, 0 failures (1 skip, the motion-budget leg). Nothing was
adopted, no default moved, no reference re-recorded. Residuals: the left's corner
distribution is **n = 2** in this draw (a second seed would give it a population); the
corner sample is **one tick per leg** plus the band minimum, so a corner contact by the
payload's **outboard overhang** while its centre is still inboard of 0.425 is not separable
with this instrument (single-digit-mm bound at this roundness); the collector was not
re-collected (the field was proven by calling the real writer, not by a shard); the ledge
class stays **untested, not zero** (P70 §4's fixture still not run); the belt height stays
1.35 by P70's verdict.

## P73 — the place-transfer height is not a lever on the place-leg slide, and the rotation is not its actuator

The owner's question after P71/P72: the left's surviving failures are **place-leg**
loaded slides (held through the transit, lost in the place leg). The hypothesis
(D1/D2/D3 linker → D1 `FRUIT_OPENARM_TRANSFER_LIFT` 0.08 → 0.14 → 0.20 → D4
evaluation vs. control) was that reaching the output line demands ~75-91 deg of
wrist rotation, that the place **transfer's height** sets how much rotation the
reach demands, and therefore that a raised transfer reduces the slide. Nothing
was adopted; no default moved.

**What was registered first.** `logs/p73/PREREG.md` (md5 `81b70bb3`, pinned at
03:28:54Z, before any run of the phase): three arms (C 0.08 / T1 0.14 / T2 0.20)
on the P66-phase-3 cell verbatim, seed 77, 15 picks, `moe_v13s` `61da390a`, one
claim each, `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1 FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1`; the primary endpoint (the
left's `clean_slip > 800 mm` legs and the left's placed count), the secondary
(rotation schedule, `clr`/`clr_edge`, landing, cycle, the right), the expansion
rule (101/202 only if seed 77 moved by >= 2 in slides or placed), the three
falsifiers (A: the tilt does not move; B: the slides do not move while the tilt
does; C: the landing regresses), and five pre-run predictions. The census that
shaped it (`logs/p73/p0_census.py`) also found the trap: the shipped corpus's
per-leg `[attitude]` tilt is **80.8-94.6 deg on both the lost and the placed left
legs**, so the only existing rotation read is blind - it is printed **once, at the
leg's end**.

**The instrument, because the existing read would have produced a wrong answer.**
Six default-off `[carry]` fields (`tilt0`, `tilt_end`, `tilt_max`, `t45`, `t75`,
`tilt_rate`) accumulate the achieved tilt from world `-Z` per guarded tick. It is
`[attitude]`'s own `acos(-rot[2,2])` on **`rot_now`, the `guard_armed` block's
existing read** for `clean_slip` - no new articulation read, no command, no
threshold. Pinned by `scripts/240_p73_tilt_selftest.py` (containment, the
`[attitude]` identity, the no-new-read property, the arithmetic, the row parsing
back) and `scripts/235` re-pinned for the inserted fields. `rl_env.TASKS_MD5`
follows `f61323f2 -> adcfd348` (metadata only).

**The measurement.** The class is **flat to the leg: 1 / 1 / 1** loaded slides
(1 of 5, 1 of 4, 1 of 5 left place legs) at 995 / 983 / 887 mm, with `cnp` 2 / 1 /
1 and the pre-contact acquisition class 2 / 0 / 0. The mechanism moves
monotonically and **the other way**: `tilt_end` **78.7 -> 93.8 -> 105.2 deg**
(+26.5) and `t45` **313 -> 303 -> 299** ticks - a higher transfer *demands more*
wrist rotation, not less. Falsifier **A does not fire** (the rotation moves);
falsifier **B fires** (26.5 deg of extra rotation, zero change in the count).
**The causal order is visibly wrong**: in **8 of 8** payload losses the onset row
is **before** the leg's 45-deg crossing (onsets 4, 133, 103, 136, 3, 4, 157, 265
against `t45` 313-561), i.e. the payload leaves at 1-41 % of the leg at a tilt
below 45 deg while the 90-105 deg sweep happens at 73-79 % - *after* the failure.
The conditional discriminator (run because rule B's literal trigger fired) says
**not inertial**: `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.20` reads **4 slides in 8 legs** against
C's 1 in 5, with the rotation at the *same fraction* of the leg (73-78 % vs
73-79 %) but **+211 ticks = +1.76 s of absolute dwell at near-top-down** - the
class tracks **time hanging in a top-down pinch under lateral load**. The escape
signature (`contacts@onset` 1, `force@onset` 7.9-11.2 N at the pinch's own 9.8 N,
`fmin 0.00`, jaws ending **closed** at 42-53 mm against the lift-leg form's 98 mm
open stop) is a **clean single-sided exit** - neither a force deficit nor a pry.
**The right settles the rotation question on its own**: median **107.3 deg**
(max 109.7) of place-leg rotation with **0.0-0.1 mm** of slip on 10 of 10 legs,
7/8 -> 10/11 -> 10/10 placed, no new class.

**What the lever does buy, exactly as predicted**: `clr` **34 -> 88 -> 142.5 mm**
and `clr_edge` **38 -> 94 -> 151.5** (+54 / +108.5 against P1's predicted +49 /
+99, so P69-B's 0.825:1 is confirmed on a second axis; no leg negative), for
**+4.5 / +7.0 % of episode ticks** (the `place low` descent +41 / +90 ticks; the
*leg* total only +22 / +17 because the transit shrank as the descent grew - **P2
partially missed**, and **P3 missed informatively**: the endpoint was predicted to
stay 85-95 deg and went to 105.2, which is exactly why A does not fire and why the
instrument mattered). P1, P4, P5 hit. No landing regression (1 `did not land` per
T arm against C's 2, no `fell off` row, `need` 248 mm against the 300 mm ceiling).

**Named consequence.** Do not spend another transfer rung (the lever's own
mechanism moves monotonically and the class does not), another rotation lever
(`FRUIT_GRASP_LEFT_TOPDOWN` / P64's pre-compensation act on a link measured off
the failure's path), or a **slower** place leg (it doubles the class). The
residual is the closed `SIM_LIMIT.md` loaded slide on a leg that carries the
payload top-down for ~0.5 m; the levers that touch it are the ones `SIM_LIMIT.md`
sanctions (a new pad asset, a real-jaw clamp-force anchor) or a workstation move
that shortens that transit at top-down - and the cheapest such change
(`FRUIT_PLACE_INNER_SHIFT`) is already measured negative (P3: 90 % -> 30 %).

**No-harm.** `scripts/accept.sh` **6/9 + `fingerprint: matches`** (rate-only
FAIL, the standing floor) with its **346/346 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical** to
`logs/p71/accept_rails_none.log` - the instrument is inert on the scripted path;
`configs/` untouched (`8952c320` / `eb697f23`, no re-record); `selfcheck.sh` PASS
(0 failures, 1 skip) including the new leg. **Provenance gap named, not fixed**:
the manifest records `lift_dz`/`lift_climb`/`scene`/`physics` but **not** the
transfer height, so a store under a different value would be indistinguishable
(it must join `assets.scene_provenance` before any recollection uses the knob).
No store was recorded here.

**Deviation (recorded).** One 2-pick fixture at T1 (`logs/p73/smoke_T1.log`) ran
**before** the registered batch to check that the knob and the instrument were
picked up; it is in no count. And the `SLOW` arm is a **directional** read (4/8 vs
1/5, Fisher p = 0.56): its value is the sign and the mechanism, which the
schedules corroborate, not a rate.
