## P74 — the place-profile speed does not move the place-leg slide, and the 800 mm threshold is not speed-invariant

P73 left exactly one measured direction unspent: it falsified the transfer height
(both ways) and the rotation, and its **slowed** place profile
(`FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.20`) read **4 payload losses in 8 place legs** against C's
1 in 5 — "the class tracks the time the payload hangs in a top-down pinch under
lateral load". The mirror test is therefore a **faster** place leg, and the
project already owns one: P44's S1 cell, `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.52`, measured at
`place0 -135.4 ticks` on the scripted line. Nothing was adopted; no default
moved; **no `src/`, `configs/` or `scripts/` file was edited** by this phase.

**What was registered first.** `logs/p74/PREREG.md` (md5 `1c3546de`, pinned
04:30:48Z, before any run of the phase): two arms (**C** the shipped place
profile, **S** `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.52`) on the P66-phase-3 / P71-phase-2 / P73
cell verbatim, seed 77, 15 picks, `moe_v13s` `61da390a`, one claim each,
`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1 FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1`; the primary (the left's
`clean_slip > 800 mm` legs and the left's placed count), the secondary (place-leg
ticks and `|v|cmd`, `clr`/`clr_edge`, the escape signature, the acquisition and
`cnp` split, any new reason, the right), five predictions (P1 the class falls,
P2 the leg is `0.673x`, P3 space unchanged, P4 no new class, P5 the right flat),
three falsifiers (F1 flat, F2 rises, F3 a guard regresses), and an expansion rule
(101/202 only if the seed-77 mechanism read is consistent **and** `placed` does
not fall **and** the acquisition guard is clean).

**The knob, resolved before the run.** `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE` is the P44 S1 cell and
changes nothing by itself: it supplies the **default string** of
`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PLACE_VMAX` at `tasks.py:3853` inside `elif
self._dynamic_capture_active:`, which the direct presentation arms
(`dynamic_pick` from `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PICK=1` × openarm → `dynamic_capture` →
`direct_capture`, `tasks.py:9677`). `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.52` and
`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PLACE_VMAX=0.52` are **limit-identical** (the registered value
keeps `a_max` at the shipped 1.089), and the direct path resolves the explicit
env var first, so naming the cell names what supplies the value when only it is
set. P73's `SLOW` arm is the manipulated-positive control for the resolution
(`|v|cmd` 0.342 → 0.196 on the same leg), and the PREREG derived the expected
numbers **offline** from `motion.jerk_limited` (`T = max(1.875d/v,
sqrt(5.774d/a), cbrt(60d/j))·1.02`, so `|v|cmd = 1.875d/T` and `ticks ∝ 1/v`
while the velocity term binds): `|v|cmd` 0.343 → 0.510 and **ticks 0.673x**,
which the C column reproduces to 0-3 ticks on the P73 corpus.

**The manipulation gate passes on every clause and every seed**
(`logs/p74/p1_report.py --check`): C `|v|cmd` median **0.343**, S **0.509**; the
per-leg tick count matches `jerk_limited` at the printed distance to **≤ 1 % on
33/33 legs**; the distance-matched S/C ratios are **0.676 / 0.677 / 0.678**
(predicted 0.673 ± 0.06); the `place low` descent stays inside its ±20 % band.
The knob is **not side-scoped** — the right's place legs shorten too (356 → 258
ticks), which the PREREG registered up front rather than discovering.

**What happened: seed 77 said yes and the expansion said no.** Seed 77 read
**2 payload losses in 4 left place legs (C) → 1 in 6 (S)** — the predicted
direction — and the registered expansion fired (`Δ slides -2`, `Δ placed +2`,
clean acquisition). Seeds 101 and 202 then read **4/7 → 4/5** and **2/8 → 2/3**,
the *opposite* direction at both. Pooled (19 C legs, 14 S legs): the registered
primary **`> 800 mm` 7/19 = 37 % → 3/14 = 21 %** (Fisher p = 0.455) while the
**mechanism count** (`clean_slip_max > 100 mm`, i.e. a payload that left the
pinch) is **8/19 = 42 % → 7/14 = 50 %** (p = 0.733); left placed 11/20 → 6/15
(p = 0.5). **F1 fires.** A single seed would have published a 15-point win.

**Why the primary moved and the mechanism did not — the phase's real finding.**
After the escape the payload free-falls while the pads continue, so the reported
class value is essentially `rate × (ticks - loss_row)`. Measured across all
three seeds: the rate rises **3.13-3.25 → 3.93-4.00 mm/tick (+25 %)** with the
pads' speed (0.32 → 0.46 m/s achieved) and the remaining leg falls **-38 %**, so
the product straddles the 800 mm line — S's four sub-threshold payload losses sit
at **659.6 / 740.9 / 798.8 / 799.1 mm** and C's one at **617.1**. **So
`clean_slip_max > 800 mm` is not a speed-invariant classifier**: quote the
**escape count** for any speed change, and keep the threshold for
height/rotation/retiming, where the remaining leg is constant. This also
re-reads P73's own 793.3 mm "held-by-the-rule" leg as part of the same band.

**The dwell is not the actuator.** With P73's slow arm the rate is **50 %
(680-tick legs) / 42 % (405) / 50 % (262)** — flat across a **2.6x** range of
dwell. So P73's `4/8` is a draw of the same ~45 % rate, and its
"time-accumulating loaded creep" reading is **withdrawn** (its own caveat said so
if the fast direction came back empty). What survives is P73's positive half,
reproduced here: the escape's onset **precedes** the wrist's 45-deg crossing on
**15/15** payload losses (`loss_row/ticks` 0.01-0.44 against `t45/ticks`
0.71-0.86), the right reaches the same attitude and slips **0.0-0.1 mm on 28/28**
place legs, and the escape's signature is unchanged — both arms read
`force_min = 0.00 N` on every loss, `contacts@onset = 1` on 6/8 and 6/7, jaws
ending in the **17.3-53.7 mm** closed form (never the 98 mm open stop), with one
`27.09 N` / `sep@onset 98.2 mm` squeeze-out on each side of the class and exactly
one `0.00 N / contacts 0` never-held leg each. **The class is stochastic given
the pinch**: neither the pose nor the clock drives it.

**The guards (P4/P5), which are the reason the negative is clean.** The failure
ledger is **identical in count**: left `cnp` **8 vs 8**, left `never-grasped`
**1 vs 1**, right `never-grasped` **2 vs 2**, `did not land` **8 vs 8**,
`fell off` **0 vs 0**, blow-ups **0 vs 0**; right placed **23/25 vs 28/30** with
**0 loaded slides in both**. `clr`/`clr_edge` are **leg-determined, not
profile-determined**: on distance-matched held legs they read **-1 mm (65 cm)**,
**-3 and -9 mm (61 cm)**, while the C arm's own four 58 cm legs span **18-49 mm**,
so the arm-median drop is leg mix (S drew a 53 cm leg whose transit passes
+4 mm). The **achieved** rotation lags ~4 points of the leg later at 0.46 m/s
(`t45/ticks` 0.75-0.86 vs 0.71-0.81; `tilt_end` 61-79 vs 68-88 deg) while the
commanded path is identical.

Two things are named rather than smoothed: **one S `cnp` is not the class** — a
place-reach/landing shortfall with the payload still held (`clean_slip 0.0`,
`clr +23 mm`, `res_end 50.2 mm` against 29-31 mm on healthy legs; the `FINGER
FLOOR` budget binds on **34/34** `place low` rows in *both* arms, so it is a
standing condition) — and **one note text is new to the batch** on a
`grasped=False` leg (`fruit left the pick station during the close (27454 mm)`,
a recycle artifact upstream of any carry leg; its C-arm counterpart reads `fruit
did not follow the gripper`).

**The time saving is real** and is a throughput candidate, not a class fix: the
left place leg goes **405 → 262 ticks (-35 %)**, the episode median **-5..-7 %**,
`|a|cmd` 0.30 → 0.72 with the `place` cone still **0.84-0.90x** of budget, and
the `place low` descent loses 5 % because the faster leg ends **12 mm** lower in
achieved z (the descent re-measures its clearance, so the release geometry and
the landing class are unchanged). P44/P46 already priced that direction's
placement cost.

**The correction to the brief, recorded.** The test was framed as "the knob is
direct-scoped, so the scripted reference cannot move". **It is not
direct-scoped**: `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE` sets the default at the same
`_dynamic_capture_active` site the scripted dynamic line runs, which is exactly
how P44 measured `place0 -135.4 ticks` there. The reference does not move because
**nothing was flipped** and the knob is an `os.environ` read — so no re-record
was owed, and none was made (`8952c320` / `eb697f23` stand).

**Provenance.** The batch spans two commits: seed 77 on `75e980a`, seeds 101/202
on `90f31a6` (another lane committed while the batch ran). `git diff 75e980a
90f31a6` is **two files, both under `logs/`** and **no `src/`/`configs/`/
`scripts/` change**, and every md5 the batch's `header.txt` records is the value
this phase registered against. `logs/` is gitignored and nothing in it is a
control input.

## P75 — the place-leg escape is a pry, not a slide: the pads are driven to their open stop in 9 ticks

**Diagnostic-only phase: one default-off trace, two registered cells, one
declared extension, nothing adopted, no default moved, `configs/*` untouched, no
`src/` change outside the trace.**

P73 closed the transfer height and the rotation, P74 closed the profile's speed
and dwell, and both left one measured fact standing: the place-leg escape's onset
is at `loss_row` = 1-44 % of the leg while the wrist's 45 deg crossing is at
71-86 %, i.e. **the payload is gone before the leg rotates**. Three candidate
mechanisms survived: (a) an **expulsion** (the pads close behind a payload already
past the lip), (b) a **slip at constant `sep`** (a genuine slide through the gap -
what `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md` says the class is), (c) a **command transient** at the
leg boundary. The brief was to settle which, at 1-tick resolution, without adding
a data source.

**The resolution argument came first** (`logs/p75/METHOD.md` §1). The shipped
`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1` rows already carry `onset_row`, `force@onset`, `sep@onset`,
`contacts@onset`, `loss_row`, `sep@loss`, `sep_end`, `clean_slip_max`, `slip_xyz`,
`q_margin`, `q_step_max`, `res_end`; `[seat]` carries 5 samples per grip;
`[diag] carry-assist` carries 3 ticks of the non-coherent branch. What is missing
is not a source but **two references**: the `sep`/force at the leg's *first* tick
(so "did the pads close before the payload moved?" cannot be asked - only "what
was `sep` at the 2 mm crossing"), and any per-tick `tcp_err` (so (c) is not
evaluable at all).

**The instrument** (`tasks.py` `303d025d`, default **0 = off = the shipped path**):
`FRUIT_PLACE_ONSET_TRACE=<ticks>` prints one `[place-trace]` row per tick for the
first `<ticks>` ticks of every `place*` leg, post-step, inside the existing W8-B
carry block - **which it also arms**, so it is self-sufficient (`guard_armed`
gains `or self._place_onset_trace > 0` as a third operand; the pre-P75 two-term
gate is kept as one operand so the four legs that pin it stay valid). Row:
`t`, `|d|` + `d=(x,y,z)` (the hand-frame displacement and its components - `z` is
the tool/finger axis, P61's escape axis), `sep` **measured** beside `gap`
**commanded**, `f=(f0,f1)`, `n`, `tcp_err`, `v_cmd`, `v_ach`, this tick's
`q_margin=…@jN`. **No articulation read**: `rot_now`, `pads`, `_tcp_pos`, `_marg`
and `gap_command` are the block's own; the two additions are `jaw_separation()`
(two finger-prim world poses the loop's own pad-midpoint call already reads) and
one tactile set per traced tick. Pinned by `scripts/241_p75_place_trace_selftest.py`
(selfcheck leg **`14be55ea`**), read by `scripts/242_p75_classify.py`
(**`4f41d983`**).

**The rule was pinned before the runs** (`PREREG.md5` **`479bb896`**): `t_d` = the
first `|d| >= 2 mm` (the diag's own `FRUIT_CARRY_GUARD_TRIGGER`); `t_sep` = the
first measured-separation drop `>= 1 mm`; `t_f` = the first tick the **stronger**
face is below half its leg-start value, or `n == 0`; `t_err` = the first `tcp_err`
20 mm above the leg's **own** steady state (the median of the last third, so a leg
that tracks with a large constant error is not a transient); `t_cmd` = `t_err` or
a `|Δv_cmd| >= 0.10 m/s` step. Class **(c)** if `t_cmd <= t_d - 2`, else **(a)** if
`t_sep`/`t_f <= t_d`, else **(b)**.

**The cells.** `A_77` and `A_101` (15 picks, seed 77/101, `moe_v13s` `61da390a`,
the P66-phase-3 / P71-phase-2 / P73 / P74 cell verbatim plus
`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1 FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1 FRUIT_PLACE_ONSET_TRACE=60`, one claim
each, 532 s and 529 s wall = **35.5 / 35.3 s/pick**, inside the untraced P74 cell's
29.7-35.4 range). **26 place legs traced (12 left)**, and **6 left place-leg
escapes**: 832.5 / 833.6 / 806.8 mm in seed 77 and 895.7 / 844.8 / 851.9 mm in seed
101, **all `cnp`** - `escape <=> cnp` on **12/12** left legs, so `clean_slip_max`
is a faithful proxy here. No rate is quotable (the trace arms the carry block and
adds two reads per traced tick, the direct loop is not reproducible, and six
escapes over two cells is a sample).

**Two sites, one mechanism.** *Inherited at the boundary* (2 of 6, both seed 77):
the place leg's **first** tick already reads `n=1`, one face at **0.00 N**, and
`sep - gap` **+25.3 / +28.5 mm** (the third such leg, +31.2 mm, held at 13.9 mm and
**placed**) - against **+8.5..+14.7 mm** (median 11.0) on the 23 normal legs, **no
overlap**. Those three legs are also the three whose **lift** leg slipped
7.9-11.3 mm - but that second separator is **not clean**: eight of the other nine
left lifts read 0.0-3.2 mm and the ninth (`A_101` ep14) reads **7.5 mm**, 0.4 mm
below the pried set, and its place leg still starts normal (+8.8 mm, two-sided) -
so the wedge fired during `grasp_lift` on those three, the place leg inheriting a
jaw at or near its open stop, but a lift-leg slip alone does not produce that
state.
*Inside the place leg* (4 of 6): `onset_row` **105 / 140 / 142 / 159**, the leg
starting clean (`n=2`, two-sided 4.28-4.95 / 4.89-5.07 N) with **`|d| = 0.0 mm for
the whole 60-tick window** - which is itself the answer to the brief's "the first
~40 ticks": for that family the payload does not begin to go there.

**The one leg the 200-tick extension resolved end-to-end** (`B_101_t200`, 8 of 15
episodes, apple 7.0 cm, left, `cnp`): `|d| = 0.0 mm` and `sep` constant to the
print **for 110 ticks**; **t=111** `|d| 0.3 mm`, `f` 5.03 -> **4.11** N, `sep`
starts **rising**; **t=112** `f = 0.00 N`, `n = 0`, `sep +1.0 mm`; **t=113**
`sep 80.0`; **t=121** `sep = 98.1 mm` = the pads' **mechanical open stop** with
`|d| = 12.6 mm`, while the force servo **closes** the command `68.7 -> 66.7 mm`;
by t=199 `|d| = 247 mm`. So the escape is **(a) expulsion**: the payload is pried
out through a *widening* gap against a closing command. **(b) is refuted** - `sep`
does not hold; the constant-`sep` legs are precisely the held ones. Note what this
does and does not do to `SIM_LIMIT.md`: it does **not** contradict the class (P41's
own ladder shows the pry is force-sensitive - `sep_max` 98.5 -> 43.5 -> 31.2 mm at
10/30/60 N - while the class did not convert), but the sentence "the pads hold and
the payload slides" is **not this interface's mechanism**, and the residue it
names is therefore **pad face geometry** (the new-pad-asset sanction), not force.

**(c) is refuted by measurement, and that closes the profile-continuity lane
before it opened**: **0 of 26** traced legs show a `|Δv_cmd| >= 0.10 m/s` step at
any tick, and at the escape tick every commanded quantity is smooth - `v_cmd`
0.202 -> 0.205 -> 0.207 -> 0.210 over t = 110..113, `tcp_err` on a straight
+0.6 mm/tick ramp - **while a held leg carries the same ramp** (25.1 -> 46+ mm over
the same window) and holds. The 4 legs whose `tcp_err` starts above its own steady
state (+20 mm) are 3 escapes **and 1 hold**. Nothing is registered for a boundary
blend. (`q_margin` at the escape tick reads 0.031-0.036 rad and 0.000-0.009 in the
60-tick cells - the standing saturation P65 measured on 86/86 legs, not the
escape.)

**Named next, post-hoc and not a result**: the four late escapes' *preceding lift*
ended **27.6-58.9 mm behind its own command** (`res_end`) against **8.6-14.6 mm** on
the eight legs that held or were pried at the boundary - no overlap, n = 12 left
legs, 4-vs-8. "Does the lift leg's tracking deficit predict the place leg's
escape?" needs its own PREREG and more seeds, and it does **not** fit a "the
catch-up feeds the slip" story: `|d|` is 0.0 mm through the fastest part of the
catch-up (t = 1-60) and the wedge fires at t = 111 with `v_cmd` already 0.20 m/s.

**Deviations (all in `METHOD.md`).** **A1** (after a 1-episode smoke, before the
measured cells) withdrew a `v_ach >= 1.5*v_cmd + 0.05` clause: on a *clean* leg
`v_ach` reads 0.095-0.099 m/s for t=1..3 while `v_cmd` is 0.000 (the arm closing
the previous leg's 19.4 mm residual), so it fired on every leg. **A2** (after the
cells) took the force reference from the **stronger** face at t=0, because a leg
that starts single-sided would otherwise read "collapsed" against its own zero -
no leg's class changes except by removing that artefact. **A3** labels a leg that
is **already** single-sided with `sep - gap >= 20 mm` at t=0 **`a0`** (inherited
expulsion): on such a leg `sep` *cannot* fall further - it is at the stop - so the
literal in-window test falls through to (b) (pre-A3 seed 77 read `a=2 b=1`, the b
being that artefact; the mechanism verdict is unchanged). **A4** marks the 200-tick
cell as an extension, not a registered cell; it is not counted in the 6 and no rate
comes from it (at 200 ticks the cost is **~3.5 min/episode**, so 200 is a
batch-lane setting, not a casual one).

**No-harm.** `scripts/accept.sh` with the knob unset: **6/9,
`fingerprint: matches`, and its 346 `[fruit]` lines are byte-identical to
`logs/p73/accept_noharm.log`'s 346** - both streams md5 **`d0079a23`**
(`logs/p75/accept_noharm.log`). The exit=1 is the standing rate floor (6/9 = 67 %
< 75 %), this tree's branch since P32. `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS, 0 failures**
(the new `P75 place-onset trace` leg). The scripted path never constructs
`SortingRLEnv` and `_place_onset_trace == 0` leaves `guard_armed`'s boolean
unchanged, so the shipped stream is byte-identical.

## P76 — the pry needs more than 30 N and the payload more than 45 N; the smallest fruit is not crushed at 60 N

**Measurement phase, one default-off `[carry]` field group, nothing adopted, no
default changed, `configs/*` untouched, no commit.** The rule and its four
amendments were pinned before the runs they govern (`logs/p76/PREREG.md`, md5
`62567d8b` → A1 `0397a929` → A2 `5e51d95b` → A3 `af7da4e5` → A4 `1991c5fa`).

**Why it was asked.** `logs/p75/RESULTS.md` settled the left place leg's escape
as an **expulsion**: the payload's hand-frame displacement is 0.0 mm for 110
ticks, the force then collapses in two (5.03 → 4.11 → 0.00 N), and the pads are
driven to their **98.1 mm mechanical open stop in 9 ticks while the force servo
closes the command** (68.7 → 66.7 mm). That makes the class **force-limited in
the pry mode**, which is why P41's ladder deleted `sep_max` (98.5 → 43.5 → 31.2 mm
at 10/30/60 N) - but P41 never ran the **direct** line under a raised cap, its
ladder has a 20 mm-wide hole between 10 and 30 N, and its 60 N rung crushed a
3.7 cm strawberry.

**The instrument.** Five reporting-only fields on the `[carry]` row, inside the
existing `if guard_armed:` block (`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG`, default "0", so unset is
byte-inert): `dia=` (the fruit's class width), `sep_max=…@t<tick>` (the leg's
**extreme** measured pad separation and its tick), `gap@sep_max=` (the commanded
gap at that tick), `sep_min=` (the minimum **loaded** separation) and `fmax=` (the
leg's peak tactile pinch). They exist because `sep@loss` is sampled at the loss
tick and the pads reach the stop **9 ticks later**, so a sample cannot answer "did
this leg pry the pads open". `sep` is `arm.jaw_separation()` - the same link-origin
read as `sep@onset`/`sep@loss`/`sep_end` and P41's offline `sep_max`, so every
number is comparable to the 98.1 mm stop. Pinned by
`scripts/243_p76_sep_selftest.py` (a selfcheck leg).

**The cells.** Eight claimed runs, ~85 min of simulator wall, one claim each: the
ladder **10 (unset) / 15 / 20 / 30 N** at seeds **77 and 101**, plus **two
declared extension cells** (45 and 60 N, seed 77) registered before they ran. The
scenario is the P66-phase-3 / P71-phase-2 / P73 / P74 / P75 cell verbatim and the
instrument is identical in every arm, so the controls cancel.

**Manipulation check, two independent confirmations per rung** - the build print
(`maxForce=<cap>/0.0N`, `F10` = the shipped 10.0 string with nothing written) and
the **live articulation** read-back (`[drive] … joint1/joint2=15.00/0.00 N` on
both arms; absent on `F10` by construction, which is why `F10` is checked as the
unset path instead). The behavioural third leg is the held-leg `force_min` median:
**9.58-9.66 / 14.19-14.67 / 18.22-19.27 / 25.32-29.19 / 39.9 / 53.9 N** at
10/15/20/30/45/60 N (85-99 % of the cap across the two seeds) - the rung **is**
the delivered force (P41's law), so no rung is a stage-only write.

**The result, and the two numbers the phase was for.**

| rung | carry legs | escape legs | at the stop | legs pried to the stop | `sep_max` on escape legs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 N | 55 | 7 | 3 | **5** | 69.6 - **98.2** |
| 15 N | 54 | 4 | 1 | **1** | 24.4 - **98.1** |
| 20 N | 55 | 3 | 0 | **2** | 69.0 - 92.0 |
| 30 N | 54 | 3 | 2 | **2** | 10.2 - **98.3** |
| 45 N (ext) | 26 | 1 | 0 | **0** | 90.4 |
| 60 N (ext) | 26 | **0** | 0 | **0** | - (corpus max **76.7**) |

* **The pry does not stop in 10-30 N.** The same **6.8 cm pear** (left, seed 77 -
  the phase's cleanest control, only the cap differs) reads `place0 sep_max`
  **98.1 / 98.1 / 98.1 / 98.3 mm** at 10/15/20/30 N with `gap@sep_max`
  66.9-69.9 mm, i.e. the pads are **25.7-31.2 mm wider than the command** at every
  low rung - P75's wedge, reproduced. **30 N does not relieve it**, which is
  exactly where this interface departs from P41's scripted ladder (98.5 → 43.5 →
  31.2 there); the direct line's catch hands the fruit over in a pose the jaw can
  wedge against, and the scripted station pick does not.
* **The pads' stop is relieved between 30 and 45 N**: at 45 N **0 of 26** legs pass
  95 mm and the corpus max is **90.4 mm** (92 % of the stop).
* **The payload is not saved by that**: at 45 N the same pear still leaves,
  **829.5 mm**, with the force collapsing to 0.00 N. The pry has only become
  *shallow*.
* **Only 60 N deletes it**: **0/26** pried (corpus max **76.7 mm**, i.e. below the
  fruit's own 68.3 mm + a 7 mm pad shell) and **0/26** escapes, with the pear at
  75.2-75.8 mm and **0.0 mm** slip.
* **Retention is not monotone** (20 N keeps it at 11.0 / 13.6 mm, 30 N ejects it
  96.8 m, 45 N loses it) and every cell is **one draw** (the direct loop conditions
  on rendered frames). Those rows are a **per-instance dose-response, not a rate**;
  what is monotone is the **pad travel**, which is what the phase asked about.

**The crush guard reads 0 legs at the registered C1/C2 in all six cells**, and the
sharpening is itself a finding. C1 was moved to the **loss tick**
(`sep@loss - dia`) before the extensions ran, because a **loaded** `sep_min` also
catches the pads pressing **each other** once a small fruit has gone: two 3.9 cm
strawberry legs at seed 101 read `clean_slip_max` **148 m / 223 m** (recycled
payloads) with the pads at their **10.0 mm closed limit**. On the loss-tick form
the **strawberry** (3.6 cm, the binding class) reads **+0.5 mm** at a **36.1 mm**
span under a **60.16 N** pinch, `force_min` **55.40 N**, held and placed. The
closest low-rung number is **-14.8 mm** (one 3.9 cm instance at 15 N, `fmax`
24.26 N, 496 mm slip) - **0.2 mm inside** the registered -15 mm rule, so the rule
does not fire, and it is a **seating** event (the close landed 24.7 mm inside the
fruit's width) whose depth the cap amplifies. That is why **P41's scripted 60 N
crush does not reproduce on the direct line**: a crush is where the close lands,
not what the cap is.

**Counts (reported, never gated).** placed **20/30, 23/30, 24/30, 24/30, 12/15,
13/15** for 10/15/20/30/45/60 N; left **6/14 → 6/9 → 7/10 → 7/10 → 4/5 → 6/6**;
`cnp` 3/2/1/2/1/0 and never-held 5/5/5/3/2/2. A count across rungs **compares
attractors** (AGENTS §2) and 13-15 attempts per cell is one draw, so none of these
is a rate; the only rate-shaped claim is the per-leg one (**0/26 pried at 60 N vs
5/55 at 10 N**).

**Deviations, each pinned before the run it governs.** **A1**: `sep_min` is the
**loaded** span, because the unconditional minimum fires on every escape leg (a
lost payload lets the servo close the pads onto nothing - `sep_end` 51.9 mm inside
a 68.3 mm fruit); the pre-A1 partial cell is kept as
`direct/DISCARDED_F10_pre_a1.log` and is not counted. **A2**: the 45/60 N cells are
**declared extensions, not rungs** (P75's A4 convention), registered to close the
crush's upper bracket. **A3**: an escape leg must have had a **pinch** (`fmax > 0`)
- one leg's `clean_slip_max` is **308 215 mm** with `fmax = 0.00 N`, a recycled
payload; never-held legs are listed separately. **A4**: the bisection ran because
F60 came back clean on **both** endpoints (A2 had made it conditional on a crush).

**No phase-2 cell is run.** The §5.1 condition is met only at a **declared
extension** (F60), so it licenses a **plan**, not an adoption: 3 seeds x 15 at
60 N with the paired carried-class endpoint, the **two-line and scripted no-harm**
(three references re-recorded and every store's provenance - the expensive item,
since a cap change **moves the branch**: P41's `accept_mf30` DIFFERS on legs
7/9/10 and the two-line `190` gate fails on the fingerprint alone), and the
**sanction**: a raised cap is not physical until a real jaw is anchored to it, so
the deliverable stays **"the sim needs 60 N per finger joint (a ~54-60 N pinch); a
real jaw would have to deliver 60 N"** and the owner decides.

**No-harm.** `scripts/accept.sh` with every knob unset: **6/9,
`fingerprint: matches`, and its 346 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical (stream md5
`d0079a23`) to `logs/p73/accept_noharm.log`** (`logs/p76/accept_noharm_full.log`;
the new fields need `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1` and the scripted path never sets it). The exit=1 is the standing rate floor (6/9 = 67 %
< 75 %), this tree's branch since P32. `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS, 0 failures**
(the new `P76 pry/crush fields` leg).

**Pins**: `tasks.py` **`9d5824ef`**, `rl_env.py` (the `TASKS_MD5` metadata-only
follow), `scripts/243_p76_sep_selftest.py` **`fc0e738e`**, `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**`84f77dcb`**, `logs/p76/p76_report.py` **`544fc6f2`**; `configs/motion_reference.json`
**`8952c320`** and `..._twoline.json` **`eb697f23`** both untouched, no reference
re-recorded, ckpt `moe_v13s` **`61da390a`**. Evidence
`logs/p76/{PREREG.md,PREREG.md5,RESULTS.md,header.txt,run_p76.sh,p76_report.py,

## P77 — the 60 N clamp at three seeds: the count converts, the escape class does not

**Evidence phase (owner-chosen), nothing adopted, no default changed, no `src/`
or `configs/` edit, no commit.** The rule was pinned before any run
(`logs/p77/PREREG.md`, md5 **`d31c3e4a`**) and the two arms are **C** = the
shipped 10 N (`FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE` **unset**) and **T** = `=60`, interleaved
by seed (77 C→T, 101 T→C, 202 C→T), **seeds 77/101/202 x 15 picks**, one claim
per cell, the P66-phase-3 / P71-phase-2 / P73 / P74 / P75 / P76 scenario
verbatim, `moe_v13s` `61da390a`, `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1 FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1` in
**both** arms. Six cells + two pricing runs, 68 min of simulator wall.

**The honesty frame, which the report carries first.** 60 N per joint is
**jaw-feasible** - a 2F-85-class jaw covers 20-235 N - but it **would bruise a
3.6 cm berry in reality**, and this simulator has **no bruise model, no damage
model and no flesh-compliance model**. A clean read is therefore a statement
about **geometry and retention**, never about fruit quality. That is why the cell
is a **sensitivity** and not a decision to ship.

**Manipulation check, three legs per cell.** (1) the build print
`maxForce=10.0/0.0N` (C, the shipped string, nothing written) or
`maxForce=60.0/0.0N` + `FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE=60 N -> openarm_left_finger_joint1=60.0
…` (T); (2) the **live articulation** read-back
`[drive] … joint1/joint2=60.00/0.00 N` on both arms, and the manifest's
`physics.finger_maxforce` = `null` / `60.0` with `readback_matches: true`;
(3) the behavioural **held-leg `force_min` median 9.72 / 9.96 / 9.71 N** in C
against **56.31 / 53.41 / 52.08 N** in T (87-94 % of the cap, P41's law). All six
cells are evaluable; `p77_report.py --check` exits 0 with 166 `[carry]` rows and
15 episodes in every cell.

**The primary: the left's placed count and its `cnp` class.**

| seed | C left placed | C `cnp` | T left placed | T `cnp` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 77 | 3/6 | 2 | 6/7 | 1 |
| 101 | 4/10 | 4 | 5/6 | 1 |
| 202 | 4/5 | 1 | 6/7 | 1 |
| **pooled** | **11/21 = 52.4 %** | **7** | **17/20 = 85.0 %** | **3** |

Fisher exact on left placed vs not: **p = 0.043**; on `cnp` vs placed:
p = 0.144. Left never-held 3 → 0. **The run level is 3/3 seeds** (+3/+1/+2
attempts) - and at N=3 the one-sided sign test's **minimum attainable p is
0.125**, so it is quoted as a ceiling, not as confirmation. **Class-standardised
at C's species mix: 0.524 → 0.927** (in the same direction as the raw pooled
0.524 → 0.850), so the delta is not a class-draw artifact; per class kiwi
4/11 → 4/4, peach 1/2 → 4/5, pear 3/4 → 5/7, apple 1/2 → 2/2, orange 2/2 → 1/1.
**The pairing that can be defended** is `(seed, arm=left, species, diameter to
0.1 cm)` greedy 1:1: only **11 of C's 21** left attempts pair, **10 are
unpairable** (a fruit the other arm never drew), both placed 5 / C-only 0 /
T-only 6, exact McNemar **p = 0.031**. It is a **descriptor**, not the primary:
the fruit presented depends on earlier outcomes (a post-treatment variable), and
a same-configuration replay proves no instance pairing exists here - **C_77
against P76's F10_77 agrees on 2 of 15 episodes and diverges at episode 2** (a
3.6 cm strawberry in P76's cell, a 6.0 cm peach here).

**The mechanism, and the pre-registered bar it fails.** Left carry legs **38
(C) / 40 (T)**; escape legs (`clean_slip_max > 100 mm` **with a pinch**, P74's
count) **7 → 3**; legs **pried** to the 98.1 mm stop (`sep_max >= 95`) **4 → 1**;
never-held 2 → 0. Right: 43/45 legs, **0 escapes, 0 pries, 0 `cnp`** in both
arms. So **M1 FAILS** (3 is 43 % of 7, not <= 1/3), **M2 PASSes** (25 %),
**M3 passes** (0 crush legs in T), **M4 passes** (C's escape set is non-empty) →
the composite **"MECHANISM: DOES NOT CONVERT"**, while **N5/N6/N7 all PASS** →
**"COUNT: CONVERTS"**. Both statements are true and the report quotes them
together: the cap **more than halves** the class and deletes three quarters of
its pries, and that is a real count gain - but the class is not closed.

**The residue is a different mode, and that is the phase's finding.** The
discriminator is the **pad opening beyond the fruit's own width**
(`sep_max - dia`), and the two arms separate cleanly:

| arm | leg (all left `place0`) | `sep_max` | `dia` | `sep_max - dia` | `fmax` | slip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | pear 6.1 | 89.8 | 61.3 | +28.5 | 14.95 | 740.0 |
| C | peach 5.8 | **98.1** | 58.2 | +39.9 | 11.38 | 918.0 |
| C | apple 7.0 | **98.1** | 69.6 | +28.5 | 16.89 | 843.4 |
| C | kiwi 6.7 | 85.7 | 66.8 | +18.9 | 14.65 | 811.7 |
| C | kiwi 5.3 | 66.8 | 53.3 | +13.5 | 13.19 | 858.7 |
| C | kiwi 6.7 | **98.1** | 66.8 | +31.3 | 15.28 | 709.0 |
| C | kiwi 5.7 | 80.4 | 57.1 | +23.3 | 12.90 | 828.6 |
| **T** | pear 6.8 | 76.2 | 68.3 | **+7.9** | 57.83 | 834.7 |
| **T** | pear 6.6 | 69.3 | 65.9 | **+3.4** | 58.79 | 844.5 |
| **T** | peach 6.2 | **98.1** | 61.9 | +36.2 | **64.52** | 782.9 |

At 10 N **all 7** escapes leave through a **13.5-39.9 mm** opening (3 at the
travel stop): the radial **pry** P75 measured. At 60 N **2 of 3** leave through a
**3.4 / 7.9 mm** opening - the pads essentially closed on the fruit - and the
payload walks out **along the tool axis**, which is P61's measured direction
(leg-frame mean unit `(-0.351, +0.240, +0.905)`, 25.2 deg off the tool axis).
**Force resists the radial pry; it does not resist the axial slide.** The third
T escape is a **full pry** (peach 6.2, `sep_max` 98.1, `fmax` **64.52 N** - above
the 60 N cap's delivered level), so 60 N buys a 4x reduction in pries, not a
guarantee. A control pry that **recovered** is named too: a kiwi 6.7 reads
`sep_max` 98.4 and slips 13.1 mm, so `sep_max >= 95` alone is not an outcome.

**P76's single draw does not reproduce, and that is the correction.** P76 read
**0/26 pried and 0/26 escaped** at 60 N (seed 77, one cell) and concluded "the
pry is deleted". At 40 left carry legs over three seeds the same cap reads
**1 pried and 3 escaped**, and the **same 6.8 cm pear** P76 saw held
(`place0 sep_max` 75.2, slip 0.0 mm) **escapes here** (76.2, 834.7 mm). P76's own
reading rule - every cell is one draw - applies to P76's own 60 N cell.

**The strawberry and the crush guard.** C **5/5** strawberry legs placed, T
**6/6 real legs** placed (`sep_max - dia` **-0.7 .. +6.2 mm**), and the 3.6 cm
fruit is held at a **36.7 mm** span under **52.6-54.2 N** - the P76 extension
read at three seeds. **C1 (`sep@loss - dia <= -15 mm`) and C2
(`force_min >= 35 N` on an escape leg) fire on 0 legs in 0/6 cells.** The one
non-placed T strawberry leg is the **recycled-payload artifact** (T_101:
`fmax` **0.00 N**, `clean_slip_max` **160 769.6 mm**, `sep@loss` 10.0 mm), which
P76's A3 rule excludes and which is named in the report rather than dropped.

**Guards.** The right is **not worse**: 21/24 → 22/25 placed, `cnp` 0 → 0,
never-held 3 → 3, escapes 0 → 0, **no new reason**. Failure ledger: the only
**reason** string on any failure in either arm is `fruit fell off the line`
(C 3, T 2 - the supply class); the `cnp` legs carry no reason note and are read
from `grasped`/`placed`. Landing class: `did not land` 0, `discharged` 0 in both
arms. Arm mix (arm = grade = lane): C 6/10/5, T 7/6/7 left of 15 → 21 vs 20
pooled, so the count delta is not a mix artifact. Cycle ticks (cell medians)
1779/1765/1795 vs 1770/1776/1753 = **-0.5 %**: the cap costs no cycle time.

**The price of an adoption (report only, nothing re-recorded).** **P1**, the
scripted acceptance at 60 N: **6/10** against the archive's **6/9**, **378 vs
346 `[fruit]` lines** (md5 `4d89c743` vs `d0079a23`; **57** identical with the
print-only rows dropped), the **first physics-line difference on attempt 0's
descent** (`|a|max` 2.061 vs 2.060 m/s²) and the **first outcome difference at
attempt 0 itself** (60 N: `grasped=True placed=True lift=+0.411 m force=60.05 N`;
10 N: `grasped=True placed=False lift=+0.138 m force=9.98 N`), and
**`fingerprint: DIFFERS`** from `configs/motion_reference.json` (`8952c320`,
which has 9 legs against this run's 10, so *any* 10-attempt run differs - but
legs 2-9 move too). **P2**, the two-line at 60 N: **8/10 = 80 %** at its own
0.60 floor with all ten descents inside their speed budgets (worst `|v|max`
0.129 against 0.160-0.161), and the `190` gate **FAILs on the fingerprint alone**
against `eb697f23` (legs 3-10 move; leg 6 descends in 92 samples at 0.129 m/s
against 88 at 0.109). Two of 18 carry legs still slip >400 mm (1485.7 and
484.2 mm, the latter at a 9.12x reported cone), but the **shipped-cap** P71
two-line has **three of its own** (805.2 / 332.9 / 112 673 mm), so that is not a
cap effect and **60 N does not make the two-line escape-free**. A flip therefore
owes **both motion references, a scripted re-baseline and every store's
provenance** - for a class that shrinks rather than closes.

**No-harm.** The phase is **env-only**: no `src/`, `configs/`, reference or
checkpoint change, so `scripts/accept.sh` at the shipped cap is untouched by
construction and both references stand (`8952c320` / `eb697f23`).
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` at the close of the phase: **PASS, 0 failures, 1 skipped**
(`logs/p77/selfcheck.log`).

## P78 — the clamp, scoped to the site: the containment is total, the dose is P77's mechanism, the count is a direction

**One shipped change - a new default-off knob and its runtime write - and
nothing adopted.** The question was mechanical: P77's global 60 N count win owes
**both motion references, a scripted re-baseline and every store**, because the
cap is a per-joint drive property written at build time on both arms of every
presentation; but P77 §2 measured that **every escape and every pry, in both
arms, is a left `place0` leg** (C 7/38 escaped and 4/38 pried, T 3/40 and 1/40,
right 0 and 0 on 43/45). The class is a **site**, so the force can be one.
Two registrations, both pinned before their runs: `logs/p78/PREREG.md`
(**`01077e1a`**, the knob + the seed-77 ladder + the blast-radius gate) and
`logs/p78/PREREG_EXT.md` (**`4a3b8081`**, the scoped-60 extension at seeds
101/202, pinned *after* the S30 three-seed read and before those cells - a
declared extension, the P76 A2 / P77 A2 convention, said so in its own first
line).

**1. The runtime write works, and it is proven three ways - this was the phase's
gate, not an assumption.** Static: `Articulation.set_dof_max_efforts`
(`isaacsim.core.experimental.prims`) has a **tensor-backend** branch that calls
the view's `set_dof_max_forces`, which writes the **live** model's
`joint_effort_limit` and then `notify_model_changed(JOINT_DOF_PROPERTIES)`
(`isaacsim.physics.newton/.../tensors/articulation_view.py:1364-1385`, `:108-114`
- on this build the engine is `physx` with the `torch` backend,
`scene.start`). That is exactly the API `scene.apply_finger_maxforce`'s own
docstring names as the one that "act[s] on a live view", and `tasks`'
`arms[side].robot` **is** that `Articulation`. Empirical, and this is what
counts: a 2-pick smoke (`logs/p78/smoke_60.log`) prints
`[drive] left place0 finger cap raise: 10.00 -> 60.00 N (readback 60.00 N)` and
the restore row, the **delivered** `place0` force reads **58.16 N**, and the
**same run's** `grasp_lift` reads **10.01 N** - i.e. the physics moved and it
moved **only on the scoped leg**. Across the ladder the place-leg **peak** force
is **29.75 / 44.99 / 56.08 N at caps 30 / 45 / 60** (99 / 100 / 93 %) against a
control of 10.69 N, while `grasp_lift` sits at **9.10-9.97 N** in every armed
cell. So the pick is untouched by construction *and* by measurement.

**2. The knob, and the containment that makes the blast radius zero.**
`FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE_SCOPE=place-left` (+ `..._SCOPED=<N>`, default 60) is
resolved by `rl_env.resolve_finger_cap_scope`, a pure function with a strict
table: **any presentation but `direct` -> `(None, None)` before any value is
read**; `direct` + unset -> `None`; `direct` + an **explicit
`FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE`** -> `None` (the global knob wins, the two cannot
stack); `direct` + `place-left` -> `{"left": cap}`; **any other token, a
non-number, a non-finite value or `<= 0` raises** (P44/P45/P52/P53's rule: a
typo must not read as a null). The task gets it as a caller-owned kwarg
(`PickAndPlaceTask(finger_cap_scope=...)`, the `lift_dz`/`lift_climb` pattern)
and `tasks.finger_cap_scope_for` - the **only** site resolver - arms the
**`place*` leg only**, per side. `_carry` became a **wrapper**: it raises the
left drive's cap through `set_dof_max_efforts` on `joint1` (never the drive-less
`joint2` mimic) and restores the cap the leg **found** in a **`finally`**, so an
exception inside the leg cannot leave it raised; the leg body is `_carry_leg`
(and `237`'s locator follows the body, every assertion unchanged). The manifest
carries `physics.finger_cap_scope`, and `finger_drive.readback_matches` is a
**real structural guard** here: it is read after the last restore, so a leaked
cap would read `false` (it reads `true`, every joint at the shipped 10.0 / 0.0).

**3. The blast radius - the deliverable - is zero, measured with the scope
armed on both scripted paths.** **B1**: `scripts/accept.sh` under
`FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE_SCOPE=place-left ..._SCOPED=60` reads **346/346 `[fruit]`
lines, md5 `d0079a23`** - **byte-identical** to `logs/p76/accept_noharm_full.log`
- with **`fingerprint: matches`**; the only failing clause is the standing
**6/9 < 75 %** rate on this tree's P32 branch, and **no scope row is printed at
all**. **B2**: the two-line under the same env reads **7/10 = 70 %**,
**`fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference_twoline.json`** and
**`190: PASS`**. **B3**: both references **unchanged** (`8952c320` / `eb697f23`),
nothing re-recorded. B1/B2 are **import/structure guards** and are documented as
such - the scripted entries never construct `SortingRLEnv` - while the
*substantive* proof that the write is real and leg-scoped is the direct line's
own §1 evidence. Both statements are needed; neither substitutes for the other.

**4. The dose. Seed 77 screen first, and it ranked the doses wrongly - P74's
lesson, again.** Ladder cells (left placed / left escapes / left pried / right /
cycle): **C 3/5 · 2 · 1 · 9/10 · 1750**; **S30 3/4 · 0 · 0 · 8/11 · 1790**;
**S45 3/6 · 2 · 1 · 8/9 · 1780**; **S60 4/4 · 0 · 0 · 9/11 · 1787**. Two rungs
passed D1-D5, so the registered economical rule sent the **lower** (S30) to
seeds 101/202 - and at three seeds its 6-leg "0 escapes" became **4/32**.
**Three-seed pooled reads (C / S30 / S60): left placed 10/18 · 12/17 (p = 0.49) ·
11/16 (p = 0.50); left escapes 8/36 · 4/32 (50 % of C) · 4/31 (50 %); left
pried 3/36 · 0/32 · 1/31; right 25/27 · 22/28 · 25/29; cycle 1774 · 1804
(+1.7 %) · 1789 (+0.8 %).** So **no rung meets its bar** (S30 fails D2 and D4,
S60 fails D2 and G7's crush leg) and nothing is adopted - but the **mechanism is

removes the radial pry and leaves the axial walk**, which is `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md`
and P61's geometry. The extension's **P5 did not fire**: a place-leg-only cap
that cannot touch the pick still moves the left count in P77's direction, so the
**place leg carries the direction**; only the magnitude is unresolved at this n.

**5. Two negatives that matter, recorded rather than smoothed.** (a) **S45's
6.8 cm pear pries at a delivered 46.05 N** (`sep_max` 95.6 mm) - more than four
times the shipped force does not stop that instance, the P76/P77 "reduces, does

seeds did not draw it). It fails the registered per-cell D3/G7 as written and is

`sep@loss - dia` values in the S30 cells are the **never-held artifact** class
(`fmax = 0.00`, 181 997 / 251 284 mm slips, P76 A3) and are excluded by the

**6. A recorded PREREG correction (the manipulation statistic).** Criterion (2)

The condition's intent - "did the physics move, not just the attribute" - is met

### P79: the pick half of the clamp - the count is not the lift's, and the one leg no token can reach is the close

`logs/p79/`, 2026-10-31, default off, nothing adopted, no default changed, no commit,
`configs/*` untouched. Registration `logs/p79/PREREG.md` md5 **`0cdfd227`** (pinned
before the first cell) + one recorded deviation **A1** (§9; amended file `afde5127`).
Direct line, `moe_v13s` `61da390a`, the P66-phase-3 / P71-phase-2 / P73 / P74 / P75 /
P76 / P77 / P78 cell verbatim, 15 picks per cell, seeds 77/101/202, arms interleaved
within a seed, 85 min for nine cells.

**The question.** `logs/p77/RESULTS.md` measured the only count win on this tree - left
placed **11/21 -> 17/20** (p = 0.043) under a **global** 60 N build-time cap - and its
price (both arms of every presentation: the scripted acceptance moves at attempt 0, so
both motion references, a scripted re-baseline and every store). `logs/p78/RESULTS.md`
contained it to a runtime cap on the left's `place*` legs at **zero blast radius** and
reproduced the mechanism (pries 3/36 -> 1/31) but not the count (+1 attempt, p = 0.50).
The one class that moved in P77 and not in P78 is P77's left `never-held` **3 -> 0**, a
**pick** class (`fmax == 0` on the carry; the pads never touched the fruit) - and the
global cap also raised the **close** and the **lift**, which the place cap raised not
at all. So: is the count the pick's, and at what force?

**The token.** `FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE_SCOPE=grasp-left` (+ `..._SCOPED=<N>`, default 60)
arms P78's machinery unchanged on the left arm's single `grasp_lift` leg. The scope dict
is now keyed **`"<side>:<legs>"`** (`{"left:grasp"}` / `{"left:place"}`), so the two
tokens are *disjoint leg classes by construction* - `finger_cap_scope_for` resolves the
class from the leg name, and neither token can arm the other's legs. Default off,
`direct` only (`resolve_finger_cap_scope` returns `(None, None)` for every other
presentation **before** it reads a value), an explicit `FRUIT_FINGER_MAXFORCE` still
wins, strict parsing, `_carry`'s `try`/`finally` restore of the cap the leg **found**,
one write site. `scripts/244` extended (45 -> **72** checks: both tokens' resolution
rows, the disjoint-class property in both directions, the label/legs helpers derived
from the dict's own keys, the single-site counts). `scene.finger_physics_provenance`
now also records the exact `sites`.

**The site proof is exact, three ways.** (1) One `[drive] left grasp_lift finger cap
raise: 10.00 -> <N> N (readback <N>)` + restore per left lift leg - **15/15** legs at
30 N and **17/17** at 60 N - and **zero** raise/restore rows on any `place*` leg or the
right arm across the six armed cells (`grep 'finger cap' logs/p79/direct/*.log | grep -v
grasp_lift | grep -v 'scope:'` = **0**). (2) The delivered pinch follows: left
`grasp_lift` `fmax` medians pooled **10.02 -> 30.09 -> 57.48 N**, `force_min` **9.75 ->
29.43 -> 49.14**. (3) The place does **not** follow: left `place*` `fmax` pooled
**10.02 / 10.05** against the control's **10.07**, and the manifest carries
`physics.finger_cap_scope.sites = {"left:grasp": <cap>}` with
`finger_drive.readback_matches: true` in every armed cell (that field is built *after*
the last restore, so a leaked cap would read `false`).

**The count is flat at the recorded dose.** Left placed **C 11/20 = 0.550 -> G60 9/17 =
0.529** (Fisher **p = 1.0000**; per-seed deltas **0 / -4 / +2**), `cnp` **7 = 7**,
`never-held` 1 vs 2 (one episode). The registered P1a (`+3`) and P1c (`rate >= 0.75`)
fail; the verdict is **NO-PICK**.

**What *does* move is the lift leg's own pinch integrity.** Left `grasp_lift` legs that
**lose a pad** during the leg (`min_contacts <= 1`, P75/P61's state): **6/20 -> 2/15
(30 N) -> 1/17 (60 N)** (60 N vs C p = 0.0975), `sep_end - gap_start` p50 10.5 -> 9.2 mm.
So the H-pick-b path (the lift ends cleanly -> the place leg inherits a good pinch, P75
measured 2 of 6 escapes as inherited) is *working at the leg*, and the class it should
feed - `cnp` - does not convert at 60 N. That is the phase's mechanism finding: **the
lift's pinch integrity is not the binding term for the placed count.**

**30 N is where the direction is, and it is a dose, not a result.** G30 reads left
**12/15 = 0.800** (p = 0.163; per-seed **+3 / -1 / +1**), `cnp` **2**, lost-a-face **2**,
place escapes **2/14** - all toward P77 - but it misses P1a's `+3` bar (12 < 14) and it
sits **below** the global arm's dose, so it is not a reproduction of P77's win. P78's
place arm at 30 N read the same shape (**12/17 = 0.706**, p = 0.49). **The dose is not
monotone** (30 N 0.706 / 0.800 against 60 N 0.688 / 0.529), and a non-monotone dose is
the opposite of the evidence that a force is the actuator - at n ~ 15-20 left attempts
per arm, **no force above the control's own 10 N is identified**.

**Where the win is, then - the register's answer.** The three controls agree tightly
(**0.524 / 0.556 / 0.550**; pooled **32/59 = 0.542**) and the two scoped 60 N arms
bracket them (**0.688** place, **0.529** grasp; pooled 20/33 = 0.606). Only the global
arm reads **0.85**. The global cap is the only arm that raised the **close**, and the
close is **not a `_carry` leg** - `_carry` is only ever called with `place{i}` and
`grasp_lift`, so *no token can reach the close by construction*. P77's `never-held`
3 -> 0 also had to happen there: a never-held carry leg has `fmax == 0` (no contact
was ever made) and a lift-phase force cannot create contact the close did not make.
**The named next spend is a `close-left` scope at the close's own site** (its own
registration, a different site), not another lift or place dose.

**Guards.** Right placed **21/25 -> 26/30 -> 25/28** (p = 0.69; 0 right escapes at
60 N); cycle **1751 / 1773 / 1772** ticks (14.6 / 14.8 / 14.8 s/attempt); crush guards
**0** in all nine cells. Left place escapes **6/18 -> 2/14 (30 N) -> 7/16 (60 N)** at an
*unchanged* force - the 60 N rise is a branch draw, not a cap effect. **The strawberry
is a scope limit, not a clean bill**: **all 30 of the batch's berry legs (nine cells,
every one grade B or C) were presented to the right arm** - the direct env sets the arm
from the grade, so no A-grade berry was drawn - and the left-only token never touched a
berry. A 60 N pick on a 3.6 cm fruit is therefore **not exposed here** (P76 measured it
on the *global* cap and found no crush; a real jaw would bruise it), so the berry risk of
this token is **untested**.

**Blast radius, re-proved with the scope armed.** `scripts/accept.sh` -> **346/346
`[fruit]` lines byte-identical** to `logs/p76/accept_noharm_full.log` (md5
**`d0079a23`**), `fingerprint: matches`, and **0** scope rows printed (the FAIL is the
standing 6/9 rate-only branch since P71). Two-line -> **7/10**, `fingerprint: matches`,
`190_twoline_gate.sh` **PASS** against `eb697f23`. No reference re-recorded.

**One recorded deviation (A1).** The registered per-cell `place* fmax <= 11.25 N` clause
fired in **1 of 6** armed cells (`G30_202`, 11.37 N) and the leg behind it **escaped**
(`place0 fmax=12.13`, `force_min=0.00`, `loss_row=114`, slip 940.1 mm) at the **shipped**
10 N cap: `fmax` is a peak contact transient that exceeds the drive cap on single legs
even at 10 N (this batch's own control reads **35.53 N** on a right `grasp_lift`; P78's
control read 79.43 / 134.29 / 155.12). The clause compared a transient against a *pooled
median* and could not separate a re-clamp from an escape, so P3 is gated on the
**structural** rows (zero place/right raises) plus the **pooled** force (10.05 vs 10.07)
and the band is printed beside it. **No verdict moves** - P1 fails independently. The
correction is appended to `PREREG.md` §9 (pin `0cdfd227` pre-run, `afde5127` amended).

**Pins.** `tasks.py` **`e8dfa6d8`**, `rl_env.py` **`7d26eb5b`** (the `TASKS_MD5`
metadata-only follow), `scene.py` **`07d6fdad`**, `scripts/244_p78_scope_selftest.py`
**`50fde0fa`**, `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **`dd4bf41a`**; `configs/motion_reference.json`

### P80: the cell's throughput today, and the two levers priced - the two-line is a 1.87x sim clock and a 1.02x wall wash, the union a cycle-time lever

`logs/p80/`, 2026-11-01, **measurement only - nothing adopted, no default changed, no
commit, `configs/` untouched**. Registration `logs/p80/PREREG.md` md5
**`b57e979a`** (pinned before any run, unchanged). Owner directive: the left-arm lane is
closed; the work moves to throughput. Scripted line, shipped scenario, `ATTEMPTS=20`,
`SEED=5` (then 6), one claim per run, one instrumentation set on every 20-attempt arm
(`FRUIT_MOTION_REPORT=1 FRUIT_CYCLE_REPORT=1`).

**What moved under the old numbers, and what did not.** P71's rails flip is the only
shipping change inside this battery's contrast: the P43 park, the P58 supply profile and
the P71 lift flip are `SortingRLEnv`-only, so the scripted line still lifts to 0.36 m
and still runs the v9 scattered supply (`PREREG` §0 says this up front, so nothing here
can be read as a test of the low lift). Two 10-attempt gate arms locate the tree: **G-S10
reads `fingerprint: matches` `8952c320` with 346/346 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical to
`logs/p71/accept_rails_none.log`** (6/9, the standing rate-only FAIL at 0.75), and
**G-T10 reads `190: PASS` + `matches` `eb697f23` with 423/423 non-camera lines
byte-identical to `logs/p71/twoline/none.log`** (7/10, 9.2 s/attempt). So the two-line
record was one draw and today's tree reproduces it exactly; the 20-attempt arm extends a
bit-identical branch rather than landing in a new attractor.

**Today's cell (shipped single arm, seed 5).** 19 executed attempts of 20 slots (one
starved), **12 placed = 63.2 %, 15.10 s/attempt, batch span 345.7 s sim, wall 478.0 s =
25.2 s/pick, inter-placement interval 26.72 s mean / 36.90 s p90, 2.25 placed/min on the
placement window and 2.08 on the batch span.** The interval is **bimodal** and that is
the mechanism: 17.5-19.6 s between two consecutive placements, 35.6-38.2 s across one
failed attempt, i.e. **26.7 s = 4.8 s idle + 1.45 attempts x 15.1 s** (186's own
decomposition). All seven failures are `grasped, not placed`, split **left 1/7 vs right
11/12** - the left's 6-of-7 is *not* the lateral tail (failed `fruit_x` 0.215-0.365
against the one placement at 0.305) and not the station (identical pick-pose jaw,
`x=0.342`, residual 43.1 mm, on every left attempt), and the wait-start `dy` does not
separate the classes either.

**The two-line's first measurement on the shipped tree.** 20 attempts, **16 placed =
80 %, 9.70 s/attempt, interval 10.77 / 18.00 s, 5.57 window / 4.96 batch placed/min =
2.48x / 2.38x**, lock-on **3.83 s left / 4.54 s right** (p90 6.80 / 9.60, 19 retry polls
each), idle **18 % / 21 %**, 44 starved half-second polls and **zero lost slots**. The
per-arm attempt span is **15.0-15.6 s - the single arm's 15.09**: the pipelining
*overlaps* two attempts, it does not make one faster. The 2.38x batch ratio is exactly
**1.88x of clock x 1.27x of count**, and the count half is the *package*, not the
scheduler: the two-line runs its own W3 dense-sheet supply (`wave=on ... grades
A:0.375,B:0.375,C:0.25`) and its own pure grade routing, and its left arm places 9/10
where the single arm's places 1/7 on the same station pose and overlapping delivered-x
band. So the 2.48x is what a **default flip would deliver** (supply and routing come
with it) and **not** "the scheduler doubles throughput".

**The seed-6 pair is where the count half collapses.** `pick_mover.py` picked the
two-line (interval -59.7 % vs the union's +5.0 %), so `S6 + T6` were spent: **S6 13/19
(68.4 %), 15.00 s/attempt, interval 26.12 s, window 2.30** - the single-arm baseline is
*stable* across seeds - and **T6 10/20 (50 %), 9.70 s/attempt, interval 19.34 s, window
3.10 -> 1.35x**. So the **clock factor replicates exactly (1.88x / 1.87x)** while the
**count factor swings 1.27x -> 0.73x**: the count advantage was +4 at seed 5 and -3 at
seed 6, and pooled the two lines place the **same** amount (26/40 = 65.0 % vs 25/38 =
65.8 %). T6's class split is P51's acquisition class (5 never-grasped + 5 cnp) with the
right arm starving (50.3 s mean interval, 30 % idle) on that sheet draw.

**Wall vs sim is the other half of the answer, and it cancels the clock.**
`logs/p80/stamp.py` stamps every line through a `tee` (the plain log stays canonical), so
wall/pick is measured, not inferred: **S20 478.0 s -> 25.2 s/pick at wall/sim 1.38;
T20 497.2 s -> 24.9 s/pick at 2.57; S6 25.2 s at 1.40; T6 23.8 s at 2.47; U20 22.1 s at
1.34; V20 21.9 s at 2.52.** The scheduler's wall cost per simulated second is **1.86x**
the single arm's, so a sim ratio r becomes a wall ratio r/1.86: **wall/pick is flat
(1.01x / 1.06x, pooled 1.03x)** and the wall placed rate is **1.28x then 0.77x - 1.02x
pooled**. The 1.86x is **the scheduler's, not the supply's**, and it is discriminated:
on the W6-B battery, which ran both lines on the *same* dense patch sheet, the single arm
reads 1.25x and the two-line 2.32x (app clock, boot 45 s); today's pair reads 1.38 vs
2.57 - the same multiplier, two trees, two supplies - so more live bodies are not it
(the single arm on the 20-body sheet is as cheap as on the 6.6-body line). **Pooled over
the two seeds: sim placed/min 2.18 -> 4.04 (1.86x), wall placed/min 1.57 -> 1.60
(1.02x).** The transferable statement is the sim one (1.87x); on this machine the harness
pays it back.

**The speed union (`FRUIT_SPEED_ALL=1`, P44's S1+S2+S3) is a cycle-time lever, not a
throughput lever.** Single arm: **15.10 -> 13.40 s/attempt (-1.70 s, bar 1.0: PASS)**,
exactly P44's three blocks (place -0.75, release -0.84, lift -0.24 = -1.83 predicted vs
-1.71 measured), **wall/pick -12 %** - but the **interval rises to 28.04 s (+4.9 %)**, the
placement window falls to 2.14 (-4.9 %) and the batch rate to 1.82 (-12.6 %), because the
placed count falls to 10/20. That fall is **not a new grip class**: 9 `cnp` + 1 `fruit did
not follow the gripper`, and the pooled drop is largely the grade draw (left share 37 % ->
60 %; arm-standardised the union is **69.3 % vs 63.2 %**). On the two-line the same
lever reads **9.70 -> 8.70 s/attempt (-12 % wall/pick)** with the interval +3.9 % and the
window -3.8 % (13/20, 5 never-grasped + 2 cnp). So: **the clock pays everywhere, the
placed-per-minute does not, at this seed.**

**The decisions (PREREG §4).** (a) Today: **2.25 placed/min window / 2.08 batch, interval
26.72 s / 36.90 s p90, 25.2 s wall/pick.** (b) The two-line **meets the standing 1.25x bar
on the sim clock at both seeds (2.48x, 1.35x)** with a **reproducible 1.87x clock**, but
its **count is a seed draw** (+4 / -3, pooled equal) and its **wall rate is 1.02x**, so the
recommendation is **keep it opt-in unless the objective is simulated-time throughput** -
and on a cell that did not pay this harness it would realize the 1.87x (a 1.89x wall
gain). (c) The union **pays on the clock (-1.70 s / -1.00 s, -12 % wall per pick) and does
not pay on throughput** (+5 % interval, -5 % window); its cost is P51's closed class, so
the count is reported and not gated. (d) Wall is **28 % harness on the single arm and 61 %
on the two-line** (`1 - 1/1.38`, `1 - 1/2.57`).

**Not claimed.** No scheduler-only control (that needs `FRUIT_SUPPLY_WAVE=0` + the single
arm's mix — a different scenario with its own reference); one seed for U/V (R3 spends the
pair on the mover); the direct line unmeasured here (its last number is P59's 26/45 with
the same harness-dominated ~35 s/pick); two recycled-payload slip artifacts in T10
reported, not gated (P76-A3's class). The battery's own exit is `fail=1` from **G-S10's
standing rate-only acceptance FAIL**, not from a broken arm.

### P81: the two-line's scheduler vs its supply package - the net 1.88x clock is the scheduler's, the feed and the overlap strength are the package's

`logs/p81/`, 2026-11-01, **measurement only - nothing adopted, no default changed, no
commit, `configs/` untouched**. Registration `logs/p81/PREREG.md` md5 **`461e1709`**
(pinned before any run, unchanged). The owner's cell: P80 measured the two-line at
**16/20, 9.70 s/attempt, 5.57 window / 4.96 batch placed/min = 2.48x / 2.38x** and
decomposed it as **1.88x clock x 1.27x count**, with the clock the scheduler's and the
count the *package's* (its W3 dense-sheet supply + balanced mix). P81 removes the
package and asks whether the **clock** survives: `FRUIT_BIARM=1 FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE=1
FRUIT_SUPPLY_WAVE=0` at `ATTEMPTS=20`, seeds 5/6, with the **50/30/20 mix from the code
default** (`balanced = (wave or patch or bed) and FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE == "1"` is False;
the runtime row is the proof: `wave=off grades=A:0.5,B:0.3,C:0.2`, **0** `A:0.375` rows
on both seeds) and **pure routing unchanged** (left A=12/11, right B=8/9, C picked=0).
Controls are P80's `S20/T20/S6/T6` on the **identical tree md5s** - not re-run.

**The clock does not need the package.** Tp5/Tp6 read **10.10 / 9.90 s/attempt** (single
15.10 / 15.00) and **batch sim 10.13 / 9.94 s per executed attempt**, so the clock
ratio is **1.80x / 1.82x** (pooled 1.81x) against the package-on **1.88x / 1.87x**
(pooled 1.88x) - **96 % / 97 %** of it, inside the pre-registered [1.75, 2.00] band at
both seeds. The successful attempt is still the single arm's: placed-only mean spans
**15.64 / 16.15 s** against the package-on 15.78 / 15.51 and the single arm's 15.05 /
15.15 - the pipelining overlaps attempts, it never shortens one (P80's finding holds).

**What the package supplies is the feed and the overlap strength.** The mean number of
arms inside an attempt (sum of per-attempt spans / batch span) falls **1.58 -> 1.30** at

### P82: where the two-line's wall goes - 51 % physics, 32 % a 5 ms poll, and the poll is removable (34.5 % of the wall, bit-identical)

P80/P81 measured the two-line's throughput and left one number unexplained: its
harness cost is **wall/sim 2.57 against the single arm's 1.38**, so its 1.88x
*simulated* clock was a 1.02x *wall* wash. This phase asked where that 1.86x goes, with
two instruments on **separate profile builds**, and the admissibility test was the
branch: a profile build whose `[fruit]` stream is byte-identical to the record has not
moved the run, so its split is a split of the recorded branch.

**The instruments.** `I2` is a per-round timer set at the arbiter boundary only -
`TickRelay.schedule`/`request`/`pause`/`resume`, `MainBridge.pump`, the physics step
the arbiter executes, and `_tick_frame` - installed by `logs/p82/profile_20.py`, which
runs `scripts/20_pick_place.py` through `runpy`. **Nothing goes inside `ik_step`**
(AGENTS §2), so the control loop is untouched. `I1` is `py-spy record --rate 100
--idle --subprocesses` on the shipped entry (56,473 main-thread samples), aggregated by
`logs/p82/ps_agg.py`. Both are declared profile builds: I2 costs **+1.0 %** of wall,
I1 **+5.9 %** (two-line) / **+8.5 %** (single), and **R1/R3 are 865/865 identical to
`logs/p80/T20.log`** while **R2/R4 are 710/710 identical to `S20`** - including the
`[biarm]`, `[task]`, `[motion]`, `[cycle]` and `[stats]` rows. I2 on the single arm
counts 0 rounds, which is itself the control that the timers only touch the arbiter
path.

**Where the wall goes** (`logs/p82/R1.timers.json`, 47,795 rounds, 23,530 shared
ticks, 502.2 s):

| term | total | per round | share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SimulationManager.step` (one PhysX `simulate(dt)` per shared tick) | 255.9 s | 10.87 ms | **51.0 %** |
| both arms' control (permit -> next request) | 78.9 s | 1.70 ms x 1.97/tick | 15.7 % |
| **`MainBridge.pump` wait** | **240.5 s** | **5.03 ms (99.2 % timeouts)** | **47.9 %** |
| `TickRelay.schedule`'s own Python | **1.14 s** | **0.024 ms** | **0.2 %** |
| `_tick_frame` (render/camera) | 0.059 s | - | **0.0 %** |
| residual (wait not covered by a segment, handoff, feed) | 166.2 s | - | 33.1 % |

The dead wall - both workers parked, main thread asleep - is **161.6 s = 32.2 %** of
the run, and the wait histogram is a **single spike at 5.07-5.08 ms**, i.e. the
timeout itself rather than a distribution of work. **The mechanism** is structural:
`CoopSession.run` drives `bridge.serve_while`, whose body is `schedule()` then
`pump(0.005)`; `pump`'s queue only ever receives *bridged main-thread jobs* (a render,
an `update_app`), never the tick requests `TickRelay.request` files. So after granting
a permit the main thread sleeps out the rest of the 5 ms while the 1.70 ms segment
runs, **twice per shared tick** (2.03 rounds/tick, one permit each).

**What that rules out.** H1 as *Python* (the arbiter's per-round work) is **0.024
ms/round** - it is real as a structure, free as a cost. H2 (render) is **0.0 %**:
`_tick_frame` is two attribute reads because the scripted battery has no
`frame_callback` and no recorder. H3 (physics) is the largest term and **not
removable**: it is one shared `simulate`, 10.87 ms. H4 (the second arm) is 15.7 % -
the only part of the 1.86x that is "two arms doing two arms' work", and the single
permit serializes it. The **single arm** (py-spy, 545.7 s sampled): samples whose
stack is inside `step` are **71.3 %** of its wall (`step` leaf 63.9 % plus the USD
change notices the app runs inside it), `update_app` **12.7 %** (its pre-pose/feed
pump renders - the two-line does not pay this), the rest small tensor-API reads and
the driver, and **no arbiter and no poll** - so its 1.38 is physics plus
an app pump.

**The one optimization** (`logs/p82/apply_wake_patch.py`, 12 asserted anchors;
`bimanual.py` `980923a6` -> **`146e6252`**, +87/-10): `MainBridge` gains
`wake_on_request` (default **off**) and a `threading.Event`; `pump` waits on the event
instead of the fixed timeout, with the timeout kept as the safety net (a lost wake
costs latency, never a stall) and `call()` also waking; `TickRelay.register/enter/
request/pause/resume/release` call `_notify()` = `_cv.notify_all()` + `bridge.wake()`.
**`schedule`'s own `notify_all` is deliberately untouched** - waking from inside
`schedule` makes the next `pump` return without waiting, and the driver loop spins.
It is behaviour-neutral by construction: it moves *when* `schedule` is called, never
which tick is stepped, which attempt holds the permit, or what any control input is.

**The proof is bit-identity at two seeds, four profile configurations and both
schedulers**: `W1`/`W2`/`W3` (seed 5, knob on, with and without the I2 timers) are
**865/865** identical to `T20`; `W4` (seed 6) **814/814** to `T6`; the single-arm cells
**710/710** to `S20` and the accept cell **346/346** to
`logs/p71/accept_rails_none.log`; and the F2 shared-station scheduler - the other
consumer of the same `bimanual.py` - is **499/499** identical off-vs-on.

**The numbers** (20 attempts, shipped scenario, same session): wall **497.2 / 501.1 ->
327.1 / 327.8 s** at seed 5 (**-34.6 %**, the repeat 0.2 % away) and **476.8 -> 312.9
s** at seed 6 (**-34.4 %**); wall/sim **2.59 -> 1.69**; wall/pick **25.1 -> 16.4 s**;
placed/min wall **1.92 -> 2.93** (seed 6 1.26 -> 1.92) - with the placed count
(16/20, 10/20), the simulated span (193.3 s, 9.70 s/attempt) and every per-leg motion
metric unchanged. The shared-station pair reads **317.6 -> 201.8 s** (2.22 -> 1.41).
The timers say where the wall went: **pump wait 240.5 -> 77.6 s** (mean 5.03 -> 1.62
ms), **timeouts 99.2 % -> 5.4 %**, **residual 166.2 -> 5.5 s**, physics and the
segments unchanged (250.7 s / 76.7 s), **rounds 47,795 -> 48,021 and rounds/tick
unchanged - no spin**. ON, the wait histogram stops being a spike and becomes the
worker's own distribution (pump mean 1.62 ms against segment 1.65 ms): the main thread
now wakes when the arm finishes instead of 3.4 ms later.

**The arithmetic, in the order it must be quoted.** The sim clock is **1.88x** and the
lever cannot move it. The harness factor was **1.81x** the single arm's, so the wall
gain was `1.88 / 1.81 = 1.03x` - P80's wash. After the lever it is **1.19x**, so the
wall gain per pick is `1.88 / 1.19 = **1.57x**`. The placed **rate** multiplies that by
the count, which is a seed draw and not the lever's (pooled placed/attempt **0.650 vs
0.658** between the two lines, **0.650 vs 0.650** ON/OFF): **1.55x pooled** (1.95x at
seed 5, 1.18x at seed 6), against 1.02x before. **So the two-line now meets the
standing 1.25x bar on the wall denominator, not only on the sim denominator** - which
is the practical consequence P80 could not reach. What is left of the harness (1.19x)
is measured and is not a poll: the two arms' control plus the permit handoff, with the
shared physics step (10.65 ms/tick, **75 % of the remaining wall**) the floor.

**Read it as a latency win, not a cheaper run.** The idle wall is denser, not shorter
work: physics goes 51 -> 75 % and the segments 15.7 -> 23.0 % *of a shorter wall*, the
CPU work is unchanged, and the loop rate is unchanged. This box runs the cell at ~3 of
32 cores (measured: 351 CPU-s over 120 s of wall), so the run was latency-bound; on a
saturated machine the same work would queue and the win would shrink towards zero.
**P80/P81's two-line wall column stays valid for the shipped tree** - the knob is off -
and the knob-on numbers are the same scenario with the wait removed.

**No-harm and gates.** No motion reference is re-recorded and none is owed
(`configs/motion_reference.json` `8952c320`, `..._twoline.json` `eb697f23`: the physics
cannot move, and the off-path replay `W0` is 865/865 identical to `T20` with a wall of
501.1 s). `scripts/190_twoline_gate.sh` **PASSes** on the knob-on log against P80's own
20-attempt reference; `scripts/accept.sh` with the knob **set** reads **6/9 +
`fingerprint: matches`** (the standing rate-only FAIL at the 0.75 floor); the two-line's
carry cones are reported, not gated, under the dynamic line's convention;
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS, 0 failures**. `configs/` untouched, no commit, no default
flip: `FRUIT_BIARM_WAKE_ON_REQUEST` is a **default-off** knob, and adopting it is an
owner decision whose named consequence is that every two-line wall number moves from
~2.5 to ~1.66 wall/sim while no sim-time number moves at all.

**Not measured.** A saturated machine (the win is latency). The collector's
`run_bimanual` path (it drives the same session, so it inherits the knob - unmeasured).
A concurrent-arm scheduler (a different design; the single permit exists because PhysX
reads are not thread-safe). And the `update_app` 12 % the *single* arm pays is recorded
but not attacked: it is the driver's feed/settle pump, it services the camera/sensor
callbacks the evaluator needs, and it is not a piece of dead work like the poll.

Pins: `tasks.py` `e8dfa6d8` (untouched), `bimanual.py` `980923a6` -> `146e6252`,
`configs/*` untouched, ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`. Evidence `logs/p82/`:
`{METHOD.md,RESULTS.md,header.txt}`, the instruments
`{timers.py,profile_20.py,run_pyspy.sh,ps_agg.py}`, the drivers
`{one_run.sh,run_p82.sh,run_p82_stage2.sh}`, the patch `apply_wake_patch.py`, the
reports `{p82_report.py,p82_ab.py}`, the cells
`{R1,R2,R3,R4,W0,W1,W2,W3,W4,F0,F1,A1}.{log,stamps,driver}`, `R1/R2/W3.timers.json`,
`R3/R4.{speedscope.json.gz,profile.txt}`, `W1.gate`, `selfcheck.log`, `smoke/` (the four

### P83: fail fast - the abort halves the failed attempt (5.14 s / 617 ticks, both seeds, to the tick) and the cell's throughput does not follow

Owner directive: *the cell pays a full attempt for every failure; fail fast.*
P80 measured the shipped scripted cell at `26.72 s = 4.8 s idle + 1.45 attempts x
15.1 s`, and **all** of its failures were `grasped, not placed`: the payload is
gone mid-carry while the cell runs out the place transfer (3.19 s), the release
(2.11 s) and the return (0.63 s). The phase built the lever, registered it, and
measured it on two seeds. **Nothing is adopted, no default changed, no commit.**

**The lever.** `FRUIT_FAIL_FAST=<mm>` (`tasks.parse_fail_fast`, unset/0 = off):
one compare per guarded tick of the W8-B tracker's own `clean_slip_max` - the
payload's displacement in the leg's frame, the number the `[carry]` row already
prints - against the threshold; on a trip the leg **breaks at that tick** and the
attempt ends at one of the **two early-exit sites the P7-2b carry monitor already
uses** (the lift boundary, and the place boundary which is before the
release/retreat block), through one predicate
`_attempt_ended_early() = _carry_monitor_skip or _fail_fast_trip`. No note is
added, so the class is unchanged (`grasped` from the shipped peak-lift predicate,
`placed = False` → `cnp`); the payload is recycled by `run()`'s own `finally`; the
next pre-pose is the driver's `go_ready` → `_goto` teleport, the path every
shipped failure takes; there is **no new exception type**, so the scripted entry,
the collector and the two-line worker handle it as a `not grasped` return. Scope
is `scripted` only, so the direct/policy handover keeps its P10-C leg-boundary
classifier skip and cannot reach the knob. `0 < mm < 100` **raises at task
construction**: the pre-run census (`logs/p83/census.py`, 43 scripted logs that
already print `[carry]` rows, 249 placed / 165 failed attempts joined to their own
outcome rows) reads the worst **placed** leg at **76.3 mm** and 164/165 failures
at `>= 150 mm`, so the registered arm is 150 mm - a 1.97x margin - and 0/249
placed attempts ever reach it.

**The design problem this phase had to solve first: the trip needs the tracker.**
`clean_slip` is computed only inside the W8-B block, so the treatment arms carry
`FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1` as well as the knob, and a treatment-vs-shipped contrast
would otherwise differ by *instrumentation plus abort*. Two controls were
therefore run: **C** (shipped, knob off) and **D** (tracker only). **G1** C5
replays P80's `S20.log` **710/710 `[fruit]` lines byte-identical**, and **G2 D5 =
C5 (710/710) and D6 = S6 (708/708)** with the diag-only rows dropped: **the W8-B
tracker is run-neutral on the scripted line** - `tcp_pose`, `jaw_separation`,
`joint_positions` and one tactile set per tick do not move the branch, unlike the
link-world-pose reads AGENTS §2 forbids. That is the first time this tree has
proved it, and it is why `F` vs `C` is admissible as an abort-only contrast.
**G3** the treatment's first 57 (F5) / 59 (F6) physics lines equal the control's
with the first trip exactly at the boundary.

**The measurement** (20 attempts, shipped scenario, P80's instrumentation set):

| | seed 5: C5 → F5 | seed 6: S6/D6 → F6 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| failed attempt mean span | **15.157 → 10.013 s** | **14.567 → 9.422 s** |
| ... in ticks | **-617** | **-617** |
| `s/attempt` | 15.10 → 12.30 | 15.00 → 12.80 |
| pooled interval mean / p90 | 26.72 / 36.90 → **35.26 / 87.30** (+32.0 %) | 26.12 / 38.50 → **27.38 / 55.40** (+4.8 %) |
| placed/min window / batch | 2.25 / 2.08 → **1.70 / 1.68** | 2.30 / 2.27 → **2.19 / 2.08** |
| placed | 12/19 → 6/14 | 13/19 → 11/20 |
| wall/pick / placed/min wall | 25.33 → 21.62 s / **1.50 → 1.19** | 25.20 → 22.30 s / **1.61 → 1.48** |
| trips | 7 | 8 |

**The saving is arithmetic and it replicates to the tick** (-5.144 s both seeds
because an aborted leg skips 1-310 ticks of its own profile plus the 50-tick leg
tail, and the attempt then skips the release block and the retreat).

**Why the throughput does not follow.** The interval is `attempts/placement x
attempt span + idle`. The span term fell and the other two rose:
attempts/placement **1.583 → 2.333** at seed 5 and **1.462 → 1.818** at seed 6,
and the idle term 2.81 → 6.56 s at seed 5 (six starved slots) against 4.19 →
4.11 s at seed 6 (none). At the control's *own* failure rate the -2.80 / -2.20 s
per attempt would have taken the interval to ~22.3 / ~23.0 s, i.e. **the abort
is worth -16 % / -12 % of the interval and it cannot set the rate**. The count is
a branch draw (pooled 25/38 vs 17/34) and two seeds cannot separate "the re-timed
presentation is harder" from "the branch is harder"; the registration forbids
reading a count difference as the lever's.

**The seed-5 starvation, attributed.** Six slots (14-19) starved while four live
fruit remained. The post-hoc probe (`logs/p83/probe_bed.sh`, `FRUIT_BED_DIAG=1`
reproducing F5 exactly - 14 attempts, 6 placed, 7 trips, `sim = 172.8 s`) prints
the first refusing predicate per candidate: the only body above the **0.399 m**
catch floor (a peach at 0.626) is **`diverted (max_retries)`**, the apple (0.105)
and pear (0.339) are **inside** the floor and only creep downstream 0.06 m per
starved slot, a strawberry is on the output conveyor (`x = 1.08`), and the feeder
has nothing to release (`admitted 2 → 0`, `skipped = 85`, `pump_next` within
0.01 s of `t`). So it is a **pool state** (a diverted upstream fruit plus two
inside the floor plus a boundary-only pump), not an abort effect - and the
seed-6 arm starves **0/20** with the same saving. The 43 `[bed-fall]` rows are all
at `y = -0.63..-1.41, z ≈ 0.02, held = False`: P32's unattended belt-loss cadence
artifact, not payloads dropped by the abort.

**The audit, and the guards.** **15/15 trips** fire with `force = 0.00 N` *and*
`contacts = 0` at the trip tick (`force_min = 0.00 N` over the leg): by the time
the displacement reaches 1.97x the worst placed leg the pads are empty. **34/34
carry legs of the 17 placed attempts read `ticks = X/X`** - not one successful leg
is shortened - with the worst placed-leg `clean_slip_max` at 0.1 / 19.8 mm. The
20-attempt motion budgets pass (worst descent `|v|max` 0.110-0.120 against
0.160-0.161, lurch 0.017-0.027 against 0.291; the only `105` FAIL is the standing
0.75 rate floor), every run accounts, no run wedged. **G6 fails by its letter
only**: each treatment arm has **one** new reason text (`fruit did not follow the
gripper`), from a **never-held** attempt (`sep = gap = 22.2 mm` on a 53.8 mm fruit,
`onset_row = 1`, `stored pad centre 415 mm from the measured pads`,
`force servo: gap=22.2 sep=22.2 closed=15.00 trips=38` - the R11-A.1 left
acquisition signature) whose `grasped = False` the shipped predicate decides; the
seed-6 **control** carries the same text (1/19). The two trip families are 9
near the end of the lift (the W8-B loaded slide) and 5 inside the place leg
(three with `onset_row = 2-3`, i.e. the loss was at the end of the lift and the
place leg was pure run-out - those are the 253-310-tick savings).

**Verdict: not adopted.** M1 (G4/G5) and M2 (-5.144 s >= 3.0 s) pass; M3 fails on
G6's letter; T1/T2/T3 fail at both seeds. `FRUIT_FAIL_FAST` stays default off.
The named re-entry is a scenario where the **presentation** is not the binding
term - the two-line, whose scheduler parks an arm on the *other arm* rather than
on the belt (P80/P81), where 5.14 s per failure is a duty-cycle gain instead of

`wall/pick` (a run that places less divides a much smaller wall by a smaller
count: 25.33 → 21.62 s/pick at 1.50 → 1.19 placed/min); quote a trip as the pair
`clean_slip >= 150 mm` **and** `force = 0.00 N / contacts = 0` (a norm alone cannot
say the payload left); read the cut off the leg's own row (`[carry]
ticks=<trip>/<total>`, `[motion] steps=<trip+1>`); and run the tracker-only
control before claiming a treatment effect.
