The saving is **class-split**, and that is the phase's finding:

| seed | class | control | treatment | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | never-grasped | 13.35 s (n=4) | 11.87 s (n=6) | **-1.48 s** |
| 5 | `cnp` | **n=0** | 11.15 s (n=4) | not comparable |
| 6 | never-grasped | 12.90 s (n=5) | 11.70 s (n=2) | **-1.20 s** |
| 6 | `cnp` | 11.54 s (n=5) | 8.20 s (n=3) | **-3.34 s** |
| 6 | placed | 15.51 s (n=10) | 15.62 s (n=15) | +0.11 s |

Against P83's **-5.14 s** on the single arm. **Why**: the shipped two-line already
truncates a lost attempt **twice**. (1) `tasks.py` returns right after the lift
when the peak lift is absent (`if not result.grasped: … return result`), so a
never-grasped attempt never runs the place leg, the release or the return - the
`[cycle]` rows prove it (no `place`/`release`/`return` segment on 4/4 and 5/5
control never-grasped attempts), and the abort can only recover the rest of the
tripping leg. (2) The **P10-C carry monitor is armed by default in a two-line
session** (`_resolve_carry_monitor_knobs`: monitor 1, two-line scope 1, confirm
8.0 mm, floor 3.5), and it ends the *next* leg at its boundary. There are exactly
two early returns between `result.grasped` and the place leg, so a control attempt
with `grasped=True` and **no `place` segment must be the monitor** - measured on
**3 of D6's 5 `cnp` attempts** (9.1-10.3 s attempts). The fail-fast is therefore
only worth the leg remainder: mean `leg_left + 50-tick tail` **1.70 s (F5)** and
**1.52 s (F6)**, and a place-leg trip additionally skips release (2.36 s) +
return (0.64 s). P83's control - the single arm - has the monitor at its shipped
`0`, which is exactly why the same knob was worth 5.14 s there.

**The delivered side flips sign between the two registered seeds**, and the
waiting terms move with it:

| seed | interval | idle (mean per arm) | lock-on | starved polls | right park-gate wait | placed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | 10.77 -> **14.39 s (+33.6 %)** | 19.8 -> **23.5 %** | 4.19 -> **4.58 s** | 44 -> **53** | 7.1 -> **9.1 s** | 16 -> 10 |
| 6 | 19.34 -> **12.21 s (-36.9 %)** | 24.4 -> **21.7 %** | 5.04 -> **4.39 s** | 33 -> 33 | 21.8 -> **13.6 s** | 10 -> 15 |

Pooled: interval **-11.7 %**, window **4.34 -> 4.54**, batch **4.03 -> 4.05**,
wall **2.39 -> 2.42**, count **26/40 -> 25/40** (equal). So "the overlap absorbs
the abort" is **supported at seed 6** (every waiting term falls, the interval
falls, the count rises) and **refuted at seed 5** (every waiting term rises, the
interval rises, nine more starved polls) - and the cell's **own control** swings
16 -> 10 placed between the seeds (P80 §7b measured the same 1.27x / 0.73x count
swing), so a 20-attempt A/B whose treatment also re-times the presentation cannot
attribute the count either way. `wall/pick` falls at seed 5 (16.83 -> 14.92 s)
while `placed/min wall` falls too (2.85 -> 2.01) - P83's read rule, unchanged.
The wall/sim here is **1.61-1.74** because P82's wake-on-request ships default on;
P80's recorded 2.57 is a different harness and is not compared.

**Verdict: not adopted.** M1 fails on G4's letter (11/12), M2 fails at both seeds
(-1.77 s and -2.62 s against P83's 3.0 s bar - the bar was calibrated on a class
mix the two-line does not draw and on a line whose monitor is off), M3 fails on

(`D5` -> `190` **PASS** against P80's 20-attempt reference; `D6` -> **PASS**

trip, the same arm's next attempt placed **3/4 (F6)** and **4/7 (F5)**, with two
of F5's three non-placements being themselves trips, so the abort does not

**Read rules from here.** Quote a fail-fast increment **by class** on a line with
the monitor on (never ~1.2-1.5 s, `cnp` ~3.3 s); a **seed is a scenario**, so a
20-attempt two-line arm needs its own reference and the treatment is a

whose own control swings 16 -> 10 cannot attribute a count - the branch-free read
is the per-class failed-attempt span. **Named next spend**: a third seed (or a
count-matched design), not another threshold.

### P85: the shipped scripted cell becomes the bimanual two-line - the flip is resolution-only (865/865, 814/814, 799/799), the acceptance moves scenario and its gate stops using the single arm's floor

**The decision.** The W3/R5 register held `FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE` opt-in because the
two-line replaces the *meaning* of the shipped cell: pure grade lanes (left = A,
right = B, C recycled at `despawn_y`), a supply package that ships with it (dense
wave sheet + balanced A:B:C 0.375/0.375/0.25), and a scheduler that overlaps the
two attempts. `docs/THROUGHPUT.md` §"What is left" and AGENTS' W3/R5 records name
the owner's sign-off as the blocker; **the owner gave it**, so this phase is the
flip plus its full re-baseline.

**The change is resolution only.** `FRUIT_BIARM` and `FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE` default
`1`, through one resolver per knob (`bimanual.resolve_biarm` / `resolve_twoline`,
plus `biarm_resolution()` for the consumers; the P43 `defaulted` origin flag) and
the log names the cell (`[biarm] scheduler: FRUIT_BIARM=1(default)
FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE=1(default)`). `FRUIT_BIARM=0` is the pre-P85 single arm;
`FRUIT_BIARM=1 FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE=0` the unchanged F2 shared-station pipeline.
Two structural choices carry the no-harm:

* `tasks.two_line_enabled()` became the **session** predicate (`session.twoline`,
  False outside a session) and `two_line_resolved()` is the ambient form
  `run_bimanual` reads. The three scope guards that use it (`_ready_move`'s skip,
  `_home_hub`, the P42 seat centre) all mean "the scheduler is *running*", which
  can only be true inside a session - so the single-arm and shared-station paths
  cannot move even with the defaulted pair on.
* the two-line's **supply package** follows the same resolution
  (`fruits.SupplyPlan.from_env(cfg, two_line=...)`) and only the three scripted
  entries pass it. `SortingRLEnv` and `scripts/60_eval_policy.py` pin
  `two_line=False`: they are not the scripted cell, so no direct/policy number
  moves, and the hybrid canary has **no path** to the flip at all
  (`accept_policy.sh` builds its own `FruitSpawner`/`PickAndPlaceTask`, never a
  `CoopSession`) - which is why it was not re-run.

**The proof that the flip is resolution-only, three ways.** The default 20-attempt
runs replay the pre-flip *explicit* two-line records line for line, dropping only
the phase's instrumentation rows (`[fruit] [carry]`, its `[fruit] [diag]
carry-assist` lines, and the new scheduler banner): seed 5 **865/865** vs
`logs/p80/T20.log`, seed 6 **814/814** vs `T6.log`, and the accel treatment
**799/799** vs `V20.log` (the union's own opt-in two-line arm). The treatment
replaying its own record is the strongest form: the flip changed reachability,
not physics. Delivered at seed 5: **16/20, 9.70 s/attempt, interval 10.77 s,
5.57 / 4.96 placed/min, wall/pick 16.57 s, 2.90 placed/min wall** - P80's numbers
with P82's wall (331.4 s against T20's 497.2 s, wall/sim 1.71x). Per arm left
9/10, right 7/10, idle 18.1 / 21.4 %, lock-on 3.83 / 4.54 s.

### P86: the release block is -0.64 s of pure dwell and it is exact at both seeds - the phase's own span clause and one motion leg keep it out of the tree

The cell is P44's S2 knob (`FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=1`) on the shipped two-line:
dwell **20 -> 0**, pad ramp **40 x (3 -> 2)**, finger ramp **16 x (3 -> 2)** =
**-76 ticks = -0.633 s** at 120 Hz, `FRUIT_RELEASE_RESYNC` off. Four cells, 20
attempts each, seeds 5/6, one claim per run, the same instrumentation on all
four (including the landing trace). PREREG `d70cfcc4`, pinned before any run.

**Admissibility.** Both controls replay P85's own records on every physics
`[fruit]` line with the phase's rows dropped: C5 **865/865** vs
`logs/p85/base20_s5.log`, C6 **814/814** vs `base20_s6`. So the tree is
unchanged **and** the per-place landing trace (`FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE`, a fruit-pose
read) is inert on this line - both controls carry it and still reproduce the
trace-free record.

**The mechanism is the profile arithmetic, to the tick.** The `[cycle]
release=` segment falls **-0.615..-0.640 s = 74-77 ticks in all four
arm-seed cells** by median (per-arm medians 2.320 -> 1.680, 2.360 -> 1.720,
2.310 -> 1.675, 2.420 -> 1.805), pooled median 2.325 -> 1.680 = **-0.645 s
(-77 ticks)** against the predicted -0.633 s (-76). The two mean-based
outliers are one 1.63 s control leg (C6) and one 1.92 s treatment leg (R6) -
both `place low` descents inside the segment - which is why seed 6's *mean*
delta (-0.56) sits below its median (-0.640). The block is 2.33 s of a 15.78 s
per-arm span, the second of the three profile blocks.

**The delivered side.** The pooled interval falls at both seeds (10.77 ->
**10.59**, 19.34 -> **11.08** s) and on **both arms at both seeds**. The seed-5
pair is the clean read - identical count (16/20) **and** identical arm split
(9/10 + 7/10), so its -0.18 s pooled and -0.48 s arm span are the lever's own.
Seed 6's -8.26 s is confounded with a +2 count draw and is quoted as such.
`s/attempt` 9.70 -> 9.50 / 9.10; window 5.57 -> 5.66 and 3.10 -> 5.41
placed/min; batch 4.96 -> 5.05 and 3.11 -> 3.94; `placed/min wall` **2.88 ->
2.95** and **1.91 -> 2.34** with the wall -2.2 % / -1.9 % (the arbiter's
per-tick cost is flat, so the wall follows the sim clock).

**The landing is clean.** `FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE` gives one row per place:
**28/28** payload-present releases land `on_belt` (16/16, 16/16, 10/10, 12/12),
release bottom 31.8-64.3 mm, impact -0.93..-0.45 m/s, bounce <= 5.6 mm - the
control's own band. The upstream-lost traces read `release_bottom = -184 mm`
(C6 has one; that is the control's own `SIM_LIMIT` class, reported separately,
never gated). P44 §9.4 reproduced on the two-line, and P45's
displacement-controlled-ramp reading confirmed: a shorter dwell does not fling.

**No class cost.** No new failure-reason key at either seed. The counts shift at
seed 6 (never-grasped 5 -> 1, `cnp` 5 -> 7) - the re-timed presentation drawing a
different fruit, P44/P46/P51's class shift, not a grip change (the cell touches
no grip code) - and the `force_min == 0.00` loaded-slide guard is flat at seed 5
(4 -> 4) and **better** at seed 6 (11 -> 7).

**What fails.** Two registered clauses, and neither is the lever's own term.

1. **P1b, the attempt-span instance of the same claim**, registered at
   `-0.633 +- 0.12 s` per seed and per arm: **-0.41 / -0.57** (seed 5) and
   **-0.27 / -0.96** (seed 6) -> the band fails at both seeds. The residual
   ("span - block") is **+0.17 / -0.12 s**, i.e. it **sign-flips**: the
   acquisition blocks re-draw because the trim moves the attempt boundary
   (`descent` **+0.24** at seed 5; `grip` **-0.35** and `place` -0.17 at seed 6),
   and over two seeds the span saving (-0.575) tracks the block to 0.04-0.07 s.
   **A per-seed attempt span is not branch-free** - P44 §3's attribution caveat,
   which this phase's PREREG §7 asserted away and the data refuted. That is a
   preregistration defect of the phase, recorded as one: the branch-free instance
   of the claim is the block itself, and it passes exactly. The re-entry
   registers the block + the interval and reads the span as a report.
2. **G2, the motion guard, fails at R6 on one leg**: the log's 12th descent
   (cycle attempt 12, right arm, kiwi, **placed**, lift +0.559 m) reads `|v|max`
   **0.164** against the 0.160/0.161 budget (2.5 % over, `a_med` 0.57 peaking at
   0.68 of the leg, `end = 12.6 mm` short, lurch 0.036 of the 0.291 bound).
   C5 0.112, R5 0.111, C6 0.132. The descent profile is **not touched by this
   cell**, and AGENTS §2 forbids re-tuning the budget to admit a configuration,
   so it is a recorded failure: the trim shifts the attempt boundary, the catch
   is presented a different fruit at a different belt offset, and one leg of one
   seed pays it.

**Gates.** C5 `190` **PASS** against `logs/p80/motion_reference_twoline_p80_20.json`
(16/20 at the 0.5 floor, fingerprint matches); C6 `190` **PASS** against a seed-6
reference written **from C6 itself** into `logs/p86/` (a seed is a scenario - P84 -
never `configs/`); R5/R6 are recorded against those two and **DIFFER by
construction** (a release-profile change re-times every attempt boundary and the
fingerprint carries each leg's duration), so they are gated on budgets only.

**Verdict.** PREREG §5's letter: **NOT a win - no default change, no `configs/`
write, no commit.** The sponsor's four-clause rule (block, interval, landing,
ledger) **passes at both seeds**, so the cell is a measured positive and the
adoption package is written and priced (RESULTS §9) but not executed: a
**two-line scope first** (the knob is read at a shared site, so a global default
would also move the single arm, the hybrid canary and the scripted collector),
three references re-recorded from same-batch runs if the flip is global,
`physics.release={dwell,pad_hold,finger_hold}` in both manifests **before** any
recollection (today a store carries no release clock at all), a 2-seed
40-attempt budget run of the trimmed branch (R6's one leg is the whole of the
motion evidence), then `accept.sh` + `demo_2min.sh` + one two-line rate batch.

### P87: the release trim ships two-line-scoped - the scope is proved bit-for-bit by replay (865/865, 868/868, 814/814, 821/821), the single arm stays 346/346, and one descent leg on one seed makes it a considered trade

P86 measured the S2 cell (`FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE`: dwell 20 -> 0, the pad/finger
settles 3 -> 2 = -76 ticks = -0.633 s) as a clean positive on the shipped
two-line and priced the adoption: the release block is read at a site **every**
presentation shares (`_grasp_carry_place_impl`), so a *global* default would also
move the single arm, the shared-station pipeline, the hybrid canary and the
scripted collector - none of which P86 measured. P87 executes the package's first
item: the trim becomes the **two-line session's default**, resolved through
`Task.two_line_enabled()` (the `CoopSession` predicate), with
`FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=0` restoring, an explicit `=1` / `FRUIT_SPEED_ALL=1` still
winning globally, and `FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE_SETTLE` unchanged. One resolver
(`tasks.release_speed_resolution`) feeds the per-attempt holds, the new
`[fruit] [biarm] release profile:` row and the store manifest's
`physics.release`; the row prints only inside `run_bimanual`, the
`[drive] finger cap scope:` convention - which is why the single arm's log carries
**no** new line at all.

**The arithmetic first, because P86's PREREG has a slip.** Its table printed the
totals as `208 / 132` ticks; the three holds sum to **188 / 112** (20 + 40x3 +
16x3, and 0 + 40x2 + 16x2). Both rows carried the same +20, so the registered
**delta (-76 ticks / -0.633 s) and every band are unaffected** - and the
measurement lands on 77 ticks, two ticks from the corrected arithmetic.

**G0 - the flip is resolution-only, and it is a replay, not an argument.** P86's
treatment cells ran `FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=1` (explicit); P87's run it **unset**.
The four cells are **byte-identical to P86's own four** on the `[fruit]` stream
(dropping the diag rows plus the one new row): C5 **865/865**, T5 **868/868**,
C6 **814/814**, T6 **821/821**. So the shipped default *is* the measured arm bit
for bit, and P86's mechanism/landing/ledger measurements transfer instead of
being re-derived - the cleanest form this repo has had for a default flip.

**The gate (PREREG `738c1b54`, pinned before the runs; 20 attempts, seeds 5/6,
arm = `FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=0` vs unset, P86's instrumentation on both).** **P1a
PASS**: the `[cycle] release=` **median** falls **-0.645 / -0.640 s** (77 / 77
ticks) and in **all four arm-seed cells** (-0.640/-0.640, -0.635/-0.615). **P2
PASS**: the pooled interval falls **10.77 -> 10.59** and **19.34 -> 11.08 s**, and
on both arms at both seeds; seed 5 is the clean read (identical 16/20 and an
identical 9/10 + 7/10 split, so -0.18 s is the lever), seed 6's -8.26 s carries a
+2 count draw. **P3 PASS** (**28/28** payload-present releases `on_belt`, in the
control's band: 32.1-64.3 mm, -0.93..-0.61 m/s, bounce <= 4.9 mm). **P4 PASS** (no
new reason key; `force_min==0` 4 -> 4 and 11 -> 7). **P5 reported, never gated**
(window 5.57 -> 5.66 / 3.10 -> 5.41, batch 4.96 -> 5.05 / 3.11 -> 3.94,
`placed/min wall` 2.92 -> 2.95 / 1.95 -> 2.35). **P6 misses its clean-pass form
and that is the phase's honest headline**: seed 5 is **0/20** legs over budget,
seed 6 is **1/20** - leg 12, 5.9 cm, **0.164 against its 0.160** per-leg budget
(2.5 % over) - and it is **the same leg P86's R6 recorded**. Forty treatment
attempts across two seeds therefore say the excursion is a **deterministic
property of that seed's branch**, not one draw's accident and not a systematic
cost of the trim (seed 5's worst is 0.111). By PREREG §5's pre-registered tier
that is a **CONSIDERED TRADE: ship, P6 documented** - not a clean pass. The budget
was **not** re-tuned (AGENTS §2), the descent profile is untouched, and a third
seed is the named next spend if the owner wants it priced further.

**Inertness, both halves.** `FRUIT_BIARM=0 scripts/accept.sh` is **346/346 raw
byte-identical** to `logs/p71/accept_rails_none.log` (raw, no filter) with
`fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference_single.json`; its exit=1 is the
standing `6/9 < 0.75` rate clause this tree has carried since P32, not a P87
effect. The shared-station pair (`=1 FRUIT_BIARM_TWOLINE=0`, 4 attempts, unset vs
`=0`) is identical on all 218 other `[fruit]` lines and resolves the same clock
(20/3/3, 188 ticks). **Deviation A1**, recorded rather than smoothed: PREREG G2b's
letter said "whole `[fruit]` stream", and the pair differs on exactly one line -
the new row's `origin` field (`scope-off` vs `explicit`), which is the label's
purpose (P43's `defaulted` convention). The claim is therefore "identical on every
other line **and** the same clock", asserted by `p87_report.py --same` plus
`--profile`, with the raw diff kept.

**Re-recorded, two-line side only, from this batch**:
`configs/motion_reference.json` `eb697f23` -> **`423896f7`** and
`configs/motion_reference_twoline.json` `eb697f23` -> **`423896f7`** (from
`logs/p87/accept10.log`, whose budgets are clean; the final-tree acceptance is

**`configs/motion_reference_single.json` `8952c320` untouched** - the single-arm

**Provenance before any recollection.** `scene._release_provenance` writes

moving one trajectory endpoint - P41's `physics` / P72's `scene` rationale.

**Re-baseline: every two-line rate, span or interval recorded before P87 is a

`FRUIT_ARM_PARK=ready` for pre-P43, `FRUIT_POLICY_TRIGGER_ACQ=0` for pre-P54, and

### P88 - the place block is exact, the delivery is not: measured, not shipped

**Why.** After P87 the shipped cell (two-line + release trim) has `place` as its
largest remaining profile block (**3.14-3.19 s** against `release` 1.70 and
`lift` 1.65), and P44's S1 cell (`FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0.52`, `v_max` 0.35 -> 0.52
at the shipped `a_max` 1.089) is the last unspent one of the three. P44 measured
it on the single arm as the largest clean single cell; P74 measured that speeding
the place does not move the loaded-slide class **on the direct line**. The place
leg is where every escape lives, so the class had to be re-measured on the
shipped cell - and P74's prediction was "no change".

**The build.** The same two-line-scoped shape as P87, one resolver per cell:
`tasks.place_speed_resolution` (the caps, the origin, the profile clock at a
**named** reference distance - the place is a transit, so its ticks are
`f(distance)`), consumed by `speed_cell_defaults(self.two_line_enabled())` at
`_carry_leg`, printed as `[biarm] place profile:` inside `run_bimanual`, written
as `physics.place={v_max,a_max,ticks,shipped_ticks,saved_ticks,
reference_distance_m,profile,origin,two_line,label}` by
`scene._place_provenance` in both manifest writers. The registered cell is P44's
pair exactly; `FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE=0` restores, an explicit value and
`FRUIT_SPEED_ALL` still win globally, `..._AMAX` pins the acceleration.

**The mechanism is exact.** The place block is **`transit(0.52, d) + 0.583 s`**:
the untouched `place low` remainder reads 0.583 s (0.578-0.588) in **all four
cells**, the per-leg tick count matches the profile re-generated at 0.52 from the
leg's own printed distance to **median 0.0 / +0.5 ticks (max |2|)**, `|v|cmd`
matches the profile's own peak to **<= 0.009 m/s**, the median leg cruises at
**0.508 m/s** (control 0.341-0.343), and every leg whose raised prediction is
`>= 0.45` reads `>= 0.482` (the short legs read 0.42-0.47 because the
acceleration or jerk term binds - PREREG amendment **A1**, pinned before the
first treatment cell). The block's **mean** falls **-0.774 / -0.767 s** against
the predicted -0.776 / -0.801.

**The gate fails.** P1a at seed 5: the block **median** falls -0.770 s against
the predicted -0.904, i.e. **0.134 s** against a +-0.12 band - and the miss is
the **leg mix**, not the cell: the prediction is built from the control's legs,
the treatment drew a longer median leg, and predicted from **its own** legs its
median is off by **-0.008 / +0.014 s**. A median is not branch-free for a
distance-dependent block (the release's fixed clock is why P86/P87's medians
were exact). P2 at **both** seeds: the pooled interval **rises** 10.59 -> 13.23
and 11.08 -> 12.11 s. P4a at seed 5: one `grasped, not placed (no note)` row - a
ledger bucket present in three of the four cells.

**The delivered read, and why.** Seed 5 places **16 -> 11**: the left's
never-held legs go **1 -> 4** (`force@onset = 0.00 N`, `contacts@onset = 0`,
`sep@onset` 59-63 mm on three of them - the **pre-contact acquisition** class,
not the place transfer), i.e. the faster leg re-times which fruit the close is
offered - the same class P51 named as the speed cells' cost. Seed 6 places
**12 -> 15** and the interval still rises because the placements spread over a
**wider window** (121.9 -> 169.5 s): the interval **is** `window/(n-1)`, so it
and the window rate are **one statistic**. Pooled **28 -> 26 of 40** and
`placed/min wall` **2.65 -> 2.61 (-1.6 %)** while the wall falls 5.6 %
(9.5 -> 8.9 and 9.1 -> 9.4 s/attempt).

**The class guard is negative** (P74 holds): place-leg escapes **0/27** in the
treatment against **1/29** in the control, all-leg escapes **5 vs 8**,
`force_min == 0` **6 vs 8**, landing **16/16, 11/11, 12/12, 15/15**, and the
descent budgets are clean on both treatments (0/20 each). The control's seed-6
leg 12 at **0.164 vs 0.160** is the standing branch leg P86's `R6` and P87's
`T6` recorded - and the treatment does not draw it.

**Not shipped, and the tree is inert.** `PLACE_TWO_LINE_DEFAULT = False`, so
`FRUIT_SPEED_PLACE` is off on every path (the measured arm is the explicit
`=0.52`); the resolver, the row and `physics.place` stay as the measurement's
instruments. Proven three ways: C5/C6 replay P87's T5/T6 **868/868** and
**821/821** on the `[fruit]` stream (the diag rows and both profile rows
dropped), a fresh unset 20-attempt run (`N5`) replays C5 **868/868**, and
`FRUIT_BIARM=0 scripts/accept.sh` is **346/346 raw** identical to
`logs/p71/accept_rails_none.log` with `fingerprint: matches` and **zero** profile
rows (the shared station's clock is unchanged, `--profile`; only the row's
`origin` label differs). **No re-baseline**: `configs/motion_reference.json` and
`..._twoline.json` = `423896f7`, `..._single.json` = `8952c320`, and the final
acceptance reads **7/10, 9.4 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**.

**Two recorded deviations.** **A1** (pinned 17:34, before T5): P1b's "every
treatment leg `|v|cmd >= 0.48`" is arithmetically wrong for short legs - at 0.52
the acceleration term binds below 0.408 m and the jerk term below ~0.19 m - so
the clause became the per-leg profile match (ticks and `|v|cmd` against the
profile re-generated from that leg's own distance) plus a median/contrast
read. **A2** (pinned 18:17, before the final acceptance): G1's "C5/C6 must PASS
the 20-attempt fingerprint" is unsatisfiable on a post-P87 clock - the only
20-attempt references are pre-trim records and the trim re-times every attempt
boundary, which is exactly why P87's own T5/T6 DIFFERED while its
`FRUIT_SPEED_RELEASE=0` controls matched. The corrected G1 keeps G0 as the
control's identity proof (byte-identical to P87) and the per-leg budget as the
substantive motion check; no verdict clause moved (the gate already fails on
P1a/P2/P4a).

**Re-entry.** A scenario where the place block **binds the interval** rather
than the count (P51/P80's rule), or a class-first registration that accepts the
count and argues the **-0.77 s** mean block saving / -5.6 % wall on its own.
The measured arm is one env var away.

### P89 - the lift block: exact, small, and not the lever; the profile table is closed

The third and last profile block of the shipped two-line cell (release 1.70 s
after P87's trim, place 3.14-3.19 s, **lift 1.65-1.70 s**). P44's **S3-v** is the
cell: `grasp_lift` `v_max` 0.30 -> **0.37** with the shipped **`a_max` 1.0** -
`logs/p44/P2_RESULTS.md` §9 measured the acceleration raise (0.36 **and** 1.9) at
**0.00 s** for a 1.42x worst cone against S3-v's 1.19x, so it is deliberately not
part of the cell. The site is the shared `_carry_leg` `grasp_lift` branch, so the
cell is scoped exactly like the release's and the place's: one resolver
(`tasks.lift_speed_resolution`), one session predicate
(`speed_cell_defaults(self.two_line_enabled())`), one row (`[biarm] lift
profile:`), one manifest block (`physics.lift`), one selfcheck leg (`249`). **The
gate failed, so the constant is False** and unset resolves 0.30/1.0 on every
path; the measured arm is `FRUIT_SPEED_LIFT=0.37` (which resolves 1.0 - the S3/S13
`=1`/`FRUIT_SPEED_ALL` pair stays 0.36/1.9, i.e. P44's recorded arms are not
moved).

**The mechanism is exact, and small for a measurable reason.** `[cycle] lift=` is
the leg plus a **constant remainder 0.412-0.422 s** in both arms (40/40 legs), so
the block **mean** is `ticks(d)/120 + remainder` and the prediction, built from
each control attempt's own printed `grasp_lift` distance, prices it at
**-0.177 / -0.193 s**: measured **-0.175 / -0.173 s** (P1a PASS, band ±0.08; the
medians -0.220/-0.195 against -0.222/-0.188). Per leg the treatment's ticks
match the profile re-generated at 0.37/1.0 from that leg's own printed centimetre
to **median 0.0 (max |5|)**, its `|v|cmd` matches that profile's own peak to
**<= 0.013 m/s** (median 0.350 against the control's 0.293), and the reference
clock is **162 -> 136 ticks = -0.217 s** at the named 0.21 m. **Why the cell is
small is arithmetic, not a wish**: the two profile regimes switch at
`d = 5.774 v^2/(1.875^2 a)` = **0.225 m** at 0.37 (0.148 m shipped), so above it
the raised leg is *acceleration*-bound - a 0.20 m leg saves 21 ticks, not the
1.233x speed ratio, and a 0.05-0.12 m leg saves nothing at all. P85's union
re-pricing had already put the lift at -0.13 s of its -1.00 s; this is the same
number, now measured on its own.

**The delivery fails at both seeds, for two different terms.** Pooled interval
**10.59 -> 13.43 s** at seed 5 - where the story is the **count** (16 -> 12

interval rises anyway because the placements spread over a **wider** window
(121.9 -> 160.9 s): `mean_gap = window/(n-1)`, P88's seed-6 pattern exactly.
Pooled **28 -> 26 of 40**, `placed/min wall` **2.67 -> 2.60** on 629 -> 601 s.
The attempt itself did get faster (`s/attempt` 9.50 -> 8.90 and 9.10 -> 9.00,
i.e. -0.60 / -0.10 s against the block's -0.175 / -0.173 - the rest is the
branch's acquisition re-draw, P86 §3).

**The class question the phase registered is answered "neither".** P44's
single-arm read was *improves* (S3-v dropped the `force_min == 0` legs 5 vs 7 and
drew no grip row); P75's was *moves* (2 of 6 place-leg escapes fire at the

**Admissibility, and the one deviation.** C5/C6 replay P88's **C5/C6** on the

### P90 - the place station has no top-down: the workstation path closes on a 10 mm cliff

The owner picked the **workstation / station-layout** path, and it had one
answerable question: *is there an output place station where the left arm can hold
the top-down attitude through the place leg - and what does moving the line there
cost?* It is answered **no**, with the count, the cliff and the mechanism.

**The instrument is P66's, retargeted.** `logs/p90/station_map.py` is a copy of
`logs/p66/ik_probe_sweep.py` (itself a copy of `logs/p62/ik_probe.py`, both kept
byte-untouched so their artifacts stay reproducible) with the target moved from the
**pick** band to the **place** pose the code actually commands -
`(x, y, output_place_z [+ the OpenArm 0.08])` - and three additions: **both arms**,
**two heights** (`z = 1.450`, the place height, and `z = 1.530`, the transfer), and
**three attitude modes**. The grid is 7 x 7 (+-0.15 m around `(0.43, +-0.50)`, 0.05
m step = P66's cell size) x 2 heights x 2 arms x 3 modes = **588 cells**, 46 min in
one claim.

**The criterion was pinned before the run** (`logs/p90/METHOD.md`, md5
`42bec0f8`, mtime 22:31:42 - before the probe file existed at 22:32:17 and before
the sweep at 22:33:39): `residual <= 6 mm AND qerr <= 2 deg AND margin >= 0.05 rad
AND pad >= 2 mm` - P66's three clauses plus the residual tolerance the brief asks
for - with `NAT`'s `qerr` clause replaced by `tilt <= 5 deg`, the `drift_end` scale
(P66's rungs read 25.1 / 3.4 / 0.7 deg) rather than an invented number.

**The three modes are the phase's design decision, because the place leg has no
attitude hold.** `_carry` clears `hold_quaternion` for `name != "grasp_lift"`, so
the place leg runs a **position-only** 3-DoF solve. `T0` (hold top-down) therefore
asks a question whose *yes* would need a code change - and that lever is already
measured **0/16** (P68's place wrist hold). `NAT` (`hold_quaternion = None`) asks
what the leg **actually achieves** there, and its *yes* is shippable by a station
move alone. `C0` (the arm's own calibrated belt-aligned `grasp_quaternion`) is
P66's "which attitude does the workspace offer" control. That split is what makes a
negative readable: it separates "the attitude is available but not commanded" from
"the attitude does not exist here".

**The answer is 0 of 588 cells, in every mode, at both heights, on both arms.**

* **`T0`: 0/98 per arm, and at the transfer height the best margin over the whole
  49-cell grid is `+0.000153 rad` (0.15 mrad)** - not one cell has a milliradian of
  headroom. The
  cells with the smallest tilt (7.46 deg at 1.450, 15.16 at 1.530) pay **172-192 mm**
  of position for it. This is P66's pick-band finding reproduced at the other end of
  the cell, and the reason both are readable the same way is that they share a
  criterion.
* **`NAT`: only 7-8 of 49 cells even solve to 6 mm** (the box `x 0.38..0.48`,
  `|y| 0.35..0.55`), **and every one reads 77.8-108.4 deg of tilt.** The best
  *solved* attitude in the entire envelope is **77.75 deg - at the shipped station
  itself** (`x 0.43, |y| 0.50, z 1.450`: `res 5.9 mm`, `margin +0.185 @ j4`,
  `tool_y +0.628`). So the station is **not improvable by moving it**: the shipped
  point is the optimum of the map.
* **`C0`: also 0/98**, on the **margin**: best `+0.037 rad @ j6` (1.450) /
  `+0.041 @ j7` (1.530) against 0.05 - and it does not solve at the shipped cell at
  all (`res 83.2 / 105.3 mm`, `qerr 45.65 / 45.86 deg`, `margin -0.000 @ j3`). That
  is the sharpest single statement in the phase, and the distinction that makes it
  readable: `T0` and `C0` are **6-DoF** solves (position + orientation) and **both
  fail at the shipped cell**, while `NAT` is the **3-DoF position-only** solve the leg
  actually runs and it arrives with **5.9 mm**. So the place station is at the **reach
  boundary** and the live leg **buys position with attitude** - exactly what
  `assets.py`'s own note says (`y_off = 0.41` from the shoulder, i.e. `|y| = 0.50`).

**The instrument is validated against the live record three ways**, statically and
without a payload: `NAT` at the place height reads **77.75 deg** against P73's live
`tilt_end` **78.7 deg** and the release-time payload offset's implied **87.9 / 91.1
deg**; the same row prints `tool_y +0.628` against P66's measured `tool_y
+0.65..+0.70` on the failing place legs (the *azimuth* agrees, not just the
magnitude); and `NAT` at the transfer does **not** solve to 6 mm (**14.9 mm**),
which is the live leg's own `res_end` **13.3-34 mm**. A static solve with no
payload, no controller and no profile lands on the same regime the closed loop
measures - which is P66's cross-check argument, repeated.

**The cliff is one 10 mm step and the shipped point is on it.** A second run
bisects the shipped column `x = 0.43` at **0.01 m** in `|y|` (104 cells): at the
place height `|y|` **0.50 -> 0.51** takes the residual **6 -> 19 mm** and the margin
**+0.185 -> -0.0000**; at the transfer the cliff sits between **0.49 and 0.50**, so
the shipped station is already **one step past it** there (which is the live
`res_end` 13-34 mm). Along `|y| = 0.50` the `x` cliff is the same kind: `x` 0.43 ->
6 mm, **0.48 -> 46 mm**, 0.53 -> 86 mm. **The shipped point is the corner of a
0.10 x 0.20 m solvable box, at the limit in both axes.**

**Robustness - the negative is not a seed, a tolerance or a bad starting pose.**
Re-seeded from the arm's calibrated place pose (`bin0_above` / `bin1_above`,
`restarts = 3`, P66's robustness-B test): `T0` is **0/14 per arm with `|margin| <= 0.060 mrad` on every cell**; `NAT` finds **28 deg** - but only on the **left**, only at
`|y| = 0.35` (**75 mm inboard of the slab's 0.425 edge**, the band that has had **no
authored surface** since P71 removed the inner rail), and 28 deg is **5.6x** the 5 deg
bar, **inside** the pre-P66 0.36 m rung's own carry-drift range (20.8-28.3 deg) and
**40x** the shipped 0.20 m rung's `drift_end` (0.7 deg). Relaxing the
residual to the live leg's own 13-34 mm admits only **worse** attitudes (96-120 deg
at `x` 0.28-0.33). The `pad >= 2 mm` clause is never binding on a solved cell (the
shipped cell reads **+46.3 mm**); it fires on **10 of 588** cells, all non-solving,
with the pads **-81.0 .. +2.0 mm** from the surface as the *consequence* of a failed
solve. And the `y` sweep - the axis `METHOD.md` §5 already flagged as a capability
rather than a free variable - is the one that fails **fastest** (10 mm).

**The costs all came back cheap; the gain is what is zero.** That is the phase's
structural result and it is why no measurement cell is registered (`PREREG.md` is
**not** written):
* **crossing** - **exactly 0 mm** for any `y` on the shipped *horizontal* transit
  (`lift end 1.530 == transfer 1.530`); **+0.30 mm/mm** inboard on the direct low
  lift (0.160 m of climb over 0.45 m of `y`), i.e. the same order as P70's belt-height
  lever (0.175:1) and 3x below the rail's 1:1, and bounded to **+5 mm** by the
  release band. `x` does not enter the crossing at all.
* **release** - the one binding column, and it *constrains* rather than costs:
  commanded `|y|` **0.378 .. 0.633** lands the payload on the slab. The shipped
  0.500 sits inside; the sweep's `0.35 / 0.40` columns are release-dead.
* **discharge** - **cannot move**: the chute (x 1.200 -> 1.361) and the tray (x
  1.35..1.95, floor 0.92, rim 1.06) are downstream in `+x` and are functions of the
  belt, not of the place point; `on_output_discharge` starts at
  `output_belt_end_x - 0.05` = 1.15. The **tray floor 0.92 and the chute end 1.12
  are absolute** and stay.
* **stations** - untouched by construction: the place target reads
  `output_belt_drop_points` + `output_place_z` and **no `pick_*`**; the two-line's
  pre-poses are solved at the pick station (`_prepare_two_line_stations`); and the
  park gate cannot see it either (`_biarm_payload_clear` fires on `|y| = 0.28`
  mid-transit, long before any admissible place point).

**One correction to the record, and it is worth carrying.** `logs/p70/RESULTS.md` §4
read the delivered place point at `|y|` 0.542-0.547 against a commanded 0.500 and
attributed the +45 mm to "the arm's outward overshoot at its reach boundary". A
census of the same rows (**43 held releases** across `logs/p70/{C,A,B}.log`,
`logs/p71/{both,none}.log` and the acceptances) says otherwise: **jaw - target =
(-1..-4, -6.5..+1) mm** - the jaw lands **on** the commanded point - while
**payload - jaw = (+52, +-42..46, ~0) mm**, `|.|` **72.6 mm** (left) / **66.4 mm**
(right), implying the tool axis **(+0.775, +-0.631, -0.04)**, i.e. **tilt 87.9 /
91.1 deg**. The offset is the gripper's own `_pad_standoff` (**70 mm** =
`FRUIT_FINGER_LEN` 0.060 + `PAD_LIFT` 0.010) hanging the payload **along a
horizontal tool axis**. Two consequences: the release point is a *function of the
achieved tilt* (so a top-down station would remove the 44 mm for free), and an
outboard move at the shipped ~90 deg attitude pushes the delivered point past the
slab's 0.675 edge **25 mm earlier** than the commanded number suggests.

**Verdict: the workstation path closes, and it closes on the *mediation* as well as
on the geometry.** Not only is there no top-down place station - **the rotation is
not the class's measured actuator**: P73 put all 8 payload losses **before** the
leg's 45 deg crossing, at a tilt **below 45 deg**, with the 90-105 deg sweep
happening at 73-79 % of the leg, i.e. *after* the failure; and the **right reaches
107.3 deg and slips 0.0-0.1 mm on 10/10** place legs. A station that removed the
rotation would remove a mediator the class does not read. So `docs/LEFT_ARM.md`'s
three named levers reduce to **two** - **a new pad asset** and **a real-jaw
clamp-force anchor** - and `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md` is unchanged by this phase.

**Scope.** Static, kinematic, no payload, no controller, no profile, and **no
output-slab geometry in the scene** (the P66 build), so a residual is kinematic and
not a contact; the `NAT` row is path-dependent in the live leg. `x` and `z` beyond
the registered ranges were not swept - `x` cannot help (it is absent from
`_payload_clearance`) and the belt-height lever is P70's closed 0.175:1. The right
arm was swept as a capability control and mirrors the left to **0.05 deg** in every
mode, so "the right does not need this" is not a measurement here (the record's
reason the class is left-only is P63's: the right places 29/30 at 25.8 deg carry
drift).

No `src/` or `configs/` edit, no default change, no commit, no reference
re-recorded. `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS, 0 failures**. Evidence
`logs/p90/{METHOD.md,MAP.md,COST.md,station_map.py,station_map.txt,station_map.log,
cost_map.py,cost_map.txt,run_p90.sh,run_p90_robust.sh,smoke.log,driver*.log,
station_rows.json,station_rows_refine.json,station_rows_seed_{left,right}.json,
station_map_refine.log,station_map_seed_{left,right}.log}`.

### P91 - the five "never measured" blocks hold 7 % of the cycle, and the one lever in them is coupled to a force

The owner asked for the **single-pick cycle** faster, **excluding the fruit wait**
("不包含等果时间"), and pointed at the five `[cycle]` blocks the record had never
profiled as levers: `descent 3.64`, `grip 2.36`, `close 1.36`, `hover 0.75`,
`prepose 0.71` - **8.82 s = 57 %** of the 15.34 s per-arm span (`logs/p87/T5.log`,
the shipped two-line + P87's release trim). `place`, `lift` and `release` were
already measured (P88, P89, P87).

**The audit is the phase's product** (`logs/p91/AUDIT.md`, `audit.py` -> `audit.txt`,
offline, three existing records). Each block is defined by its own marks and the
emitting line (`_cycle_begin` at `tasks.py:9969`; `prepose` at `:10148`, `hover` at
`:10205`, `descent` at `:11487`, `close` at `:12539`, `grip` at `:13457`), and the
sub-terms are the *printed* loop counts, so the model is checkable: the descent
reconstructs to 4 % on all three logs. The decomposition is **wait 4.09 s +
failure tax 0.76 s + arm motion 3.63 s**, and the speedable pool is **1.08 s =
7.0 %** - three of the five "blocks" are not what their names say:

* **the descent is not a descent.** Its block is the **fruit-arrival wait**
  (2.17 s, `arrived=True after N steps`) plus a **scheduled** wait (0.59 s,
  `dynamic descent: waited N ticks`) plus the profiled leg (0.74 s). The schedule
  makes the block **invariant**: the wait exits when the fruit is
  `speed*(t_desc + FRUIT_DYNAMIC_DESCEND_MARGIN)` away, so
  `block = wait + leg = lead/speed - margin` and **a faster leg just waits
  longer**. Two independent legs agree - the profile arithmetic (the 5.5 cm leg
  is **jerk-bound**: 86 ticks at `a_max` 0.8 *and* at 1.6; 64 only at `v_max`
  0.25 **and** `a_max` 1.6) and the measurement (`t_desc` spans **0.03 s** while
  the block's own sd is **8.9 ticks**: the leg is not an available variable at
  all; what moves the block is the per-fruit handover lead). **A profile cell on
  the descent can only break the catch window; it cannot compress the block.**
* **the grip is 1.75 s clean / 2.36 s mean**, and the bimodality is **P40's
  tax**: a failed probe **+1.53 s**, a burnt cap **+2.29 s**, and the mean
  carries **0.61 s** of it. Measured, not sped. Inside the clean **210 ticks** the
  60-tick **validation ramp** is the only profile (the 54-tick belt-break beside
  it is the P3 anti-shear constant), and it is a **1:1** lever: the single arm's
  40-tick probe's clean block is **190 ticks** against the two-line's **210** -
  Δ 20 with an identical 150-tick remainder.
* **the close** is catch-up 0.63 + a 22-tick ramp + a 48-tick hold (direction
  contested: R11-B/P18b measured a *slower* close converting the direct carried
  class 48 -> 27), **the hover** is `move_to` at the IK step cap (no profile; R3's
  residency negative on this line), **the prepose** a tuned 45-tick blend + a
  20-tick session pump.

So the cell was the **grip's probe ramp**, `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PROBE_TICKS` 60 -> 24
two-line-scoped (`probe_ticks_resolution`, the fourth of the scoped family; the
`[biarm] take-off profile:` row; `physics.takeoff`; the `250` leg), and it
measured the **lever exactly and lost anyway**. The clean `grip` block is a
deterministic constant and it fell **210 -> 173 ticks = -0.31 s against the
registered -0.300** at **both** seeds and in both modes (seed 6's cheap re-seat
1.95 -> 1.65), which is the 1:1 prediction confirmed to one tick. **And the block
mean rose** (+0.23 / +0.38) because the **mode mix moved**: first-probe success
**14/20 -> 5/20** and **18/20 -> 9/20**. The mechanism is that **the ramp's
duration *is* the validation's detection margin** - the grasp test is
`fruit_z - z_before > 4 mm` and 6 mm over 60 ticks leaves 2 mm of slack where 6 mm
over 24 does not - **and the force servo's squeeze window**, because
`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_TAKEOFF_SQUEEZE_S = 0.10` s lives inside the probe's own ticks. The
class moved with it at both seeds: `never-grasped` **4 -> 6** and **1 -> 4**, a new
`carried-not-placed` 0 -> 3, the loaded-slide guard (`force_min == 0.00 N`) **4 ->
9** and **7 -> 11**, and the delivered pinch **9.65 -> 7.77 N** at seed 6 with
**10/18 held legs under the 9.0 N floor** against P41's 9.7-9.9 N plateau. The
delivered side rose at both seeds (interval **10.59 -> 13.01** and **11.08 ->
12.20 s**; window 5.66 -> 4.61 / 5.41 -> 4.92 placed/min; `placed/min wall`
2.95 -> 2.32 / 2.34 -> 2.33) - **P88/P89/the union/the fail-fast for the fourth
time**: a 0.30 s block delta is not deliverable on this cell.

**Not shipped.** `PROBE_TWO_LINE_DEFAULT = False`, so unset resolves the shipped
60-tick probe on every path; the measured arm is `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PROBE_TICKS=24`,
the machinery is default off, and no reference was re-recorded (`423896f7` /
`8952c320` / `423896f7` untouched). The guards that **passed** are what makes the
negative readable: landing **16/16, 11/11, 12/12, 12/12 `on_belt`**; the catch
window residual median **5.9 mm in all four cells**, `end=` max 10.6-12.7 mm (bar
25), grasp 16/14/19/16 with the 14/20 bar met; all four cells' motion budgets
clean.

**Read rules this phase adds.** (1) **A block is wait + tax + motion, and only
the motion is a lever** - audit before registering, and check whether a "block" is
*scheduled* (the descent), *taxed* (the grip) or *unprofiled* (the hover) before
pricing it. (2) **A tick trim on a validation can invert the block**: the clean
instance falls by exactly its ticks while the block *mean* rises, so the
branch-free read is the **mode-aware clean instance**, never the mean. (3) **A
tick cell can be coupled to a force** - read the delivered pinch (`[carry]
force_min`) and the loaded-slide guard beside any take-off change. (4) The
driver's `[run] attempt` window pairing **slips** when the two arms' attempts
complete out of print order (`T5`: 6 adjacent rows, |`total - window`| to 6.79 s);

## P92 - the census says the scenario lane is not empty, and the servo's chase is a symptom

2026-11-02, `logs/p92/`. Owner directive: the shipped cell reads 70 % (28/40, two
seeds) and the delivered speed is at its floor, so the remaining term is
*success*; hardware (a new pad asset, a real-jaw clamp-force anchor) is out of
scope, so find the scenario-side losses. Nothing was adopted, no `src/`,
`configs/`, `datasets/` or checkpoint change, and no reference was re-recorded.

### What the census had to be careful about

The brief lists ten same-tree logs. They are **two scenarios**, not ten samples:
`p87/T5` and `p87/T6` are the distinct seed-5/seed-6 cells, and `p88/{C5,C6,N5}`,
`p89/{C5,C6}`, `p91/{C5,C6,N5}` are byte-identical replays of them (each phase's
own proof, re-verified here on the `[fruit]` stream). Pooling all ten would
multiply n by five and make every share below four times too confident. So the
census reads **40 distinct attempts**, and the pre-P87 clock (`p84/{D5,D6}`,
26/40) is a **separate block** - same scenario, different release clock, never
pooled. `p80/{T20,T6}` are its replays and carry no `[carry]` diag, so 4-5 of
their rows cannot be classified; they are counted as unclassifiable rather than
guessed.

### The classification, and why the summary text is not evidence

The two-line arms run concurrently and the `[task]` prints are arm-agnostic, so
the only sound association is the attempt boundary (`[task] target … with <arm>
arm` -> `[biarm] result <arm> index=…`) plus the `[carry]` rows that name that
arm. The result row alone cannot separate the two failure classes the brief asks
for - both present as `fruit did not follow the gripper` - so the class comes
from the legs: a `cnp` is a payload that left a pinch that existed (`fmax > 0`
then `force_min == 0`, a `loss_row`, `clean_slip > 100 mm`); **never-held** is a
leg with `contacts@onset == 0`, `force@onset == 0.00 N` *and* `fmax == 0.00 N`,
i.e. no pinch ever existed.

### The census: 9 + 3, and the three are not an acquisition class

Twelve failures: **9 `cnp` (75 %) + 3 never-held (25 %)**, zero
`fell off the line`, zero lost slots, 1-2 `diverted`. The never-held attempts are
**exactly** the attempts whose `dynamic catch-up: residual` exceeds the 6 mm
tolerance (**3/3 vs 0/37**), which is P47/P48's live pre-contact discriminator
reproduced on the two-line.

But "never-held" is a label about *when*, not *what*. Three reads settle it:

1. **`gap_start - dia <= -14 mm` is 5/5 failed against 7/35 otherwise**
   (Fisher one-sided **p = 0.0012**). `gap_start` is the commanded pad gap the
   carry leg found; -14 mm means the pads were commanded *inside* the fruit's own
   width. The five are the 3 never-held **and** the 2 seed-5 `cnp` - one event
   seen at the leg start. The T5 peach is the plainest: its close froze at
   **66.3 mm** around a **68.9 mm** fruit (-2.6 mm, a correct seat) and the lift
   leg then started at **54.5 mm**. Something squeezed 11.8 mm inside the fruit
   between the freeze and the carry.
2. **The servo's own travel is the mechanism.** The `[task] force servo:` row
   prints, per arm, `closed=` - how far the integral law walked the command
   inward. **`closed > 0` on 11 attempts, all 11 failed; 1 failure in the 29
   without it** (p = C(12,11)/C(40,11) = **5.2e-09**). The 11 hold all 3
   never-held and 8 of the 9 `cnp`: the cell's *whole* failure set is one
   mechanism. In the code's own terms it is `_force_servo_step` closing by `STEP`
   while the force sits under `max(2.0 N, 0.8 * ref)` for 3 ticks, bounded by
   `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_FORCE_RANGE = 15 mm`; on a marginal grip the settle reference
   reads **`ref = 0.00 N`**, so nothing tells the servo the jaws are empty and it
   walks the full range (`closed = 15.00 / 18.00 / 20.20 / 25.00 mm`,
   `trips = 38-88`).
3. **The pre-P87 block reproduces it**: 14 chases, 14 failures; 0 failures in 26
   without (`logs/p92/chase.txt`).

So the addressable class is 3 attempts *as a count* and **0 as a mechanism**: the
never-held class is the same close collapse as the 75 %, detected one phase
earlier. The attractive supply reading - 2 of the 3 at the delivered
`x = 0.386 / 0.391`, at the record's 0.39 clean edge - **does not survive** the
pre-P87 block, whose six never-held span `x = 0.273 / 0.279 / 0.291 / 0.368 /
0.391 / 0.414`. That is the finding that corrected the phase's own first
registration (D1).

### The non-classes, measured

* **Starvation is a wait, not a loss.** Every cell ran 20/20 attempts. The
  `no eligible fruit` polls (45 / 37) sit inside the wait, and the failures'
  `descent` blocks are *longer* than the successes' (3.50 vs 3.05 s at seed 6;
  4.21 vs 3.50 at seed 5) - the failures are not the starved ones. The handover
  `queue` is **3.25 on successes vs 3.17 on failures**: no depth signal.
* **The diversion is a pool slot.** `diverting … after 2 failed attempts` names a
  *slot*, and its second attempt is a **different instance at seed 6**
  (`x` 0.299 -> 0.343, i.e. the slot was recycled) and the *same* one at seed 5
  (0.239 / 0.241). A "retire it sooner" rule would change one attempt in 40 and
  remove a slot; recorded as a non-lever.
* **P38b's low-tail margin purchase has no events.** The delivered x minimum is
  **0.1998 m**, 20 mm above the left arm's 0.180 admission floor, and there is
  not one low-tail failure in 40 attempts. The record's registered-not-run lever
  is at the wrong end of *this* distribution; the tail that exists is the **top**.

### Arm 1: the band's top (`PREREG.md` 07c54712, cells T5/T6)

`FRUIT_SUPPLY_X_MAX` 0.36 -> 0.33. The reason this is the cleanest A/B the
scenario admits: `respawn` draws `x = uniform(x_min, x_max)` - one draw whose
*value* the bounds map affinely and whose *count* they do not change, and no code
branches on x - so the treatment is **the identical release stream, laterally
compressed by 0.8125**: same species, diameters, grades, release times, along
positions. The build row prints `lateral x=0.20-0.33` in both treatment cells.

Measured (20 attempts x 2 seeds, controls replayed line-for-line with P91):

| | C5 | T5 | C6 | T6 | pooled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| placed | 16/20 | **18/20** | 12/20 | **18/20** | **28 -> 36** |
| `cnp` | 2 | 2 | 7 | **1** | 9 -> 3 |
| never-held | 2 | **0** | 1 | 1 | 3 -> 1 |
| chase (`closed > 0`) | 4 | **2** | 7 | **3** | 11 -> 5 |
| pooled interval | 10.59 | **10.13** | 11.08 | **9.84** | better at both |

The cleanest single read is the **first attempt at seed 5**: same slot, same
fruit (left kiwi 5.4 cm), same release time, same instrumentation, only the
lateral position differs - `x = 0.3908` in the control (never-held) becomes
`x = 0.3616` in the treatment (placed, lift +0.29 m). And the *class* movement is
at both seeds, not just the count: the closed loaded-slide class, which the
record closed across its cell parameter space, **falls 9 -> 3** (seed 6: 7 -> 1).

**Verdict: NOT ADOPTED**, on the pre-registered G3. T6's leg 1 reads `|v|max`
**0.222 against its 0.161 budget** (+38 %) with `a_med 0.97`; the control has its
own standing over-budget leg at seed 6 (leg 12, `0.164/0.160`, +2.5 %, the same
leg P86/P87/P88 recorded as a branch fact), so the treatment's is a different leg
at 15x the excursion. The same seed's branch also carries a **419 N** carry leg
(`fmax 419.25 N`, in-hand 1.545 m/s, `cone 6.18x`) with **1313 mm** of pad-centre
bookkeeping offset - absent from both controls (0 rows > 500 mm). The budget was
not re-tuned (AGENTS section 2), and the count is a draw (the same control swings
16 -> 12 between these seeds), so the rule stops it. The mechanism claim is
therefore the **class set**, not the rate: the stations sit at a **band edge** of
R10-A's top-down reach at the shipped band's top (left x = 0.36 -> `y
0.00..+0.10` with the station at 0.00; right x = 0.36 -> `y -0.10..0.00` with the
station at **-0.10**), and at x <= 0.33 both are inside the neighbouring x = 0.28
column's band. That is an interpolation between two measured columns, not a new
reach measurement, and it is the named next spend.

### Arm 2: the servo's contact gate (`PREREG_A1.md` e5150253, cells R5/R6)

The census's chase read is the strongest discriminator on the tree, so the phase
tested its causal reading directly with the cell's own documented, default-off
discipline (`FRUIT_FORCE_REENTRY=1`, P7's "FARM Port A": run the integral law only
while the contact estimate is confident, otherwise **hold** the gap).

The gate does exactly what it says: **31 and 29 force-mode entries** with **890
and 1730 withheld chase ticks**, the chase set **11 -> 3**, and the held-leg pinch
untouched (median `force_min` **9.42 / 9.36 / 9.72 / 9.10 N** - the P41 plateau
on all four cells), landing 28/28 on belt. And **the count does not move**: 16 ->
16 at seed 5, 12 -> 12 at seed 6 (pooled **28 -> 28** against the 30 bar), with
the classes **re-distributing** (`cnp` 9 -> 8 - seed 5 *up* 2 -> 3, seed 6 down
7 -> 5 - against never-held 3 -> **4**, seed 6 *up* 1 -> 3, plus five
`grasped, not placed (no note)` rows) and the interval **worse** at both seeds
(10.59 -> 11.59, 11.08 -> 13.48). **G2 fails at seed 5** (`cnp` 3 > 2):
**NOT ADOPTED**.

The transferable finding: **the chase is the signature, not the cause.** With the
chase withheld the payload still leaves (or was never in the pinch), and the same
physical event then presents one phase later as never-held. A discriminator with
p = 5e-09 can still be a *symptom*; only an intervention separates the two.

A detail worth keeping: with the gate on, the branch **re-draws into the high-x
tail** - R5 presents a left kiwi at **x = 0.405**, R6 at **0.388 / 0.364** - which
is exactly the zone arm 1 removes. A recovery change lets the presentation
wander; a supply change bounds it.

### What this phase leaves behind

* **The scenario lane is not empty, and the lever is the presentation.** The
  record's "the loaded slide is closed" is true of the *cell's* parameter space
  (force, seat, pads, attitude, height, station, speed, clock) and **not** of
  *which lateral column the fruit is presented in*: 9 -> 3 on the same class.
* **The chase (`closed > 0`) is the census's general instrument** (11/11 and
  14/14) and **not** its causal read.
* **The re-entry, priced**: (1) diagnose T6's leg 1 and the 419 N leg (the
  `carry-assist` `|offset| = 1313 mm` family - a hand-frame/bookkeeping
  pathology, and the `stored pad centre … re-anchoring` rows are the same
  family); (2) a **third seed** (two seeds both at 18/20 is suspiciously tight);
  (3) if clean, both motion references re-recorded from same-batch runs, the
  acceptance and the two-line gate re-based, every store re-baselined with the
  **`supply.x_min/x_max` manifest field added first** (`assets.scene_provenance`
  does not carry the supply band, so a store under 0.20-0.33 and one under
  0.20-0.36 are currently indistinguishable), and the direct/policy interface
  measured (it builds its own profile from the same `SupplyPlan.from_env`).
* **No-harm**: the controls replay `logs/p91/{C5,C6}.log` 1033/1033 and 970/970
  modulo one profile row's `origin` label (the resolved clock is identical - the
  P87 A1 convention), `selfcheck.sh` PASS (0 failures), `accept.sh` 7/10 +
  `fingerprint: matches` + `190: PASS` (this tree's standing branch),
  `211_bed_audit.py` ok (115 checks), 64/64 payload-present releases on belt.
* **Deviations** (all in `logs/p92/RESULTS.md` section 9): the pre-P87 block
  corrected registration 1 (D1), F1b's delivered-max "bound" is mis-specified
  because the delivered x is a distribution (D2), the fingerprint clause is
  recorded not gated because every 20-attempt two-line reference predates P87's
  clock (D3), `census.py`/`p92_report.py` evolved after the battery header (D4),
  `chase.py` is a new instrument created after `PREREG.md` and pinned in
  `header_r.txt` (D5), and the control at seed 6 has its own standing
  over-budget leg (D6).
* **Re-baseline: none** - nothing shipped.

## P93 - the re-entry: both red flags are branch artifacts, and the third seed refutes the count

2026-11-02, `logs/p93/`. Owner directive: P92's named re-entry, and the goal is
the **success rate**. So: diagnose the two guard failures, add the third seed,
and land the adoption package **if** the gate passes. It does not: the band stays
`FRUIT_SUPPLY_X_MAX=0.36` and the only shipped change is metadata.

### The diagnostics: one attempt, two flags, both of them the control's too

Both flags sit on **seed 6, attempt 0, the right arm's first kiwi**, so the whole
diagnostic is one attempt read twice. `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_TRACE=1` gives one row per
tick for `descent`/`catchup`/`close`/`carry`; the two traced cells (`D6C`/`D6T`,
`ATTEMPTS=4`) reproduce the untraced P92 cells **to the number**
(`0.108/10.6 mm`, `0.222/58.9 mm`, `480.6 mm`, `1169.1 mm`) and each was run
twice, so the event is deterministic and the trace is run-neutral at that
attempt. One first-pass mistake is recorded as D1: both cells initially wrote
into the shared `logs/dynamic_trace/` and overwrote each other's attempt-0 file,
so each got its own `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_TRACE_DIR` and both cells were re-run.

**`T6`'s leg 1 is a jam onset.** A chase is excluded *by construction* - the
descent's target is computed before the leg (`intercept=-0.0831`) and the
commanded profile is the same 88 samples in both cells, so there is no moving
target to chase. Over the leg the payload moves **90 mm at exactly the belt
speed** (0.123 m/s) and ~0 mm in `z`: the leg does not displace it. What it does
is **arrive on it** - at the first tick after the leg the pads read **71.1 N over
2 contacts** with the jaw span closing 97 -> 76 mm around a 62 mm kiwi, and the
payload is then driven **down through the belt** (`z` 1.197 -> 0.005, peak `|vz|`
4.6 m/s). The control does the same thing at the same attempt (41.8 N, `z` ->
0.818). And both payloads are **already at 2.4x belt speed when the leg starts**
(0.284 / 0.286 m/s, ~4.2-4.7 rad/s of spin), so the disturbance predates the leg.
Its source is **open**: no trace covers the wait/pre-pose window, and the leading
candidate is the other arm's pre-pose transit, whose 1.9-2.6 mm minimum
separation the record already measures. PREREG §1a's binary reading also turned
out **not applicable as written** (D2): the `descent` phase is traced **once**,
at the leg's start (`tasks.py:11509` emits before the profiled descent), so there
is no per-tick contact read *inside* the leg - the phase reads the two states
either side of it and says so.

**The 419 N / 1313 mm leg is a bookkeeping artifact with a physical
consequence.** All three registered clauses pass: `|offset| = 1313 mm` against
the hand's own tool scale of 70 mm (`_pad_standoff`) and **20-62 mm on every
other leg of the batch**; the payload sits 1180 mm from the fingertip (1132 mm of
it in `-z`); the commanded `jaw_target` is 1313 mm from the measured pads; and
the pads *are* on the payload (`contacts@onset=1`, `sep@onset 46.6 mm` inside a
61.6 mm fruit). The path is `tasks.py:11047` - `_gripper_offset` is set to
`rot.T @ (payload - tcp_position())`, a *tool* offset only while the pads are on
the payload - applied **only** in `_carry`'s **incoherent** branch
(`centre - rot @ offset_tool`, `:5361-5366`), which **does not consult
`hand_is_jaw`** while the coherent branch (`:5331`) and the place loop (`:6079`)
both do. So the payload's distance from the tool becomes a commanded 1.3 m jump;
the 419 N, the 1.545 m/s in-hand peak and the 2361 mm `clean_slip_max` are that
arm flight. **The control carries the same defect at 116 mm.**

Per PREREG §1c both are **branch artifacts**: present in the same-seed control,
and the monotonicity route needs two seeds carrying the event while only seed 6
does (seeds 5's attempt 0 reads 5.9 mm in **both** arms). The per-instance
witness for "branch, not band" is the direction: that attempt delivered
`x = 0.2507` (T) against `0.2447` (C), i.e. **6 mm further out** - the wrong way
for a band whose mapping compresses `x` by 0.8125.

### The seeds: the class clause survives, the count does not

Two fresh seeds (101, 202), control vs `FRUIT_SUPPLY_X_MAX=0.33`, 20 attempts
each, P92's instrumentation verbatim, one claim per run. Controls **16, 12, 15,
15**; treatments **18, 18, 14, 15**. Never-held **2->0 / 1->1 / 0->0 / 2->1**
(pooled **5 -> 2**, p = 0.44); `cnp` **2->2 / 7->1 / 5->6 / 3->4** (pooled
17 -> 13, p = 0.54). Placed pooled **58/80 (72.5 %) -> 65/80 (81.3 %)**, Fisher
**p = 0.2604**, and **the whole pooled gain is seed 6's +6**: the fresh seeds
read `15 -> 14` and `15 -> 15`. The two fresh controls are **15/20 twice**
against seed 6's 12/20 - so P92's `28 -> 36` was measured against the *worst* of
the four control branches the tree has. The delivered side follows the count,
not the band (interval better at 5/6 and worse at 101/202).

**Verdict: NOT ADOPTED**, on three named clauses: rule 2 (seed 101's placed count
falls 15 -> 14), G1 (`cnp` rises at both fresh seeds), G3 (`T202` leg 14,
0.183/0.161). The count clause was deliberately stricter than the project's own
doctrine; it fires anyway, and the doctrinal read says the same thing.

### G3, read across 160 legs: the motion budget is arm-symmetric

The four over-budget descents sit **two in controls** (`C6` leg 12 +2.5 %, the
standing P86/P87/P88 branch leg; **`C101` leg 9 `0.224/0.160` = +40 %**) and
**two in treatments** (`T6` leg 1 +38 %, `T202` leg 14 +14 %) - 2.5 % of 160
legs - and they are **uncorrelated with the catch-up**: `C101` leg 9 and `T202`
leg 14 both run clean catch-ups (every residual <= 6.0 mm), while `C5`'s two
missed catch-ups (251.0 / 87.6 mm) run descents **inside** budget. So the
over-budget descent is a stochastic branch property of this scenario in either
arm, which is what AGENTS §2 means by "the ratio has no clean gap and the budget
cannot tell a boundary strain from a real push". The budget was **not** re-tuned.
`C101`'s leg 9 is the phase's cleanest single read: **a control cell on the
shipped band produces the same excursion class the treatment was refused for at
seed 6** - so a one-leg G3 failure in a two-seed A/B is not evidence against a
scenario change.

### The power statement, for whoever wants this lever certified

At the observed 8.75-point pooled difference, the two-sided 0.05 / 80 %-power
sample is **364 attempts per arm** (5-6 times this phase's), with the
**never-held class** as the registered endpoint and the count as a report. That
is the named next spend; not another two-seed batch.

### What shipped: `supply.band`, the provenance gap P92 named

PREREG §6 made this the precondition for any recollection and it is metadata
only. `assets.supply_provenance(plan)` returns the resolved band
(`x_min`/`x_max`), the along draws, the two mixes and the **resolved schedule
name** (`bed > patch > wave > scatter`, else `fixed`); **both** manifest writers
call it under the same key `supply.band` (`scripts/40_collect_demos.py` and
`SortingRLEnv._supply_band_provenance`, the latter inside a `try/except`). The
gap it closes is specific: the *collector's* shard manifest already carried
`supply.x_min`/`x_max` and both mixes (`datasets/v12d_s02/manifest.json` reads
`x_max: 0.36`), while the **direct env's** rollout manifest carried only its P58
profile block - so a direct/rollout store under 0.20-0.33 and one under 0.20-0.36
were indistinguishable. A store without `supply.band` predates P93. Pinned in the
existing provenance leg (`scripts/239_p72_clr_edge_selftest.py` section 6: the
signature, the arithmetic, all four branch orders, the `SupplyPlan` field set
read from the dataclass's own AST, one call site per writer).

### No-harm, and the pins

`selfcheck.sh` PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped); `accept.sh` **7/10, 9.4 s/attempt,
`fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`** with its **449 `[fruit]` lines
byte-identical (449/449)** to `logs/p91/accept_final.log`; `211_bed_audit.py` ok
(115 checks); `106` OK; `107` PASS (21 checks). No motion reference was
re-recorded and none is owed (`423896f7` / `423896f7` / `8952c320` stand).
`tasks.py` untouched (`7ba4bb58`, so `rl_env.TASKS_MD5` stands).

### Deviations, all in `logs/p93/RESULTS.md` section 8

D1 the shared trace directory cost one wasted pair (fixed, and the re-run doubles
as the determinism proof); D2 PREREG §1a's binary reading is not applicable as
written (one descent row, not per tick); D3 forty stale `logs/dynamic_trace_*.json`
from 2026-10-26 were moved to `/tmp/opencode/`; D4 the report's summary line
mixes pooled and per-seed verdicts and section 4 is the binding statement; D5 the
§1c monotonicity route is unreachable by construction at one carrying seed.

**Re-baseline: none** - nothing shipped.

## P94 (2026-11-02): the `_gripper_offset` command jump is bounded - a carry-command fix, and the only legs it moves are the two that could not be a tool offset

**The defect P93 named, fixed.** `_gripper_offset[side]` is written once per grasp
at the grasp routine's entry as `rot.T @ (spawner.position(sample) -
arm.tcp_position())` (`tasks.py:11047`) - a **tool** offset only while the pads are
on the payload, and the payload's **distance** when the fruit was far out then.
`_carry`'s **assisted** branch applied it unguarded
(`arm.tcp_target_for_jaw(centre - rot @ offset_tool)`, `:5361-5366`) while the
**coherent** branch (`:5326`), the **`_carry` tail** (`:6087`) and **`_place_low`**
(`:14258-14287`) all guard it with `hand_is_jaw` - and `_release_lower` refuses
past its own 0.20 m `FRUIT_RELEASE_ARM_TRACK`. Two facts make the site live rather
than a corner case: the shipped OpenArm hand takes the **assisted** branch on
**every** leg (`self._coherent[arm_name]` is only set `True` when the *pre-close*
fingertip error is `<= 20 mm`, and the openarm fallback prints
`openarm fingertips <N> mm from the fruit; closing anyway` and does not set it -
measured 20/20 at `58.3-64.3 mm`, and 1638/1638 `carry-assist` rows across the P91-P93
corpus read `coherent=False`), and the documented reset (`if not coherent:
_gripper_offset[...] = [0, 0, wrist_back]`, `:11609`) is **dead code** - it sits
inside `if coherent:` (`:11054`) - so the raw value is what the carry reads.

**The fix is one ternary.** `FRUIT_CARRY_OFFSET_MAX` (metres; unset **0.20 m
shipped**, `=0` restores the pre-P94 expression bit for bit) via
`tasks.parse_carry_offset_max()`: past the bound the jaw hand is commanded the
**pads** (`centre`) - the coherent branch's own command, i.e. the same
`hand_is_jaw` guard the reference sites use - and inside it the command is
unchanged. The bound is not a new constant: 0.20 m is `FRUIT_RELEASE_ARM_TRACK`'s
own pad/arm-relation threshold. The guard is **jaw-hand only**, so the
kinematic-pad hand keeps its offset at any magnitude (for it the number really is
a tool offset).

**Why a bound and not the unconditional guard.** The unconditional `hand_is_jaw`
form would move all 142 legs by their own 11-117 mm reading - a re-calibration of
the carry on every attempt, unattributable on a 20-attempt cell. P94 registered
**F1** instead: *a leg below the bound must not move*. It did not (0 legs), which
is what makes the fix shippable as "the defect's removal and nothing else". The
unconditional form stays the named replacement (`logs/p94/RESULTS.md` section 9).

**The measurement** (`ATTEMPTS=20`, the shipped two-line default, P92/P93's
instrumentation, four seeds - 5/6 = P92's control records, 101/202 = P93's fresh
pair - plus `N5` the tree check and `P5` the post-flip replay):

* **Admissibility**: `N5` (unset, pre-flip tree) is **1033/1033** `[fruit]` lines
  identical to `p92/C5`, and a second pre-flip unset cell (`P5_preflip`) is
  **1033/1033** too; after the default flip, `P5` (unset) is **974/974** identical
  to `T5` (explicit `0.20`) - the shipped default **is** the measured arm.
* **The invariant**: the largest applied jump in any treatment cell is **117 mm**
  (an unguarded leg's own reading, T6) and every leg whose reading is above the

* **F2, the prefix identity**: seed 5 is identical to its control for **111**

* **Counts**: placed `16->17` (seed 5), `12->12`, `15->15`, `15->15`; `cnp`

  The +1 at seed 5 is **not** a conversion - the guarded leg stays `never_held`

* **The acceptance**: the gate of record **moved**, and its own A/B names why. With
