## P95 (2026-11-02): where the incoming fruit gets its disturbance — the other arm's pads

P94 shipped the carry-side bound and named the open item: the *upstream* cause of
a payload already displaced at the grasp's entry. P93's evidence was one number -
the seed-6 attempt-0 right kiwi at **0.284 m/s, 4.2-4.7 rad/s of spin when the
descent leg starts** - with a written caveat that *"no trace covers the
wait/pre-pose window"*.

**The instrument.** `FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE=<max rows>` (`tasks.py`, default off): one
row per control tick for the **selected fruit** through its whole attempt -
position, linear and angular velocity, the belt's encoder speed, and every live
fruit within 0.15 m (offset, velocity, mass, diameter, carried flag). Armed at
the attempt's start (before the pre-pose blend), flushed from `note_result`, one
JSON per attempt; the phase column is the existing `FRUIT_CYCLE_REPORT` mark, so
the table joins the `[cycle]` breakdown with no new bookkeeping. `..._ARM=1` adds
each arm's jaw centre / TCP / both finger links / measured jaw span (the
articulation-link read of AGENTS section 2 - a separately declared cell);
`..._NOOP=1` is the instrument's own control (same hook, same per-tick calls, no
readback), the `FRUIT_PROXIMITY_TRACE=2` pattern.

**The measurement of the measurement.** Both cells replay their records end to
end: `F6` (fruit only) and `A6` (fruit **+ both arms' link reads**) are **970/970**
on the `[fruit]` stream against `logs/p94/T6.log`, and `A5` is **974/974** against
`logs/p94/T5.log`. So the fruit trace is branch-neutral as §2 predicts, and - as
a *measured* result, not an assumption - **this two-arm read set is too**: 3 prims
per arm, on a baseline that already reads the active hand's TCP and both fingers
every tick, where the rule's 7-10-prim read across many links moved runs by 3-14 s.
The rule stands; this read set is inside it. Every geometry number in the phase is
therefore a number of the recorded branch.

**A documentation detail the record should carry.** `_cycle_mark("descent")` fires
*after* `_approach`, so the rows labelled `descent` are the leg's **end** (the
catch-up's first tick); the leg's start is `first_descent_tick - steps`, from that
leg's own `[motion] approach … steps=`. That is why the phase-per-sample trace had
nothing to say about the wait window - not merely because it samples sparsely.

**The witness, reproduced to the digit.** On the unmodified branch the leg's start
(tick 339, t=17.225 s) reads `v = (-0.2529, -0.1254, +0.0338)`,
`w = (0.1955, -8.3608, -0.1637)`, fruit `(0.24465, 0.0002, 1.19947)` - P93's own
`descent` row, i.e. **2.37x belt**. The departure is at **t=16.98**, **0.25 s
before the leg**, inside the descent's own hover wait. On those ticks:

* the fruit takes `+0.402 m/s` in **x** and `+0.133` in **z**, with the spin going
  `0.004 -> 21.6 rad/s` in three ticks;
* the **left** hand's *measured* jaw span collapses **98.0 -> 59.8 mm over 15
  ticks and springs back to 98.0 by t=17.25** (a commanded close does not spring
  back, and the finger drive is stiffness-limited to **0.1 mm** at P41's
  `k=1e5 N/m` and the 10 N/joint cap, so a 38 mm span change cannot be commanded -
  it is a contact displacing the pads; the left arm's own close on its own pear is
  at 20.475 s);
* the left hand's pad point is **+2 mm** from the fruit's surface, with the pad
  **-16 mm** along the belt away;
* the active (right) hand is **160-190 mm** away at its hover (`sep` 98.0, no
  descent for another 0.25 s).

**What the other arm was doing is in the log**: `[biarm] left: station acquired at
t=16.4s`, `[task] target pear (grade A, 6.9 cm) with left arm` at 16.45, `at pick
pose after 0.71 s … jaw=[0.3429, 0.0122, 1.2795]` at ~17.16, `[cycle] attempt 1:
prepose=0.71 hover=0.75 …`. The left jaw descends from its parked `z=1.3581` to
`1.2795` during that blend, so its **pad plane sweeps from `belt_top + 0.107`
down to `belt_top + 0.029`** - *through* the fruit band (the kiwi's top is
`belt_top + 0.058`) and **29 mm below** it. The strike is 0.53 s into that 0.71 s
blend.

**The other four classes, excluded by measurement.** (b) *release*: no teleport,
no velocity zeroing; the spawn drop **is** a real departure class (airborne at
`z=1.230`, `|v|` to 0.665 m/s) but only **2/40** attempts start that way and both
settle in 8 ticks, ~4 s before the leg - and P38/P50 measured the release offset
as the *static* per-instance shift (mechanism closed), which this phase does not
reopen. (c) *belt/cleat*: the kick is `+x`/`+z` with 21.6 rad/s of spin; the belt
drives `-y` only, P38 measured its lateral contribution as exactly **0.000 mm**
over 475 transits, and no cleat exists on this line. (d) *depenetration /
fruit-fruit*: the nearest neighbour (the left pear) sits 125 mm away running
`0.1201-0.1205 m/s` with **nb swing 0.0004 / 0.0001 / 0.0 / 0.0 m/s** on the strike
ticks - a mutual impulse would show there and in mass-weighted momentum, and
neither moves. (e) *the grasping arm*: 160-190 mm away, at its hover.

**The census** (2 seeds x 20 attempts). Departures before the descent leg
(peak one-tick `|dv| >= 0.05 m/s`): **3 arm-other clusters, all in the one
attempt**; 2 release drops; 4 unattributed (the fruit is still upstream at
`y=0.42-0.65` - its own rolling transient after the release); **no arm-self and no
fruit-fruit**. Every other leg starts at **1.00x belt** (19/20 at seed 6, 20/20 at
seed 5), so an overspeeding payload at the grasp entry is **not** a property of
the line - it is one event, and that event is the pad strike. And the exposure is
**one-directional**, because the stations are `left y=+0.000` / `right y=-0.100` on
a `-y` belt: a **right**-arm fruit must cross the left station, a **left**-arm
fruit stops at its own. Measured as the *other* hand's closest pad point before
the leg: **right-arm attempts n=19, median 31.6 mm, min 0.0, 5/19 <= 6.4 mm**;
**left-arm attempts n=21, median 217.2 mm, min 126.3, 0/21**. Of the four inside
6 mm exactly **one** displaces the pads - **1 contact / 40**, inside a 4-5/40
contact band; the other three are zero-impulse grazes (seed-5 attempt 16 passes at
0.0 mm with `|v|` exactly 0.120 m/s, spin exactly 0.0 and `sep` 98.0 throughout).

**Why it costs the attempt.** The hover latches the grip point
(`_dynamic_grip_target`, `x = 0.273` at t~14.9) and the descent is static and
open-loop, so the strike's **28 mm** lateral offset at the leg's start (43 mm of
drift during the leg, `x -> 0.202`) against a **6 mm** catch-up tolerance puts the
pads *on* the fruit (`58.15 N` after 5 ticks, span 99.1 mm frozen at 88.3 mm),
drives it down through the belt (`z 1.198 -> 0.818`) and the attempt ends
`never_held` (`force@onset = 0.00 N`, `contacts@onset = 0`). The phase claims no conversion:
there is no counterfactual cell, and it does not need one - the defect is an
invariant violation, not a rate.

**The fix, priced and not built.** A *clearance pre-pose*: the two-line pre-pose
must be a pose whose pads clear the tallest fruit (`jaw_z >= belt_top + 0.155`),
with the descent still starting at the hover. The left station has no such pose
today and the record says why - P39: *"the left station is the calibrated pick
point (`y = 0.00 = cfg.pick_y`), so `_prepare_two_line_stations` skips its solve"*
- so the change is a **second station solve at hover height**, using the right
station's own machinery (residual 6.7 mm). It is not a one-liner: the pose is a
solved joint vector, not a scalar, so there is no `FRUIT_*`-style bound to bound
it. And it **moves every attempt**, unlike P94's bounded ternary, so it owes both
motion references, the acceptance re-base and every two-line store. The two other
forms are worse (a cross-lane pre-pose gate spends the pipeline overlap the
two-line's rate is made of; a station separation is reach-bounded on the right at
-0.10 and map-closed for the place station by P90). At 1/40 the expected
conversion is 2.5 points against P93's own **364 attempts per arm** for 8.75
points at 80 % power, so the adoption argument has to be the **invariant**: a hand
inside another lane's fruit band is a defect however rare. **Registered as P96**,
with this report's pre-leg contact census as its primary endpoint - which is now
one command (`FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE=... FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE_ARM=1` then
`python3 logs/p95/probe.py` section 5; criterion `pad gap <= 6 mm` **and**
`other-hand span swing >= 2 mm` within +-4 ticks, the span being the verdict because
the gap is a +-5 mm indicator - the finger plates are angled at a 98 mm span).

**Recorded deviations (METHOD A1).** The spin-jump threshold is **2.0 rad/s**, not
0.5 (a kiwi rolls; 0.5 rad/s fired on the transport's own tumble and produced 149
"departures", almost all rolling jitter); the contact verdict is the
gap **and** span-displacement pair; and the leg's start is log-derived, not a
jaw-height rule (a height rule finds the leg's *end*).

**Shipped**: the default-off instrument, a `252` selfcheck leg (67 checks: the
switch table, the one `_step_sim` hook and that it is *not* in `ik_step`, the
fruit-only default path, the no-op arm returning before any read, the single
arming/disarm/flush sites with their thread-locality, the executed row shape, the
0.15 m neighbour filter, the arm gate, the four env names), and `rl_env.py`'s
`TASKS_MD5` metadata-only follow. `configs/` untouched, **no motion reference
re-recorded and none owed** - the instrument is inert, proven on **3,334
`[fruit]` lines across 4 cells** - the shipped acceptance included, 420/420
byte-identical to `logs/p94/accept_final.log` - rather than argued. `selfcheck.sh` PASS (0
failures, 1 skipped). Pins: `tasks.py` `cc4eea66`, `rl_env.py` `41608912`,
`scripts/252` `880ce131`, `selfcheck.sh` `ed646df6`, `probe.py` `a78f0924`,
`METHOD.md` `b79e9a08`; refs `30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320`; ckpt `moe_v13s`
`61da390a`. Evidence: `logs/p95/{METHOD.md,RESULTS.md,probe.py,probe.txt,
run_p95.sh,header.txt}`, the cells `{F6,A6,A5}.{log,stamps,driver}`, the traces
`logs/p95/{tr6,tr5}/`.

## P96 (2026-11-02): the clearance pre-pose — the invariant is restored, the count is a draw, so the owner decides

P95 priced this fix and did not build it. P96 built it, measured it, and did
**not** ship it — the count clause failed by its letter while the invariant
clause passed cleanly. Everything below is in `logs/p96/`.

**The prior question first: can the station hold a clearing pose at all?** The
offline map (`prepose_map.py`, 36 cells per arm at `x` 0.32/0.34/0.36 and depth
0.095-0.20, in a `T0` and a position-only mode; `prepose_check.py`, the attitudes
and a static pad witness, `restarts = 3`) says **yes, on both arms**, and it also
measured the shipped pose statically for the first time: the calibrated left
pre-pose (the left station *is* the pick point, so `_prepare_two_line_stations`
never solved for it — P39) sits **on the j3 limit (+0.000 rad)** with its pad
point **46 mm below the tallest fruit's top**, and the shipped right pre-pose
(its own `T0` solve at depth 0.095) sits at +0.007 rad. That is P95's live
`belt_top + 0.029` read as geometry, with no run.

**The height arithmetic is the phase's most transferable finding**:
`jaw_achieved = target - residual`, so a target of exactly P95's `0.155` achieves
**0.149-0.152 and does not clear** — every solve lands its 6 mm residual *low*.
The registered target is therefore **0.165** (achieved 0.160 left / 0.155
right), and `FRUIT_BIARM_PREPOSE_CLEAR_Z` raises outside `[0.155, 0.25]`.

**The attitude is not the file.** `configs/waypoints.json`'s declared left
`grasp_quaternion` is the top-down `T0`; `waypoints_oriented.json`'s is 85 deg
from vertical; the *calibrated joint config* the pre-pose actually blends to
stands at **0.7 deg**. So the fix's hold is the pose's **own measured attitude**
(`capture_hold_pose`, `FRUIT_BIARM_PREPOSE_CLEAR_HOLD=calib`), not a file value —
and the alternative (`nat`, position-only, the place leg's form) is kept
reproducible. From the *oriented* seed the two forms read 0.31 rad of margin and
look equivalent; from the **shipped** seed they are 0.020/0.013 (`calib`) against
0.000 on the right (`nat`), which is why the shipped seed decided it.

**The census (the primary endpoint).** Four cells, 20 attempts each, identical
instrumentation (`FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE=2500 FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE_ARM=1
FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1 FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE=1` + the P80 reports), control `=0`,
treatment `=1`. The **control reproduces P95 to the digit**: min gap **0.0 mm**,
`<= 6 mm` **4/40**, **1 contact/40**, and the contact is seed-6 attempt 0's right
kiwi at t = 16.99 s (gap +1.8 mm, span swing 26.4 mm). The **treatment reads min
+5.9 mm, `<= 6 mm` 1/40, contacts 0/40** — and the one remaining row is the
instrument's own floor (a 6.9 cm pear 36.9 mm above a *fixed* 31 mm proxy radius,
0.1 mm of span swing), not a near-miss. Per arm the exposed lane moves most:
right min **0.0 -> +5.9**, `<= 6 mm` **4 -> 1**, contacts **1 -> 0**.

**The count.** Seed 5 **17/20 -> 12/20**, seed 6 **12/20 -> 15/20**, pooled
**29/40 -> 27/40**; per arm pooled **-1 and -1** (left 15/21 -> 14/20, right
14/19 -> 13/20). So the registered G3 (*pooled >= control **and** neither seed
lower by more than one*) **fails by its letter at seed 5**, and the phase reads
it as a draw: the whole movement is seed 5's left arm (9/10 -> 5/10, four `cnp`),
which is exactly P93's "a 20-attempt two-line count is a branch draw" at n = 40.

**The cost is zero, and slightly negative.** The `[cycle]` `prepose` block is
**0.71 s in every cell** (a fixed 45 + 20 ticks), `release` p50 1.69 -> 1.68 s,
and the **`hover` block falls 0.78 -> 0.61 s** because the hand now starts at the
hover height instead of diving 56 mm below it. Wall 819 -> 828 s over 40
attempts; landing **29/29** and **27/27** `on_belt`; **0/20** over-budget descent
legs in both treatment cells (C6's one is its record's own leg 12 — the
P86/P87 documented branch leg, identical in `logs/p94/T6.log`).

**Decision: not adopted; `PREPOSE_CLEAR_TWO_LINE_DEFAULT = False`.** Per the
registration, a fix that restores the invariant *without* losing a placement
ships, and one that trades placements for clearance is the owner's call. This is
the second case (-5 / +3 on two draws, flat per arm), so the measured arm stays
an env value (`FRUIT_BIARM_PREPOSE_CLEAR=1`) and the re-entry is a **4-seed**
cell with the contact census as the endpoint (P93's power rule); more margin on
the biggest fruit is priced in the map (`..._CLEAR_Z=0.18`, at the right arm's j1
margin 0.000).

**No-harm, proven rather than argued.** G0: with the phase's `[ftrace]` row and
the P84/P85 sealed diag rows dropped, **`C5` = `logs/p94/T5.log` 808/808** and
**`C6` = `logs/p94/T6.log` 825/825** — so the trace stack is branch-neutral on
this cell (P95 reproduced), and the treatment differs by the lever alone.
(`PREREG_A2` corrects the reference: `p92/{C5,C6}` predate P94's guard and
diverge at its own row, `|v|max` 1.108 -> 0.270.) The shipped acceptance is
**8/10, 9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**, its **419** physics
`[fruit]` lines byte-identical to `logs/p94/accept_final.log`; `selfcheck.sh`
PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped) with the new `253` leg (39 checks); `106` OK and
`107` PASS (21 checks). No reference re-recorded, none owed - **the knob is off
by default** - and the collector's manifest gained `collection.prepose_clear` /
`prepose_clear_defaulted` / `prepose_clear_z` so a store recorded under the
clearance pose is identifiable (**a manifest without `prepose_clear` predates
P96**; the stations were already carried, the *pose* was not). Pins:
`tasks.py` **`e1095446`**, `rl_env.py` `TASKS_MD5` follow, `scripts/253` new,
`logs/p96/{PREREG.md,PREREG_A1.md,PREREG_A2.md}` `bb057405` / `a2e63f60` /
`724009a0`; refs `30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320`; ckpt `moe_v13s`
`61da390a`. Evidence: `logs/p96/{RESULTS.md,PREREG*.md,prepose_map.py,
prepose_rows.json,prepose_check.py,prepose_check_rows*.json,pg_census.py,
pg_census.txt,p96_report.py,p96_report.txt,gates.sh,run_p96.sh,header.txt}` and
the cells `{C5,T5,C6,T6}.{log,stamps,budgets}`.

## P97 (2026-11-02): the clearance pre-pose ships as the two-line default - the invariant is the argument, the count is not

P96 built the clearance pre-pose, measured the invariant restored, and left it
opt-in because its "no lost placement" clause failed at seed 5. The owner has
decided: ship it as an **invariant fix**. The argument is P95's geometry - the
shipped pre-pose is the calibrated grasp configuration, its pad point sits **46
mm below the tallest fruit's top** on the **j3 limit (+0.000 rad)**, and the
stations are ordered so a right-arm fruit must cross the left station while that
hand blends there: 1 pad contact in 40 attempts, 5/19 right-arm attempts inside
6.4 mm. A hand inside another lane's fruit band is a defect regardless of its
rate (P94's precedent), so the count - P96's two-seed draw **29/40 -> 27/40**
(seed 5 -5, seed 6 +3, per arm -1/-1) - is published, not claimed.

**The flip is one constant, and its inertness pass found a real defect.**
`PREPOSE_CLEAR_TWO_LINE_DEFAULT = False -> True`; the resolver table is P96's
(unset + two-line -> on `default`, no session -> `scope-off`, `=0` -> off
`explicit`, `=1` -> on) at P96's measured arm unchanged (`belt_top + 0.165`,
`hold=calib`, achieved jaw +0.160/+0.155, pad points +0.079/+0.075, margins
+0.020/+0.013 rad, band [0.155, 0.25]). The first post-flip acceptance was
**byte-identical to the pre-P97 record** (8/10 + `matches 30fb99f8`, 419/419 vs
`logs/p94/accept_final.log`) - because `_prepare_two_line_stations` runs
*before* `CoopSession` is created and resolved
`prepose_clear_resolution(self.two_line_enabled())`, a **session** predicate that
reads False on the first batch. P96 could not see it: every treatment cell set
`=1` explicitly, which bypasses the predicate. The fix passes `run_bimanual`'s
resolved `two_line` into the solve (`_prepare_two_line_stations(two_line)`, one
call site, pinned by the `253` leg). That run is kept as
`logs/p97/accept_inert_pre_fix.log`, the evidence that the default had been
silently off.

**The flip is resolution-only, three ways.** (1) `=0` acceptance: **8/10,
9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches 30fb99f8`**, **419/419** physics lines
identical to `logs/p94/accept_final.log`. (2) Single arm: **6/9, 14.8

## P99 (2026-11-02): the candidate planning is not the lever - the wait is not the interval

The owner asked whether the **fruit planning between the feeder and the arms**
can raise efficiency, because the inter-placement interval "looks long". The
record's priors said no (`logs/w8/R3_RESULTS.md`: the adaptive selection lead is
bit-identical because the shipped 1.5 s floor *is* the measured setup;
`logs/p58`/`logs/p59`: 0/42 starved feed rounds; `logs/p80`: 44 starved polls,
0 lost slots), so the phase was a **census first**, with a pre-registered
decision rule (`logs/p99/PREREG.md`, md5 `0acc5692`, pinned before any cell was
read) so the answer could not be written after the fact.

**The instrument is one reporting block.** The shipped records print the slot
chain but not the attempt's end, and `[bed-sel]` (`FRUIT_BED_DIAG=1`) prints
only counts. `FRUIT_BED_DIAG=2` now prints, from the same `diag` list
`select_target` already fills, the **selector floor** of that decision and **one
row per live fruit** (`idx/grade/along/x/z/r` + the first refusing predicate);
`=1` and unset are byte-unchanged and no control path gains a read. The attempt
end and the park split come from the existing `FRUIT_BIARM_PARK_TRACE=1`
(P84 proved it neutral).

**Two proofs before a number was quoted.** Both census cells replay their
same-seed P94 record with the instrument's rows dropped: **C5 = `logs/p94/T5.log`
974/974** and **C6 = `logs/p94/T6.log` 970/970** `[fruit]` lines - so P98's
revert resolves off on this cell *and* ~500 `[bed-sel]` rows plus 120 park rows
move nothing (a 1-attempt smoke pair had read 78/78 first). The derivation
reproduces every published interval to the digit: **9.37 / 11.08 / 10.59**
(P94 §5) and **10.77** (`logs/p84/D5.log`, P80), with the park split a fixed
**2.5 s** of motion + **0.25 s** feed and every gap closing to ±0.05 s.

**The wait split (per attempt slot).** Seed 5 (17/20, interval **9.38**):
park-gate **0.03**, park-motion **2.47**, feed **0.27**, starved polls
**0.17**, dead 2.94, span 15.08. Seed 6 (12/20, **11.08**): 0.82 / 2.69 / 0.25 /
**0.86**, dead 4.62, span 13.72. So the slot-loop wait is the **park return and
the feed gap, not fruit**: starvation is 0.9 % and 3.9 % of the interval. Two
populations that must never be pooled: the **batch prime** (6 polls before each
arm's first attempt, 3.0 s once per batch = 0.17 s/placement) and the in-chain
polls (6 and 31).

**The candidate read, which is what the question was.** The belt is *stocked*
(7 live fruits at the decision instant) and the arm still has nothing its own
grade can catch in **12/32** and **37/57** decisions; ~2.5 of those fruits are
already *inside the catch floor*, i.e. they will be past the pick point when the
1.5 s setup ends. `window <= 1` on **37 of 40** selections - when the arm has a
candidate there is exactly one, so **there is no choice to optimise**. Own lane
empty while a cross-lane fruit was at/above the floor: **10/32** and **35/57**
(61 % at seed 6). **Delay-aware headroom: 0.000 s on 40/40** - the shipped
two-line rule already takes the nearest own-grade fruit above the floor
(`tasks.py:8111-8115`), verified rather than assumed.

**The convertible seconds, and the decision they force.** Pooled over 29
placements and a 10.2 s mean interval: **(i) cross-lane in-attempt arrival
1.258 s/placement (12.3 %)**, **(i') cross-lane in-chain polls 0.603 (5.9 %)**,
**(ii) delay-aware 0.000**, **(iii) joint/park-gate 0.531 (5.2 %)**. The
candidate-planning total **(i)+(i') = 1.862 s/placement = 18.2 %** - and the
whole of it is **cross-lane**, which PREREG §3 had already registered as the
special case: left arm = lane 0 = grade A, right arm = lane 1 = grade B, the
place is `run(state, bin_index)` with the arm's own lane, so a cross-lane pick
is a **sort error**, not a semantics switch (`tasks.py:11688`: "the arm cannot
change lanes mid-attempt ... the sort error is recorded").

**It was still priced, with the shipped knob.** `FRUIT_GRADE_ROUTING=0` (the V2
any-grade fallback) at both seeds, same instrumentation: **starvation 37 -> 0**
polls, **arrival wait 1.62 -> 0.67 s**, `window <= 1` 19/20 -> 5/20, **park gate
0.03 -> 0.62 s/attempt** (both arms never idle, so their station dwells collide
- the constraint the shipped starvation was *absorbing*), **interval 9.38 ->
10.01 (+6.8 %) and 11.08 -> 11.66 (+5.3 %)**, **window rate worse at both**
(6.40 -> 5.99, 5.42 -> 5.15), **batch span better at both** (181.1 -> 174.3,
182.6 -> 166.9), count a draw (29 -> 30 of 40), **17/40 fruit mis-sorted**, and
seed 6 loses 2 payloads upstream (`release_bottom = -184 mm`, the stranding
class). **The transferable sentence: the wait is not the interval.** ~1.1 s per
attempt of pure fruit wait removed (0.95 s of arrival + 0.17 s of polls) took
**0.57 s off the per-attempt cycle (18.02 -> 17.45 s) and 0.64 s onto the
interval**, because the interval is the *sequencing* of two
overlapped arms: seed 5's placements bunch in pairs (4.5 / 1.8 / 0.4 s between
the arms, then 16-18 s), the fallback's are evenly spread (p50 13.00 -> 11.70,
mean 9.38 -> 10.01). One arm's wait is often the slack the other arm's sweep
needs.

**Verdict: no lever, no default change, `configs/` untouched**
(`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` all stand). The 18.2 % is the **price of
grade-pure routing**, spendable only by changing the workstation (a diverter or
a second bin per arm), not by planning - and if it is ever wanted, its price is
measured here: +5-7 % of interval and 42 % mis-sorts on a count that is a draw.
The named open item is the **park return** (2.5 s/attempt, ~13 % of the
interval): a return-path/clearance object, whose pose/scheduling levers (P43,
W2/W3, P69/P90) all closed, and whose untried form is a ready pose on the
station side of the body.

Guards: landing **17/17** and **12/12** in the census cells (belt index = arm),
G5 **17/17**, G6 **13/13** payload-present (15 release rows, the other 2 `release_bottom = -184 mm`, reported separately);
grade ledger 0/40 cross-lane in the census cells and 17/40 in the pricing arms;
motion budgets are P94's own (the census cells are byte-identical to those
records) and the pricing cells are a moved branch where
`105 --min-success-rate 0.0` reads **PASS** on both; `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**PASS, 0 failures, 1 skipped**; and the **acceptance is inert**: `scripts/accept.sh`
reads **8/10, 9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference.json`,
`190: PASS`** with its **420/420** `[fruit]` lines byte-identical to
`logs/p98/accept_revert.log` (`logs/p99/accept_noharm{,_sim}.log`), so the
diag-only change moves nothing on the scripted path and both references stand.
Pins: `tasks.py` **`7c1386e9`** (P98's `6ce29b56` + the `=2` block, +17/-1),
`rl_env.py` `TASKS_MD5` metadata-only follow, `logs/p99/{census.py,
p99_report.py,run_p99.sh,run_p99_grade.sh,PREREG.md}`; tree `13726ca`; ckpt
`moe_v13s` `61da390a`. Evidence `logs/p99/{CENSUS.md,RESULTS.md,PREREG.md,
PREREG.md5,census.py,census.txt,p99_report.py,p99_report.txt,run_p99.sh,
run_p99_grade.sh,slots_C5.csv,slots_C6.csv,header.txt}`, cells
`{C5,C6,G5,G6}.{log,stamps,driver}`.

## P101 (2026-11-03): the platform survey — the arm stays, the end effector moves

**A plan, not a measurement.** No simulator run, no `src/` change, no `configs/`
change, no reference re-recorded. The artifact is `docs/PLATFORM_SURVEY.md` plus
this entry. Every external row is marked **verified [V]** (primary source fetched
2026-11-03), **reported [R]**, or **unverified [U]**; prices are quoted only
where a vendor page printed one.

**The decision.** (1) **Do not change the dual-arm platform.** OpenArm is
2 x 7-DoF, 4.1 kg nominal / 6.0 kg peak payload per arm, CAN-FD, **Apache-2.0
software + CERN-OHL-S-2.0 hardware**, **$6,500 for a complete bimanual system**,
ships an **Isaac Sim 6 USD with an Isaac Lab `OPENARM_BI_CFG`**, and is a
**first-class LeRobot robot including the bimanual config**
(`bi_openarm_follower`). Its `OPENARM_BI_CFG` effort limits are 40/27/7 N.m at
2.175/2.61 rad/s - the same 2.1x headroom P44 measured. The one arm-side defect
on record, **no top-down place station in +-0.15 m** (P90, 0/588 cells), is a
reach-envelope property the cell already worked around (P66/P71), not a reason to
re-buy the arm. (2) **The platform change is the end effector**: tactile on the
existing jaw first, a hand second.

**Why the hand is not the speed lever.** P52's numbers stand: the policy owns
**14.2 %** of a placed episode and a 1.5x on the whole phase is worth at most
**4.8 %**. A hand therefore has exactly one business case - the **`cnp` class**
(P92: 75 % of failures; P93 four-seed pool: 17 of 25) - and the survey's kill
criteria are written on that class, not on cycle time.

**What the survey found that the repo did not already know.** (a) The direct
env builds **one** camera, not two - `policy/data.py` stacks RGB + depth + mask
into 5 channels per frame at `obs_horizon = 2`, i.e. **10 input channels** from a
single 240x424 head view; the second camera exists only on OpenArm **2.0**'s
gripper hardware (an Arducam B0495 in the palm), and the sim's asset is the 1.0
bimanual USD. Any hand stage must *add* the wrist view. (b) **OpenArm 2.0's
fingers are explicitly replaceable and its gripper has an in-hand camera**, so a
tactile pad is a reprinted finger, not a new gripper. (c) **There is no Isaac Sim
USD for LEAP or ORCA** - Isaac Lab's asset list has `allegro`/`shadow_hand`/
`kuka_allegro`/`openarm`/`so101`, not them - so a hand stage either
converts an MJCF or uses Allegro as a 16-DoF stand-in. (d) **Half the open-hand
ecosystem is non-commercial**: LEAP's CAD and Aero's design files are
CC BY-NC-SA, DIGIT's design files are CC BY-NC, while 9DTact is explicitly
commercial-OK and ORCA's hardware licence is `NOASSERTION` (resolve first).

**The tactical recommendation.** Stage (i) two **GelSight Mini** ($510 each,
USB-UVC) or two 9DTact on reprinted fingers, with the *sim* half done first for
free by upgrading the tactile channel from 2 scalars to a **contact-patch field**
(contact points + normals off the existing `ContactSensor`); kill if the patch
channel does not beat the 2 scalars in sim, or if slip onset is not visible
**>= 10 ticks (83 ms)** before `clean_slip > 2 mm` on >= 70 % of escapes - the
W5-C measurement (payload out within 0-3 ticks of force collapse) says a 30 Hz
vision sensor is a labeller, not a reflex. Stage (ii) a hand, gated on a **free
sim pull-test** (a lateral+axial force ramp on 2-pad vs 3-finger vs 4-finger+thumb,
critical wrench >= **1.5x** in the axial direction P61 measured) - ORCA (17 DoF,
tactile integrated, <2,000 CHF, MJCF MIT) or Aero ($314, 7 DoF/16 joints) for the
pilot, with the recollection at **>= 150 episodes**. Stage (iii) tactile on the
hand, gated on **+5 points** over the same hand without it.

**Architecture (a), not (c).** Keep the 9-D arm chunk and the sampler/RTC path;
add an **8-D hand latent** decoded to the hand's joints, conditioned on the same
FiLM vector plus a phase token from the existing 5-expert router, with the hand
**inert outside `grip`/`close`/`release`** and its targets clamped *by
construction* (P53: a post-hoc clamp was free but null on 7 DoF; on 16 DoF it is
a hardware risk). P52's "the chunks are noise" (within-chunk min p50 2.44 rad/s,
0/60 below 0.30) and P53's 10.9 % out-of-range emission are the reasons a
17-dim diffusion target is the wrong first move, and they are the reasons a
supervised decoder is the right one.

**The baseline to beat** (P93's four control seeds): **58/80 = 72.5 % placed**,
interval **10.59 / 11.08 / 12.16 / 11.53 s**, 9.50/9.10 s per attempt, wall
**2.37-2.91 placed/min**, and the shipped acceptance **8/10 at 9.0 s** (P98).
The brief's "9.4-11.1 s" is the two-seed subset; the four-seed interval range is
**10.6-12.2 s**, and the class share is **75 %** on the P92 census against
**68 %** on the P93 pool - quote the range.

**Data cost of the hand**: schema 25-D -> **40-D** (22 arm joints + 16 hand + 2
tactile) with a second camera, every store invalid (`demos_v12` 158 episodes,
`p33_pear` 180 / 32,670 windows), a **>= 150-episode** recollection whose
measured wall anchor is **2 h 6 min for 158 episodes** (W3, one shard, no wedge),
and **all three motion references re-recorded** (P71's collider-set precedent).

Pins: **this phase touched no `src/` or `configs/` file**; the working tree
carries another phase's in-flight P100 park-profile edits (`tasks.py`, `scene.py`
and the metadata-only `rl_env.py` `TASKS_MD5` follow), which are **not** this
entry's and were **not** measured here - so this entry asserts no `src/` pin.
The three motion references are untouched and read `30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` /
`8952c320`, ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`. `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS (0
failures, 1 skipped)**; `scripts/106_index_audit.py` **OK**; `scripts/107_collect_merge_test.py` **PASS (21 checks)**. Evidence
`docs/PLATFORM_SURVEY.md` (sources §6, with the unverified rows named).

## P100 - the park return is 36 % slack and it does not transfer (the throughput lane closes)

The owner's item was P99's: the **park return**, 2.47 s (seed 5) / 2.69 s
(seed 6) of motion per attempt slot, ~13 % of the inter-placement interval once
it is halved over two arms. The question was whether the only remaining
free-space motion could be priced and adopted. Answer: **priced, and no.**

**The path first.** `_biarm_park` (`tasks.py:10157`, called from the worker's
`finally` at `:9763`) gates on the other arm and then `go_ready` -> `_ready_move`
-> `_transit_to("ready")` -> `_ready_transit`, which is `_catch_up_drive`
(20 ticks) + `_lift_clear` (step cap 0.04 rad/tick) + `_blend_to`'s min-jerk
ramp (90) + its settle hold (120), with `_recover_ready` above `TRANSIT_TOL`
0.08. The A/B smoke read `catch_up=40 lift=44-55 blend=90 settle=120` =
**274-299 ticks**, i.e. the block P99 measures as 2.5 s. Only the last two
stages are fixed; the arm carries nothing on this path. Every knob that already
existed is either **single-arm scoped** (P9-A's `FRUIT_READY_SKIP`/`_SETTLE`,
because `scope = self._active_session is None and not self.two_line_enabled()`)
or **measured out** on this block (`FRUIT_BIARM_HOT_ARM` negative,
`FRUIT_BIARM_PREFETCH` 0/40 reservations), and `FRUIT_BIARM_PARK_EARLY` moves
the *gate* (0.03/0.82 s per P99), not the motion.

**The lever** is one new two-line-scoped resolver,
`tasks.park_profile_resolution(two_line)`, reading `FRUIT_BIARM_PARK_BLEND` and
`FRUIT_BIARM_PARK_SETTLE`, shipped 90/120 with `PARK_TWO_LINE_DEFAULT = False`.
The scope is **enforced in the resolver**, not argued: without a two-line
session the env is not read, which is what keeps the driver's own pre-session
prime transit (it prints the same `[ready]` row before `run_bimanual` installs
the session) on the shipped clock. The first smoke with an unguarded read moved
that prime transit's ramp to 45 ticks, so the guard is a measured correction,
and the `254` leg pins it.

**The cell: 60/75 = 135 of 210 ticks, -0.625 s.** Chosen from a smoke ladder
rather than the model: `45/45` ends one park 0.122 rad from ready and fires
`_recover_ready` (`rec=1`), `45/90` buys the same ticks with a 33 % larger
commanded joint step, `60/75` spends the same total on motion with more posture
margin (`q_step` 0.0963 against the posture gate's 0.15).

**Measured (8 cells, 20 attempts each, seeds 5/6/101/202, interleaved
control -> treatment per seed, one claim per run).** The mechanism is
**exact**: the fixed clock is -75 ticks on every park of every treatment cell,
the measured block falls **2.53 -> 1.91 s pooled (-24.6 %)** with
-0.61/-0.60/-0.62/-0.66 s per seed, `q_step` peaks at 0.0978 rad/tick (65 % of
the posture gate's 0.15; 11.7 rad/s, i.e. 2.2x the arm's 5.45 rad/s limit - the
far-seed parks saturate, as the shipped 0.0652 = 1.4x ramp already does), and `post_err` moves 0.0131 median -> 0.0170-0.0282. The
cost is the readiness margin: the shipped park arrives ~5x inside
`TRANSIT_TOL`, the trim ~1x (worst 0.0795 rad), with **0** recoveries in 80
treatment parks beyond the one 6.2 s jammed transit **seed 6's control also
has** (post_err 1.2047, `rec=1`).

**The delivered side is the answer.** Interval -2.8 %, +9.8 %, +0.2 %, -5.4 %
at seeds 5/6/101/202 - **pooled 11.04 -> 11.09 s (+0.5 %)** - while placed moves
59 -> 63 of 80. The saving is **re-absorbed inside the slot loop**: dead time
(park+gate+feed+polls) 2.91 -> 2.89, 4.43 -> 4.82, 3.66 -> 2.90, 4.03 -> 3.71 s.
At seed 5 the park gate grows +0.38 s; at seed 6 the starved-poll term goes
0.78 -> 2.05 s/slot and the poll count 31 -> 82, because an arm that returns
earlier simply waits for fruit. At seed 101 the dead time **does** convert
(-21 %) and the interval still does not move (12.16 -> 12.18), because the
interval is the *placement* sequencing of two overlapped arms and not the slot
loop. That is P99's sentence one level down: **a motion is not the interval
either.** Seed 6's rise is not a tail artefact (the treatment's first 11
intervals also average 12.98 s against the control's 11.08).

Verdict per the registration: **P1 passes at all four seeds, P2 fails** (it was
registered as "the interval falls at every seed"), and two other registered
clauses are recorded as **design errors rather than results**: P1b's "zero
`rec`" (the seed-6 *control* carries one), and P4's key-level reading (the
`grasped, not placed (no note)` bucket appears in two *controls* of the same
battery, so the key cannot separate a new class from a standing one). The
descent budgets fail on **both** arms - the largest excursion in the battery is
the control C101's 0.224/0.160 = +40 %, the same leg P93 already recorded - and
were not re-tuned.

**The clearance census** (trace-on pair at seed 5, invasive: no rate from those
cells) reads min **48.0 -> 57.7 mm** with **0 of 20 689 and 0 of 20 007 samples
< 30 mm**, 0 bands; the closest pair is the two right fingers at the other arm's

### P102: a patch tactile sees the loaded slide 0.17-0.94 s before the pinch is lost - and the 2-scalar force channel is the late one (2026-11-03)

The platform survey (`docs/PLATFORM_SURVEY.md` §5.1, stage (i)) asked one
question and set its own kill: *can a PATCH-based tactile see the loaded slide
early enough to act?*, "slip visible >= 10 ticks early, or `cnp` does not fall
>= 30 % -> kill". The premise on record was W5-C's "where force collapses the
payload is out within 0-3 ticks", read as the **slip's** clock. **It is not: it
is the normal force's last moment.** Measured on the shipped cell, the payload's
in-hand displacement crosses **2 mm 21-113 ticks (median 60 = 0.50 s, min 21 =
0.17 s) before the pinch is lost**, and **when the force finally collapses the
payload is already 4.5-46.4 mm out of position**.

**The instrument** (default off, reporting only): `FRUIT_TACTILE_PATCH=<ticks>`,
one `[tactile]` row **per pad per tick** on every carry leg - the payload
centre's projection on the pad's face (`u` across the finger, `v` down it), its
displacement since the leg's first **seated** tick (`dc`), the patch's occupancy
of the pad's face rectangle (`frac`), the signed distance to the nearest border
(`edge`), the per-pad force and the shipped `clean_slip`. Derived from geometry
the sim already has: the payload is a sphere, the pad is the measured plate
(`61.000 x 84.902 mm`, `logs/p66/COLLIDER_READ.md`) and the frame comes from the
**measured** jaw axis plus the **tool axis**. Two design points, both measured:
**the pad rectangle's origin must be the plate's face centre, not the link
origin** (`TACTILE_PAD_LONG_ORIGIN = finger_length - half_long`; without it the
shipped `_pad_standoff` seat reads `frac` 0.062 / `edge` -23.8 mm, i.e. every
good seat scores as off the pad - against 0.646 / +9.8 with it), and **the
long-axis sign must come from the tool axis** (the jaw axis' sign depends on
which finger link is on which side: measured `v = -66 mm` on one grasp and `+66`
on another before the fix). The patch model is the payload's **equatorial disc**,
which is deliberately **generous** - a real soft pad images a *smaller* patch,
and a smaller disc clips off the pad *later* - so a negative would have been
decisive; the positive therefore needs the hardware check (§below).

**Neutrality, three replays.** Same cell, same batch, the knob the only
difference: `T5` vs `C5` **975/975** and `T6` vs `C6` **971/971** `[fruit]` lines
identical with the phase's own `[tactile]` rows dropped; and `N5` (a re-run on the
final tree, after the close-out relocated the block) **17071/17071 `[fruit]`
lines identical with the rows KEPT** - 16 096 of them the instrument's own. So the
instrument is inert *and* deterministic. `logs/p91/C5.log` is **not** a valid
control on this tree: it predates P94's `_gripper_offset` guard and diverges at
its own guarded row (`jaw_target` `[0.4053,0.0...]` vs `[0.3997,0.4...]`), the
P96 `PREREG_A2` divergence; P100's cells add park/ready rows. The same-batch pair
is the only proof, which is why the phase spent two extra cells on it.

**The population** (40 attempts, seeds 5/6): **29 placed / 7 `cnp` / 4 no-grasp**,
70 carry legs -> **60 held, 6 seated escapes, 4 never-held**. The attempt join is
exact - the k-th `grasp_lift` a side takes is that side's k-th attempt, so every
leg maps to its `[run]` outcome - and it decides the business case: **all 6 seated
escapes sit on `cnp` attempts and 0 of the 29 placed attempts carry one**, while
all 4 no-grasp attempts carry a never-held leg. **A tactile can reach 6 of the 11
failures (55 %) and none of the successes; the acquisition class is unreachable
by any pad.**

**The lead, and why the threshold does not matter.** `dc` at 1 / 2.12 / 4.25 /
8.49 / 10 mm gives a median lead of 61 / 60 / 53 / 46 / 44 ticks and **all six
escapes clear 10 ticks at every one** - the motion is a ramp, not a step, so the
detector's threshold is not the design variable. `frac < 0.75 frac0` leads by 34
(5/6) and `edge < 0` by 29 (5/6). **False positives:** 2 of 60 held legs trip at
2.12 mm (5.8 and 10.4 mm) and **both of those attempts placed**; the `frac`
thresholds trip 0/60; a held leg's patch is motionless (`dc_max` median 0.02 mm).
The mechanism is visible tick by tick in the `left place0` escape: the payload
walks **45.6 mm across the finger** over 113 ticks while one pad still carries
8-10 N (the other face 0.00 N throughout - P75's one-sided pry), and the force
reaches 0.00 N one tick before `clean_slip` passes 50 mm.

**The survey's P1 clause is not evaluable as written** - it asks for a lead over
`clean_slip > 2 mm`, but the patch centroid's displacement **is** the payload's
relative displacement (`dc/clean` median 0.77-1.00 on the six escapes), so it
crosses that line on the same tick (0-1). A clause comparing a signal with
itself; **recorded, not re-read** (P100's precedent). The decision-relevant
reference is "before the pinch is lost", and that is the 21-113 ticks.

**What this does and does not settle.** It settles the **cell**: the relative
motion has 0.17-0.94 s of notice, 7-189 mm/s, with the patch *on the pad* at the
start of the walk (`frac` 0.52-0.79, `edge` +4.0..+17.2 mm) - so a 30 Hz pad gets
5-28 frames (median 15), and the survey's "30 Hz can label the slip, it
cannot catch it"
(which was the *force* channel's 25 ms budget) is corrected. It does **not**
settle the **sensor**: the sim's patch is derived from the payload's ground-truth
pose, the pads are rigid and adhesion-free (`logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md` §3) and there
is no visuotactile renderer in the loop, so "a soft pad images this" is the
survey's T2 bench, not a sim result. **Stage (i)'s kill does not fire**; the next
spend is the **reaction**, registered and not built: a re-grip at `dc >= 2 mm`
(the tree's own `clean_slip`) fires on 8 of 70 legs (6 escapes + 2 benign) at
P40's **1.24 s** two-line failed probe = **0.25 s/attempt worst case = 2.6 %** of
a 9.7 s attempt against P3's +5 %, and the cell is the **sim-only
perfect-detector re-grip** scored on the survey's **P2** (`cnp` 6 -> <= 4 of 40,
placed +8 points) and P3.

One more measured correction, which narrows the class and the instrument: a
`slip_max > 100 mm` rule alone picks up the **failed catch**, not a slide - one
"escape" carries a **318 mm** pad-to-payload offset under a **21.8 mm** span on a
68.9 mm fruit (the hand closed on air, and its 22.2 N is a flank contact). So
`is_escape` needs the **seat** (a loaded pinch **and** the patch on the pad), and
that is P76 A3's rule applied to `clean_slip` rather than to the force.

### P103: the perfect-detector re-grip converts nothing and destroys two placements - and the tree's own 8 mm slip gate is the ceiling (2026-11-03)

**One default-off knob, nothing adopted, no control law of its own.**
`FRUIT_SLIP_REGRIP=<mm>` (unset/`0` = the shipped path bit for bit; `0 < mm < 1`
raises, because a held leg's patch moves 0.02 mm median over 60 legs) takes its
**trigger** from P102's channel - the patch centroid's displacement `dc` since
the leg's first tick, gated on **P102's own seat** (`max(f0,f1) > 1 N` **and**
`edge > -TACTILE_PAD_HALF_LONG`, so the arm carrying an empty hand cannot trip
it) plus the shipped abort ceiling `slip <= FRUIT_SLIP_REACT_MAX` - and its
**action** from the tree's shipped slip re-seat: `_carry_leg` already carries one
behind `FRUIT_SLIP_RECOVERY` (`target = fruit - rot @ slip_ref`, the pad centre
that restores the leg-start relation, applied in one go and **re-based into the
remaining command list** so it costs no tick). That block is gated
`not hand_is_jaw` because it was written for the kinematic pad hand; on the
OpenArm hand the pads *are* the robot's fingers, so restoring the relation means
re-basing the arm's own command list - which is what the block does. The knob
only swaps the trigger. Scope: a two-line session (`two_line_enabled()`), so the
single arm, the shared station, the direct/policy handover and the hybrid canary
resolve to off.

**The cells.** Four seeds x 20 attempts (`C5/T5`, `C6/T6`, `C101/T101`,
`C202/T202`, interleaved, alternating C/T order; two fresh seeds per P93's rule),
the shipped two-line scenario, `FRUIT_CARRY_DIAG=1` **and** `FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE=1`
on **both** arms so the A/B is the knob alone. `PREREG.md` **`73bdf35e`** was
pinned before any 20-attempt cell; the only earlier run is a 6-attempt **build
smoke** (`logs/p103/smoke.log`), recorded in PREREG §0 because it changed the
action's temporal form: the first build re-seated at most once per 40 ticks and
the payload walked **3.07 -> 30.41 mm inside that window**, so the registered
form is the shipped block's **per-tick** shape.

**Inertness, proved three ways.** `FRUIT_SLIP_REGRIP` unset: the acceptance is
**8/10, `fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`** with its **419/419** `[fruit]`
lines identical to `logs/p98/accept_revert.log` (sealed: P100's park row
dropped); the batch's own controls replay P102's current-tree controls **825/825**
(seed 5) and **837/837** (seed 6); and the read the knob adds is one
`jaw_positions()` + one tactile set per armed tick, **no `ik_step` work and no
articulation read** (P95 proved a 3-prims-per-arm set inert on this line,
970/970 / 974/974). So the A/B is the action, not the instrumentation and not the
batch.

**The ledger.** 137 carry legs, **12 re-seated** (801 re-seat ticks), first fire
at `dc` **2.14-5.74 mm** (median 2.38) on 11 of 12 legs, **5-163 ticks into the
leg**. **1 of 12 re-seated legs placed.** Joined per leg to its attempt (P102's
join: a side's k-th `grasp_lift` leg *is* that side's k-th attempt - checked) and
then to the same index on the same seed's control, **7 of the 12 are
same-instance pairs**: **0 of 5 control `cnp`s converted** and **2 of 2 control
placements destroyed**. The other 5 diverged (the branches re-draw as soon as the
action moves a command - P92/P93's rule).

**The harm, one witness.** Seed 5 attempt 17, the same fruit in the same slot on
the same line, one arm difference: control `clean_slip_max` **5.8 mm**,
`force_min` 6.17 N, `sep_max` 41.9 mm -> **PLACED**; treatment **153.1 mm**,
`force_min` **0.00 N**, `sep_max` **98.4 mm** (the pads at their open stop) under
`fmax` **117.87 N** on a 29.6 mm fruit -> fail. P102 priced `dc >= 2.12 mm` at
"2 of 60 held legs, both placed" - measured *without acting*. **The trigger's
false-positive cost is its physics, not its clock (which is zero).**

**Why it cannot convert, and it is the phase's most useful sentence: the
reaction's ceiling on this tree is 8 mm, not 100 mm.** The two-line session's own
**P10-C carry monitor** is armed with `FRUIT_CARRY_MONITOR_CONFIRM_MM = 8.0`, so
an attempt whose lift leg reads `clean_slip_max >= 8.0 mm` is truncated at the
leg boundary and never takes its place leg. The re-seat *did* hold the payload on
**7 of 12** legs (5.7-22.7 mm against the controls' 100-2372 mm) - **but only 1
stayed under 8 mm, and that one placed** (seed 6 attempt 9, 5.7 mm). Six "held"
legs at 8.3-22.7 mm were truncated anyway. The class boundary is a **harness
constant**, not physics.

**The endpoints.** P2 fails both ways: **P2a** (survey literal, seeds 5+6, 40)
reads `cnp` **7 -> 3** (inside the "<= 4" bar) **but placed 29/40 -> 29/40 = +0.0
points** - the `cnp` class fell only because **4 of them became never-grasped**
(the payload lost *before* the lift's peak), the P92 shape ("the chase is the
signature, not the cause") with a harm added; **P2b** (pooled, 80) reads `cnp`
**11 -> 9 (-18 %)** and placed **59/80 -> 54/80 (-6.2 points)**, Fisher
**p = 0.49** (never-grasped 10 -> 17, p = 0.20 - **not significant at n = 80**,
and mostly branch: the action touched 12 legs). **P3 fails at every seed**: the
interval **9.37/11.08/12.16/11.53 -> 9.85/12.92/12.92/15.19 s** (+5.1 / +16.6 /
+6.2 / +31.8 %, **+15.3 %** on the mean), window **5.49 -> 4.83**, batch **4.86 ->
4.33**, `placed/min` wall **3.77 -> 3.71**, `s/attempt` **9.10 -> 9.40 (+3.3 %)**.
The action costs no tick by construction, so the interval movement is the
**branch** - a failed attempt re-draws the slot loop - which is P83/P88/P89/P91's
"a block delta is not deliverable on this cell" one level down.

**Guards.** G1 **PASS** (419/419 + `matches` + `190: PASS`); G2 **PASS**
(825/825, 837/837); G3 **PASS** - **113/113** payload-present releases
`on_belt`, **0** off, 2 upstream-lost rows reported apart; G4 **4 named legs of
160, arm-symmetric - 2 controls and 2 treatments** (`C6` leg 12 0.164/0.160, the
standing branch leg P86/P87 recorded; `C101` leg 9 0.224/0.160; `T101` leg 9
0.261/0.160; `T202` leg 11 0.226/0.161) and **the budget was not re-tuned**
(AGENTS §2; P93's finding - a stochastic branch property at ~2.5 % of legs in
either arm); G5 **fails by its letter at seeds 5 and 202** (the bucket `grasped,
not placed (no note)` appears in the treatment only - the key P100's A4 already
found in two *controls* of the same battery, **recorded, not re-read**); G6
**PASS** (20/20 on all eight cells, no slot lost). `logs/p103/gates.sh` exits
**1** and its only failing clause is G4's four named legs - the script's own
"any over-budget leg fails" rule is stricter than the registered "name it".

**Verdict: the survey's stage (i) closes - DETECTED BUT NOT CONVERTIBLE.** P102's
mechanism stands untouched; what dies is the premise that *acting* at 2 mm buys
the placement. **The sensor is not justified by this**: a perfect detector was
given for free and the reaction still lost placements, so a real pad can only do
worse on the trigger. **Nothing ships** (`FRUIT_SLIP_REGRIP` stays opt-in), the
knob is one bool when unset, and the owner's decision is whether a pad is worth
buying for the **supervision/labelling** case P102 established (the slide is
visible for 0.17-0.94 s), not for a reflex. Named, not registered: (1) the
**8 mm monitor gate** is the binding term a future reaction would have to beat;
(2) any such reaction must first **separate the false-positive class** (a slide
the pinch survives) from the real one, which P102's channel cannot do at 2 mm.

### P104: stage (ii)'s free half - 4 contacts beat the pinch by 1.9-2.0x and 3 by 1.5x, the pads do not pry, and the static capacity is 10-20x the load the cell applies (2026-11-03)

**A fixture, not a policy run; nothing shipped, no `src/` or `configs/` change,
no commit, both references untouched.** The owner's plan moved to stage (ii) of
`docs/PLATFORM_SURVEY.md` after P103 closed stage (i) (detected, not convertible,
and a net harm on the false-positive class), and §3.3's **T1** is the gate: a
hand must beat the pinch by **>= 1.5x** axially or the hypothesis is dead for
<$0. This phase answers it offline (`analytic.py`) and then with a fixture on the
sim's own fruit meshes (`fixture_probe.py`, `run_p104.sh` -> `fixture.txt`, 63
cells, 2 m 51 s, no wedge).

**The analytic frame answers by arithmetic, and says so.** `n` independent point
contacts, Coulomb, no peel, and the seat's normals perpendicular to the tool axis
(a pad clamps where the payload's surface is tangent to its face, i.e. at the
widest ring - `logs/p42/SEAT_CENSUS.md` §0 measures the pads' midpoint 1.4-4.7 mm
off the payload's centre), so the axial pull is tangential everywhere and
`F_crit = n * mu * N_c`: 2 contacts = 1.00, **3 = 1.50**, **4 = 2.00**, and the
ratio is **mu-free**. A distal lip is a *different mode* (the pull is carried by
a contact normal anti-parallel to it), so its ideal ratio is unbounded. At
`mu_eff` 0.45 / `N_c` 4.90 N the pinch is 4.41 N; at the measured pair
friction (1.13-1.45) it is 11.07-14.21 N. The bar is met by the 3-contact form
**exactly at its letter** and by the 4-contact with 0.5x to spare - in this
model, for any mu. **The scale is the caveat**: the shipped `a_max` 1.089 puts
the cell's axial demand at `m(g+a)` = 0.17 / 0.91 / 1.20 N for the strawberry /
pear / orange, i.e. **3.7-26x below the conservative pinch capacity** - and the
cell still loses the payload, so the static capacity is not the binding term.

**The fixture.** One payload, `n` pads on **force-capped position drives**
(k = 1e5 N/m = `finger_damp02`, cap **4.90 N** = the measured per-face pinch,
P41's 9.75-9.9 N over two faces), the measured plate **61.000 x 84.902 mm** with
its distal plane 80.5 mm below the jaw centre (`logs/p66/COLLIDER_READ.md`,
`tasks.FINGER_TIP_BELOW_JAW`) so the shipped **10.5 mm lip** is reproduced, the
pool's own mesh/mass/friction draw, a 150-tick close on a pinned payload,
90-tick settle, then a **5 N/s** axial ramp (with gravity) to a 40 N cap. Seven
forms: `pinch_plate` (the shipped pinch), `pinch_tip` (16 mm matched control),
`tripod` (3 at 120 deg), `quad` (4 at 90 deg), `lip` (+ a static distal ledge),
and the two **moment** cells (pull 20 mm off-axis). Three fruits x three repeats;
the per-cell manipulation check is that **every contact carries the same normal
force** - 4.75-4.94 N on the tripod, 4.80-4.90 on the quad.

**The measurement (sustained break-away, applied + weight, mean of 3).**
`pinch_plate` **11.03 / 14.21 / 12.69 N** (pear / orange / strawberry),
`pinch_tip` 11.19 / 13.04 / 13.07, **`tripod` 18.11 / 18.90 / 19.74**,
**`quad` 21.81 / 26.59 / 25.97**, `lip` **no break inside 40 N** on all three.
Ratios to the shipped pinch: **tripod 1.64 / 1.33 / 1.56** (mean 1.51),
**quad 1.98 / 1.87 / 2.05** (mean 1.97), lip `>3.63 / >2.82 / >3.15`. **The
arithmetic holds within 10 %** in every cell, and the pads **do not pry** (radial
travel at break 0.06-1.52 mm of an 80 mm stroke), so the `n/2` survives contact
- which is the only thing a fixture can add to arithmetic. The pinch's break
carries the tree's **one-sided** signature: **4.92 / 2.93 N** at its 2 mm event
on the pear, against the 61 mm plate cell's 4.90-4.94 / 4.90-4.94.

**Two findings that change how the bar must be read.** (1) **The survey's own
criterion fails the 3-contact form.** Break at `clean_slip > 2 mm` reads
**1.05 / 0.94 / 1.48x** for the tripod (`fixture_table.txt`), because a 3-contact
grasp **re-seats** after 2 mm and carries on to 18-20 N while the pinch's 2 mm is
already its end (11.11 -> 11.19 N) - the 4-contact passes it (1.75-2.10x) and the
sustained number is the one that means "critical wrench". (2) **The load the cell
applies is not the load the bar tests.** With the payload hanging on the grasp
under its own weight (0.17-1.20 N, i.e. the lift's demand), the two-pad pinch
**slides 3.20-3.84 mm on the pear** - 1.6-1.9x the 2 mm escape threshold and
30-36 % of the 10.5 mm lip - while the tripod slides **0.36-0.44 mm** and the
4-pad **0.15-0.25 mm**: **9-15x at the operating load**, not 1.5x. The fidelity
error is in the conservative direction (the fixture's capped pads follow the
payload inward; a real close freezes the gap at the fruit's width), so the ratios
are a lower bound. **Under a 20 mm off-axis pull** the tripod's advantage falls
to **1.15 / 1.33 / 1.47x** - the slipping payload tips and unloads one contact
(3.57 / 5.06 / 3.64 N at break) - so the hand's win is **axial-specific**.

**Verdict.** Stage (ii)'s **kill does not fire**: the 4-contact form clears the
1.5x bar at every fruit size and both controls, under both criteria, and 4+
contacts is what every candidate hand has (ORCA 17 DoF, LEAP 16 DoF/4 fingers,
Allegro 16 DoF/4 fingers, DexHand 19 DoF). The 3-contact form sits **on** the bar
(1.51-1.53 mean, 2 of 3 fruits, fails the 2 mm criterion), so a three-finger hand
is not a purchase. **But a positive is necessary, not sufficient**, and the
phase's own numbers say why: the pass is on a quantity the pinch already exceeds
by 10-20x, so it does not predict a `cnp` conversion; the **lip** - the geometry
case the survey's hypothesis actually names - wins the fixture unboundedly while
the tree has already measured that same geometry as a **pipeline negative**
(`logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md` §3: the ledges bat the payload, no-contact 2 -> 9 of 15);
and the approach/acquisition (4 of P102's 11 failures) plus the policy are
untouched. The two cheapest next spends, both cheaper than the hand: a **creep
endpoint at the operating load** (the metric already exists as `clean_slip >
2 mm`) and §3.2's **T2 bench** (~$1,020), the only test that can *confirm*.

Recorded as by-products, not acted on: the implied pair friction is
**`mu_app` = 1.05-1.45** on every form, i.e. consistent with PhysX's default
**average** combine of the pad's 2.0 with the fruit's draw (1.26-1.41) and **not**
the *minimum* the `scene._add_physics_material` comment assumes - so `mu_eff`
0.45 is 2.3-3.2x pessimistic and the measured pinch is 11-14 N, not 4.4 N. No
comment or constant was edited (that is a cone re-measurement's work, not this
phase's). Also recorded: the third contact pays only when it is **loaded** - at a
3 mm commanded interference one tripod pad carried 3.09 N of 4.9 and the tripod
was worth **1.01x**, which is why the registered manipulation check (all contacts
at the same normal force) forced the 5 mm setting (`METHOD.md` A1).

### P105: the hand stage's design - the asset is a probe not a purchase, the observation is 34-D, and the action never widens (2026-11-03)

**A plan, not a measurement.** `docs/HAND_STAGE_PLAN.md` (md5 **`2c3ef8cb`**) is
the concrete plan for the dexterous-hand stage P104 licensed: the asset, the
observation/action schema, the policy architecture, the data plan, and five
milestones with kills. No simulator run, **no `src/` change, no `configs/`
change**, no default moved; the three references stand
(`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320`, verified by md5). `scripts/106_index_audit.py`
is **OK** ("every index matches the files it describes").

**The asset decision, and why it is a probe.** The first sim hand is the
**Allegro 16-DoF** because its USD is the only 4-finger hand that is both
**Isaac-native and direct-drive**: `…/Assets/Isaac/6.0/Isaac/Robots/
WonikRobotics/AllegroHand/allegro.usd` (verified HTTP 200, 1 626 251 B, listed in
the 6.0 bucket - the survey's "no LEAP, no ORCA USD" stands), and its 16 joints map
1:1 to 16 PhysX drives with **no tendon**. LEAP and ORCA are tendon-driven, so
their MJCF→USD conversion is a schedule risk that would be spent before the
question M2 asks. **But the fixture that passed P104's bar was a radial 4 x 90 deg
`quad` and no candidate hand is radial** (Allegro/LEAP are 3+1, ORCA/DexHand are
anthropomorphic 5-finger) - so the Allegro is a **mount and topology probe**, and
the form that licenses a purchase is a **4-pad surrogate** (the fixture's geometry,
in-scene). The phase **pre-registers its own prediction**: the Allegro's sustainable
axial capacity reads **1.2-1.6x** - at or below the 1.5x bar - because three
finger normals point the same way and behave as one friction cluster, `n_eff ≈ 2`
in P104's own arithmetic. If that holds, the hand's win is **form closure**, and
the tree has already measured a form-closure aid as a **pipeline negative**
(`FRUIT_FINGER_SCOOP`'s ledges bat the payload, no-contact 2 -> 9 of 15,
`logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md` §3) - which is why M2 also runs an **approach-and-close**
cell, not only a seated pull.

**The mount is a defect the plan had to find first.** `openarm_left_hand` is a
**PhysicsRevoluteJoint** (`axis=Z`, `stiffness=0`, `damping=0`, `maxForce=3.4e38`,
`assets/openarm_flat/openarm_flat_deinst.usda:3845-3857`) and `openarm_left_ee_tcp_joint`
is a second one (`:3869-3880`) - i.e. **the gripper hangs on two undriven revolute
joints about the tool axis**, which is also why four of the 25 proprio channels are
dead. Measured over 40 `datasets/demos_v12` episodes, `joint_positions` columns 16
and 19 (`openarm_{side}_hand`) move **6.8e-4 / 8.7e-4 rad** and columns 20/21
(`ee_tcp`) **2.2e-7 / 9.4e-7 rad**, against 0.43-3.12 rad on every arm channel. So
a 1.1 kg hand must be **welded** (22 -> 46 DOF with both hands) and the two joints
are not constants to keep.

**The schema: 25 -> 34-D, not 40.** v2 = **14 arm + 16 active-hand + 4 tactile**;
the two finger pairs go (the hand replaces them), the four dead channels go (2 hand
joints welded, 2 TCP joints welded), the finger-opening scalar goes (the hand's
joints *are* the opening) and one tactile channel per fingertip replaces the two.
**The inactive hand is not carried** - P36's 2x2 measured the inactive arm's
proprio to be null (park image **0/58 vs 35/57**, p = 8.8e-15; park-proprio
**17/60 vs 18/55**, p = 0.687, `logs/p36/A_RESULTS.md:82-85`), so 16 more channels
of the same kind is an untested bet at 16x the width. **The action vector never
widens**: it stays 9-D and `action[7]` becomes the hand's **synergy scalar**, so
the scripted primitive, the collector, the store and the hybrid evaluator all keep
working; the 16 joints come from an **8-D supervised latent** off a second head on
the same trunk. Vision becomes **two encoders summed** (head 5ch x 2, wrist
3ch x 2), not ten stacked channels, because the mast view's global context and the
wrist's 60 mm patch are different statistics.

**The architecture is (a) hand-conditioned head, and the reason is measured.** (c)
diffuses 16 more dimensions on top of chunks P52 measured to be **noise** (min p50
2.44 rad/s, 0/60 below 0.30, `|2nd|/|1st|` 1.16) and emissions P53 measured to be
**10.9 % out of range** with a clamp that is free but null - for a hand that is a
hardware event, so the decoder is `tanh`-in-range **by construction**. (b)
(two-stage at the close) is predicted to fail on P42/P75 (the seat is already
centred 1.4-4.6 mm, the walk is 104-276 mm, and 4 of 6 escapes fire *inside* the
place leg where (b) cannot reach), so it is the safety net. The inference budget is
read on **two denominators**: a decision is 71 ms (model 47.4 + render 20.0 +
camera 3.6, `logs/p43/P2_RESULTS.md:264`) but only **10.6 % of the episode wall**,
so the wrist view's +24 ms is +34 % of a decision and **+3.6 % of an episode** -
affordable, at a thinner RTC margin (h <= 7 -> h <= 11 of 16), not a new failure.

**The data plan found a second defect: the collector cannot produce the store.**
`dataset.py:147-152` discards every failed attempt (`if not success: ... return
None`), so a hand store through `scripts/40_collect_demos.py` contains **zero `cnp`
examples** - and `cnp` is **75-77 %** of this cell's failures (9 of 12 in P92's
two-seed population, 17 of 22 in P93's four-seed one). That is exactly the
successes-only limitation P33 phase 3 recorded. The plan therefore takes the
**direct-rollout path** (`110_rl_rollout --record`, which keeps failures) for M4's
first checkpoint and adds `--keep-failures` to the collector only before M5. Cost:
**150-200 episodes, 2.5-3 h, ~15 GB** against the measured 158 episodes / 2 h 6 min
anchor (`logs/w3/HANDOFF.md:10-11`), and the fine-tune is **30-40 min** (6 epochs x
201 s at 38 990 windows, `logs/w3/50_finetune_v13s_dense.log:9-14`).

**The baseline arithmetic is corrected, and it changes the gate.** P93's four
control seeds read **58/80 = 72.5 % with 22 failures = 17 `cnp` + 5 never-held**
(the counts close: 58 + 17 + 5 = 80). The survey's "25 failures, `cnp` 68 %" is
three failures too many and the 68 % follows from the wrong denominator; `cnp` is
**77 %**. On P102's attempt join, **6 of the 7 `cnp`** carried a seated escape
(86 %) and the 4 no-grasp attempts all carried never-held legs whose discriminator
is the catch-up residual (**8/8 no-grasp vs 3.6 %**, 220-481 mm - hand-over
timing, `logs/p47`, `logs/p48`). So the hand's ceiling is **93.8 %** (all 17
convert), the measured seated share puts it at **91.3 %**, and the survey's P4 bar
of 82.5 % is only **8 of those 17** - one binomial sd on 80 attempts is **5.0
points**, half the bar. **M5's primary is therefore the `cnp` rate (17/80 -> <=
8/80) with placed as non-inferiority**, not the placed count.

**The five milestones**, each with its kill: **M1** the asset in scene (close+lift,
4.90 N per contact, 4 tactile channels, **station still reachable**; kill = the
station or the TCP frame breaks; 24-40 h); **M2a** the in-scene pull test
(`>= 1.5x` sustained axial and **creep <= 1.0 mm**; kill = both forms below the bar,
which closes the hand path to the pad-face sanction; 16-24 h); **M2b** the
approach-and-close cell (no-contact <= 1/15; 8-16 h); **M3** the scripted hand
(acceptance not worse than 8/10, 0 clearance contacts, landing 100 %; kill = the
station is too tight; 80-120 h, the largest item); **M4** the policy (+8 points over
the scripted hand; kill = ship the scripted hand; 24-40 h); **M5** adoption
(`cnp <= 8/80`, placed `>= 58/80`, all three references re-recorded; 16-24 h).
Total **170-265 h labour, ~26 h simulator, ~17 GPU-hours**, and **no hardware
before M3** - M2 licenses the geometry, M3 licenses the purchase.

**What it does not price**, so nothing is implied: the flange bolt pattern and the
tendon/cable routing (**[U]**, bench), the MJCF/URDF conversion (**40-80 h** [E],
post-M5), a real jaw's clamp-force anchor, a visuotactile renderer (still the
survey's T2 bench), and the wrist camera's optics (a new sensor model).
