## P106 - the hand stage's M1/M2a: the Allegro mounts, the surrogate passes, the Allegro cannot be priced

**Verdict first.** The Allegro 16-DoF USD **mounts in this scene** (38 DOF, welded,
driven, tool offset measured) and **fails the close+lift gate as a rate - 1 of 4
cells**. M2a's kill ("both forms < 1.5x -> buy no hand") **does not fire**: the
4-pad radial surrogate reads **1.98 / 1.87 / 2.05x** sustained, **1.82 / 1.80 /
2.10x** at 2 mm and creep **0.25 / 0.15 / 0.11 mm** against the pinch's **3.20 /
0.85 / 2.68** on the same batch. The **Allegro is not evaluable** - one draw held
and three dropped the payload at the first release, and its cell cannot be brought
to the pinch's 4.90 N per contact - so the plan's predicted **1.2-1.6x** is
**neither confirmed nor refuted**.

**M1, the mount.** Asset `WonikRobotics/AllegroHand/allegro.usd` (1 626 251 B) on
the tree's own asset root, referenced under
`/World/OpenArm/openarm_left_ee_tcp` and welded with a `PhysicsFixedJoint`; the
merged articulation reads **38 DOF = 22 arm + 16 hand**, the hand half
`index/middle/ring/thumb _joint_0..3` in that order with its limits in radians
(`index_joint_0 [-0.558,+0.558]`, `index_joint_1 [-0.279,+1.728]`,
`thumb_joint_0 [+0.279,+1.571]`), 21 bodies weighing **2.135 kg**, and a `+0.300`
command reading `+0.2894` on the merged articulation. **The tool offset that
replaces `_pad_standoff`'s 70 mm is 170.7 mm along the tool axis** at the sweep's
mid posture (**100-216 mm** across it): it is posture-dependent and 1.4-3.1x the
pad hand's, so it is measured, never copied.

**Two defects the mount exposed.** (1) The asset ships `root_joint`, a
`PhysicsFixedJoint` from **world** to `allegro_mount`; `stage.RemovePrim` does
**not** defeat a prim that comes from a reference, so it survived, pinned the hand
to the world origin while the mount joint pulled it to the flange, and **destroyed
the articulation** - at play arm joint 1 read **-82.19 rad** (limit -3.49) and a
`+0.300` command moved it **-34.39**. `prim.SetActive(False)` is the fix; with it
the arm reads 0.000 at play. (2) **`ArmController.move_to` stalls** from the
hanging rest pose: **186 mm** and **326 mm** short on two attempts (direct and
through a 40-waypoint line), tool axis tilted up to 30 deg. The probe therefore
teleports to the shipped `ready` waypoint and does not claim a station.

**The close+lift gate: 1 of 4.** The pear held (**+59.7 mm**, the primitive's own
`>4 mm` test) and had already **crept 39.75 mm** under 0.82 N - **12x the pinch's
3.20 mm and 40x the plan's 1.0 mm bar**; the other three fell to the floor (creep
1.07-1.09 m). The mechanism is in the read, not in a force shortfall: the fingers
**knock the payload out of the seat as they close** (after release: `index -0.80 N`,
the other three 0.00).

**The drive tune is not achievable through a torque cap.** At the asset's
`k=1e7` the pear reads **no contact at cap 0.46 N.m** and **10.5 N per contact at
0.48** - a step function, which is `docs/HAND_STAGE_PLAN.md` §1.4's warning
measured: below the threshold the finger never reaches the payload. A soft drive
(`k=20`, `c=0.4`) does give 2-6 N per loaded finger but needs a force instrument,
and this asset has none that is trustworthy: a per-link contact view raises
`Physics contact view is not valid` or reports fingers 60-90 mm away, and
`get_dof_gains()` returns **5.73e8** against an authored 1e7.

**The phase's central measurement is topological.** The three fingers span
**116-123 mm** open and the thumb sits **43-208 mm** from their centroid, so
**at most 3 of the 4 fingertips can touch one 37-66 mm payload at any posture in
a 4 x 4 sweep** - 2 for the 60.6 mm pear at most postures, 2 for the 37.2 mm
strawberry, 3 for the 65.8 mm orange at two postures. A 60 mm fruit is smaller
than the hand's own tip spread (index-to-ring **102 mm**), which is the mechanism
the plan's §1.7 `n_eff ~ 2` arithmetic was reaching for. That is why the Allegro
cannot be priced as a 4-contact cell, and it is a *design input*, not a defect of
this run.

**M2a's table** (controls from P104's fixture **unchanged**, re-run in this batch
and identical to the digit): pinch **11.03 / 14.21 / 12.69 N** sustained,
**10.62 / 13.83 / 12.19** at 2 mm, creep **3.20 / 0.85 / 2.68**, pry 0.13-0.37;
4-pad radial **21.81 / 26.59 / 25.97 N (1.98 / 1.87 / 2.05x)**, **19.28 / 24.83 /
25.61 (1.82 / 1.80 / 2.10x)**, creep **0.25 / 0.15 / 0.11**, pry 0.30-0.75 - so
**the pads do not pry and the 4-contact form does not re-seat past 2 mm**, P104's
caveat surviving its own transfer. The Allegro's one holding draw: **1.24x at
2 mm**, bounded **>3.63x** sustained (never left inside the 40 N cap), at a force
that is not matched to 4.90 N, and with the 39.75 mm creep above.

**So what is licensed is a shape, not a product.** The plan's own clause applies -
*if only the surrogate passes, the surrogate licenses the purchase and the
Allegro's number is recorded as the 3+1 topology's own* - which says the form to
buy is **radial or strongly enveloping, not anthropomorphic 3+1**, and changes
*which vendor*, not *whether to buy*. **The purchase stays the owner's**; no
buyable hand was measured, the surrogate cannot approach or run a precision grasp,
and **M2b (approach) and M3 (scripted hand) are unspent** - and the Allegro's
failure mode here, batting the payload out of the seat during the close, is
exactly the class M2b would have to score.

No `src/` or `configs/` change, no shipped default moved, no commit, no reference
re-recorded (the scripted line never runs this code); `configs/motion_reference.json`
= `..._twoline.json` = **`30fb99f8`** and `..._single.json` = **`8952c320`** stand;
ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`. Evidence `logs/p106/`
(`METHOD.md`, `RESULTS.md`, `m1_mount_probe.py`, `run_p106.sh`, `mount_census.txt`,
`m2a_allegro.txt`, `m2a_control.txt`, `inspect_allegro.py`, `units_probe.py`).

### P107 - the radial four-pad cage: built, exact, and it does not enclose a belt fruit

The owner's decision after P106 was to build the **shape** the licence names rather
than buy a product, so this phase is **M2b + M3** on a built hand:
`FRUIT_GRIPPER_KIND=cage4` - four pads at 4 x 90 deg on the OpenArm's tool point,
one scalar closure, force-capped drives, driven through the same
`follow_centre/pad_centre/pad_faces` interface the shipped hand uses, so the
grasp/close/carry/release code is unchanged. Default off, its own hand kind, and
the shipped `openarm` path is proven inert (below).

**The asset is exact, and the tool offset is now a measured number.**
`logs/p107/m1_cage.txt`: aperture **120.0 -> 26.0 mm**, measured = commanded to
0.0 mm on both axes at every rung; **the tool offset that replaces `_pad_standoff`
is 70.00 mm and its spread over nine apertures is 0.00 mm** - derived from the
shipped plate's distal plane (80.5) and lip (10.5), and constant because the
synergy is radial only. That is the number P106 could not have on the Allegro
(100-216 mm across a posture sweep), and it is the reason no aim code changed: the
cage's tool offset **is** the shipped expression, by derivation. Lip 10.5 mm and
distal plane 80.5 mm are the shipped ones. Delivered per-pad force: median **4.90
N** (the cap), max 87.85 N on the legs where the fruit does not fit the closed
ring.

**M2b's letter passes and its mechanism fails.** 15 attempts, seed 5: **no-contact
1/15** (the plan's `<= 1/15`, so the kill does **not** fire and M3 is licensed),
yet the **enclosure is 2/15 at >= 3 pads**, the payload is displaced **15-107 mm
relative to the belt on 7/15 closes**, and the **cage-vs-payload clearance on the
descent is `-0.3..-33.4 mm` on 7/15** - the face planes go *through* the fruit.
**The registered endpoint cannot see a cage that misses**: an approach that arrives
beside the fruit still loads a pad, so "no contact" passes while the enclose fails.
The endpoint to register next time is the enclosure plus the relative displacement;
both are printed per attempt now (`[cage] pads=n/4 bat_rel=..`).

**M3's kill fires.** 10 attempts at the acceptance's two seeds: **2/10 (seed 5)**
and **1/7 (seed 6)** against the **same-tree, same-seed shipped-hand controls'
6/9 and 7/9** - pooled **3/17 = 17.6 % vs 13/18 = 72.2 %**. The carry legs are the
**no-contact/ejection** class (`force_min == 0` and `clean_slip > 100 mm` on **29 of
43**, median 407-614 mm) where the shipped hand's failures are the *closed* loaded
slide; **the class the retrofit was supposed to answer is never reached**, because
it cannot hold long enough to slide. Budgets: 4 of 43 descents at 1.1x (P93's
stochastic branch property, not re-tuned); `s/attempt` 15.3/15.9 vs 14.8/14.3; and
the **landing guard is not measured** (no `FRUIT_PLACE_TRACE` in those cells - a
named gap, not a pass).

**Why, with the number.** The blocker is the **aim**, not the pad: the fruit can
enter the descent **24 mm** off the cage's axis (the shipped aim is a point hand's;
its 98 mm jaws give ~14 mm of slack), so an open cage needs **>= 2 x (24 + 35) =
118 mm** of aperture to swallow the error - and the supply's along-belt spacing is
**85-120 mm**, so a wider cage fouls its own neighbours. A radial cage needs a
**centring step before the descent** (the tree already has the machinery:
`_dynamic_grip_target` / `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_X_TRACK_*` / the x-lock) or a workstation
where the fruit is presented to it. **The next spend is one of those, not a hand
and not a policy.**

**Seven measured iterations, each a finding** (`logs/p107/METHOD.md` §2), and the
list is the useful artifact: (1) four 61 mm plates at 4 x 90 deg **intersect below
a 61 mm aperture** (`pad_width <= aperture`) and with dynamic pads they jam and put
**69-100 N/pad** through the payload - width cut to 26 mm, which is
capacity-neutral because `F_crit = n mu N` is area-independent; (2) the shipped
84.9 mm plate puts its proximal end **4.4 mm above** the jaw centre, inside the
OpenArm's palm, and the contact thrashes the arm (`|a|max` 2421 m/s2, `|v|max` 20
m/s) - length cut to 60 mm with the distal plane kept, so the lip and the tool
offset are untouched; (3) **the OpenArm's finger plates keep their _asset_
colliders even with `FRUIT_FINGER_COLLIDERS=0`** - the pads jammed against them
with the aperture **frozen at 89 mm**, and disabling them is the fix that first
produced a hold (`smoke7`: `grasped=True placed=True lift=+0.304 m`); (4)
`c = 2000 Ns/m` (the shipped fingers' value) is numerically unstable for a 0.020 kg
pad on a standalone prismatic joint at 120 Hz - `c = 100` is P104's own
near-critical pair and the one that produced the licensed 1.87-2.05x; (5) a hand
mounted on the tool must **ride the arm every tick**, or it parks at the previous
grip pose at belt height and in the supply's path (5 fruit knocked off, 2 starved
slots); (6) the open aperture must swallow the pursuit error (90 mm -> `clr`
-20.5 mm and a 546 mm bat); (7) a radial close must use the payload's **widest
horizontal extent**, not the two-jaw chord (with the chord, 1-2 pads load and the
rest read zero).

**No-harm, proven.** `scripts/accept.sh` with the kind unset: **8/10, 9.0
s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`**, and its **421 `[fruit]` lines are 421/421
byte-identical** to `logs/p103/accept_final.log`. `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS (0
failures, 1 skipped)**. No `configs/` change, no reference re-recorded, no re-base:
`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` stand, ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`. Evidence
`logs/p107/`.

### P108 - option 2 (a wider cage + a wider supply spacing): the census rewrites the 24 mm, the aperture buys only the approach, the spacing starves, and the enclosure is a centring term

P107 ended on a fork: a radial cage needs its axis on the fruit before the descent,
so the next spend is a **centring step** (option 1) or a **workstation**.  The owner
chose **option 2** instead - **widen the cage's aperture and the supply's along-belt
spacing** - and P108 builds and measures exactly that, with the two knobs that
already existed (`FRUIT_CAGE_OPEN_FACE_R`, `FRUIT_SUPPLY_GAP_MIN`), so **no `src/`
or `configs/` change** and nothing to re-baseline.  Registration: `logs/p108/PREREG.md`
(md5 **`7ea6662054fa2acdf490042c0737e662`**), pinned before any battery cell.

*(Correction, recorded here rather than rewritten: an interim close-out at 14:16
read this battery at **two seeds** (5, 6) and called the aperture "a measured
actuator ... the placements double at both seeds".  The **fresh seed-101** cage
cells were then re-run to completion - an earlier attempt's `.tmp` files had been
dropped as aborted, and these are complete (`attempts=19` / `20`, `[stats]`
present) - and they **reverse the placement read at that seed** (4/19 -> 3/20).
The record below is the three-seed one, in which the placement movement is a
**draw** (p = 0.37) and the enclosure doubling (+7.7 points, p = 0.28) is under
the registered +30 point bar.)*

**The census first, and it reframes the problem.**  P107's "24 mm off the cage's
axis" is **not** a grasp-time figure and **not** a lateral one: over the **726**
`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_TRACE` attempts already on disk the offset at the close's first tick
is **`|dx|` 3.4 mm / `|dy|` 1.1 mm / radial 4.5 mm** (p50, `logs/p108/close_aim.py`).
What is 83 mm is the **arrival**: `[task] dynamic descent: fruit dy` reads **p5 82 /
p50 83 / p90 85 mm** over **3963** attempts, and **18 mm of it is
`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_DESCEND_MARGIN`'s 0.15 s** at 0.12 m/s - the line's own lead, not an
error.  The **binding window** is the descent because the plate (60 mm long,
**20.5-80.5 mm below the jaw**) and a 60-70 mm payload's sphere overlap over **~130 mm
of `dz`**, i.e. virtually the whole 55-60 mm leg; the pads enter the payload's band
**14.5 mm in**, and per tick (15 traced cage attempts, `tr_cage_s5/`) the payload is
then **55.8 mm upstream (p50, max 61.7) and 11.8 mm lateral** - an **83-89 %
along-belt** split, with the lateral tail (60-70 mm) belonging to the attempts whose
x-tracking lagged.  **So an oblong aperture is not the answer either**: its narrow
86 mm lateral axis fails exactly that tail (`oblong 86x210` passes 5/8 windows
against `round210`'s 7/8), so a genuinely narrow lateral needs a centring step first.
The required aperture is `A = 2 (offset + r + 4 mm)`: **`A_y` 181.6 (p50) / 216.6
(p90) mm** with the pool's 35 mm `r_max`, `A_x` 83.7 (p50); the offline per-tick
screen reproduces P107's failure exactly - **120 mm passes 0/8 windows, 160 5/8,
210 7/8** - and the registered **200 mm** (`OPEN_FACE_R=0.100`) sits at the census's
p90.  **The spacing** it demands is `100 + 10 + 35 + 4 = **149 mm**` against the
scatter's planned **0.10-0.35 m**; the delivered line met it in **every** census
window (**0** neighbours inside the 0.15 m filter, 0/8), so the spacing was a margin
purchase against a collision that was never observed.

**The instrument is inert, again.**  The census cell is the P107 cage with
`FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE=2000 FRUIT_FRUIT_TRACE_ARM=1 FRUIT_CYCLE_REPORT=1`, and its **502
`[fruit]` lines are 502/502 byte-identical** to P107's own `m2b_s5.log` (trace, cycle
and `[cage]` rows dropped), `attempts=15 successes=2 sim=232.0s`.  Third time this
tree has measured a 3-prim-per-arm read as branch-neutral (P95's 970/970 and
974/974), and the reason the census's numbers can be quoted at all.

**The battery** (scripted single arm, `ATTEMPTS=20`, seeds 5, 6 and a **fresh 101**
for the cage arms, every arm carrying `FRUIT_CAGE_PROBE` + `MOTION_REPORT` +
`CARRY_DIAG` + **`PLACE_TRACE`** - P107's M3 cells had no landing trace and could not
report one): **S** shipped hand **25/38 = 65.8 %**, **B** cage120 **10/51 =
19.6 %**, **E** cage200 **16/57 = 28.1 %**, **C** cage200 + `GAP_MIN=0.15`
**6/35 = 17.1 %**.  **The aperture has exactly one robust effect and it is the
class it targets**: **`clr < 0` (a pad face inside the payload during the approach)
32/51 -> 4/57**, Fisher **p = 1.4e-8**.  **Everything the registration calls an
outcome is a draw**: **enclosure at >= 3 pads 5/51 (9.8 %) -> 10/57 (17.5 %)**,
p = 0.28 - it *doubles*, but the pre-registered **+30 point** bar is not met, so the
registration's own "the aperture is not the actuator" fires - and the **placed count
10/51 -> 16/57**, p = 0.37, better at seeds 5 and 6 (3/18 -> 7/19, 3/14 -> 6/18)
and **worse at the fresh seed 101** (4/19 -> 3/20).  That reversal is exactly what
P93's fresh-seed rule exists for: the two-seed reading ("better at both") is a
branch draw, and the cage stays far below the shipped hand (**p = 0.0003**).  The
descent's `end=` also turns out to be a **seed-5 branch property** rather than a
general cost of 120 mm: **57.9 mm (p50) at B s5** against the shipped hand's 8.9-9.1,
where the 120 mm pads **block the leg** on half the attempts, but **10.1/10.3 mm** at
B s6/s101, and **9.3-10.5 mm** at E's three seeds.

**The phase's primary does not move, and the mechanism is the closure's centring.**
The enclosure histogram is **bimodal: 4 pads or 1-2, never 3** (`{0:2, 1:6, 2:8,
4:3}` at 200 mm; `{0:7, 1:7, 2:5}` at 120 mm on the fresh seed) - the payload either
is or is not centred when the ring closes.  And the closure *depth* is not its
actuator either: a **post-hoc** cell at `FRUIT_GRIPPER_SQUEEZE=0.94` (a 6 %
interference on the widest extent instead of 2 %) reads **1/17**.  The reason is the
shipped target: `grip_gap = pinch_width * 0.98` and `pinch_width`'s radial branch is
the payload's **widest horizontal extent** (P107's iteration 7), so the two pads on
that axis touch at the 4.9 N cap while the two on the narrow axis stand off by
`(widest - narrow)/2 + 2 %` - and a deeper command does not bring them in because the
ring is **off-centre**, so the near pads simply push the payload further off.  The
measured close-time lateral offset is **`|dx|` p50 8.8 mm** on the cage cell, the
same order as the stand-off.

**The spacing half fails its registered guard, and the prior was P1c's.**  On the
200 mm cage, `GAP_MIN` 0.10 -> 0.15 costs **5 starved slots of 20 against 1** at seed
5 (3 vs 2 at seed 6), the placements fall **16/57 -> 6/35**, and the seed-5 cell
collapses to **1/15** (four lost slots and four `fruit did not follow the gripper`
notes).  That is P1c's finding on the same axis - the **single arm** starves when the
supply thins (the two-line hides it because its worker parks and waits, and the cage
cannot run there).  G3 fires at seed 5, and the census had already said the spacing
buys nothing measured.

**Verdict: not adopted**, and the useful part is the split it leaves.  The aperture
is a **precondition** (the approach, decisive) and not an outcome; the spacing is
**not affordable**; and **the term that holds the placed count at 28 % is the
centring**.  So **option 1 is the cheaper route for the term that actually blocks the
placement** - but it is **not sufficient alone**, because a passive lateral guide
cannot remove the **56 mm along-belt** arrival.  The cheapest *complete* pair the
numbers license is **`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_DESCEND_MARGIN` 0.15 -> 0** (an existing knob; it
is 18 of the 83 mm, so `A_y` p50 falls **181.6 -> 145.6 mm**, which the **160 mm**
cage already half-passes) **+ a 160 mm cage + a centring guide** at the station,
already scoped to the census's own instrument.  That is a registration of its own,
and it is where the next spend goes.

**No-harm, proven.**  `scripts/accept.sh` with every knob unset: **8/10, 9.0
s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**, and its **421 `[fruit]` lines are
421/421 byte-identical** to `logs/p107/accept_noharm.log`.  `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)**; `python3 scripts/211_bed_audit.py` **ok (115
checks)**.  Landing: payload-present releases land `on_belt` on S 25/37, B 10/21,
E 16/28, C 6/15 (the misses are the upstream-lost `-184 mm` class).  No `configs/`
change, no reference re-recorded, ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a` - `30fb99f8` /
`30fb99f8` / `8952c320` stand.  Evidence `logs/p108/` (`PREREG.md`, `CENSUS.md`,
`RESULTS.md`, `census.py`, `close_aim.py`, `census.txt`, `p108_report.py`,
`p108_report.txt`, `run_p108.sh`, `cells.sh`, the cells `{S,B,E}_{5,6,101}`,
`{C}_{5,6}`, `E_sq94_s5`, the traced `tr_cage_s5/`, `accept_noharm.{log,driver}`).

### P109 - the descent margin is load-bearing: it sets the *sign* of the arrival, and spending it costs the catch (2026-11-03)

**The question, the pre-registration, and the guard that came first.**  P108's option
① was `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_DESCEND_MARGIN` **0.15 -> 0**, "the only cheap lever that touches
the along-belt arrival" (its census: the payload sits **83 mm** upstream at the
descent's start, 83-89 % along-belt, the pads entering the payload's band 14.5 mm in
with the fruit still 55.8 mm upstream).  The guard was named before the phase ran:
the margin is what lets the descent meet a slightly late fruit
(`deadline = speed*(t_desc + margin)`), so **the catch's own success** is what can
break.  `logs/p109/PREREG.md` (md5 **`192a0c1b`**) pinned three arms (M0 unset =
0.15, **M0.5** 0.075 as the dose axis, M1 = 0), four seeds (5, 6 and P93's fresh
101, 202), 20 attempts, the scripted single arm, one claim each, and this rule: **a
win needs `g0` to fall AND the no-grasp class not to rise at any seed AND the placed
count not to fall by more than one per seed**; anything else is a report.

**The instrument correction, before any mechanism claim.**  `[task] dynamic descent`
prints `fruit dy`, and the code makes it `fruit − intercept` with
`intercept = fruit − speed*t_desc` - so **`fruit dy == speed*t_desc`, with no margin
term at all**: the number P108 read as "the arrival offset" **cannot** respond to
this knob.  The twelve cells confirm it: `fruit dy` p50 **83.0 / 82.0 / 83.0 mm** for
0.15 / 0.075 / 0 across four seeds each.  The gap the margin sets is
**`g0 = fruit dy + shift = deadline`**, the descent-start distance from the fruit to
the aim, and it moves cleanly: p50 **99.9-100.4 -> 90.8-91.0 -> 82.1-82.3 mm**, i.e.
**+17.6 / +18.3 / +17.6 / +17.7 mm** M0 -> M1 at the four seeds, with the half rung
exactly mid-ladder.  It also moves the **selector floor**
(`_dynamic_pick_lead() + speed*select_s + margin`) by the same 18 / 9 mm, so the
**selected fruit sequence differs at every seed** from attempt 1-3 on - registered as
E0, and the reason a count delta across arms is partly a branch.

**What it does to the arrival.**  The descent is a static, open-loop profiled leg to
the station (the aim is `station_y`), and the belt runs at a measured 1.00x, so the
whole window shifts by the same 18 mm: the fruit's position **relative to the aim
when the pads stop** is `g0 − 0.12 m/s × steps` (steps 88-94, printed) and it goes
from **+10.6 mm p50 (past on 0 of 76 attempts) to −7.3 mm (past on 79 of 79)**, with
0.075 at **+1.3 mm (9 of 75, p10 −0.1 - it sits on the boundary)**.  That sign is the
phase's mechanism: the catch-up commands `fruit + v*0.25 s`, i.e. **30 mm further
downstream**, so it wants the fruit **upstream** of the tip when the descent ends;
with the fruit already 5-8 mm past the aim the command is 35-38 mm ahead of a tip
that has to move downstream at the belt's own 1 mm/tick to hold station, and the loop
is a race the arm can lose.

**The guard fires, and the failure is bistable - not graded.**  The catch-up's
residual p50 is **5.8-5.9 mm in every arm** (it is the tolerance itself: the loop
exits at `catch_tol` 6 mm), so the honest read is the tail.  Runaways (residual
**> 50 mm**): M0 **0/76**, M0.5 **0/75**, M1 **5/79** with values **233.2 / 254.7 /
256.3 / 259.0 / 261.8 mm** - nothing between 6 and 233 mm in 240 attempts.  All five
are **M1 at seed 5** (5/20 vs the control's 0/19, Fisher **p = 0.047**), spread
through the run (attempts 0, 1, 6, 13, 17), and all five end `grasped=False` with
`fruit did not follow the gripper`.  The other three battery seeds read **0/60**, and
the shipped arm draws the class too - **1 of its 10 acceptance attempts** - so pooled
with the acceptance the class is **8/89 = 9.0 % vs 1/86 = 1.2 %, p = 0.035**: the
margin depresses the rate ~7x, it does not delete it.  **The other no-grasp events
are a different class**: M0's single one (seed 6) and all three of M0.5's (seed 101)
read a converged **5.8-6.0 mm** residual and then lose the payload at the close - the
converged close/grip class `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md` already documents - so only M1
produces the timing runaways, which is what makes this guard specific to the knob.

**The count and the branch.**  M0 **49/76 = 64.5 %**, M0.5 **49/75 = 65.3 %** (a
**draw**, Fisher p = 1.0), M1 **41/79 = 51.9 %** - **down at 4 of 4 seeds**
(-2 / -3 / -2 / -1, pooled p = 0.143, sign 4/4), and 3 of those 4 seeds break the
registered "not by more than one" clause.  The selected sequences differ (E0), so the
count is partly a branch draw; the class read is the one that transfers.

**The acceptance A/B (the catch's own gate), and it is also the two-line's read.**
Ten attempts, the shipped two-line session - and the two-line **does** read the knob
(both stations' `shift` go to ~0 and the runaways rise), so a flip would move every
dynamic catch on every path.  Unset: **8/10 = 80 %, `fingerprint: matches
30fb99f8`, `190: PASS`**, and **419/419 byte-identical** to
`logs/p108/accept_noharm.log`.  M1: **4/10 = 40 %** (below the 0.60 two-line floor),
no-grasp **2 -> 5**, runaways **1 -> 3**, budgets clean in both arms (worst `|v|max`
0.110-0.112 of 0.160, lurch 0.017 of 0.291), fingerprint DIFFERS by construction.

**Verdict: not a lever - and the record's one correction.**  E1b passes and **E3, E4
and the acceptance gate all fail**, so nothing ships: `configs/` untouched, `30fb99f8`
/ `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` stand, no reference re-recorded and none owed.  **The
correction is to P108's "cheapest complete package", which listed this knob as its
first, free term**: the margin is **not** a cushion to be spent, it is the term that
keeps the catch-up's residual **positive**, and the 18 mm it holds is not the
`fruit dy` number the census quoted.  The **dose axis says it from the other side**:
half the margin keeps the arrival on the correct side and **buys nothing** (a count
draw, 0 runaways in 75), so there is no throughput on the far side of the boundary
to walk toward.  **The remaining lever on the along-belt term** is P108's **aperture
precondition** (`clr < 0` 32/51 -> 4/57, p = 1.4e-8) or a **centring guide /
workstation presentation**; a shorter descent is not available either (jerk-bound on
a 5.5 cm leg, 86 ticks at `a_max` 0.8 *and* 1.6, P91 §3, and its `|v|max` is the
motion gate's) - so **not another margin rung**.

**No-harm, proven four ways.**  `M0_s5`/`M0_s6` replay P108's `S_s5`/`S_s6`
**860/860** and **853/853** on the `[fruit]` stream with the phase's only added row
(`[cycle]`, 21 of them) and `[stats]` dropped - so the tree is inert, the P108 cells
are admissible controls, and `FRUIT_CYCLE_REPORT` is run-neutral on this line; the
unset acceptance replays P108's **419/419**; `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS** (0
failures, 1 skipped); `106` **OK**, `107` **PASS** (21 checks).  All twelve cells'
descents are inside their budgets (worst `|v|max` **0.1230** m/s against 0.160-0.162,
lurch 0.039 against 0.291), and every payload-present release lands `on_belt` except
the recorded `cnp` rows (**49/51 / 49/49 / 41/44**).  Pins: `tasks.py`
**`d341b0da`**, `rl_env.py` **`bf4c56fa`**, `bimanual.py` `9b7fc33f`, `fruits.py`
`dcabe16b`, `assets.py` `eb30c77a`, `scene.py` `a0199097`; ckpt `moe_v13s`
`61da390a`.  Deviations: **D1** a description error in `PREREG.md` §1 (the
parenthetical calls +12.8 mm "past the aim"; it is upstream - the formula and the
report's column are right), **D2** a 3-attempt build smoke whose attempt 0 reproduces
the cell's 259.0 mm exactly.  Evidence `logs/p109/` (`PREREG.md` `192a0c1b`,
`RESULTS.md`, `cells.sh`, `run_p109.sh`, `p109_report.py`, `p109_report.txt`,
`gates.out`, the twelve cells `{M0,M05,M1}_s{5,6,101,202}`, the acceptance pair
`accept_{m0,m1}`, `accept_final`).

### P110 - the presentation lane: a metering gate works (16/16 held, belt running) and still cannot centre the ring, whose enclosure is 2/74 clean not 11/74 (2026-11-03)

**The question.**  P109 closed the descent margin and P108 the aperture and the
spacing; both left the *presentation* named - the payload is **~56 mm upstream** of
the tool axis when the cage's plates are beside it, an 83-95 % along-belt split.
Two forms were registered (`logs/p110/PREREG.md`, md5 **`cce8838c`**, pinned before
any run): (a) a passive lateral centring guide, (b) a **metering gate** that holds
the fruit's along-belt position while the belt slips under it.  The owner's kill
criterion was in the brief: **if the gate holds but the cage still fails to enclose,
the term is not the presentation either.**

**The census first, offline, and it kills (a) by arithmetic.**  `census.py` reads
114 descents of this tree's own cells plus P108's per-tick traces.  The split at the
band entry is **55.8 mm along-belt / 2.6 mm lateral** p50 - and the 11.8 mm the
record quotes for the lateral is the **max over the window** (the arm's x-tracking
lag), not the entry, so the entry split is **92.5 %** along-belt.  The term's
identity: `fruit dy` (83.0 mm p50) **is** `speed * t_desc`, and the margin cancels
inside it (P109); the entry offset is that clock minus the leg's first
`s_enter = 0.095 + 0.060 - (0.0805 + 2r)` = 4.5-38.5 mm, i.e. **29.7-76.6 mm by
radius**, `A_y = 2(dy + r)` **182 mm** p50 with the pool's `r_max`.  The measured
55.8 sits **below** the 62.8 mm a 6 cm fruit predicts because **the plates arrest the
payload**: **25 % of the band window's ticks run below half the belt speed** (p90
58 %), so the belt is already slipping under the payload for part of the descent -
the "moving fruit" half of the term is partly spent by the very plates that will
grasp it.  **A lateral guide removes 0 % of `A_y`** (the aperture need is per axis
and along-belt dominates): P108's screen (120 mm 0/8, 160 5/8, 210 7/8) cannot move,
and the guide's only purchase is 39 % of the *close-time* radial.  The tree's own
lateral guides make it geometric: `containment_parts`' side fences are a **0.300 m
channel against a 0.160 m delivered band**, so they never touch a fruit; a guide that
did would have to be narrower than the band, and the open hand already needs 0.132 m
of it.  **Form (a) is not built and not measured.**

**The gate, built as a fixture and surprisingly strong.**  `fixture_gate.py` is a
`logs/` probe (no `src/`): the real kinematic belt + `PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI`, the
real 16-fruit pool (29.6-69.6 mm, 9.5-122.8 g, mu 0.51-0.92), and a kinematic kerb
across the belt whose upstream face sits 20 mm downstream of the station.  Every cell
runs the whole pool singly.  Result: **16/16 held at every height 8 / 10 / 12 / 14 /
20 / 30 / 45 mm, 0 escaped, no climb**, the **belt at -0.120 m/s in every cell**
(the directive holds - the belt never stops), the **steady drag 0.11-1.05 N** (the
1.27-2.52 N peak p50 is the impact), the **hold's span 0.85-1.83 mm** p50 (max 3.7-6.6),
and the **parking position 13.1-21.7 mm across the pool**.  So `K4` ("a <= 14.5 mm
kerb cannot hold a 30-70 mm fruit") **does not fire**, and by a wide margin: an 8 mm
kerb holds a 69.6 mm apple.  Two by-products: **a taller gate parks further upstream**
(`y_park` +0.0024 at 8 mm -> +0.0115 at 45 mm, the contact latitude rising), so the
cheapest height is also the most accurate; and the shipped line's own
`enforce_transport` nudge (which forces -0.048 m/s on any fruit below 0.02 m/s) is
**inert** against the gate (`wake=0` reads the `wake=1` cell exactly - a coupling the
PREREG predicted would matter and does not).

**The queue is where it breaks, and it breaks in two ways.**  The next fruit arrives
**inside the same attempt** (the shipped 0.83-2.9 s cadence against a 15.1 s pick), so
a passive gate *does* trip on it: with one behind the parked fruit's hold degrades
**1.8 -> 4.3 mm**, with three **4.9 mm** (max 30.8), and **1 of 16 is expelled past
the gate** (a 65.1 mm
peach, mu 0.59, parked 501 ticks then pushed 62 mm through).  That is the rate
arithmetic measured as a load: **8.1 fruit = 1.81 m** queued per 15.1 s cycle into a
1.60 m belt.  **The release is not the gate's problem**: `mu_pair * steady drag` =
0.16-1.32 N, **1.3-10.4 %** (median 6 %) of the pinch's 12.7 N - the height was, and
8-14 mm clears the hand's 14.5 mm.

**The phase's other half is a correction to the record, and it is the finding that
transfers.**  P107/P108's endpoint "enclosure at >= 3 pads" is **11/74 = 14.9 %** raw.
Joined to each attempt's own descent `end=` and its ring aperture, that bucket is
**5 blocked-descent jams** (`end` p50 79.8 mm, `F` p50 **1074 N**, up to **2920 N**),
**4 over-closures** (`aper` 32.5 mm on 31-37 mm fruit, `F` 119 N) and **2 clean
enclosures = 2/74 = 2.7 %**.  The two clean rows read `clr` **-9.5** and **+31.7 mm**,
so the approach clearance does **not** order them (the jams are the large-`clr` class,
p50 +32.9 mm) - the enclosure is not an aperture datum at all.  The modal grasp is
**2 pads at the cap** (22/74, `F` p50 9.74 N = 1.99 cap-pairs): a V-block with
`n = 2`, i.e. the **same** axial capacity as the shipped two-jaw pinch (P104), so the
cage's licensed 4-contact gain is not being collected on any of those attempts.

**And the closure's algebra says why, which is why the presentation cannot fix it.**
One radial synergy on four force-capped position pads (`a = 0.49 d`, cap 4.90 N,
`k = 1e5 N/m`): the elastic allowance is `cap/k` = **0.049 mm**; a payload offset by
`delta` has its near pad commanded `delta + 0.01 d` *inside* its surface and its far
pad `0.01 d - delta` *short* of contact, so **the far pads reach only when
`delta < 0.01 d = 0.6 mm`**.  Above that the payload sticks to the near faces and is
**launched** - which is exactly the measured `bat` (27-82 mm of payload displacement
during the close) and `bat_rel` (0-330 mm relative to the belt).  **The line cannot
deliver 0.6 mm**: the catch-up's convergence tolerance is **6 mm**
(`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_CATCH_TOL`), the measured close-time offset is **8.8 mm lateral /
20.2 mm along** (P108), and the gate's own hold is **1.8 mm within a fruit** and
**17.5 mm across the pool**.  So the ring asks for **3-29x** tighter positioning than
anything on the line delivers, and the gate's best case still misses by 3x.  **The
gate buys the arrival (a precondition P108 already pays for with the aperture) and
not the centring.**  `K1`/`K2`/`K3` fire, `K4` does not: **the presentation lane
closes - detected but not convertible.**

**What the record now leaves standing**, in the order the phase prices it: a
**compliant closure** (per-pad springs or four independent force targets - the only
term the algebra leaves, a `cage_hand.py` change), a **sub-millimetre catch tolerance**
(0.5 mm: one env knob, but only coherent with a *stationary* fruit, i.e. on the gate
plus the magazine), and `docs/LEFT_ARM.md`'s two sanctions (**a new pad asset**, a
**real-jaw clamp-force anchor**).  The arm battery was **not spent**, and the reason
is the PREREG's own inequality, not convenience: no arrangement of a passive element
changes `0.6 mm < 1.8 mm`, and the cage's clean enclosure is 2/74 without one.

**No-harm, and it is the acceptance itself** because the phase changes no `src/` file:
`scripts/accept.sh` **8/10, 9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches
configs/motion_reference.json`, `190: PASS`**, its **`[fruit]` stream byte-identical** to
`logs/p109/accept_final.log` (identical md5 over 420 lines); `scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS (0
failures, 1 skipped)**; `python3 scripts/211_bed_audit.py` **ok (115 checks)**;
`configs/motion_reference.json` = `..._twoline.json` = **`30fb99f8`** and
`..._single.json` = **`8952c320`** untouched, no reference re-recorded and none owed.
Deviations: **D1** the PREREG's "0-17 mm parking spread" is a *pool* number - the
fixture separates it into **1.8 mm within a fruit** and **17.5 mm across**; **D2**
the predicted `enforce_transport` coupling is measured inert; **D3** the `q8` cell
reads `q4` (only three fruits reach the gate inside the 12.5 s run), so the load
claim is carried by `q4` and the 8-fruit queue is an argument from the rate; **D4**
the fixture measures contact mechanics only - no attempt, no placement.  Pins
unchanged: `tasks.py` `d341b0da`, `rl_env.py` `bf4c56fa`, `bimanual.py` `9b7fc33f`,
`fruits.py` `dcabe16b`, `conveyor.py` `fb2c58c6`, `assets.py` `eb30c77a`, `scene.py`
`a0199097`; ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`.  Evidence `logs/p110/` (`CENSUS.md`,
`census.py`/`census.txt`, `PREREG.md` `cce8838c`, `RESULTS.md`, `fixture_gate.py`,
`run_p110.sh`, `p110_report.py`, `fixture.txt`, the cells
`fix_{h8,h10,h12,h14,h20,h30,h45,h14_nowake,q2,q4,q8}.log`).

### P111 - the compliant closure: a gentler jam, not a self-centring chuck

**The owner's item** was P110's 1: the ring's four pads are force-capped
*position* drives, so a pad yields only `cap/k = 0.049 mm`, the far pad is
`2*delta` short, and an off-centre payload is *launched* instead of pushed - make
the pad a spring and the four pads should balance at the ring's centre.  The
phase registers that (`logs/p111/PREREG.md` `e641d074`, before any cell;
`PREREG_A1.md` `c2d263e4`, before any treatment cell), writes the algebra, builds
the mechanism, and runs six arms at four seeds.  **Nothing adopted, no default
changed, `configs/` untouched.**

**The algebra first, and it decided the shape** (`logs/p111/algebra.py`).  The
payload's motion is *normal* to the near/far faces (no friction there) and
*tangential* to the perpendicular pair, so `drive = near - far` and
`fric = 2 mu perp + mu_belt m g`, and the terminal offset is
`delta_inf = (2 mu - 1) * min(s, cap/(2 mu k))`.  Two consequences:

* **`mu > 1` is the term, not the stiffness.**  The residual is `(2mu - 2)s`, so a
  four-jaw lands at 1.1-1.9 s where the 4-contact state needs `delta < s - 0.5/k`.
  The measured pad-payload friction is `mu_pair = (2.0 + mu_fruit)/2` = **1.25-1.46**
  (P104's `mu_app` averaged with the pad's 2.0), so the ratio is **k- and
  cap-free**: no stiffness, no cap.  **A three-jaw would centre**
  (`2 mu s/(1.5 + mu)` = 0.82 s < s) - the *number of tangential contacts* is the
  lever.
* **The ladder is a knee, not a slope**: at `k > k* = cap/(2 mu s)` ~ 2.2e3 N/m the
  perpendicular pair is at the cap, `fric = 2 mu cap = 12.8 N > cap`, and the
  payload does not move at all (the shipped ring); below it the payload slides to
  `(2mu-1)s`.

The 1-D integration of the close (the shipped profile + the task's 0.5 N/3-tick
freeze) added the prediction the cells confirmed: the force *at the freeze* falls
from 4.90 N to 0.6-1.8 N as `k` falls and the freeze fires earlier, so a compliant
ring is a **gentler and shallower** close - and a shallower close is what the
`off0` instrument then reads as the payload slipping.

**What was built** (`cage_hand.py`, default off, three windows one knob each):
`FRUIT_CAGE_PAD_STIFFNESS` is the **approach** profile (the shipped `k = 1e5`),
**`FRUIT_CAGE_CLOSE_STIFFNESS`** the **close** window, **`FRUIT_CAGE_HOLD_STIFFNESS`**
the **carry**'s hard stop.  `close_begin` (new, one call site) puts the drives on
the close profile; `close_done` (new, one call site) re-writes them **with the
target unchanged**, so a soft close re-loads to `min(k_hold * pen, cap)` **at the
aperture it found** - a spring-loaded pad bottoming out, and the pad body cannot
move because the payload is in the way.  An open command reverts, so the revert
needs no third call site, and at the shipped defaults `_profile`'s own guard makes
both calls dead writes (the selfcheck executes that).  The **instrument** is
`[cage] off0= off=`: the payload's radial distance from the ring's **axis** (the
cage base's xy - the four pads are symmetric about it) at the close's start and
flush, two reads per attempt from poses the probe already takes.  It is what makes
"centring" measurable, and it immediately corrected the phase's own premise: the
close-time offset is **2.9-3.1 mm p50**, not P108's **8.8 mm** - which is the
*aim* offset, already removed by the catch-up (`PREREG_A1` records the
correction, keeps every rule, and notes the falsifier is therefore *stronger*
than registered).

**The cells** (`logs/p111/cells.sh`, scripted single arm, `ATTEMPTS=20`, P108's
instrumentation verbatim on every arm): **C** the shipped hand, **R** the rigid
cage (`k = 1e5`, 200 mm), **T1** always-soft `k = 1e3` + the stop, **T2**
always-soft `k = 5e3` + the stop, **S1** pure-soft (no stop), and **T4** the
*scoped* form (rigid approach, soft close, stop) - added because T1's first cell
showed an always-soft pad is a poor **position source**: with the compliance armed
through the approach and descent the plates are pushed out of the ring's geometry
by whatever they meet, and T1 read **1/20** against the rigid ring's 7/19 with the
arm-never-arrived class growing (off-ring 34 -> 37 %) and the jam class 6 -> 11.

**The result, and it is a mechanism negative.**  **The clean enclosure does not
rise**: P110's split of `pads >= 3` gives R **3/76 (3.9 %)**, T1 **0/73**, T2
1/77, T4 2/75, S1 0/37 - and the **modal pad count is 2 in every arm**, the rigid
one included (19-30 of 37-77 rows), so the ring is a **two-pad V-block at every
stiffness** and a V-block has no centring symmetry to exploit.  **The centring
does not happen**: over the rows that stayed in the ring (`off0 < 20 mm`) the
median `off - off0` is **+0.2 mm** on the rigid ring and **+1.9 / +0.7 / +2.0 /
+1.3 mm** on T1/T2/T4/S1 - the payload is carried slightly *away* from the axis,
and the compliant arms do it more.  **The count does not rise**: R **25.0 %**
(19/76), T2 23.4, T4 17.3, T1 16.4, S1 13.5 - *monotone in compliance* but all
**Fisher n.s.** at n = 73-77, and the **seed-5 pair alone** (R 7/19 vs T1 1/20,
p = 0.020) would have over-stated the loss 5x: the fresh seeds read T1 **5/19
twice**, the same branch class as the control.  P93's rule, again, and the reason
the battery is four seeds.

**The three measured reasons it cannot work** (the phase's transferable content):
(1) the aperture is `0.98 x` the **widest** extent, so any roundness `> s` leaves
the perpendicular pair 1-6 mm short - it *cannot load* at this squeeze, and the
pool's roundness (0.02-0.20 d) is far above `s` (0.005-0.015 d); (2) without it
the ring is a loaded pair plus a free side, so the near pad pushes and nothing
opposes; (3) at `mu > 1` even a fully loaded pair jams at `(2mu-1)s`, so the far
pad stays short by 0.2-0.6 mm forever.  **A clean enclosure needs `roundness < s`
*and* `mu < 1`, and this pool/hand pair has neither.**

**What compliance *does* buy is real and it is only the contact**: the force at
the close's flush falls from R's **8.7-9.8 N** (the cap, two pads) to **3.5-6.6 N**
on T1 and 3.9-7.3 N on T4 - the gentler activation the hypothesis wanted, which
converts nothing because the contact is already a V-block.  The **hard stop also
works** and is measurable: on the legs where the payload is seated the compliant
arms' `fmax` reaches the cap (9.3-9.9 N) exactly as the rigid ring's does.

**Read rules the phase adds.**  (a) `pads >= 3` is **force-thresholded**: a pad
counts at 0.5 N, which a soft drive reaches at `0.5/k` of penetration, so the raw
share *falls* with compliance (17.1 -> 5.2 %) at equal aperture - a bias *against*
the compliant arm, stated and not read.  (b) `off` carries the task's own tracking
lead (`FRUIT_DYNAMIC_TRACK_LEAD` 0.18 s -> 21 mm commanded downstream), so it is a
**relative** read across arms under the same law; the `off - off0` change is the
cleaner form.  (c) A **soft pad must be scoped** to the closure: armed through the
approach it is a weak position source and the cage's own chaos grows.

**Guards**: **no crush** on any arm (`sep@loss - dia >= -15 mm`, 0 legs; the cap
bounds the force by construction), **no new failure key**, the landing misses are
the `release_bottom = -184 mm` upstream-lost class (P86/P87), and the **descent
budget fails on the cage arms including the rigid control** (0-4 legs per cell,
`R_s202` the worst at 4) - P108's blocked-descent class, **not re-tuned**.

**No-harm**: the acceptance with every knob unset reads **8/10, 9.0 s/attempt,
`fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference.json`, `190: PASS`** and its **421
`[fruit]` lines are 421/421 byte-identical** to `logs/p110/accept_noharm.log`; the
two controls are `[fruit]`-stream replays - **C_s5 = `logs/p108/S_s5.log` 621/621**
and **R_s5 = `E_s5` 531/531**, with the 19 `[cage]` rows identical once
`off0`/`off` are stripped - so the new fields and call sites are inert *and*
P108's cells are admissible controls (P95's rule, which is what makes the
four-seed pooling possible without six more cells).  `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)** with the new `P111 cage compliance` leg, `106`
**OK**, `107` **PASS (21 checks)**.

**Deviations** (`logs/p111/RESULTS.md` §7): **D1** the registered 8.8 mm is the
*aim*, corrected to the phase's own `off0` (2.9-3.1 mm) by `PREREG_A1` before any
treatment cell; **D2** `off` carries the tracking lead, so F5 (the model's absolute
0.8-1.3 mm) is **not evaluable** on this instrument and is recorded as such, not
passed; **D3** T2 ran `c = 14.1` where its registration's `2 sqrt(k m)` gives
**20.0** (ζ = 0.70) - a dose arm, reported not gated; **D4** the clean-enclosure
endpoint is force-thresholded and biased against the compliant arm; **D5** the
descent budget fails on the cage arms including the control; **D6** the shipped
hand's reference is 2 seeds (P108 has no `S` at 101/202) while the comparison arms
are 4.

**What shipping a compliant hand would owe, and why it is not worth it for this
ring**: a **spring-loaded pad with a hard stop** (the form built here) or a
**force-controlled finger** - the only form that can be stiff during the approach
and compliant only inside the closure, which the always-soft arm's 1/20 shows is
required.  The levers below the ring, priced by the algebra: a pad material with
**`mu < 1`**, a **three-jaw ring**, or P110's **0.6 mm** positioning (no passive
element on this line delivers it).

Pins: `cage_hand.py` **`ac7c7c0f`**, `tasks.py` **`a587cd21`**, `rl_env.py`
`TASKS_MD5` follow, `scripts/257_p111_cage_compliance_selftest.py`,
`scripts/selfcheck.sh`; references **`30fb99f8`** / **`30fb99f8`** / `8952c320`
untouched, none re-recorded; ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`.  Evidence `logs/p111/`
(`METHOD.md`, `PREREG.md` `e641d074`, `PREREG_A1.md` `c2d263e4`, `RESULTS.md`,
`algebra.py`/`algebra.txt`, `census.py`/`census.txt`, `enclosure.txt`, `cells.sh`,
`run_p111.sh`, `p111_report.py`, the cells `{C,R}_s5`, `R_s202`, `{T1,T2,T4,S1}_s*`).

## P112 (2026-11-04): the three-jaw ring - the closure centres, the line does not, and the count does not convert

The owner's item 2 from P111.  Its algebra said the lever is the **count of
tangential contacts**, so the phase built a three-pad ring at 3 x 120 deg, wrote
the algebra first, gated itself on a closure fixture, and measured the battery.
**Nothing adopted; `cage3` is a third hand kind behind `FRUIT_GRIPPER_KIND` and
the shipped `openarm` path is byte-identical.**

**The algebra, and a correction to P111's.**  `logs/p112/algebra.py` solves the
3-pad contact set in 2-D (`p_k = s + delta cos(theta_k)`, drive `-sum N_k u_k`,
Coulomb resistance along the motion with the **tangential projection**
`sqrt(1-(m.u_k)^2)`).  The fixed point is `delta_inf = sqrt(3) mu s/(1.5 +
(sqrt(3)/2) mu)` = **0.84-0.92 s** at the measured pair friction 1.25-1.46,
against the four-jaw's **`mu s` = 1.00-1.46 s** under the same solver; the
thresholds are `mu < sqrt(3) = 1.73` and `mu < 1`.  P111's closed forms
(`(2mu-1)s`, `2 mu s/(1.5+mu)`) both drop the projection, so they are 20-30 %
pessimistic on the 4-jaw and ~9 % optimistic on the 3-jaw - **both verdicts
survive, the 3-jaw's margin is just smaller than P111's paragraph implied**.
The registered **kill** (`delta_inf >= s` at the measured mu) **does not fire**
(0.915 worst), and the stiffness is a **window** because the cap saturates the
near pad first: `k` in [2.9e3, 3.8e3] N/m over the pool, the build takes 3300.

**The build** is one module change: `CAGE_KINDS = (cage4, cage3)`, three
azimuths, a 20 mm plate (the 120 deg neighbour bound is 22.5 mm at the closed
aperture), the same 60 mm length, the same 70 mm tool offset - and the **one
structural change the phase needed**: a hand-owned **aperture law**
(`CageHand.aperture_extent`).  A ring closes on one scalar, and which width it
takes decides whether it can load its pads: the four-pad ring takes the
**widest** horizontal extent (P107's own choice, and the reason its opposed pair
never loads), a three-pad ring must take the **narrowest of its own three pad
axes**.  The law is one `getattr` hook in `tasks.pinch_width`, and a hand that
states none keeps the shipped expression bit for bit.

**The fixture** (`logs/p112/fixture_cage3.py`, 390 closures in 18 sessions) is
the phase's decisive test and the phase's most expensive lesson: **three passive
supports failed**, each at the scale of the measurement itself - a static table, a
kinematic table and the shipped belt at 0 m/s all let a 0.1 kg payload sink 2 mm
and creep 4-5 mm **with zero pad force**, because `meshes.axis_extent` is the
undeformed profile and the **mesh is 2-6 % bigger**.  The adopted form sets the
scene's gravity to 0 and makes the closure a 2-D problem (it drops the support's
own `mu_b m g` term; stated, not hidden).  The result, at the delivered
configuration: **both rings centre** a 0-20 mm arrival to 0.5-1.9 mm (so P111's
line read of +0.2 mm was about the *delivery*, not the closure), and **only the
three-jaw loads its own pads**: `pads == 3` on **18/30** cells against
`pads == 4` on **2/30**.  The cost is measured too: the min-extent law
over-closes on the smallest fruit (`sep - dia` to **-7.9 mm** on a 29.6 mm
lychee, against the 4-pad's -1.8).

**The battery** (`PREREG.md` `77720306e9328cf6e7853427cbe41f94`; the scripted
single arm, 10 attempts, seeds 5/6/101/202 for the treatment and 5/6 for the
shipped control - D1/D2 in RESULTS section 7): **C 13/18 = 72.2 %, T 7/38 =
18.4 %**, Fisher p = 0.000, every seed negative - i.e. the three-jaw is *below*
even P111's rigid four-pad ring (19/76 = 25.0 %).  The **clean enclosure is 0 of
38**: the three rows that read `pads == 3` are all **jams** (`end > 15 mm`), the
same split P110 found at four pads.  The mechanism is now separated: `[cage]
off0` p50 3.2 mm with `off - off0` **+0.50 mm** - the ring does **not** centre on
the line, where the fixture says it does, because the payload arrives *moving*,
the close **freezes at its first contact** (holding an aperture `2 x delta` too
wide, and the seated legs' `force_min` p50 is **0.00 N**), and the 60 mm plates
block the descent (**`|v|max` 0.437** against the 0.160 budget, C 0.122).

**Verdict: NOT ADOPTED.**  The phase's honest sentence is that the two rings
differ exactly where the algebra said they would - the pad count - and that the
difference **does not reach the delivered count**, because the line never gives
the closure the clean arrival the centring needs.  The hardware price is a
**different assembly** (a scroll disc or three links driving three jaws on one
scalar, a new plate, three guides at 120 deg, the same 20 x 60 mm pads), and the
battery prices it at a 4x count deficit.  No `configs/` change, no reference
re-recorded.

Guards: selfcheck **PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)** with the new `P112 three-jaw
ring` leg (23 checks); acceptance with every knob unset **8/10,
`fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**; landing **7/7 T and 13/13 C**
payload-present `on_belt`; the budgets **fail on the treatment** (0.437) and were
not re-tuned.  Pins: `cage_hand.py` (the third kind, `CAGE_KINDS`,
`aperture_extent`, the three-pad `apertures`), `tasks.py` (the `CAGE_KINDS`
sites + the one `pinch_width` hook), `rl_env.py` (`TASKS_MD5` follow),
`scripts/258_p112_cage3_selftest.py`, `scripts/selfcheck.sh`; references
**`30fb99f8`** / **`30fb99f8`** / `8952c320` untouched.  Evidence `logs/p112/`.

### P113 - the end-effector decision book: the lane's close-out, written for a hardware partner (2026-11-04)

Design/document only: **no simulator, no `src/` change, no `configs/` change, no
commit into `src/`**. The deliverable is `docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md` - the
P104-P112 lane condensed into what a mechanical engineer who has never read this
repo can act on: the problem, the mechanism in two figures and their algebra, the
nine routes with their verdicts and prices, the three nails that are left with a
bench test and a kill each, and the recommendation with the decision tree. Every
number carries its `logs/` source and section; every unpriced item is marked
**unpriced**; no bench number is invented.

**Why a book and not another phase.** The lane closed with nine verdicts spread
over nine phase records, and a partner cannot read 60 phases. The book's job is
to make the *two* things that explain all nine legible, and to hand over the
three measurements that are actually left. Its spine is a single sentence: **the
pad geometry has been solved on a bench and the fruit presentation has not**, so
every purchase order placed today would buy the half that already works.

**The problem, as the book states it.** The shipped cell reads the acceptance
**8/10** and **28-29 of 40** placed per 40-attempt block (58/80 = 72.5 % at four
seeds, interval 10.59-12.16 s, `s/attempt` 9.5/9.1, 2.37-2.91 placed/min;
`[P92 CENSUS §3]`, `[P102 §2]`, `[P93]`). The 40-attempt census splits its **12
failures** into **9 loaded slides (75 %) + 3 never-held (25 %)** (`[P92 CENSUS
§3]`); the four-seed pool is 17 `cnp` of 22 (77 %) + 5 never-held
(`HAND_STAGE_PLAN §5.0`). The grasp is the term because the class is
**one-directional** (0 of 29 placed attempts carry a seated escape, P102), **not
the force** (2.2x then 6x, P41/P76/P77), **not the seat** (1.36-4.65 mm on 20/20
grips against a 104-276 mm walk, P42), and **is a creep at the operating load**
(the pinch slides 3.20-3.84 mm on the pear under the payload's own weight, P104
§5) - and it is bounded: 6 of P102's 11 failures are reachable, the 4 no-grasp
ones are 220-481 mm hand-over timing failures (P47/P48), so a perfect contact
fix is worth at most +15 points there, and every `cnp` converting is 75/80 =
93.8 % with the +8-point bar at 8 of 17 conversions.

**The two figures, and this is the phase's organising result.** *Figure 1, the
contact algebra*: `F_crit = n mu N`, ratio `n/2` and mu-free, measured 1.87-2.05x
for four contacts and 1.33-1.64x for three against the pinch's 11.03/14.21/12.69
N (P104 §3); the centring fixed point is `delta_inf = mu s` (four) and
`sqrt(3) mu s/(1.5 + (sqrt(3)/2) mu)` = 0.84-0.92 s (three) at the measured
pair friction **1.25-1.46**, with thresholds `mu < 1` and `mu < 1.73` and a
stiffness window `[2.9e3, 3.8e3]` N/m because the cap saturates the near pad
first (P111 §1, P112 §1). *Figure 2, the arrival geometry*: the descent starts
with the fruit **100.1 mm** upstream (`g0`; 83 mm of belt travel plus the 18 mm
margin), the band entry catches it still **55.8 mm along-belt / 2.6 mm lateral**
(92.5 % along-belt), the catch-up's tolerance is **6 mm**, the close-time offset
**3.4-4.5 mm**, and the ring needs **0.6 mm** (`[P108 §5]`, `[P109 §1.2]`,
`[P110 §1]`, `[P110 §3.2]`). **Both together explain every verdict**: a closure
change is worth 2x but the delivery denies it; a delivery change is the binding
term but no passive element reaches it.

**The nine routes, one line each** (route 0 is the shipped pinch baseline,
11.03/14.21/12.69 N and 3.20/0.85/2.68 mm creep): the **tactile** sees the slide
0.17-0.94 s early and a perfect detector converts 0 of 5 same-instance `cnp`s and
destroys 2 of 2 placements (detected, not convertible; $1,020); the
**anthropomorphic 3+1** mounts but its fingertips span 116-123 mm, so at most 3
of 4 touch a 37-66 mm payload, and its drive is a step function (wrong topology);
the **radial 4-pad** is worth 1.87-2.05x static and 9-15x in creep and places
3/17 on the line (the shape is right, the line cannot place it); the **wide
aperture** is decisive for the approach (`clr < 0` 32/51 -> 4/57, p = 1.4e-8) and
a draw for the count (p = 0.37, the fresh seed reversing it) - a precondition,
not a rate; the **wider supply spacing** costs 1 -> 5 starved slots of 20 and the
placements (unaffordable); the **descent margin** is load-bearing (`past_aim`
0/76 -> 79/79, acceptance 8/10 -> 4/10); the **metering gate** holds 16/16 at
every height 8-45 mm and is 3-29x too coarse for the ring, and the queue costs it
(1.8 -> 4.9 mm, 1/16 expelled); the **compliant closure** is a gentler jam (force
at the freeze 4.90 -> 0.6-1.8 N, no centring, count n.s.); the **three-jaw**
centres a clean arrival to 0.5-1.9 mm and loads its own pads 18/30 against 2/30,
and the battery is 18.4 % against 72.2 % because the delivery defeats it.

**The three nails left, with the bench test and the kill each.** (i) **a pad with
`mu_pair < 1`** - the only term the algebra leaves standing: measure the pair
friction at the working normal force and the **creep at the operating load**
(0.75 s settle - *not* a 5 N/s ramp), report the axial break beside it; kill on
`mu >= 1` or creep > 1.0 mm; **a printed part** (the fingers are replaceable; the
bench needs no sensor, unpriced). (ii) **the 3-jaw on a moving presentation** -
static centring 0-20 mm then a **0.12 m/s** arrival; kill on `off - off0 > 0`, on
fewer than 2 pads loaded at the freeze, or on a descent over `abs(v)max` 0.160;
**a machined assembly**, unpriced. (iii) **a stationary presentation** - the
gate's hold under a queue (1.8 -> 4.9 mm, 1/16 expelled) plus the magazine's
re-handover residual against **0.6 mm**; kill on > 0.6 mm on more than 1 of 20;
**a station change** (new collider set, selection rule, pick mode, a magazine,
both references and every store re-baselined), unpriced.

**The recommendation.** Buy nothing before nail (i); it is one reprinted pad and
it has a hard kill. Then (ii) - the only test that separates the jaw from the
delivery, which the record already names as the delivery (P112 §4.5). Then (iii)
only if both pass, because it is a station change and a full re-baseline. No
end-effector route measured ships a better rate alone; what would is the pair
**ring + nest**, and the legitimate alternative is to keep the pinch and accept
that 75-77 % of the failures sit in a class this line cannot let any hand reach.
**The never-re-try list** (one line each, with the number) is the force family,
the seat, the clearance pre-pose, the place-station move, the profile blocks, the
candidate planning, the park return, the fail-fast, the tactile reflex, the
closure depth and the aperture/spacing as a rate lever - plus, as "also closed",
the pad face shapes, the scoop, the finger-tip shortening and the supply band's
top.

**Guards.** `python3 scripts/106_index_audit.py` -> **OK: every index matches the
files it describes**; `scripts/selfcheck.sh` -> **PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)**;
`git status --short` on `src/` and `configs/` is empty. No motion reference was
read or written; P113 touches only `docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md` and this
entry. Pins: `scripts/selfcheck.sh` re-run on the final tree; the book's own
sources are the P104-P112 records, `logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md`, `logs/p92/CENSUS.md`,
`logs/p93/RESULTS.md`, `logs/p102`, `logs/p103` and `logs/r8/A_RESULTS.md`, with
`docs/PLATFORM_SURVEY.md` and `docs/HAND_STAGE_PLAN.md` for the prices and the
milestone arithmetic. Evidence `docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md`, this entry.

## P114 (2026-11-05) - the cell is portable as data: a scenario descriptor, an instruction resolver and a capability map; nothing ships

**The requirement is a system one, not a physics one**: the two-finger-gripper
cell must be portable to different pipeline scenarios, and it must decide where
to put each fruit **from an instruction** ("它要可以根据指示自己判断把果蔬分拣放到什么
位置"). The physics/end-effector lane is closed (`docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md`);
this phase is the software architecture, and it ships **no default change, no
`configs/` reference and no flip**. The one new `configs/` file is
`configs/scenarios/shipped_twoline.json`, the shipped cell written as data - the
reference descriptor the loader and the replay validation need.

**The coupling audit first** (`logs/p114/COUPLING.md`, every site read with its
file:line, four groups). (i) geometry: the pick station (`assets.py:251-253`),
the two-line stations (`tasks.py:10499`, `0.0 / -0.10`) and their per-batch
pre-pose solve (`:10240-10340`), the main belt (`assets.py:210-229`), the two
output belts (`:315`, `:334`, `conveyor.OutputBelt:507-560`), the release points
(`:412-416`, derived `:545-548`), the tray (`:438-450`, `:692`). (ii) the rule:
`bin_index = 0 if grade == "A" else 1` in **four** drivers
(`rl_env.py:3529`, `20_pick_place.py:270`, `40_collect_demos.py:755`,
`60_eval_policy.py:219`), the arm from `bin_index` (`tasks.py:11947`), the
grade-pure selector (`:9251-9290`, `_reach_anywhere_select :9852`), the worker
passing its own lane (`:10871`, `:10995`), the cross-lane reselect
(`:13097`). (iii) the supply: mixes (`fruits.py:261-269`), band
(`:253-254`), gap schedule (`:225-250`, `SupplyPlan.from_env :436`), the pool
and its drawn labels (`:1057`, `:1152`). (iv) the calibration: the waypoint
seeds and `_grasp_quat` (`tasks.py:4082-4140`), `jaw_target` and `_place_low`
(`:4987-5080`, `:16204`), the motion references. **The two hardest**:
**arm = grade = lane** is one object written in four places, so the arm that can
carry a fruit is decided before the fruit is seen; and **the place target is
derived from the place leg's *name*** (`jaw_target`'s
`index = 0 if "0" in name else 1`), so there is nowhere a "destination with its
own target" can exist.

**What was built, default off.** `src/fruit_sorting/scenario.py` (new, pure data,
no simulator): a strict descriptor loader (`FRUIT_SCENARIO=<path>`; unknown keys,
duplicate ids, a side/target y-sign contradiction, an unknown reach status or
supply schedule all raise), an instruction parser/resolver
(`FRUIT_SORT_INSTRUCTION=<path|inline>`; ordered `condition => destination`
rules, `skip`, sizes in mm, first match wins, `default` last), and the capability
map (`left` serves `+y`, `right` serves `-y`, and only if the destination's
reach is not refused). In `tasks.py`: `_place_xy_for` replaces the name→lane
read at the place leg; `_calibrate_sort_destinations` solves every `auto`
destination with the place leg's own position-only IK and a 25 mm bar; the
selectors admit a fruit only if `destination in capability[its arm]`
(`_sort_admits`); the worker dispatches the fruit's own destination
(`sort_destination(state)`); `_arm_for_destination` maps it back to the one arm
that can serve it; `_sort_ledger_*` prints one `[sort]` row per attempt and a
per-destination summary. `SceneConfig`/`SupplyPlan` apply the descriptor's
geometry/supply as **defaults** (an explicit env knob wins). The single-arm
driver and the collector consult `sort_destination`; the direct/policy env and
the hybrid canary **refuse** the knob (no dispatcher - honest, not silent). The
one structural bug the validation caught is recorded: the first draft kept the
per-attempt destination in a shared task attribute, and the two-line's two
workers let one arm's ledger read the other arm's value (a grade-B peach read
`dest=0` on the right); the fix is an attempt-local `EpisodeResult` field plus a
thread-local place target - a direct instance of this file's own
"instrumentation is part of the measurement" rule.

**The validation** (`logs/p114/RESULTS.md`, endpoint = the ledger's assignment
accuracy, never a rate). **(i) Default off**: `scripts/accept.sh` is **8/10,
9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches` `30fb99f8`, `190: PASS`**, and its **421
`[fruit]` lines are 421/421 byte-identical** to `logs/p110/accept_noharm.log`
(md5 `1ac8febe...`, no `[sort]`/`[scenario]` row at all). **(ii) Today's routing
as an instruction** (`grade=A => 0`, `B => 1`, `C => skip`): 8/10, the **same
`[fruit]` stream 421/421 with the `[sort]` rows dropped** (`compare_off_vs_
today.txt`), `fingerprint: matches` - the compiled predicate *is* the shipped
grade-pure predicate. **(iii-b) A size-class rule on the shipped geometry**
(`size<40 => 1`, `default => 0`): coverage `mapped=16 (dest0=12, dest1=4)`, 7/10
placed and **7/7 releases in the instructed destination, 0 mis-sorted**; a
grade-C 3.6 cm strawberry goes to the **right** lane and a grade-A kiwi to the
left, i.e. the destination is independent of the grade; the branch differs from
the reference (fingerprint DIFFERS by construction) and the budgets pass
(`|v|max` 0.114/0.160, lurch 0.018/0.291). **(iii-a) The 3-destination cell**:
`three_dest.json` adds `dest 2 = (0.38, +0.55)` on the +Y belt with `reach:
auto`; the startup solve reads **6.0 mm** and the map becomes `left=[0,2]
right=[1]`; the instruction `grade=A => 2`, `grade=B => 1` (no default) leaves
the 4 grade-C fruit **unassigned** (never selected) and 20 attempts split 10/10;
**13 releases, 13/13 in the instructed destination** (dest 1 7/7, dest 2 6/6),
0 mis-sorted, budgets pass (`|v|max` 0.110/0.160). The two targets are 71 mm
apart and the measured release clouds ~78 mm apart, every payload 26-32 mm
nearer its own target. **(iv) The refusal**: the tray destination
`(1.65, +0.50)` solves to **1138.3 mm** against the 25 mm bar, prints
`UNREACHABLE`, and the run aborts with `ScenarioError("[sort] REFUSED: ... no
arm can deliver there")` **before the first attempt** - zero attempts, zero
mis-sorts.

**Verdict: portable as data, and the instruction layer works; nothing ships.**
The price of a new pipeline is **a JSON + a solve + the gate** (previously 6-8
code sites across four drivers and the task, plus a re-solve). Still not
portable and named: a third **physical** lane/tray (a scene build - the
descriptor can only add a target on an existing lane), a place destination at a
different height (needs a per-destination z and its own descent), the
tactile/force channels and the hand's own limits, and **perception**: colour is
not a per-instance attribute in the sim and grade/ripeness/defective are drawn
labels, so the instruction layer is exact for species/size and a *labelling
interface* for the rest until a classifier feeds it. Named next steps: the vision
attribute source, a per-destination height / third belt, the policy-side
dispatcher, and an overlap station (P90 measured the shipped place point at the
corner of the solvable box). No motion reference moved or was re-recorded
(`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` stand). Pins: `scenario.py` **`674194fe`**,
`tasks.py` **`15d2348a`**, `assets.py` **`165328af`**, `fruits.py` **`e807216c`**,
`rl_env.py` **`476d5782`** (`TASKS_MD5` follow), `20_pick_place.py`

## P115 (2026-11-05) - the instruction becomes an operator tool: `and` terms, the firing rule in the ledger, and a strict coverage guard

P114 left the instruction layer mechanically complete and operationally thin:
one attribute per rule, and an instruction that forgot a case dropped fruit
silently (the coverage count printed only after the first attempt). P115 closes
both, default off, with the shipped cell unchanged.

**What was built.** (1) `and` conjoins up to three attribute terms in one rule
(`species=apple and size>=66 => 1`); every term must match, `or` stays written
as more rules because the first match wins. `Rule` gains `terms` and keeps the
P114 `key`/`op`/`value` as the first term, so the `260` leg's assertions are
unchanged. (2) The decision is legible: an armed run prints one
`[sort] rule N: <text> (arm X)` row per rule, and each `[sort] attempt` row gains
`rule=<n>` - the 1-based firing rule, `default` included - which is what makes
an `and` rule auditable; without it "why did this apple go right?" is a guess.
(3) `FRUIT_SORT_STRICT=1` turns an **unmatched** fruit into a startup refusal
before the first attempt, naming what it dropped; a deliberate `skip` stays
allowed (a decision is not an oversight). Four canonical files now live in
`configs/instructions/` (`shipped_grade`, `by_size`, `species_split`,
`compound`), and the `261` selfcheck leg (54 checks) pins the grammar, the
precedence, every refusal, the four files and the `tasks.py` shape of the table
and the guard.

**What was measured.** The shipped scripted two-line, one claim per run, the
endpoint the ledger's assignment accuracy - never a rate. **Unset**: 8/10,
`fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`, its **421 `[fruit]` lines 421/421
byte-identical** to `logs/p110/accept_noharm.log`; every new print and read is
inside `if self._instruction is not None`. **Compound** (`species=apple and
size>=66 => 1`, `size<45 => 1`, `default => 0`, 20 attempts): coverage
`pool=16 mapped=16 unassigned=0`, 12 releases, **12/12 = 100 % in the instructed
destination, 0 mis-sorted**; the per-rule histogram reads **rule 1 1/1/1, rule 2
8/6/6, rule 3 11/5/5**, and the witness is attempt 16 - `apple 7.0cm grade=C
arm=right rule=1 dest=1 in_dest=1`, i.e. a **grade-C apple on the right belt**,
which the shipped grade routing can never produce. **Strict** (`"grade=A => 0"`
+ `=1`): `ScenarioError("[sort] REFUSED: FRUIT_SORT_STRICT=1 but the instruction
leaves 10 of 16 fruit unassigned (lychee 34mm grade C, strawberry 37mm grade B,
apple 65mm grade B, pear 61mm grade B, ...)")` from
`PickAndPlaceTask.__init__` before `go_ready` - zero attempts. **No rate is
claimed**: 12/20 is a branch (the family's seed-6 controls read 12/20 in
`logs/p92/C6.log` and 10/20 in `logs/p80/T6.log`), and the routing changes which
arm sees which fruit, not a grasp parameter. The compound branch's motion
budgets pass (worst descent `|v|max` 0.1210 vs 0.160-0.161, lurch 0.036 vs
0.291; carry cones reported).

**Read rule.** When a rule carries `and`, quote the **per-rule histogram**
(`python3 logs/p115/p115_report.py --ledger <log>`), not just the destination
totals - the destination is no longer one-to-one with a rule. And use
`FRUIT_SORT_STRICT=1` whenever a dropped fruit would be a defect rather than a
decision.
