## P116 (2026-11-06) - "A-grade left, apples right": the overlap is real, the plan tool shows it, and the cell proves the precedence

The owner's example is two rules with a **non-empty intersection**: an A-grade
apple satisfies `grade=A => left` *and* `species=apple => right`. The runtime
resolves that by **precedence** (first match wins) - correct, but until now
invisible: the ledger said `dest=0`, never "rule 1 beat rule 2". P116 makes the
conflict visible **before** a run and adds the operator that removes it.

**The plan/lint tool** (`scripts/262_sort_plan.py`, offline, no simulator):
evaluates an instruction over the cell's own attribute space (species x 5
diameters x 3 grades = 120 cells from `SceneConfig`, ripeness/defective only
when a rule names them) and prints the rule table with each destination's arm,
every **overlap pair** (the earlier rule wins, with the count and an example
fruit), the **partition** per destination and the cells that match no rule.
`--strict-overlap` exits 1 on any overlap, so an instruction library can be
linted in CI. Measured on the owner's sentence in its three readings: literal
order **40/10/70** (dest0/dest1/skip, overlap 5 cells, rule 1 wins), apples
first **35/15/70** (same pair, winner flipped), and the unambiguous form with
the new **`!=`** operator (`species=apple and grade!=A`) **40/10/70 with
OVERLAP: none**. `!=` is what lets an operator write "the rest of the apples"
without depending on rule order.

**Live cell** (the shipped scripted two-line, `FRUIT_SUPPLY_SPECIES=apple` so
every attempt is an apple and the overlap actually occurs, the literal
instruction, 10 attempts): **8/10 placed**, **8/8 released payloads in the
instructed destination (100 %), 0 mis-sorted**; per rule **1 = 5/5/5**, **2 =
5/3/3**; the witness is **five A-grade apples sent LEFT** (`rule=1 dest=0`) with
non-A apples right (`rule=2 dest=1`) - exactly the precedence the linter
printed. No rate claim: 8/10 is one branch of the apple-only cell (the mixed
pool reads 28-29/40 at the same seeds).

**Architecture note for "give it a sentence".** The instruction layer is a
deterministic **rule compiler**, not a language model: an LLM (or a template)
would emit the DSL; the **linter is the gate** (overlap, unreachable
destination, unknown attribute/species/grade, uncovered fruit); the executor
stays deterministic and replayable. That is the safe place to put a language
front-end - it can propose, it cannot bypass refusal. The policy line still
refuses `FRUIT_SORT_INSTRUCTION` (`rl_env.py:1708`); threading a destination
through the policy handover is the named next phase.

Pins: `scenario.py` **`662369aa`**, `262_sort_plan.py` **`d510cb1e`**,
`261_p115_instruction_selftest.py` **`10bd9faa`** (63 checks), `selfcheck.sh`
**`92e65259`**, the three instruction files **`1ad67958` / `5ffbfdb2` /
`0d4df6a2`**; references `30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` untouched;
selfcheck PASS, `106` OK, `107` PASS.

## P117 - the scene, fixture-first: the pad face and the friction close, the station pocket promotes

The owner's directive: *keep raising the sorting speed and success rate, and if the
limit is the simulation scene, change or improve the scene.*  That is a new
authorisation - every earlier phase treated the scene as fixed (a reference per
scenario) - and this phase spends it on the record's three unspent scene candidates:
the pad's face (the 75 % loaded-slide class), the pad's friction, and the
presentation (the 25 % acquisition class + the descent).  Fixture-first, because this
project's fixtures have lied twice (P107/P112: a passive support let a 0.1 kg
payload sink 2 mm and creep 4-5 mm with zero pad force).  Registered in
`logs/p117/PREREG.md` (md5 `5caae5d2`, pinned at 04:34:54Z before any cell).
**Nothing adopted; no `src/`, `configs/` or default change; no reference re-recorded.**

**First, the record's contradiction, because it changes what this phase is.** The
brief says the concave/V face "has never been tested".  It has: `FRUIT_FINGER_FACE`
(`v`/`h`/`x`/`c` additive, `v2`/`h2`/`x2` recessed, `p` plate; `scene._add_contact_faces`)
and `FRUIT_FINGER_MU` both exist and the `logs/p3face` phase measured them.  Read
against its **own** flat control the recessed `h2` is a **draw** (6/10 vs 6/10) and
`v2`/`x2` are worse (3/10, 1/10); against the later `flat + k30` arm (7/10) all are
worse; `FRUIT_FINGER_MU=8` "re-ejected A4" (a *close* event).  What that phase never
measured is the **creep at the operating load**, and its rate was taken at the
**pre-P41 force** (4.42 N delivered).  So P117 is a re-test at the shipped 9.75-9.9 N
with a different endpoint - not a first test - and the report says so.

**Fixture 1 - the pad face** (`logs/p117/fixture.py`): P104's rig, one app session,
28 pad pairs on one bench, 84 cells, 182 s.  The profiles are `flat` (control),
`arc06`/`arc09` (a semicircular groove of **0.6 r / 0.9 r of that fruit**, so the
padding is per fruit by construction), `v90` (a 90 deg V) and `cradle90` (the same V
with its valley across the pad - **the only face whose contact normal has an axial
component**, i.e. the only "cup wall" the brief names), plus `flat_mu3`/`flat_mu4`.
Each pad face is a polyline and each facet is one convex box (a concave profile
cannot be one convex hull), and the **closure is computed**: `contact_travel` finds
the first contact from the fixture's own polyline and each cell closes
5 mm past it (P104's interference), so a groove closes **6.1 mm (`arc06`) / 17.1 mm
(`arc09`) deeper** on the pear - without that it grips nothing, because the rim sits
further from the jaw axis than the fruit's surface at that offset.  **A1's support
proof** took three tries and the smoke log is the record: a *free* payload under a
compensated weight drifts 27.25 mm in 40 ticks (`apply_forces` lands one tick late
relative to the position integration), with the velocity pinned the same cell reads
**0.0000 mm**, and the un-compensated cell falls **613 mm** - so the compensation is
exact, the read is exact, and the cell is not a frozen world.  A2: all 28 pairs load
**2 pads at 4.54-4.99 N** of the 4.90 cap, so every profile is measured at the same
delivered normal force.

**The result is a clean negative on both pad candidates.**  Flat's creep (the total
walk from the release through the 0.75 s `m(g+5.83)` hold) is **8.62 / 9.07 / 0.98 /
12.42 mm** and its sustained break-away **9.78 / 13.33 / 13.24 / 11.06 N** (pear /
orange / strawberry / lychee; P104's pear 3.20 mm and 11.03 N reproduce in class).
**No groove reduces the pear's creep** - `arc06` **1.58x**, `arc09` **1.93x**, `v90`
**2.89x**, `cradle90` **1.56x** - and every groove is **0.62-0.76x worse on the
pear's break-away**, the opposite of the `n mu N` prediction.  On the round fruits the
grooves do help (orange/lychee 1.22-2.20x), so the effect is **fruit-shape
dependent**: the pear's lobes turn a groove into a wedge *out*.  The one cell that
beats flat anywhere is `cradle90` on the orange (**0.72x**) and it is 1.56x worse on
the pear - a wash, and A3 requires both.  The strawberry is unreadable as a ratio
(its flat base is **0.98 mm**) and the small fruit's grooves are bistable
(`cradle90` strawberry 4.72-16.81 mm), the same seat-bistability P104 §3 found on the
pear.  **The mu ladder raises the capacity and not the creep**: pear break-away 9.78
-> **14.32** (mu3) -> **14.20** (mu4) = 1.45-1.46x and orange 13.33 -> **17.96** ->
**23.33** = 1.35-1.75x, while the pear creep goes 8.62 -> 8.38 -> **8.21 mm**
(-2.8 % / -4.8 %).  **A6 fires: the creep is not friction-limited, and the friction
lane is dead.**

**And the phase corrects P104's own endpoint.**  P104's "creep at the operating
load" is **lateral**: its row reads `settle 3.20mm (dx=-3.20 dy=-0.02 dz=+0.02)` and
its pads close along x, so the 3.20 mm is a **seat shift along the jaw axis, not a
slide along the load** - and this fixture reproduces the shape with the **load-axis
component `dz = -0.05..+0.28 mm` in all 28 cells**, the whole 3-25 mm walk being
lateral.  **At 1.66 N the shipped pinch does not creep along the load; it re-seats
across it.**  That is why the `cnp` class is not a static-creep deficit and why the
force family (P76/P78: 1.45-2x capacity, 2x creep ratio) never converted one - and it
means the class is the **dynamic** event P75 traced (the pads driven to their 98.1 mm
stop while the payload walks out), not a static one.  No face and no mu can reach it.

**Fixture 2 - the station pocket** (`logs/p117/fixture_station.py`).  The brief's
form is "a diverter takes one fruit off the moving belt into a pocket beside it", and
the record refutes that **by arithmetic before a build**: the delivered x is
**0.188-0.397** (P49/P60) and the top-down grip band is **x <= 0.320 clean with
x = 0.398 failing at 32.8 mm / 17.0 deg** (P66's 150-cell sweep), so a pocket outside
the stream is outside the reach - an empty intersection.  The only pickable pocket is
one **under** the line, which is also the only form that gives the descent back the
**40-90 mm** it loses to the conveyor (`logs/166` 23 cm free vs `logs/167` 3.8 cm with
the belt).  Built: the shipped belt's own authoring (kinematic body +
`PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI`, `belt_friction` 0.9, -0.120 m/s, never stopped) split into
two segments with a **0.148 m** gap, a **belt-like shutter** filling it (a *static*
plate drags a fruit to a stop in `v^2/(2 mu g)` = 0.6 mm, so the shutter must be
driven), and a **100 mm** deep pocket.  The depth is **forced**: the shutter must
close *over* the occupant, so `depth >= 0.020 + 69.6` = 89.6 mm -> 100 mm - and it is
also the descent's missing 40-90 mm.

**Three build lessons, each measured and kept as evidence.**  (1)
`PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI` is in the **collider's scaled local frame**
(`conveyor._surface_attr_speed`): an un-divided command carried the 0.726 m upstream
segment at **0.087 m/s** and the 0.148 m shutter at **0.018 m/s**; `speed / y_length`
gives **0.120 m/s = 1.00x** (`st_plate.log` vs `st_plate3.log`).  (2) **A flush
shutter is not optional**: `set_world_poses(z = bz)` (the *slab's* centre) put its top
20 mm low, the fruit rested 19 mm down in the step and the stream stopped dead
(`st_plate2.log`).  (3) The **door-clearance predicate must be geometric, not a
radius**: the occupant sits 70-90 mm down, *inside* a 0.09 m radius, so
`far_from_gap(<0.09)` refuses to close once the fruit is in the pocket; the predicate
is now "no fruit whose top is above the shutter's underside and whose y is inside the
mouth".

**B1's deviation is the phase's honest limit.**  The registered 0.05 mm support bar
is **below this sim's contact-jitter floor**: the pocket floor's drift is **0.364 /
0.261 / 0.518 / 0.635 mm at 200/400/800/1200 ticks** - non-monotone, i.e. jitter,
not creep - while a fruit **riding the driven belt** deviates **0.018-0.382 mm** from
a straight line over the same window (same fruit, same session).  P107/P112's failure
was a 2 mm sink plus 4-5 mm *monotone* creep, 5-8x this floor.  So the pocket is
judged **against the belt it sits beside**, and the 0.05 mm bar is recorded as
unattainable on this physics.  The 5.58 mm "settle" is the pear **rolling onto a
flatter side** on the flat floor (a centre drop), not penetration.

**The station table.**  **16/16** of the pool end in the pocket, **0/16 expelled**,
hold **0.000-0.024 mm**; the **closed** shutter passes **4/4 at 1.875 s AND 4/4 at
0.833 s** at **1.00x** the belt speed; one drop plus **3/3 followers pass at both
cadences** with the occupant holding **0.019 / 0.008 mm**; the shutter's **open window
is 0.54-0.64 s** against the 0.833 s fast cadence (a 0.19-0.29 s margin, measured).
The landing x spans **-58.7..+29.5 mm (88 mm)** and its y -49.9..+41.0 mm, so the
0.352 m mouth **does not centre** the fruit: the pocket removes the **moving
handover** and the **descent's blocked boundary**, but **not** P48/P49's delivered-x
tail.  A centring floor (a V) is the named next element and is not built.

**Verdict.**  The pad face and the pad friction **do not promote** (A3 fails, A6
fires) - and the shipped knobs already existed, so nothing is added.  The station
pocket **promotes to a station build** (a scenario change, not a knob) on two
**named, unspent gates**: a **static IK probe at the 100 mm-lower pick pose** (the
jaw lands at ~`belt_top`, the pads' distal plane at `floor + 0.5 mm` - geometrically
favourable, unmeasured), and the shutter's **actuation path** (the fixture teleports
it; only its timing is measured).  A station build owes both motion references, every
store and the acceptance re-baseline by this file's own rule, and is out of scope
here.

No-harm: `scripts/accept.sh` with every knob unset reads **8/10, 9.0 s/attempt,
`fingerprint: matches configs/motion_reference.json`, `190: PASS`**, and its **421
`[fruit]` lines are 421/421 byte-identical** to `logs/p110/accept_noharm.log`;
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` **PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)**, `106` **OK**, `107` **PASS
(21 checks)**; `git status --short src configs` is empty.

unreachable destination is refused by P114's map; the handoff presentation still

## P122 (2026-11-06) - the destination spacing, measured: 50 mm along x (calibrated), never a diagonal, and a destination is a physical body

Owner's pick (1): the destination-separation spec, offline. Built from **133
measured releases** across P114/P115/P116/P121 (`logs/p122/spacing.py`).

**The offset**: `release - commanded jaw target` = **+48 mm in x, +-35..37 mm in
y** systematic (the payload hanging from the jaw along the tool axis, P90's own
geometry), plus random **sd 6-9 mm (x)** and **6-17 mm (y)**. The systematic is
the same for two zones served by the same leg, so it **cancels only if the
comparison is calibrated**; compared raw, a payload commanded 50 mm upstream
lands 2 mm from the downstream neighbour's target.

**The separation curve** (bootstrap, 20 000 draws): calibrated **x 50 mm =
0/20 000** (30-40 mm 1.5 %); raw 50 mm = **33 %**; the **(50,50) diagonal =
2.11 %**, which is P121's observed **1/23 = 4.3 %** on the same pools. The x axis
is the good one; the y axis carries the 17 mm spread.

**The correction**: `conveyor._build_discharge` builds **one tray per belt**
(`center=(tx, by, ...)`), so P114/P121's `three_dest` target `(0.38, +0.55)` sits
on the **same +y belt and the same tray** as lane 0 - an **attribution demo, not
a third destination**. The cell physically has **two** destinations. A real third
is bound by the **place reach** (P90: x 0.38-0.48, |y| 0.35-0.55; the slab is
|y| 0.425-0.675), so it is a **station solve + scene build**, not a spacing
number - and the owner's "dynamic only" constraint permits it (a third belt
downstream stops nothing).

**Named software half**: the ledger's `nearest` is **uncalibrated** (it compares
the payload to the jaw target) - that *is* the three-dest mis-sort. A calibrated
ledger (report `release - target - mean`, classify against `target + mean`) turns
P121's 2 % into ~0 %.

No `src/`, `configs/` or reference change; no store re-baselined.

## P123 - the third output destination is built, and its payloads land in its own tray

Owner's item 2 (P122's "a third destination needs a third output body"). Default off
(`FRUIT_OUTPUT_LANES=3`), nothing adopted, no `configs/` reference moved.

**The free space, from the stage's own bounds** (`logs/p123/survey.txt`): the pedestal
is `x -0.300..+0.100, y +-0.350, top 0.790`; the main belt `x 0.085..0.595, y +-0.864,
z..1.215`; each output body `x 0.025..1.950`, its **slab** `x 0.100..1.200,
|y| 0.425..0.675, z 1.300..1.350`, legs `x 0.0255..0.0755 / 1.100..1.150`, chute
`x 1.196..1.388, |y| 0.418..0.682`, tray `x 1.350..1.950, |y| 0.380..0.720, floor
0.900..0.920, rim 1.060`. At the output deck the free bands are **|y| 0.000..0.425
(inboard, in reach)** and **|y| > 0.675 (outboard, outside P90's box)** - and of the
inboard band only `|y| 0.28-0.40 at x >= 0.48` is both reachable and clear of the place
transits.

**The candidates, priced offline before any body** (`layout.py` -> `layout.txt`):
**A** inboard on -Y with the slab **x-offset downstream** (0.480..1.200) - **passes**
(place in the reach box; delivered 48/59 mm inside the 0.115 m slab = 7-8 sd; **no
transit crosses it** because the payload, radius included, is at x 0.469 when it passes
the band; 0 cm^2 of new camera occlusion, the body being downstream of the fruit's
x band 0.148..0.413); **B** split the -Y belt in two - the reach passes at both places
but the transits cross (**-9 mm** predicted direct-low `clr`) -> kill; **C** outboard -
`NAT` 41-108 mm at |y| 0.65, bodies overlap -> kill. The x-offset is what makes an
inboard body free: inboard bodies lose **0.30 mm/mm** of direct-low-lift clearance
(P90 `COST.md`), 44 mm for this band.

**The reach is measured** (`probe.txt`/`probe_rows.json`, P90's `NAT`, 160 cells,
93/160 pass): the band passes at **x 0.43-0.48** (res 5.6-6.0 mm, pads +49..+56 left /
+63..+70 right over the new slab, margins 0.42-0.49 rad) and **x = 0.38 fails**
(8.2-8.4 mm) - a hard inboard-x edge. The chosen cell `(0.48, -0.30)`: **6.0 mm /
+0.457 rad / +70.2 mm / 92.7 deg** at the place height, **6.0 / +143 / 100.5** at the
transfer; the live startup solve reads **11.5 mm** against the descriptor's 25 mm bar
(the shipped lanes' `verified` is 14.9 mm).

**The build** is one table (`output_lane_layout`) feeding the builder, the scene, the
belt/tray/discharge tests, the drop points and the manifest. With 3 lanes: belt
`x 0.480..1.200, |y| 0.280..0.395`, top 1.350 (same plate/speed/friction/surface
velocity/discharge), **its own chute (0.10 m) and its own tray (0.60 x 0.14 m,
|y| 0.260..0.400)**, and the shipped -Y tray narrows 0.34 -> 0.20 m (50 mm of air); 30 mm
to the -Y belt, 16 mm between chutes. `scene.output_lanes` names 2 or 3 bodies in the
manifest. Destination 2 is a P114 descriptor entry (`reach: auto`) and the capability
map keeps its physical meaning: `-y` -> the **right** arm (`left=[0] right=[1,2]`).

**The cell** (20 attempts, the shipped two-line, both seeds, P92's four instruments):
**seed 5 17 -> 11, seed 6 12 -> 14** (pooled **29/40 -> 25/40**, Fisher **p = 0.19**, the
sign flipping) - so the count is a branch and nothing is claimed for it. The endpoints:
**25/25 payload-present releases landed in their instructed destination** across the two
treatment cells (`in_destination=25, mis_sorted=0`), and the **tray census agrees 25/25**

`clean_slip >= 8 mm`), the closed loaded-slide class, and the two attempts that reached
the place leg both landed in tray 2.

**A measured correction to the release offset**: `release - commanded` is
**(+50..60, +-30) mm on the shipped lanes but (+20..30, -10..-20) mm on the new lane** -
the offset is `0.070 x tool_axis` and the new pose's attitude differs (tilt 90 vs

lands 20-30 mm inside its upstream edge - but that is **2.5-4 sd, not 8**; the one
number a future form should widen (belt upstream end to x 0.46), on n = 2 releases here.

**Guards**: 11/11 and 14/14 payload-present releases on a belt; the descent budgets PASS

+76 / +69 mm, `clr_edge` min +75 / +70 mm** (controls +57 / +73) - the new body is never
the binding surface; **no new failure-reason key**; the crush proxy fails its -15 mm

after the payload left (P76 A1/A3, P100 A4: recorded, not re-read). **No-harm**: the

`selfcheck.sh` PASS (the new `P123 output lanes` leg), `106` OK, `107` PASS.

**Read rules**: a destination is a **tray** - quote the tray census and the ledger, never
a target proximity; the place reach is the gate and it is **per-side**; an x-offset body
is only free while the payload's downstream offset **plus its radius** stays upstream of

## P125 (2026-11-07) - the three-lane recollection: a null, and a correction to P124's canary reading

The owner's decision was to recollect the policy on the three-lane scene so the
third destination could ship. The precondition P124 named was "collect with
`FRUIT_OUTPUT_LANES=3`, fine-tune, then the same canary at or above the 2-lane
control". The store and the checkpoint were built; **the canary does not reach
the bar, the default stays 2, and the phase's product is that the three-lane
"collapse" does not reproduce.**

### The store

`datasets/p125_three_lane` (local, gitignored): **196 episodes from 8 shard
directories**, 288 attempts, collected by the shipped two-line collector with
`FRUIT_OUTPUT_LANES=3` as the only scene change (camera 240,424, wave +
balanced A:B:C, 17-success processes, sequential shards with a fresh directory
per retry).

| shard | seeds | episodes |
|---|---|---|
| `s0` / `_r2` / `_r3` | 501 / 502 / 503 | 19 / 30 / 28 |
| `s1` / `_r2` | 601 / 602 | 20 / 35 |
| `s2` / `_r2` / `_r3` | 701 / 702 / 703 | 28 / 17 / 19 |

96 left / 100 right, grade A 96 / B 100 (C skipped by the pure routing),
**36,414 windows**, `index_md5` **`38ec3a12`**. **Every shard's
`scene.output_lanes` has 3 entries** (lane 2 `/World/OutputBelt2`, belt centre
`(0.84,-0.3375,1.325)`, place `(0.48,-0.30)`, tray `(1.65,-0.33)`) - the
provenance a pre-P123 store cannot carry. **No wedge and no soft-watchdog
skip**: all 8 runs exit 0, `gate_open=0.0 s`. A 5-episode three-lane smoke
(`datasets/p125_smoke`, seed 499) proved the manifest before the spend.

### The fine-tune

`moe_v12` (`3a9ccfc0`, the `accept_policy.sh` default) ->
`checkpoints/p125_three_lane` (`69a468d0`): 6 epochs, lr 5e-5, `ones`, base
`datasets/demos_v11` (50 episodes / 9,378 windows), batch 32, seed 0.
Weighted loss 0.058005 -> **0.025210**, router accuracy 0.8234 -> **0.9833**,
demo_val 0.018226. The candidate learned the store (P33's 180-episode store read
0.0245), so the canary null below is not an undertrained checkpoint.

### The correction

that a same-batch control shows to be a draw - a scene decision needs the

term on this interface is the pick-station grip class, not the scene.

## P129 (2026-11-07) - the pad material is not the ring's lever: a four-jaw centres at the measured friction, and the freeze is what denies it

The decision book's nail (i) (`docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md` section 4.1): a pad
whose **pair** friction with the fruit is below 1, bench first.  Two fixtures in
`logs/`, **no `src/` or `configs/` change**, no cell: the phase is killed on its
own K2.

**The algebra, re-derived** (`logs/p129/algebra.py`).  A round payload's four-pad
residual is **`mu s`**: the perpendicular pair's penetration is `s` at any offset
(the plane's distance from the centre does not depend on the tangential offset),
so `drive = 2 k delta` against `2 mu k s`.  The decision book quotes
`delta_inf = (2 mu - 1) min(s, cap/(2 mu k))` from P111, but that is neither what
P111's `closed_form` computes (`mu s + mu_b m g/(2k)`) nor the geometry; the
threshold `mu = 1` is the same in all three and the residual differs 2x at
`mu = 0.6`.  With the 0.5 N contact trigger the **four-contact** state is a
*stiffness window* `k in [0.5/(s(1-mu)), cap/(s(1+mu))]`, empty above
**`mu = 0.815`** per fruit and **0.613** pool-wide (one stiffness, `s_max/s_min` =
2.35); at `mu 0.6` it is `[4223, 4400] N/m`, a 1.04x sliver that excludes the
shipped 1e5.  At the measured mu the four-pad window is EMPTY and the three-pad's
is `[3113, 3677]`, containing P111's measured window (which was a three-pad
number).  The condition the *line* actually meets is the third one: capture from
an offset needs `mu < cap/(2 k s)` = 1.07-2.51 at `k = 3300` and **0.05-0.12 at the
shipped 1e5**.  Also found: P112's `algebra.py` `fixed_point` subtracts the drive,
so its trial runs *away* from the centre (its closed forms are fine).

**Bench A** (P117's rig, `fixture_pinch.py`, 60 cells + an 18-cell friction sled).
`flat` reproduces P117 to the digit (pear 8.47 vs 8.62, orange 9.07, strawberry
0.98, lychee 12.42), so the instrument is P117's.  **A0** - a flat cube between
two pads, pulled until it slides: the pair tracks the target with a constant
**+0.02-0.03** (measured **0.43 / 0.63 / 0.82 / 1.02 / 1.22 / 1.38** at targets
0.40-1.36, `sumN` 9.80 N), i.e. **`mu_pair < 1` is real and controllable** - the
whole phase rests on it and it holds.  **A1** - the load-axis creep (`dz`, the
direction the load acts) is **-0.03..+0.03 mm at every mu and fruit**, so the
book's creep clause *passes* even at pair 0.6; the **total** creep is
**mu-invariant** (pear 8.47 -> 8.68 -> 8.70 -> 8.55 -> 8.59), confirming P117's A6
on a 2.2x ladder and showing why the total cannot be the verdict (it fails the
incumbent).  The axial break falls as `2 mu N` (pear 9.45 -> 4.49 = 0.48x, orange
0.49x).  **The trade is retention**: at pair 0.6 and 0.8 the two smallest fruits
are **ejected during the seat** (0 pads, 1.2 m fall) on 12/12 cells, against 12/12
held at pair 1.0+ - a squeeze-out at P117's **5 mm** interference (its
constant-force design), harsher than the line's 1 % seat, so it is the price of a
*shared* material rather than a prediction of the line.

**Bench B** (P112's protocol, `fixture_ring.py`, 160 cells).  The support proof
passes (pads home -> drift **0.0000 mm**; a frictionless payload centres 10.00 ->
0.02 mm).  A **sphere cannot test this** and that is a finding: every sphere cell
centred to 0.00 mm at both pair 0.6 and 1.35, because the sphere's surface leaves
the 26 mm plate beyond `delta ~ 9 mm`, so the payload slides in **friction-free
whatever the material**.  The payload is therefore a **square prism**, the
algebra's own 2-D case.  Result: **the full close is clean on 8/8 cells at every
pair 0.6-1.35 and both stiffnesses (80/80 cells, `off_end` 0.00-0.86 mm)** - a
position-controlled close keeps pushing (the near pad at its 4.9 N cap) while the
friction is `2 mu N_perp` (0.8-2.1 N), so the payload slides in and four pads
load.  **The first-contact freeze is the term that denies the enclosure**: at the
shipped close the clean count is **3/8 at the 1.35 control and 5/8 at pair
0.6/0.8** (+2 cells, 0/5 mm arrivals only), **2/8 at every mu** at the soft close,
and the 20 mm residual is 3.3-33 mm at every mu - against a line arrival of
**55.8 mm**.  cage3 was not evaluable on a square payload (the support proof
fails: a three-fold ring cannot centre a four-fold face set), recorded as D1; the
three-pad algebra is P112's own measurement and is reproduced.

**The kill**: K1 does not fire, **K2 fires** (the shipped pair already encloses
under a full close, 4/4 control cells at 10-20 mm), K3 not uniform -> **no build,
no cell**.  The transferable sentence: **the algebra's centring is a sub-millimetre
residual and the line's problem is a 6-56 mm one**; a V-block on the line is the
**widest-extent aperture law plus the first-contact freeze**, not friction.

**Named next, priced**: the ring with `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_CLOSE_FREEZE=0` and the
**shipped** material - the fixture says it envelopes a 0-20 mm arrival with all
four pads - a single-arm `cage4` cell at 2 seeds x 20 attempts, endpoints P110's
clean enclosure + the placed count; and if a low-mu pad is ever wanted elsewhere,
A1 prices it (0.48-0.49x break-away, the 34-37 mm class ejected at a 5 mm seat,
the load-axis creep unchanged), so scope it to the ring.

**Guards**: `scripts/accept.sh` with every knob unset **8/10 = 80 %,
`fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**, its **421 `[fruit]` lines 421/421
byte-identical** to `logs/p127/accept_restored.log`; `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)** with the new `P129 pad material` leg
(`scripts/265_p129_material_selftest.py`, 18 checks: the four cage knobs' unset
path, the openarm finger material's two default sites, the pair arithmetic
1.25-1.46, the algebra's 0.815 / 0.613 / 4223-4400); `106` **OK**; `107` **PASS
(21 checks)**.  No reference re-recorded (`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320`).
Evidence `logs/p129/`.

## P131 (2026-11-08) - the ring's over-closure is the law, not the drive; the fix removes it and exposes the V-block

The owner's question after P130: `cage4` + `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_CLOSE_FREEZE=0`
converts the rate (+28.7 points), but over-closure became the dominant failure
(22/40, "the aperture below `dia - 4 mm`"). Is the ring driven inside the fruit
by the force-capped drive, or is the aperture law wrong? The rule: fix the law
if it is the law; publish the negative if it is the drive.

**The census first** (`logs/p131/census.py`, offline, before any code edit): 72
`[cage]` rows (P130's `F5`/`F6` freeze off + P108's `B_s5`/`B_s6` freeze on),
each joined to its approach's `end=`, its `grasp_lift` `[carry]` row and its
`[run] attempt` outcome, with the fruit's radial/axial extents recomputed from
`meshes.axis_extent` (the `pxr` import stubbed; the profiles are arithmetic).
On the 80 shipped-law freeze-off rows `aper / (0.97 min(radial, axial))` is in
**[0.96, 1.02] on 75/80, p50 0.998** - the close runs to the **two-jaw**
`deep = 0.97 x min(radial, axial)`, i.e. the fruit's **height** on an upright
flat fruit, and never to the ring's `0.98 x widest`. The measured span is at or
above the command on every row (`sep_end - aper` p10 **+0.0 mm**; P131's
close-time `sep - aper` p10 **+0.00 / -0.01 mm**), so **the drive is not the
term**.

**Two metric artefacts inflate P130's 22/40.** (1) The strawberry's class `dia`
is its **height**: `R/dia = 0.792`, so `aper < dia - 4` flags every strawberry
grasp at `aper/R` 0.95-0.98. (2) A ring that **missed** the fruit
(`off > 15 mm` at the close's end) also reads `aper < dia - 4` with no fruit
between its pads. Corrected (seated `off <= 15 mm`; over = `aper < R - 4 mm` or
`F > 29.4 N`), P130's split is **clean 11/40, over 7/40, miss 15/40, vblock
4/40, jam 1/40**. The 7 over-closures are tomato 2 / peach 2 / apple 3 at
`aper/R` p50 **0.874**, and **6 of the 7 placed** - the over-closure is a
geometry defect, not the failure class; the **15 misses** are.

**The build** (`FRUIT_CAGE_APERTURE`, default `shipped`, the P107 expression bit
for bit): `max_extent` (the mesh's largest axis - a screen) and `pad_axes` (the
max over the ring's **own four pad axes** in the cage base frame, the P112
analogue; equal to the shipped axes for a top-down hand).  One task route makes
it operative: for an armed radial hand `deep = pinch_width x
FRUIT_GRIPPER_SQUEEZE` (0.98) and the two-jaw **2.5 mm interference floor is
dropped** (the ring reaches its cap at `cap/k` = 0.049 mm; 2.5 mm is 8.5 % of a
29 mm berry).  Unset keeps the shipped target and floor on every hand.  The
`[cage]` row gains `law= ext= deep= sep=` (the measured span at the flush); the
probe is default off and the acceptance stays 421/421.  New selfcheck leg
`scripts/266_p131_cage_aperture_selftest.py` (the unset path recomputed bit for
bit, the two laws, the tilted base case, the cage3 invariance, the two routing
branches, the row fields).

**The cells** (`cage4` + freeze off, the scripted single arm, the P130 scenario:
`FRUIT_BIARM` left unset, so the refused cage scheduler still scopes the
wave/balanced supply, 20 attempts, the P108/P110 instrumentation).  The
pre-registered `U5 == F5` replay is **not available**: two identical unset runs
diverge at attempt 0 (`at pick pose` 0.84 vs 0.86 s, the peach's `fruit_y`
0.4832 vs 0.4812) - the cage cell is **not bit-reproducible** (the P39 `F1`
precedent, on a new mode).  So the control is the fresh same-tree `U5`/`U6`.

| cell | law | placed | clean | over | vblock | miss | jam | n/c |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `U5`/`U6` (control) | shipped | **10/20, 10/20** | 7+6 | 3+4 | 2+1 | 6+8 | 1+0 | 0 |
| `P5`/`P6` | `pad_axes` | **3/20, 9/20** | 4+7 | **0+0** | 7+6 | 8+5 | 0 | 1+1 |
| `M5` | `max_extent` | 3/20 | 3 | 0 | 7 | 8 | 0 | 1 |

* **The over-closure is removed**: 7/40 -> **0/40**, exact Fisher **p = 0.0117**.
  The witness is a 62 mm tomato at **50.7 -> 59.8 mm** (`aper/R` 0.818 ->
  0.965, drive at 61.3 mm) and the 69-70 mm apples **61.0-61.7 -> 68.0-68.2 mm**.
* **The enclosure does not convert**: clean **13/40 -> 11/40** (p = 0.81) and the
  **V-block rises 3/40 -> 13/40** (p = 0.0103), because the arrival is `off0`
  p50 **3.6/3.5 mm** (control) / **4.3/5.6** (treatment) against P110's
  `delta < 0.6 mm` for all four pads to reach.  The old 10-13 % over-closure was
  **masking** the V-block by driving every pad deep - at the 4.9 N/pad cap, so
  the ring enclosed violently and 6/7 of those attempts still placed.
* **The placed count is a branch**: 20/40 -> 12/40 (p = 0.11; per seed 10 -> 3
  and 10 -> 9), with the `P5` draw carrying one 2.0 m ejection.  Not a rate.
* **`max_extent` is a measured negative**: 9/20 rows have `ext > R + 2 mm`
  (pear 4, kiwi 2, **strawberry 3** - its height is its largest axis) and
  **0/9 place**; the ring closes on air.  A blind "close wider" is not the fix.

**Guards**: crush **0 legs**; landing payload-present **9/9, 10/10, 10/10, 10/10,
3/4, 9/9, 3/3** - the one failure is `P5` attempt 4 (a 3.0 cm lychee held at
9.97 N in a V-block, flung **2.0 m** during the place leg, the cage's closed
loaded-slide class, not a release miss), so `logs/p131/gates.sh` **rc = 1** on
that letter only; descent budgets **PASS on all five** (worst `|v|max`
0.130-0.144 vs 0.160-0.162, lurch 0.039-0.065 vs 0.291, not re-tuned); no new
reason key.  **No-harm**: `scripts/accept.sh` with every knob unset **8/10,
9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`, `190: PASS`**, its **421 `[fruit]` lines
421/421 identical** to `logs/p127/accept_restored.log`; `scripts/selfcheck.sh`
**PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)** with the new `P131 cage aperture law` leg;
`106` **OK**, `107` **PASS (21 checks)**.

**Deviations, recorded**: **D1** the non-reproducible cage cell (above; the
control is fresh, every count is one branch); **D2** the PREREG's D2 bar was the
P130 control's 11/40, the fresh control is 13/40 and `pad_axes` is 11/40 (-2,
inside the control's 5-7 per-cell spread; p = 0.81) - a draw; **D3** a P130
by-product the logs expose: `F5`/`F6` ran the refused-default two-line
**wave/balanced** supply while the P108 `B_s5`/`B_s6` "controls" are
`FRUIT_BIARM=0` **scatter** cells, so P130's 19/40 vs 6/32 crosses two supplies
and the freeze's same-supply effect is not in that record.

**The answer**: the law was the bug; the fix is real; the over-closure was not
the binding failure.  The remaining blocker is **centring** (P110's 0.6 mm, or a
workstation that presents the fruit on the ring's axis), not the closure law.
`FRUIT_CAGE_APERTURE` stays **default `shipped`**; `pad_axes` is the measured arm
if it is ever paired with a centring step.  No `configs/` change, no reference
re-recorded (`30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` / `8952c320` stand).  Pins: `cage_hand.py`
`0f56b2ff`, `tasks.py` `76dbfc6b`, `rl_env.py` `b11113fb` (`TASKS_MD5` =
`76dbfc6b`), `scripts/266_p131_cage_aperture_selftest.py` `de1d28f6`,
`scripts/selfcheck.sh` `5dd45f91`; ckpt `moe_v13s` `61da390a`.  Evidence
`logs/p131/`.

## P132 (2026-11-08) - the serrated pad face: the sustained walk is at the rig's floor, and the static pad-asset lane closes

**The question.** The owner picked the last geometric route: a new pad asset for
the loaded-slide class (`logs/p42/SIM_LIMIT.md`'s sanction; the decision book
`docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md` §4). The class is 75 % of the shipped two-line's
failures (`cnp`), the ceiling is 93.8 %, the shipped cell 58/80 = 72.5 % at four
seeds. The record has measured force (10-60 N, a draw at six seeds), friction
(1.45-1.84x capacity, creep -5 %), the concave/V/cradle face (1.56-2.89x worse on
the pear), and the **creep is lateral** (a seat shift along the jaw axis, `dz`
-0.03..+0.03 mm), while the class itself is a **dynamic pry** (P75: a 0.3 mm
slide, the force collapses, the pads reach their 98.1 mm stop while the payload
walks along the tool axis). The untried form is the one that acts on that walk:
**ridges perpendicular to it** (across the pad's width, spaced along the tool
axis), a ratchet. P117's grooves run the other way.

**The fixture** (`logs/p132/fixture.py`, P117's rig: the pool's own mesh/mass/
friction, the 61.0 x 84.9 mm plate, 4.90 N/face, k = 1e5, the 150-tick close, the
90-tick settle, the 90-tick `m(g+5.83)` hold, the 5 N/s ramp; 48 cells, 112 s):
`flat`; `serr` (5 ridges, 1.0 mm, 8 mm pitch, 60 deg flanks); `serr45` (the same
at 45 deg flanks - the brief's "at 45 deg" is read as the flank angle); `lip20`
(the flat face with a 20 mm lip - fixture-only, 9.5 mm below the shipped distal
plane). **A1:** zero pad force + weight compensated, 200 ticks -> **0.000 mm**; no
compensation -> falls **613 mm**. **A2:** 48/48 cells load 2 pads at 4.54-4.99 N.
**A3:** every facet is 10.0 mm thick on x.

**The result: no shape promotes.** The **load-axis walk** (the displacement during
the 0.75 s hold, the phase's primary) is **at the floor for the incumbent and both
serrations** - pear +0.03, orange -0.00, strawberry +0.00, lychee -0.00 mm, and
the shapes +0.02..-0.04 - so the rule's first clause (`<= 0.6 x flat`) is not
resolvable; a 0.01 mm against a 0.00 mm control is noise, not a reduction. The
**2 mm break-away** (P104's escape threshold, P75's trigger) is a draw to worse on
the small classes: `serr` 1.16x pear / 3.44x orange / **0.77x strawberry** /
**0.35x lychee**, `Fexit` 0.98-1.38x; `serr45` 1.54x / 1.00x / 0.75x / 1.13x;
`lip20` 0.50x / 2.08x / 1.08x / 1.02x. The **one measurable walk** is `lip20`'s
pear **-2.82 mm** (down) with a **0.50x** 2 mm break-away: the deep lip gives the
payload more room to seat, not less. The serration *does* reduce the **total/
lateral** creep on pear/lychee (6.70 -> 5.47, 12.05 -> 7.86) but not on the orange
(8.76 -> 9.71) - a lateral seat effect, the direction P117 already closed, and not
monotone. **Crush** is `dia - 10 mm` (the 5 mm interference per side) for every
profile, inside P76's -15 mm rule, and the delivered force is the 4.90 N cap.

**A fixture defect found while building, and it changes the flat control.** P117's
`author_pad` built the facet frame `(tan, nf, w_axis)`; that is **left-handed for
one pad of every pair** (tan=+y, nf=+x, w=+z gives tan x nf = -z), and
`_quat_from_columns` turned the box 90 deg. Measured world extents: `flat S00L
(10.0/62.2/84.9)` vs `flat S00R (62.2/10.0/84.9)` - the right pad carried its
**62 mm length on the thickness axis** and its face sat 30 mm behind its body. The
first battery's small fruits fell on *every long-axle profile including `lip20`*,
which is a flat face with no ridges: the facet, not the serration. The fix is one
line, `w = cross(tan, nf)`; the corrected flat control reads pear `creep_op`
**6.70**, strawberry **12.22**, lychee **12.05** mm (P117/P129's 8.62 / 0.98 /
12.42 were that rig's; the strawberry's 0.98 was the 62 mm block's cradle). The
A/B is on the corrected rig for all profiles. The teeth are anchored at the
**fruit's widest row**, not the pad's face centre (the face centre is 31.95 mm
above the equator; P117's `asin(|u*|/r)` is corrected to `|u* - u0|/r`); for the
pear the widest is 2.5 mm above the distal plane, so the **downward** side has
less than one 8 mm pitch - a 5-ridge downward ratchet is not buildable inside the
shipped 10.5 mm lip (P39/P69's belt constraint from the other side). The four
upper teeth are the ones an upward walk meets.

**Verdict: no build, no cell, the static pad-asset lane closes.** The rule is the
fixture first; a promoted shape would have been built on the OpenArm fingers,
default off, at the shipped 10.5 mm lip / 80.5 mm distal plane, then the two-line at
seeds 5/6 x 20 with same-seed controls. None of that is licensed. The **dynamic
residual** is named: the class is a dynamic pry and this rig is a static pull, so
the negative is about the *static* pad-asset lane; a blind dynamic cell is the only
test that could overturn it, and it is not registered. The workstation, the decision
book's only remaining geometric route, is excluded by the owner's constraint (no
stop/diverter/guide/pause).

**No-harm**: no `src/` or `configs/` change, `FRUIT_FINGER_FACE` still defaults to
`flat`, no `serr` token in `src/`; the new `267` leg pins the unset path and the
geometry. `scripts/accept.sh` **8/10, 9.0 s/attempt, `fingerprint: matches`,
`190: PASS`**, its **421 `[fruit]` lines 421/421** identical to
`logs/p127/accept_restored.log`; `selfcheck.sh` **PASS (0 failures, 1 skipped)**;
`106` **OK**, `107` **PASS (21 checks)**. References `30fb99f8` / `30fb99f8` /
`8952c320` untouched; no re-record. Pins: `tasks.py` `76dbfc6b`, `rl_env.py`
`b11113fb`, `scene.py` `b3bf8067`, `assets.py` `24d29679`, `fruits.py` `c8f19228`,
`cage_hand.py` `0f56b2ff`; `logs/p132/PREREG.md` `e31db91f`; ckpt `moe_v13s`
`61da390a`. Evidence `logs/p132/`.

## P133 (2026-11-08) - the end-effector decision book is closed with the bench that answered its nails

`docs/END_EFFECTOR_DECISION.md` §7 (design/handover), plus a STATUS note in §4
and §5 pointing at it. What the bench said:

* **Nail (i), `mu < 1`: closed.** The four-pad residual is `mu s`, the four-contact
  state a stiffness window empty above `mu` 0.815 per fruit / 0.613 pool-wide,
  and capture needs `mu < cap/(2ks)` (a rigid close fails it at any mu). The pair
  is controllable (`pad_mu = 2t - mu_payload`, +0.02) but its price is the
  small-fruit ejection (12/12 cells at pair 0.6-0.8, break-away 0.48-0.49x). The
  ring centres and loads all four pads at the **incumbent 1.35** (80/80
  full-close cells) - friction is not its term.
* **The ring's real terms**: the **close freeze** (P130: +28.7 points, p=0.0135,
  47.5 %), and **centring** (P131: the aperture law ran to the two-jaw target; the
  fix removes the over-closure 7/40 -> 0/40 but exposes a 3.5-5.6 mm arrival
  against the ring's 0.6 mm). `FRUIT_CAGE_APERTURE` stays `shipped`.
* **A new pad asset: closed** (P132): the ratchet's walk is at the rig's floor,
  worse on the small classes, and the 10.5 mm lip cannot hold an 8 mm pitch. The
  fixture defect is recorded: P117's strawberry 0.98 mm was a left-handed facet
  frame (one pad 62 mm thick), corrected to 12.22 mm.

Revised recommendation: **no geometric purchase**; the one open measurement is
the **real-jaw force anchor** (fidelity, not rate); the workstation is the only
path to the ring's centring and the owner's "dynamic only" constraint excludes it.

## P135 (2026-11-09) - a tracker, not a formula: the handover was the term

The owner's brief: the target's motion is not guaranteed to be uniform, and its
position and diameter must come from a model, not from the simulator. The
record's own numbers said where to look - `logs/p95`'s other-arm strike displaced
an incoming fruit 28 mm at 0.284 m/s and the attempt ended `never_held`.

Four formulas were in the catch: the aim (`_dynamic_aim`, once at the pre-pose),
the handover gate (`fruit - grip <= speed*(t_desc+0.15)`, `speed` = the belt
scalar), the open-loop descent, and the catch-up's `fruit + velocity*0.25`.

**Built.** `tracking.FruitTracker` (CV + adaptive process noise; exact on the
model, a step followed by the third tick); the correction defined **against the
conveyor** so it is zero when the belt is the belt; `_approach(track=...)`
re-aiming every tick; the catch-up closing on `predict_at(lead)`; and
`FRUIT_TRACK_WAIT=1`, the handover as a **prediction** test.

**Measured, and the negative first.** A velocity impulse on the fruit is damped
by the belt in ~30 ms: the catch-up absorbs 0.10-0.35 m/s lateral and 0.10-0.30
downstream in <= 24 ticks, 24/24 grasped, and the cost lands in the *carry* class
(0-2 of 3 placed at dx 0.35). So the impulse is not a tracking test - it is a
confirmation of the class split.

**The conveyor is.** A sine on the belt speed (`FRUIT_BELT_WAVE_AMP`), the fruit
riding it with no slip. The shipped gate then starts the descent at the wrong
time and the fruit arrives **298, 339, 407 mm** away: two/one of three attempts
spend the catch-up's whole 200-tick budget and fail. The re-aim alone cannot fix
it (80 mm clamp, the miss is upstream of the descent). The prediction gate fixes
all of it: **17/16/16 and 16/15/17 ticks at 5.4-5.9 mm**, timeouts 2 -> 0 and
1 -> 0, at both wave rungs. On the nominal belt the gate is algebraically the
shipped one (0.02 vs 0.018 m), and the nominal cell is a tie (11/13/11 ticks vs
10/13/11; 0/3 vs 0/3).

**Perception.** `perception.py`: RGB-D + instance mask -> back-projection through
the authored lens and the camera prim's pose -> trimmed sphere fit. Bench
(`FRUIT_TRACK_APPLY=0`): **4.70 mm median / 6.41 p90** position, **3.42 / 4.29 mm**
diameter - the registered bars pass. In the loop: **2/2 grasped**, catch 13/38
ticks at 5.9 mm, the filter's velocity 0.116/0.118 against the belt's 0.120.
Two integration rules: the descent's start must **force** a camera frame (else the
30 Hz period eats the only anchor and no filter is ever created), and a refused
frame must return `None` (a cached estimate fed back is a lie the filter cannot
see). The camera's own limit is measured: the hand occludes the fruit exactly
when it matters - the mask shrinks 48 -> 22 px and the fit's z drifts 11 -> 44 mm
- so the module refuses a cap below 60 px and the estimator predicts through it.

No-harm: acceptance 8/10 + fingerprint matches + 190 PASS with 421/421 `[fruit]`
lines byte-identical to `logs/p127/accept_restored.log`; selfcheck PASS with the
new `P135 tracker` leg; 106 OK, 107 PASS. Nothing ships; `configs/` untouched.

## P141 (2026-11-11) - the belt state becomes an observation, and the encoder was an echo

The owner's plan: the belt is not uniform, so the policy must see its state. Two
things came out of it.

**The defect.** The first 3-episode wave collection recorded `belt_speed` with
ptp 0.0000 - every frame exactly 0.1200. The channel read
`Conveyor.encoder_speed`, which `step()` recomputes **only when the cleats
exist**, and the cleats have been off by default since P43/P71. It is the
setpoint echo the P27 note always said it was, so with a belt that changes speed
the trigger, the descent's schedule and the 26th channel all read 0.12 while the
belt ran 0.08-0.16. `Conveyor.surface_speed` returns the value `_apply_speed`
writes into PhysxSurfaceVelocityAPI, and both readers now use it. Constant belt:
the same number, acceptance 459/459.

**The inputs** (all gated, default off): the goal gains (v_belt, a_belt) 8 -> 10,
refreshed every tick; the 26th proprio column becomes per frame when the store
carries the trace; the horizon is a config (4). a_belt has one implementation and
the loader and the live loop share it. Warm starts preserve the function at step
0: zero columns for the goal, 0.5*[w,w] for the visual kernel (a static window
reproduces the 2-frame embedding to 4.8e-07).

**Measured.** 10 episodes / 1733 windows under the wave, belt_speed 0.08-0.16,
median ptp 0.08. Fine-tune: 11011 windows, 6 epochs, loss 0.0149, router 0.993,
demo_val 0.0133, artifact 10/26/4, 4.603 M params. The channels are **used and
measurable**: replacing them with the constant-belt belief moves the chunk 1.18
mrad (goal pair 0.84, proprio column 0.43), and the calibration says that is
worth ~2 mm of fruit position (goal x +1 mm = 0.54 mrad). Latency: 26.4 ms p50 at
DDIM 16 vs 13.4 at 8, so EXEC_STEPS=2 (16.7 ms of sim) is inference-bound at 16
and fits at 8 - the coherent pair is EXEC_STEPS=2 DDIM=8, not adopted.

**Not claimed**: no rate (10 single-arm episodes; the direct A/B is blocked by
P139's park slot and the on_output_belt(final) scorer), no task-time gain, and
the two-line wave store is unbuilt (the collector wedged on its first attempt).
The live integration loads and steps the 10/26/4 checkpoint; the episode then
hits P139's defect, which is that lane's standing item.

## P142 (2026-11-11) - the guard was dormant, and the despawn scan parked owned bodies

Two bookkeeping failures fabricated the direct lane's zero.

1. The P139 handover guard was written **inside** `if FRUIT_SAMPLE_DIAG == "1"`,
   so the shipped loop never ran it: the live rollout printed "openarm fingertips
   103342 mm from the fruit; closing anyway" with the guard present. It now runs
   outside the gate, and the abort is physical: `sample.parked` or
   `pad_error > FRUIT_HANDOVER_PAD_ERROR_MAX` (1.0 m). The flag term (`_foreign`)
   is reported, not gated - the station reselect legitimately re-protects the
   presented fruit, measured at 349 mm and 77 mm against the defect's 101-103 m.

2. `FruitSpawner.update`'s despawn loop skipped only `parked`, so `_recycle_end`
   parked a held/protected body while the attempt still read
   `position(sample)` - a teleport to the park slot. The recycle is deferred now
   (`_pending_recycle`), drained by the next update after the attempt releases
   the body; the [sample] row reads a real floor position instead of the slot.

3. The score endpoint is declared: `FRUIT_SCORE_ENDPOINT=release` scores the
   task's own `placed` (on_output_belt 0.5 s after the release) instead of the
   finalize-time position, because with the rails removed a placed payload can
   roll off in the last second. Default `final`; the row names it only when armed.

Measured: with the reselect off (close on the fruit the descent aimed at), 2
episodes read 1/2 with `success=True grasped=True placed=True` - the first
success=True in this investigation. With the reselect on, both cells read 0/2 and
the log shows why: the presented fruit was at the station when adopted and is 1.14
m away (or on the floor) by the close, i.e. the descending hand knocks it off.
That is the P95 class, inside one attempt, and the remaining term is the
reselect's timing - it is decided during the close, after the descent aimed at
another fruit. Named, not built.

No-harm: acceptance 7/10 + fingerprint matches + 459/459 [fruit] lines identical;
selfcheck PASS with the 26-check P142 leg; 211 ok (115 checks).

## Video re-record (2026-11-12) - the head view now shows the -Y placement

The recording's `head.mp4` aimed at (0.34, +0.22, 1.10) from z=2.00, which puts
the **-Y (right) output lane** at the far edge of the frame: the right placement
was outside the picture. The video entry script now overrides the head pose
**for the recording only** - z 2.00 -> 2.35, target (0.34, +0.22, 1.10) ->
(0.55, 0.00, 1.10), i.e. lifted and turned toward the output deck - through
`FRUIT_VIDEO_HEAD_Z` / `FRUIT_VIDEO_HEAD_TARGET_{X,Y,Z}`, and says so in the log:

    [video] head camera z=2.35 target=(0.55, 0.0, 1.1) (shipped 2.00 / (0.34, 0.22, 1.1))

This is a **video-only** override: `SceneConfig`'s head camera is the policy's
input, so its pose is a scene contract and no measured path changes. A raised
*observer* was tried first and rejected on the frame (a steeper pitch made the
whole-cell composition worse - `logs/video_final_raised/observer.mp4`).

Re-recorded `logs/video_final/` (3 two-line cycles = 6 placements, all
`grasped=True placed=True`, 71.6 s each, 2148 frames): `head.mp4`,
`observer.mp4`, `gripper.mp4`, `side_by_side.mp4`, `preview.png` (a frame at the
right arm's place). The previous files are kept in `logs/video_final_prev/`.

## Video playback (2026-11-12) - this machine has no H.264 decoder

"Why won't the video open?" The files are fine: `ffmpeg -f null` decodes all 2148
frames of every one, they are H.264 High / yuv420p / level 3.1 with `+faststart`
(moov before mdat). The **player** is the problem - this box's GStreamer has no
H.264 decoder at all:

    gst-inspect-1.0 avdec_h264     -> no such element
    gst-inspect-1.0 openh264dec    -> no such element
    gst-inspect-1.0 vah264dec      -> no such element

`totem` (GNOME Videos, the double-click default) is a GStreamer front end, so it
refuses every MP4 the recorder writes. `gst-inspect-1.0 vp9dec` / `vp8dec` /
`jpegdec` DO exist, so a VP9 WebM plays there.

Fixed two ways: `70_record_video.py` now writes a **VP9 `.webm` beside every
MP4** (`FRUIT_VIDEO_WEBM=0` disables; best effort), and `logs/video_final/` has
the copies plus a GIF of the right-arm placement and a 4x3 contact sheet for
anything that will not play video at all. `ffplay` and VLC both work on the MP4s;
`gst-discoverer-1.0` reads the WebM as VP9 848x480 71.6 s and `decodebin !
videoconvert ! fakesink` decodes it with zero errors.

## Reproducing the old clip's content on the current tree (2026-11-12)

The old `video_final` (10-07) shows three B-grade lychees taken by the **right**
arm to the **-Y** lane. A plain `FRUIT_BIARM=0` re-record picks an A-grade lychee
instead (the shipped scatter mix is A:0.5/B:0.3/C:0.2, and lane 0 = grade A), so
the clip looked different for a reason that has nothing to do with the camera.

`FRUIT_SUPPLY_GRADES` needs **all three** keys with a positive weight (`_mix_env`
refuses a partial or zero mix), so the reproduction is `A:0.01,B:0.99,C:0.01` -
largest-remainder allocation gives 16/16 B - plus `FRUIT_SUPPLY_SPECIES=lychee`:

    FRUIT_BIARM=0 FRUIT_SUPPLY_GRADES=A:0.01,B:0.99,C:0.01 \
    FRUIT_SUPPLY_SPECIES=lychee FRUIT_VIDEO_DIR=logs/video_single_lychee \
    FRUIT_VIDEO_HEAD_Z=2.35 FRUIT_VIDEO_HEAD_TARGET_X=0.34 \
    FRUIT_VIDEO_HEAD_TARGET_Y=0.22 FRUIT_CYCLES=3 \
    scripts/run.sh scripts/70_record_video.py

Reads `classes=strawberry:0,lychee:16`, `cycle 0/1/2: lychee grade=B lane=1`,
`target lychee (grade B, 3.4 cm) with right arm`, 3/3 `grasped=True placed=True`,
1798 frames / 59.9 s - the old clip's script (1725 / 57.5 s, same fruit, same arm,
same lane), on today's tree and with the raised, band-free head pose.

## P143 (2026-11-12) - the moving catch is the default on every path

`_dynamic_pick_mode` now returns True with `FRUIT_DYNAMIC_PICK` unset, on every
hand and every path; `=0` restores the P1 indexed line. This is the owner's
adoption of P142's corrected metric: the trigger already fires on a predicted
intercept while the indexed primitive aimed at a frozen position (0.06-0.36 m of
drift at 0.12 m/s), the correct-output rate doubles (53/75 = 70.7 % against 25/75 =
33.3 % after subtracting the mis-sorted placements) and the cross-lane ledger goes
0 against 35 (p = 1.6e-13). The counts alone are a direction (+13.3 points, CI
[-15.2, +15.2], p = 0.154) - the quality term carries it.

No-harm and gates: accept.sh 7/10, fingerprint matches, 459/459 [fruit] lines
identical (the scripted path already resolved True, so the flip is inert there);
the hybrid canary reads 8/10 PASS (top of its 5-8/10 spread, and handoff is a path
the flip does reach); selfcheck PASS with the P142 leg at 35 checks.

The videos exposed something the numbers hid: the direct presentation's trigger is
`off` by default, so the shipped direct cell is the **pure policy** and reads 0/4 -
it never enters the primitive, and the episodes end on P139's park-slot label. With
`FRUIT_POLICY_TRIGGER=arrival` the same checkpoint reads 3/4, and handoff (the
canary) 8/10. So "the model's effect" only means something with the interface
named; arming the trigger by default for direct is a separate flip with its own
re-baseline, not made here.

Validation videos: 121_policy_video.py gains a raised `overhead.mp4` (960x540, z
2.35 with the shipped aim, 0 black rows, both lanes) - the policy's head stays
424x240 and keeps its aim because it is the model's input. Clips for moe_v12 and
moe_v13s (the two adopted checkpoints) live on the external disk with a README.

## P143 addendum (2026-11-12) - what the three numbers actually measure

A correction to the first write-up: with `FRUIT_POLICY_TRIGGER=off` (the shipped
default) the handover is not "off" - it fires when the **policy itself** commands a
close within 6 cm (`finger < 0.030`). What the 0/4 clip shows is that moe_v13s
**never closes**: 0 closes in 7 episodes across two clips (no `policy closed on the
fruit` row), while moe_v12 closes in 2 of 6 and places 1.

So the three interfaces measure three different things:
  self-close (trigger off)  -> the model's own acquisition: v13s 0/7, v12 2/6 (1 placed)
  arrival (external rule)   -> the model as an approach controller: 3/4
  handoff (canary)          -> station teleport + primitive: 8/10 PASS

P143 settles the primitive (whenever the handover fires it is the moving catch);
arming the trigger by default for direct is a separate flip.

The clip directories are renamed to the mode they measure -
mode_selfclose_*, mode_arrival_*, mode_selfclose_indexed_* - with a README that
defines the three axes (presentation / fire rule / primitive), because the old
names (`..._direct_...`, `..._dyn_...`) conflated them.

## P143 diag (2026-11-12) - the model closes ~13 cm short, and a goal lead does not fix it

FRUIT_HANDOVER_DIAG=1 adds gap_min / finger_min to the episode row, tracked where
the policy's own close is evaluated (no extra read). Measured on moe_v13s, direct,
trigger off:

  left  arm: gap_min 155 mm, finger_min 0.0140
  left  arm: gap_min  75 mm, finger_min 0.0131
  right arm: gap_min 153 mm, finger_min 0.0046
  right arm: gap_min 140 mm, finger_min 0.0157
  right arm: gap_min 128 mm, finger_min 0.0066

So the model DOES close the finger (fully), but at 128-155 mm from the fruit, and
the handover gate needs 60 mm - the primitive never fires, the fruit is recycled,
and the episode ends on P139's label. 13 cm at 0.12 m/s is ~1.1 s of travel.

FRUIT_GOAL_LEAD=1.0 (goal shifted by v*lead, zero-shot) is a NEGATIVE: 155 -> 158
and 75 -> 83 mm. The goal is conditioning; the arm position is the learned mapping,
and every demonstration starts with the arm already at the grasp pose, so "one
second behind a moving fruit" is out of distribution.

What works: the hybrid (8/10 canary; 3/4 direct+arrival). What could close the gap:
DAgger on the hybrid's own episodes, with gap_min as the scoring number.

## P143 / A (2026-11-12) - the DAgger round: acquisition halves, success does not

The lane already existed (`--dagger`: the env runs the scripted pick-phase expert,
records its command as the label and the policy's as policy_action). 24 episodes
(seeds 77/101, direct, 240x424, 2/24 success), fine-tuned from moe_v13s + demos_v11
(6 epochs, loss 0.0166).

gap_min, the number that did not exist before:
  moe_v13s        140 mm median (155, 75, 153, 140, 128)
  p143_dagger      63 mm median (1, 5, 26, 48, 60, 60, 66, 71, 81, 99, 102, 103,
                                 139) - 6 of 12 reach the 60 mm gate
  p143_dagger_cw   86 mm median (close-weight 4x) - worse, not adopted

Success is still 0/12 because the gate is a conjunction on one tick: the episodes
either arrive and hold the finger open (1-23 mm, finger_min 0.030-0.041) or close
far out (0.0-0.02 at 86-139 mm). One episode met both and grasped (then lost the
payload to the loaded slide).

Next: a 60-100 episode store at the same recipe, then teach the conjunction
(close when gap < 0.05) rather than the expert's ramp.
